We find that increasing the effective nonlinear dissipative strength suppresses the synchronized region. Restricting the two oscillators to the three-level qutrit subspace, a parity symmetry reduces the stationary-state problem to an exact $41$-dimensional linear system, allowing to compute the synchronization order parameter. In this reduced description, results in the limit of large dissipation agree closely with those from the full dynamics, while exhibiting in the limit of small dissipation a double-peak synchronization structure accompanied by a phase reversal.

papers.title: A New Perspective on Cumulative Residual Rényi Entropy
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a new cumulative residual Rényi entropy (CRRE), which addresses limitations of the existing cumulative residual Rényi entropy. The conventional measure suffers from two primary drawbacks: its failure to converge to the cumulative residual entropy (CRE) as the order parameter approaches unity, and its lack of guaranteed positivity. Our proposed CRRE resolves these issues, offering a theoretically consistent and always nonnegative measure of uncertainty in residual lifetimes. We explore its mathematical properties, including its relationship with existing information measures. Furthermore, the concept is extended to its dynamic version, and its time-dependent characteristics are investigated. A non-parametric estimator of the proposed CRRE is developed, its almost sure convergence is established, and is validated through Monte Carlo simulation. The effectiveness of CRRE as a tool for quantifying uncertainty is confirmed through its application in chaotic theory and financial data.

papers.title: Trading energy for coherence in mode discrimination
papers.abstract: Energy is arguably the main resource in classical physics; coherence is the prototypical quantum resource. In this paper, we study the interplay between these two resources in the task of optimal mode discrimination. This task, motivated by cryptography and metrology, consists of finding in which mode a signal has been encoded, for a given finite set of possible modes. After recalling that the task can be cast as a semi-definite program, we solve completely the case of two-mode discrimination under a hard energy constraint $n\leq N$. Specifically, we identify the region of modes overlap, for which the maximal energy state (the Fock state with N excitations) is the best choice for discrimination. For other overlaps, having access to coherence leads to better discrimination.

papers.title: A parabolic flow approach to generalized Gauduchon metrics
papers.abstract: We give a parabolic proof of the Fu-Wang-Wu theorem for semilinear elliptic equations associated with generalized Gauduchon metrics. Fixing a Hermitian metric $ω$, we introduce a flow $\partial_t v-Δv=ψ(\vert\nabla v\vert^2)+\langle B,dv\rangle-c(t)-f(x)$ for the conformal factor, whose stationary points solve the semilinear elliptic equation of Fu-Wang-Wu. Under the growth condition $\liminf_{t\to+\infty}ψ(t)/t^μ>0$ for some $μ>\tfrac{1}{2}$, we prove that the flow exists uniquely for all time and converges; the limit solves the elliptic equation and is unique up to addition of a constant. Our convergence argument does not rely on a gradient-flow structure or a monotone energy functional. In particular, this recovers, by a flow method rather than the continuity method, the existence and uniqueness theorem of Fu-Wang-Wu on $k$-th generalized Gauduchon metrics, providing a new parabolic approach to their elliptic theory.

papers.title: Second-Order Flows for Approaching Stationary Points via the SAV-E Approach
papers.abstract: Second-order flows represent an emerging computational framework for approaching stationary points of variational energies, characterized by damped hyperbolic partial differential equations. In this paper, we develop a scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) method for this class of flows, referred to as SAV-E. The resulting scheme is linear and decoupled, and we prove unconditional modified-energy stability. We further establish subsequential convergence to stationary points for the Ginzburg-Landau and conserved Swift-Hohenberg models under suitable assumptions. Numerical experiments support the analysis and demonstrate robustness and efficiency compared with representative baselines and the corresponding gradient flows.

papers.title: Uniqueness of twisted linear periods over Archimedean division algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\DD$ be $\R$, $\C$, or $\HH$, and let $H=\GL_p(\DD)\times\GL_q(\DD)$ be the block diagonal subgroup of $G=\GL_{p+q}(\DD)$. We prove that $\dim\Hom_H(π,η)\leq1$ for every irreducible Casselman--Wallach representation $π$ of $G$ and every smooth character $η$ of $H$.

papers.title: Acoustic scattering from quantum dynamics
papers.abstract: Scattering of sound waves propagating in a compressible fluid is linked to the quantum dynamics generated by a class of non-Hermitian Hamiltonian operators. The scattering amplitude is expressed in terms of the corresponding evolution operator. This is used to provide a new proof of the reciprocity theorem in acoustic scattering, conduct analytic low-frequency acoustic scattering calculations, and study the scattering of sound waves by a finite planar array of delta-function point scatters embedded in an infinite acoustic slab. A detailed discussion of acoustic scattering properties of a homogeneous acoustic slab including a pair of delta-function point scatters on one of its faces is provided.

papers.title: On the Optimisation Landscape of Overparameterised Weighted MMD
papers.abstract: We study the optimisation landscape of the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) over weighted atomic measures. For the one-dimensional Gaussian kernel, we show that, for any compactly supported target distribution, sufficiently many particles ensure that every local minimum has arbitrarily small MMD. Moreover, any stationary point whose MMD remains bounded away from zero is unstable under an unweighted gradient flow over the particle locations. These results hold both when the weights are constrained to the simplex, and when they are unconstrained but optimised at each step. When the target is itself finitely supported, we further strengthen this result: beyond an explicit particle threshold, there are no spurious local minima, and every spurious stationary point is unstable. To our knowledge, these are the first finite-particle overparameterisation guarantees of their kind for weighted MMD optimisation.

papers.title: ANOVA approximation for high-dimensional control systems
papers.abstract: We study the data-driven approximation of control-affine systems, where the drift and each control vector field exhibit a low-dimensional structure. While the ANOVA (ANalysis Of VAriance) decomposition is tailored to low-dimensional structures, a straightforward implementation does not exploit control affinity, rendering the approximation computationally expensive. We propose a coupled least squares approach for given state-control samples, whose ansatz is affine linear in the control by construction and can be realized by a preprocessing of the ANOVA index sets. Based on a Marcinkiewicz--Zygmund inequality for the resulting ansatz space, we prove a probabilistic $L_2$-error bound with explicitly given constants. Separate error control on drift and input vector fields renders the approach flexible to, e.\,g., parameter changes. Finally, we numerically illustrate the identification of the coupling structure via global sensitivity indices on discretizations of a nonlinear advection-diffusion equation, the shallow water equations and the viscous Burgers equation.

papers.title: Endpoint regularity of Radon transforms associated with real analytic phases in the plane
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the endpoint Sobolev regularity of Radon transforms associated with real-analytic functions in the plane. We establish all of the failure of endpoint regularity for real-analytic phases. On the one hand, the critical endpoint regularity $L^p(\mathbb{R}^2)\rightarrow L^p_s(\mathbb{R}^2)$, corresponding to extreme points of the reduced Newton polyhedron of phase function, is true if only and only if $p=2$. For generic extreme points, this failure of endpoint regularity generalizes a result of Christ \cite{christ}. On the other hand, we find that the endpoint Sobolev regularity also fails on a bounded segment of the reduced Newton polyhedron when the bisectrix $y=x$ intersects one of unbounded faces at a relative interior point. In particular, our results imply that the Radon transform is not bounded from $L^p$ into $L^p_{1/n}$ with $p=n/(n-1)$ or $p=n$, where the phase functions are real-valued homogeneous polynomials $S(x,y)=a_1x^{n-1}y+a_2x^{n-2}y^2+\cdots+a_{n-1}xy^{n-1}$ with $n\geq 3$ and $a_1a_{n-1}\neq0$. This answers a problem of Phong and Stein in 1994. Moreover, the main results of this paper also give examples which show failure of critical Sobolev regularity for degenerate Fourier integral operators satisfying finite type conditions formulated in \cite{Seeger93,seeger2}. Based on earlier results and our proof of several remaining cases, we conclude that all of other critical endpoint Sobolev estimates are true for Radon transforms associated with real-analytic phases in the plane. Therefore, all failures of endpoint regularity estimates are clearly determined.

papers.title: Does Policy Mirror Descent Converge in Policy with Non-Decomposable Mirror Maps? A Counterexample
papers.abstract: Policy mirror descent (PMD) refers to a class of policy optimization methods associated with different mirror maps. For a broad class of decomposable Legendre mirror maps encompassing many standard choices, Li and Wei [2026] show that the PMD policy sequence converges to an optimal policy from any admissible initialization under any positive constant step size, even when the optimal policy is not unique. In this note, we provide a counterexample with assistance from OpenAI's GPT-5.6 model, showing that PMD with a non-decomposable Legendre mirror map need not converge in policy.

papers.title: Resolvent Expansions at All Spectral Thresholds for Three-Dimensional Discrete Schrödinger Operators
papers.abstract: This paper studies resolvent expansions at all four spectral thresholds for the discrete Schrödinger operator $H=-Δ+V $ on $\Z^3$, where $Δ$ denotes the discrete Laplacian on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ and $V(n)$ is a real-valued decaying potential of $\mathbb{Z}^3$. At the thresholds 0, 4, 8, and 12, we first give a complete classification of the threshold types and derive the corresponding resolvent expansions in weighted $\ell^2$-spaces, including the non-generic cases of resonances and eigenvalues. As a result, we establish the Jensen-Kato type time-decay estimates of the evolution $e^{itH} P_{ac}(H)$ to discrete Schrödinger equations with thresholds singularities on $\Z^3$, with decay $O(t^{-3/2})$ when all thresholds are regular and $O(t^{-1/2})$ otherwise. These results provide a three-dimensional lattice analogue of the Jensen--Kato classical analysis at zero energy threshold on $\mathbb{R}^3$.

papers.title: GPU-Accelerated Preprocessing for Large-Scale Linear Programming
papers.abstract: GPU-accelerated first-order methods are increasingly effective for solving large-scale linear programs (LPs), yet LP preprocessing remains predominantly CPU-based and can become costly. A key challenge is that dependencies among presolve reductions and frequent modifications to sparse LP data make efficient GPU parallelization difficult. To address this challenge, we develop GPU-Preprocessor, a GPU-native LP preprocessing framework that integrates folding and presolve. To efficiently implement folding on GPUs, we adapt a randomized partition refinement algorithm to LP folding, using sparse matrix-vector products and parallel sorting to construct stable row and column partitions. For presolve, we introduce a new piecewise-linear reformulation rule that exploits underlying convex piecewise-linear structure to obtain sparser LP representations. We also develop a framework that combines phase scheduling with a Scan-Plan-Apply design to coordinate presolve rules and reduce sparse-matrix reconstruction overhead through batched updates. Numerical experiments on three LP benchmark sets show that GPU-Preprocessor achieves greater average problem-size reductions than PSLP and Gurobi Presolve, with SGM10 preprocessing-time speedups of up to $43.9\times$ and $677.7\times$, respectively. Here, SGM10 denotes the shifted geometric mean with a 10-second shift. On the largest tested quadratic assignment problem LP relaxation, these speedups reach $126.3\times$ and $2{,}207.9\times$. When integrated with the GPU-accelerated LP solver HPR-LP, GPU-Preprocessor achieves SGM10 speedups of $2.5\times$ to $5.0\times$ in combined preprocessing and solving time over HPR-LP without preprocessing. The code is available at https://github.com/PolyU-IOR/GPU-Preprocessor.

papers.title: Coupled reciprocal-sum inequalities for Neumann eigenvalues in rank-one symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a rank-one symmetric space of compact or noncompact type and real dimension $m=kn$, where $k\in\{1,2,4,8\}$ is the real dimension of the underlying division algebra. Meng and Wang proved sharp isoperimetric inequalities for reciprocal sums of the first $p$ or $\ell$ nonzero Neumann eigenvalues, with indices strictly below $m$ in the nonconstant-curvature cases. We keep the whole $m$-dimensional transplanted first eigenspace of an equimeasurable geodesic ball and treat its mass and stiffness forms as a coupled generalized eigenvalue problem. For every bounded connected smooth domain in a noncompact rank-one symmetricspace we prove the full sharp estimate \[ \sum_{j=1}^{m}\frac{1}{μ_j(Ω)} \ge \frac{m}{μ_1(B)}, \] where $B$ is a geodesic ball with $|B|=|Ω|$; equality characterizes geodesic balls. The Hopf-direction contribution is encoded by a positive, unital, trace-preserving projection on symmetric matrices, and the finite-dimensional closure is supplied by a positive-projection Jensen inequality. In compact type, under the localization hypothesis of Meng--Wang, the same full estimate is obtained whenever $\cot^2 R\ge k-1$, where $R$ is the radius of the comparison ball, as well as in the isotropic endpoint cases and for Hopf-balanced angular second moment. Consequently the complete $m$-term inequality holds for all complex and quaternionic projective spaces under the original localization assumption, and for the Cayley plane when $R\le \arctan(1/\sqrt7)$. In the remaining admissible Cayley interval we exhibit a finite-dimensional obstruction showing that the affine tangent-matrix bounds alone cannot yield the full trace estimate. This obstruction concerns the proof mechanism and is not a counterexample to the unresolved spectral inequality.

papers.title: Safety stock calculation with heteroscedastic, autocorrelated and heavy-tailed forecast errors, an adaptive parametric method.e
papers.abstract: This study develops and validates an adaptive parametric method for sizing safety stock when forecast errors are autocorrelated, heteroscedastic, asymmetric, and heavy-tailed. Using four years of weekly forecasts from a fast-moving consumer goods company, the analysis identifies substantial positive autocorrelation, departures from normality, systematic forecast optimism, and heterogeneous relationships between forecast volume and error variance. The proposed method integrates several corrections into a modular, sequential safety-stock architecture. It constructs cumulative forecast errors over the operational action period, selects an SKU-specific parametric distribution, and determines a baseline protection point using an expected-shortage condition consistent with the target beta fill rate. A forecast-scaled module adjusts dispersion when error variance depends on forecast volume, while a Cycle-End Exposure safeguard limits within-cycle shortage risk when large replenishment lots increase exposure. Performance is evaluated through discrete-event simulation against the company's current method. The proposed method reduces average inventory by 9.9% and maximum inventory by 19.5%, with no statistically significant deterioration in beta fill rate or average stockout duration. The proportion of weeks without stockouts declines slightly, without evidence of more persistent or operationally severe shortages. The heteroscedasticity module provides selective benefits, with greater service improvements as variance dependence intensifies. The resulting framework is interpretable, adapts to SKU-specific statistical profiles, links distributional features to safety-stock outcomes, and can be integrated into existing ERP environments.

papers.title: The orientation-reversing minimal stretch factor problem in small genus
papers.abstract: We determine the minimal stretch factors among all orientation-reversing pseudo-Anosov mapping classes of the closed orientable surfaces of genus two, three and four.

papers.title: Online reduced-order modeling from primal solver trajectories for PDE-constrained optimization
papers.abstract: Repeated high-fidelity state and gradient evaluations make large-scale PDE-constrained optimization computationally expensive. Reduced-order modeling provides a natural way to reduce the cost of these repeated high-dimensional computations. However, existing reduced-order modeling approaches often rely on converged high-fidelity states for model construction or updating, while their reduced spaces may lose accuracy as the design moves beyond the region represented by the available data. To address these limitations, we present Reduced-order Trajectory-based Optimization (RETO), an online framework that constructs local reduced-order models (ROMs) directly from unconverged primal solver trajectories. Each local ROM is built from snapshots collected during a finite number of high-fidelity primal iterations, without requiring full-order convergence, and supports multiple low-cost state evaluations, adjoint-based gradient evaluations, and design updates. New solver trajectories are generated at updated design points to reconstruct the local ROM and continue the optimization. Across three distinct PDE-constrained optimization problems, RETO achieves solution quality comparable to that of full-order optimization, with speedups of approximately 8 to 22 times in cases without discontinuities in the state fields. Even in the transonic inverse-design case involving moving shocks, RETO retains an approximately threefold speedup. The transonic results further show that the online local ROM progressively captures evolving shock-related flow features as new primal solver trajectories are incorporated. These results demonstrate the value of unconverged primal solver trajectories as an online information source for reduced-order optimization, allowing the reduced basis to evolve with the design rather than requiring a basis that covers the entire design space in advance.

papers.title: Dimension of the Green measure of skew products with dominant exponent in the fibers
papers.abstract: Let $f(z,w)=(p(z),q(z,w))$ be a polynomial skew product of $\mathbb{C}^2$ of degree $d\geqslant 2$ and let $μ$ and $μ_p$ be the Green measures associated to $f$ and $p$ respectively. Let $λ_1 > λ_2$ and $λ_p$ be the Lyapunov exponents of $(f,μ)$ and $(p,μ_p)$ respectively. We show that if $λ_2 = λ_p$, then $μ$ is exact dimensional and: \begin{equation*}\dim_Hμ=\frac{\log d}{λ_1}+\frac{\log d}{λ_2}.\end{equation*} The proof relies on the continuity of the conditional measures obtained by Jonsson, on the fact that $μ$ has constant Jacobian $d^2$, and on a fibered version of a normal form theorem for the inverse branches of the iterates of $f$.

papers.title: Finite volume quotients of bounded domains with piecewise smooth boundary
papers.abstract: We prove that a bounded pseudoconvex domain with piecewise $C^2$-smooth boundary which has a finite volume quotient for the complete Kähler-Einstein metric is biholomorphic to a product of complex unit balls. More generally, the same conclusion holds for a bounded domain possessing a boundary point satisfying Kodama's conditions (C.1)-(C.5), provided the quotient has finite volume for a complete $\operatorname{Aut}(D)$-invariant Kähler metric. For piecewise Levi-flat boundary the product is a polydisk and in the smooth pseudoconvex case it is a single ball.

papers.title: Stability of the P_2 semi-Lagrangian scheme
papers.abstract: Among the various space interpolation operators used in high-order semi-Lagrangian schemes, the case of finite element interpolation presents a somewhat incomplete stability theory, partly due to the impossibility of applying in a standard form the framework of Von Neumann analysis, even in the constant coefficient case. In this work, the stability of the P_2 semi-Lagrangian scheme is stated in the case of the constant coefficient equation on a uniform mesh, using a suitable extension of the Von Neumann technique to treat block circulant matrices.

papers.title: On several judicious partitioning problems of graphs and hypergraphs
papers.abstract: Judicious partition problems ask for vertex partitions of graphs or hypergraphs that optimize several quantities simultaneously. In this paper, we investigate judicious partitions of graphs and hypergraphs in which each class meets many edges and establish the following results. (1) Every hypergraph with nonnegative edge weights and all edges of size at most $2$ has a bipartition in which each vertex class meets edges of total weight at least $(w_1-Δ_1)/2+2w_2/3$, where $w_i$ is the total weight of the edges of size $i$, and $Δ_1$ is the maximum weight of an edge of size $1$. (2) Every hypergraph with all edges of size at most $3$ has a bipartition in which each vertex class meets at least $m_1/2+3m_2/4+7m_3/8+o(m_1+m_2+m_3)$ edges, where $m_i$ is the number of edges of size $i$. (3) For any integer $k\ge4$, every graph with $m\ge2(k-1)(k-2)$ edges has a partition into $k$ classes, each meeting at least $2m/(2k-1)$ edges. Both the coefficient of $m$ and the edge threshold are best possible. (4) For all sufficiently large $m$, every $4$-uniform hypergraph with $m$ edges has a partition into four classes, each meeting at least $4m/7$ edges. The first three statements are conjectures of Bollobás and Scott, and the last is a conjecture of Bollobás and Thomason on 4-uniform hypergraphs. All of the above results are best possible.

papers.title: Smooth periodic extensions by extrapolation and blending for FFT-based differentiation
papers.abstract: Non-periodic functions on closed intervals are extended into sufficiently smooth periodic functions through a continuous Hermite interpolation framework with necessary and sufficient endpoint conditions, using smooth blend-to-zero operators and short extrapolation recurrences. A matrix-free method is introduced for generating these smooth periodic extensions on the fly directly from function values at equidistant points. No precomputed continuation operator or auxiliary basis construction is required. The resulting extensions can then be used for FFT-based differentiation of non-periodic functions. Numerical tests are provided to show the effectiveness of the method, including for the highly accurate solution of a 1D linear advection equation.

papers.title: Spectral truncations of SU(2) and the spectral localizer
papers.abstract: We study operator systems arising from Peter-Weyl and Dirac spectral truncations of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ in the sense of Connes-Van Suijlekom. We determine operator system invariants for these systems, including the $C^*$-envelope and uniform bounds on the propagation number. For Peter-Weyl truncations, we find $\mathrm{prop} \leq 2$ for all connected compact Lie groups, generalizing known results for the torus. We also carry out an analysis of the spectral localizer by Loring and Schulz-Baldes on $\mathrm{SU}(2)$. In this analysis, we find numerical evidence that an index map for operator systems previously proposed by Van Suijlekom only captures the right information in a suitable interval of the parameter $κ$, instead of the limit $κ\downarrow 0$.

papers.title: The volume of foliated surfaces with geometric genus one
papers.abstract: We prove the sharp volume bound $\mathrm{vol}(\mathcal{F})\ge 1/6$ for complex foliated surfaces of general type with positive geometric genus. We also study the equality case and apply the bound to the algebraic integrability and finiteness of small volumes on irregular surfaces.

papers.title: Drift and joint minimal displacement for groups acting on hyperbolic spaces
papers.abstract: We obtain a uniform lower bound for the drift of random walks on hyperbolic spaces in terms of joint minimal displacement. Our main theorem applies to weakly acylindrical actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and is quantitative in all relevant constants. For discrete isometry groups of Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature, the required assumptions are automatically satisfied by the Margulis lemma. This yields uniform gaps at zero in drift spectra for pinched negatively curved Hadamard manifolds, hyperbolic groups, and mapping class groups acting on curve graphs.

papers.title: Free-Material Optimization in a Peridynamic World
papers.abstract: We study free-material optimization for nonlinear bond-based nonlocal diffusion and its localization as the interaction horizon $δ$ vanishes. Bond conductivities are subject to pointwise bounds and a global material budget constraint. After normalization, the asymptotic behavior of these problems is governed by the fraction $θ_δ$ of potentially active bonds that can be assigned the maximal conductivity. We identify three distinct limiting regimes. If $θ_δ\to0$, the normalized optimal values converge to those of the classical vanishing-material optimal design problem, equivalently formulated as a Lipschitz-constrained state problem or a measure-valued flux problem. For $θ_δ\toθ\in(0,1)$, we obtain a directional local free-material problem governed by the upper tail of the directional $p$-strain over position-direction space. Thus the state variable localizes, while the limiting constitutive law retains an internal directional variable inherited from the bonds. If $θ_δ\toθ\geq1$, the limit is the isotropic local $p$-Dirichlet problem. A convex minimax argument eliminates the normalized conductivity variable exactly, after which the analysis combines convex duality, nonlocal compactness, and $Γ$-convergence for convex integrands. We prove a unified $Γ$-convergence result for the reduced state energies whenever $θ_δ\toθ\in[0,+\infty)$, yielding convergence of normalized optimal values and compactness and identification of optimal states throughout the full parameter range. At the vanishing-material endpoint, we additionally recover optimal measure-valued local fluxes from optimal nonlocal two-point fluxes.

papers.title: On the Lattice Tilings by Lee Balls: Q-Polynomials, Group-Ring Equations, and a Decision Algorithm
papers.abstract: More than 50 years ago, Golomb and Welch conjectured that no tilings of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ by Lee balls of radius $r$ exist for $n \geq 3$ and $r \geq 2$. This conjecture remains open even under the additional assumption that the tiling is a lattice tiling. In general, there are two known effective approaches to the lattice case which are based on symmetric polynomials and on the arithmetic of group-ring equations, respectively. In this paper, we develop both approaches. First, we determine all coefficients of the Q-polynomials associated with Lee balls; previously, only leading coefficients and certain special cases were known. Second, for arbitrary radii, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of lattice tilings by Lee balls in terms of group-ring equations, extending earlier results for radii $r=2$ and $3$. We then derive new necessary conditions for such tilings. For every radius $3\le r\le 50$, we prove that the set of dimensions for which no lattice tiling exists has positive density in \(\mathbb{Z}^+\). We also give an algorithm that combines the available necessary conditions and apply it to all pairs $(n,r)$ for which the corresponding Lee ball of radius $r$ and dimension $n$ has size less than $2^{30}$. Among these $1{,}358$ pairs, the combined method excludes $1{,}356$, leaving only $(n,r)=(35,3)$ and $(805,3)$.

papers.title: From Global to Tail Convergence: Dynamics of $α$-Stable Score-Based Generative Models
papers.abstract: Score-based generative models driven by $α$-stable L{é}vy processes have been proposed as an alternative to Brownian diffusion models, with empirical evidence suggesting improved sampling and better modeling of heavy-tailed data. Yet theoretical guarantees for these models remain limited. We develop a non-asymptotic convergence analysis for scale-preserving $α$-stable generative dynamics, covering both compactly supported and power-law targets. In p-Wasserstein distance, we quantify the effects of early stopping, initialization, score approximation, and time discretization, and show exponential decay of the initialization error. A comparison with Brownian dynamics reveals that global Wasserstein convergence alone does not fundamentally distinguish the two models: both initialization errors decay exponentially with the forward horizon on the common class of heavy-tailed targets. A sharp separation emerges instead in the tails. At any positive generation time, stable dynamics produces power-law tails with index $α$, whereas Brownian dynamics remains light-tailed. For a target with tail index $ν$, asymptotically correct extreme-quantile scaling is possible precisely when $α$=$ν$. These results identify tail-index matching as a principled mechanism behind the ability of stable generative models to capture extreme events.

papers.title: On blow-up for the supercritical defocusing nonlinear scalar wave equation
papers.abstract: We study finite-time singularity formation for the scalar defocusing nonlinear wave equation $-\partial_t^2u+Δu=u^p$. First, for fixed $d\geq4$ and odd $p\geq3$, we establish a conditional blow-up result under the assumption that a smooth self-similar imploding profile exists for the leading-order relativistic Euler system, with associated normalized coefficients satisfying quantitative analytic radius conditions. Second, we verify both the profile and the analytic radius conditions in dimensions four and five for all sufficiently large odd $p$. Using finite speed of propagation, we obtain a dimension-independent threshold $p_0$ such that, for every $d\geq4$ and every odd $p\geq p_0$, finite-time blow-up occurs for some smooth, compactly supported, real-valued initial data. The proof combines a normalized formulation that separates the leading periodic oscillation from the unknown modulation, growth of the spatial analytic radius induced by an outgoing property, and frequency-dependent matrix multipliers that control the cumulative growth caused by the periodic linearized potential.

papers.title: Prefixes of Coxeter elements are Coxeter elements of the reflection subgroups they generate
papers.abstract: Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system of finite rank, let $T$ be its set of reflections and let $c \in W$ be a Coxeter element. For $x$ in the interval $[1,c]_T$ of the absolute order, let $P(x)$ be the subgroup generated by the reflections $t\le_T x$. We prove that $x$ is a Coxeter element of $P(x)$ with respect to the canonical Coxeter generators of $P(x)$, that $P(x)$ is generated by the factors of any reduced reflection factorization of $x$, and that the Hurwitz action on the reduced reflection factorizations of $x$ is transitive. The proof reduces the general case to the case of a Coxeter system whose Coxeter matrix has entries in $\{1,2,3,\infty\}$, which was treated by Hubery and Krause.

papers.title: Quantum-enhanced phase interrogation of a fiber-optic strain sensor
papers.abstract: Fiber-optic sensors enable high-sensitivity measurements of various physical parameters. Here, we demonstrate a quantum-enhanced interrogation of an all-fiber-optic Fabry-Perot resonator, employing entangled two-photon interference to probe directly strain-induced optical phase shifts. The resonator is interrogated by a narrow-linewidth laser that is frequency-locked to its resonance mode, thereby exploiting the cavity's inherent sensitivity to variations in the fiber length. To access the phase fluctuations transferred to the interrogation field due to external perturbations on the sensor, we implement an in-fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer readout. This configuration allows the sensor to operate both with classical coherent light and with entangled photon pairs generated via spontaneous parametric down-conversion. Harnessing two-photon entangled states corresponding to an N = 2 NOON state, we experimentally demonstrate a reduction of the measurement noise below the standard quantum limit. These results provide clear evidence of the quantum advantage in enhancing fiber-optic sensors under practical constraints on optical power.

papers.title: Quantum-enhanced Search for Galactic Dark Photons Using Cat-State Cavities
papers.abstract: We present a quantum-enhanced search for the Galactic dark-photon background (GDPB), a relativistic and anisotropic vector field that can be produced by dark-matter decay or annihilation in the Milky Way halo. We reinterpret an existing quantum-enhanced dark-photon dataset obtained with a superconducting circuit QED platform originally developed for wave-like dark-photon dark-matter searches, consisting of a high-$Q$ niobium cavity in the $\mathrm{TM}_{010}$ mode dispersively coupled to a transmon qubit. By preparing four-component cat states and performing repeated quantum non-demolition parity measurements, analyzed with a hidden Markov model, we extract photon-transition probabilities for multiple cat amplitudes and integration times. The coupling to the GDPB is governed by a polarization- and angle-dependent cavity overlap function, which predicts a distinctive diurnal modulation of the excitation rate for both longitudinal and transverse polarizations. From the absence of such modulation, we set 90\% confidence-level bounds on the kinetic-mixing parameter $ε$ for two benchmark production mechanisms (parametric and cascade decay) over the relativistic mass range $m_X \ll ω_c$.

papers.title: Global well-posedness of the energy-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the three-dimensional torus with additive Lévy noise
papers.abstract: This paper establishes global well-posedness for the defocusing energy-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the three-dimensional torus with a class of additive Lévy noises. For arbitrary deterministic initial data in the energy space, we construct probabilistically strong solutions that are pathwise unique in the critical solution class. Continuous dependence on initial data, convergence of finite-activity approximations, and a vanishing-noise limit hold on finite time intervals. When the effective noise is nonzero, quantitative bounds for mass exit times imply almost-sure unboundedness of the mass and exclude free scattering. The expected energy then admits a cubic lower bound in time. The analysis couples pathwise critical perturbation theory with energy estimates adapted to Poisson compensation and stopping-time arguments based on the exact mass balance.

papers.title: Finite Volume Methods
papers.abstract: This chapter focuses on finite volume methods. The finite volume method is a discretization method that is well suited for the numerical simulation of various types (for instance, elliptic, parabolic, or hyperbolic) of conservation laws; it has been extensively used in several engineering fields, such as fluid mechanics, heat and mass transfer, or petroleum engineering. Some of the important features of the finite volume method are similar to those of the finite element method: it may be used on arbitrary geometries, using structured or unstructured meshes, and it leads to robust schemes. The finite volume method is locally conservative because it is based on a ``balance'' approach: a local balance is written on each discretization cell that is often called ``control volume;'' by the divergence formula, an integral formulation of the fluxes over the boundary of the control volume is then obtained. The fluxes on the boundary are discretized with respect to the discrete unknowns.

papers.title: Continuous and compact embeddings for a class of modular sequence spaces
papers.abstract: In this article we prove the existence of continuous and compact embeddings for a class of modular sequence spaces generated by Orlicz functions. The class under consideration contains sequence spaces of Orlicz-Sobolev type, including certain special cases that have played an important role in a number of applications regarding problems arising in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, as well as Nakano's class of Lebesgue sequence spaces with variable exponents. In a few exceptional cases we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for such embeddings to hold, in many others only sufficient conditions and in that situation we clearly indicate why these are not necessary by means of additional criteria and specific examples. Our results are complementary to those already available in the literature. We illustrate them with several concrete examples.

papers.title: Asymptotic stability and Rayleigh-Taylor instability of stratified states for the three-dimensional rotating primitive equations with gravity
papers.abstract: We study the 3D rotating primitive equations with gravity in a horizontally periodic channel, with viscous horizontal velocity and no density diffusion. For every Coriolis parameter, stably stratified equilibria are asymptotically stable. Small compatible \(H^4\) perturbations yield global classical solutions with uniform \(H^4\) bounds. The oscillatory density and velocity decay like \((1+t)^{-1}\); the density converges at the same rate to a stratified profile, its horizontal mean faster. For small data, the limit profile is the decreasing vertical rearrangement of the initial density, the unique potential-energy minimizer among rearrangements, independent of rotation, viscosity, and initial velocity. Kinetic plus available potential energy is dissipated exactly by viscosity and decays like \((1+t)^{-2}\), and each fluid particle settles where the limit density equals its own. These rates are optimal for every rotation rate. The linearized problem has real, slowly decaying normal modes, viscously overdamped high-vertical-wavenumber internal gravity waves, whose small solutions show the \(H^r\) density rates \((1+t)^{-(1-r/4)}\), \(0\le r<4\), pressure rate \((1+t)^{-1}\), and energy rate \((1+t)^{-2}\) cannot be improved uniformly for small data. Key difficulties are the loss of a horizontal derivative in the vertical velocity, the failure of \(H^1(\mathbb T^2)\subset L^\infty\), and rotation-induced coupling of divergent and vortical motion, controlled at top order by a positive power of the initial low-order energy. If the stratification is unstable somewhere, every horizontal mode is linearly unstable with real growth rates and the equilibrium is nonlinearly unstable; rotation strictly lowers each growth rate, with an explicit Taylor-number bound depending on the horizontal wavelength, but leaves their supremum unchanged.

papers.title: Gaussian approximation for the integrated intensity of counting processes: application to Hawkes processes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish quantitative central limit theorems for the integrated fluctuations of the intensity of a counting process. Building on the work of Coutin and using the Clark-Ocone formula, we first derive a general upper bound on the Wasserstein distance between a Gaussian random variable and the normalized integral of the centered intensity. We then apply this result to subcritical linear Hawkes processes. In this setting, we prove that the integrated fluctuations of the intensity converge in distribution to a centered Gaussian random variable, with a convergence rate governed by the tail behavior of the resolvent associated with the underlying Volterra equation.

papers.title: Void-Free Through-Glass Vias for Multilayer Surface-Electrode Ion Traps
papers.abstract: Through-substrate interconnects are a key technology for scaling surface-electrode ion traps (SEITs) toward large electrode counts and complex architectures. Dielectric substrates such as fused silica offer superior RF performance compared to silicon, but the reliable fabrication of void-free through-glass vias (TGVs) remains challenging. In this work, we demonstrate a SEIT fabricated on a fused silica substrate incorporating TGVs. The via-holes are formed using Selective Laser-Induced Etching and subsequently metallized with gold by electroplating. A patent-pending geometry-assisted bottom-up plating approach enables void-free filling using constant-current electroplating without electrolyte additives or pulsed deposition schemes. Electrical characterization across multiple wafers confirms a TGV-level yield above 98.8 %, demonstrating the robustness and reproducibility of the developed TGV technology. The TGVs are combined with multilayer SEIT fabrication, enabling vertical signal routing to all electrodes while maintaining an unaffected trapping surface without wire bonds. To interface the trap with external control electronics, a glass interposer providing signal fan-out to a larger pitch is designed and fabricated. The trap chip and the interposer are integrated using thermocompression bonding, forming a compact chip-to-chip assembly. The presented technology demonstrates the first fully integrated multilayer SEIT on fused silica incorporating void-free TGVs.

papers.title: The Weil-Petersson diameter of moduli space for large genus
papers.abstract: We determine the large-genus order of the Weil-Petersson diameter of $\mathcal{M}_{g,n}$ for each fixed number of punctures: namely, $\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{M}_{g,n})\asymp\sqrt g\log g$. The main new ingredient is an integrated Ricci estimate for geodesics that minimize in moduli space and have thick endpoints, with no systole bound along their interiors.

papers.title: Coherent-State Integrals Beyond the Domain of Operator Products
papers.abstract: Inserting a resolution of the identity between two operators turns a matrix element of their product into a phase-space integral. For unbounded operators the product need not exist on the vector at hand, while the integral may still converge. We follow this gap through the chain $e^{μa^2}e^{λa^{\dagger2}}$ of two-photon exponentials, where it can be traced completely. Five regions of parameter space appear: where the Bochner conditions of the strong formulation hold, where the product exists as a vector, where it exists as a sesquilinear form, where the coherent-state integral converges, and where the Fock-space series converges. The first three are strictly nested inside the intersection of the last two, and these two overlap without either containing the other. A single Hermite-type function agrees with the matrix element where it exists and with the integral and the series wherever they converge, so the integral carries the analytic continuation of the matrix element beyond the domain of the product and beyond the convergence of its Fock series. On the real slice of parameter space, an iterated form of the integral also reaches every point where the series converges. The analysis rests on a weak composition lemma whose hypotheses concern only the bra, the ket and the resolving family. For bounded chains the same identity is unconditional, and worked examples of that kind are given in a companion paper.

papers.title: On the sum of eccentric subgraph numbers of the vertices of a connected graph
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected graph. The eccentric subgraph number $ε(v)$ of a vertex $v$ of $G$ is defined as $ε(v)=\min\{f_G(v,u): u\in V(G)\}$, where $f_G(v,u)$ is the number of connected subgraphs of $G$ containing both $v$ and $u$. The eccentric subgraph index $ES(G)$ of $G$ is defined as $ES(G)=\displaystyle\sum_{v\in V(G)}ε(v).$ In this paper, we obtain the unicyclic graph that maximizes the eccentric subgraph index among all unicyclic graphs on $n$ vertices with a fixed girth. The graph that maximizes the eccentric subgraph index among all unicyclic graphs on $n$ vertices is also obtained. We then characterize the trees that maximize the eccentric subgraph index over trees on $n$ vertices with fixed diameter. Among all connected graphs on $n$ vertices with a fixed number of pendant vertices, the graph which maximizes the eccentric subgraph index is also characterized.

papers.title: The regular inverse Galois problem over fields avoiding a curve
papers.abstract: Let $k_0$ be a field of characteristic $0$, and let $C/k_0$ be a smooth geometrically integral curve of positive genus with $C(k_0)=\varnothing$. We prove that the regular inverse Galois problem is solvable over every field existentially closed in the class of $k_0$-fields avoiding $C$, including the curve-excluding fields of Johnson and the author. To this end, we show that for every finite group $G$, there is a parameter variety over $\mathbb Q$ whose function field admits a regular realization of $G$ without adding points to $C$. Finally, we establish $\mathrm{RIGP}$ over the variety-excluding fields of Szachniewicz and the author, when the excluded variety is a locally closed subvariety of an abelian variety.

papers.title: On Completely Positive and Semidefinite Programs for Moment Bounds on Maximum of Random Quadratics
papers.abstract: Completely positive programs are known to provide an exact representation to several NP-hard optimization problems. In this work, we look at the maximum of random quadratic functions and compute the maximum expected value over ambiguity sets defined with moment and support information. We propose exact completely positive programs and semidefinite programs when the random variables are Bernoulli, nonnegative and unrestricted in support. Our experimental study demonstrates the utility of these formulations.

papers.title: Exponential functionals of two random walks and stationary measures of discrete growth processes
papers.abstract: We study random walks with geometric or log-gamma increments, reweighted by certain exponential functionals. We establish precise asymptotics for all moments of exponential functionals, revealing a phase transition as the drifts of the walks vary. To describe the large time limit of reweighted random walks, we introduce a discrete $T$ transformation on random walk paths and establish Girsanov relations. As a corollary, we show that the stationary measures of geometric last passage percolation and the log-gamma polymer on a strip converge to their half-space counterparts as the strip width tends to infinity. In the log-gamma case, this provides an alternative proof of a recent result in arXiv:2607.17030.

papers.title: Maximum Likelihood Degrees via One-Edge Chordal Completion
papers.abstract: The maximum likelihood degree of a Gaussian graphical model measures the algebraic complexity of its likelihood equations. This paper studies maximum likelihood degrees of Gaussian graphical models through chordal completion. When a graph becomes chordal after one missing edge is added, its maximum likelihood degree is determined by the maximal cliques and clique-tree separators containing that edge. This recovers Uhler's formula for complete bipartite graphs with one part of size two, and extends it to deleted-spine clique books, whose degree is unchanged when a page is thickened to a clique. For several fill edges, the same method gives a product formula when no clique or separator bag contains two fill edges. We also determine four classes of vertices at which clique blow-up preserves the degree. Two follow from known results, and two are established here.

papers.title: Remarks on prescribed scalar curvature functions
papers.abstract: This short article is devoted to the study of the positive solution of Yamabe-type semi-linear equation with prescribed coefficient on general closed manifolds. Our main result is to provide some sufficient conditions for the existence of the positive solutions and give some examples to show that those conditions are sharp. An application to scalar-flat manifold settles a long standing question in prescribing scalar curvature problem in negative form.

papers.title: Invariable Generation of Groups of Homeomorphisms
papers.abstract: We provide a sufficient condition for a group of homeomorphisms of a compact Hausdorff space to be non-invariably generated, generalizing previous results proved using the dynamics of a group's action. We exhibit new applications among Scott-Röver-Nekrashevych groups and among groups of tree automorphism of with (almost) locally prescribed actions.

papers.title: The fence conjecture for convex projective polygons
papers.abstract: We prove the fence conjecture of Dumas and Wolf: for a convex projective polygon with at least five vertices, every zero of the Pick differential lies in the interior of the region obtained by cutting off the triangles at consecutive triples of vertices. The proof gives a stronger estimate for arbitrary properly convex domains. In affine-sphere coordinates normalized at a Pick zero, the domain contains the closed disk of radius $2^{-1/4}$ and its closure lies in the open disk of radius $2^{1/4}$, unless it is a rotated square. The proof compares the canonical Monge-Ampère potential of the domain with that of a normalized square. Their third-order contact gives alternating local sign sectors. A planar separation argument and the maximum principle show that the negative sectors belong to four distinct components, each meeting a different side of the square. Rotation gives the inner disk bound, and conormal duality gives the outer bound. Both constants are optimal for the class of properly convex domains normalized at a Pick zero. The argument requires neither boundary smoothness nor any restriction on the multiplicity of the Pick zero.

papers.title: C1 Virtual Element Methods for the Optimal Control of Oseen Equations with Stream-Function Formulation
papers.abstract: This work analyzes a $C^1$-conforming virtual element method for the optimal control of generalized Oseen equations, formulated using the stream-function on simply connected polygonal domains. The method is based on a conforming discretization in $H^2$ of arbitrary order $k \ge 2$. The discrete scheme considers an approximation of the state and co-state equations which involves a specifically designed operator for the convective term and a \textit{variational discretization} of the control variable. We derive quasi-optimal a priori error estimates in the $H^1$ and $H^2$-norms for the stream-function, and in the $L^2$-norm for the control, under standard assumptions on the family of polygonal meshes. The proposed method recovers the fluid velocity, vorticity, and pressure using suitable projections. Finally, we report several numerical experiments to support the theoretical findings using different polygonal meshes including the cavity problem. We highlight that this analysis also covers OCPs governed by Brinkman and Stokes equation.

papers.title: Algebraically Integrable Smooth Convex Bodies
papers.abstract: We prove that a convex body with $C^\infty$ boundary in an odd dimension $n\ge3$ is algebraically integrable if and only if it is an ellipsoid. This answers Arnold's problem for smooth convex bodies. Together with Vassiliev's even-dimensional nonexistence theorem, it gives the classification in every dimension $n\ge2$. More generally, in odd dimensions, a convex body with $C^\infty$ semialgebraic boundary is an ellipsoid whenever its section volume function satisfies a joint algebraic relation.

papers.title: Weighted composition--differentiation operators on mixed-norm, derivative Hardy and F(p,q,s) spaces
papers.abstract: We study weighted composition--differentiation operators on mixed-norm, derivative Hardy and F(p,q,s) spaces. Explicit dyadic criteria yield boundedness, compactness and two-sided norm and essential-norm estimates, including endpoint and quasi-Banach cases. We also obtain multiplier and approximation results, Schatten criteria on weighted Dirichlet spaces, and exact singular values for monomial weights and linear symbols.

papers.title: Time-Inconsistent Singular Dividend Control with Regime Switching and Bankruptcy
papers.abstract: This paper studies infinite-horizon equilibrium dividend distribution for a firm whose surplus follows a diffusion under observable Markov regime switching and is absorbed at bankruptcy. Dividend payments are modeled as singular controls, and non-exponential discounting leads to time inconsistency. We formulate equilibrium control laws and establish a verification theorem for a general finite-state model with surplus-dependent coefficients. For a two-state model with constant positive drifts and volatilities and bi-exponential discounting, we prove the existence of a regime-dependent equilibrium barrier policy for arbitrary positive switching intensities. The policy retains surplus below the prevailing regime's threshold and distributes any excess immediately. Numerical experiments examine how shareholder patience and economic conditions affect dividend decisions. Over the parameter ranges considered, greater discount-rate dispersion at a fixed initial average rate raises both barriers, while switching speed can generate nonmonotone responses and reverse their ordering.

papers.title: Calabi metric on the space of k-Hessian potentials
papers.abstract: Let $(X,ω)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $1\leq k\leq n$. We consider the space of smooth $k$-admissible potentials introduced in the study of the Hessian-cscK equation by Guo--Smith--Tong. The complex $k$-Hessian equation identifies this space, modulo constants, with the space of smooth positive densities of fixed total mass. We compute the differential of the Hessian density map and use it to pull back the Fisher--Rao metric. The resulting Riemannian metric is \[ G^{\HC,k}_{\varphi}(u,v) =\int_X \bigl(Δ_{\varphi}^{(k)}u\bigr) \bigl(Δ_{\varphi}^{(k)}v\bigr) \,ω_{\varphi}^{k}\wedgeω^{n-k}. \] We then show that the square-root Hessian density map \[ \varphi\longmapsto 2\sqrt{\frac{ω_{\varphi}^{k}\wedgeω^{n-k}}{ω^n}} \] is a global Riemannian isometry onto the positive part of the $L^2(X,ω^n)$-sphere of radius $2\sqrt{V}$, where $V=\int_Xω^n$. For $k=n$, this recovers the spherical description of the classical Calabi metric. We also derive the curvature, geodesic and diameter formulas, and prove a quantitative local comparison between adjacent Hessian--Fisher distances.

papers.title: Sharp radial--angular mixed norm Fourier extension and global stability on spheres
papers.abstract: We study the sharp Fourier extension inequality from $L^2(\mathbb S^{d-1})$ to the radial--angular mixed space $L^q_{\mathrm{rad}}L^2_{\mathrm{ang}}$. Our work is motivated by and builds upon the foundational analysis of Carneiro, Oliveira e Silva and Sousa \cite{COS}, who initiated the sharp mixed-norm spherical restriction problem from the viewpoint of spherical-harmonic decomposition. Their reduction revealed that the extremal problem is governed by a competition among the individual harmonic modes, and their results established degree-zero extremizers in several important ranges of exponents, including even integer exponents and the endpoint case. The present paper addresses this question by establishing a complete modal ordering result. Building on their spherical-harmonic reduction, the sharp-constant problem is reduced to the weighted Bessel moments \[ I_{ν,k}(q) := \int_0^\infty |J_{ν+k}(r)|^q r^{2ν+1-νq}\,dr, \qquad ν:=\frac d2-1. \] For every integer $d\ge2$ and every finite admissible exponent $q>2d/(d-1)$, we prove \[ I_{ν,k}(q)<I_{ν,0}(q), \qquad k\ge1, \] and hence constants are the unique nonzero extremizers of the sharp mixed-norm extension inequality. In dimensions $d\ge3$ we prove the stronger strict ordering \[ I_{ν,0}(q)>I_{ν,1}(q)>I_{ν,2}(q)>\cdots. \] We resolve this difficulty by combining exact Hankel asymptotics with a finite remainder comparison. The modal ordering also yields the optimal quadratic global stability inequality. For every finite admissible $q$, \[ C_{d,q}^2\|f\|_2^2 -\|\widehat{fσ}\|_{L^q_{\mathrm{rad}}L^2_{\mathrm{ang}}}^2 \ge Γ_{d,q}\|f-P_0f\|_2^2, \] with the best possible coefficient. When $d\ge3$, this coefficient is explicitly \[ Γ_{d,q} =(2π)^d \left[ I_{ν,0}(q)^{2/q}-I_{ν,1}(q)^{2/q} \right]. \]

papers.title: The Big Match under translation-invariant charges
papers.abstract: We study two-player zero-sum stochastic games in which a stream of stage payoffs is evaluated by a translation-invariant charge on the set of stages. Every patient valuation, that is, every diffuse charge that obeys the time value of money principle, is translation-invariant, and by Mertens and Neyman each player has, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a strategy that is $\varepsilon$-optimal for all patient valuations simultaneously. We show that this robustness breaks down for translation-invariant charges. In the Big Match with $0$--$1$ payoffs, whose uniform value is $1/2$, every strategy of Player 1 is worthless: for every strategy of Player 1 and every $δ>0$, Player 2 has a pure reply, and there is a translation-invariant charge under which Player 1's payoff is less than $δ$. Consequently, the Big Match has no value with respect to all translation-invariant charges. This contrasts with finite Markov decision processes, where every stationary Blackwell optimal strategy is optimal for every translation-invariant charge. We pose questions on robust guarantees in general stochastic games and on optimality with respect to a fixed translation-invariant charge.

papers.title: Model-Induced Hazard Geometry and Functional Representations in Survival Analysis
papers.abstract: Individualized survival predictions are often summarized by scalar risk scores or event probabilities at selected time horizons, although clinically relevant risk may also differ in its temporal organization. We consider finite-dimensional representations of individual hazard trajectories through interpretable hazard functionals, such as peak timing, cumulative hazard over prespecified intervals, and persistence of elevated risk. A central issue is that the richness of such representations is constrained by the hazard geometry supported by the underlying survival model. We formalize this through model-induced tangent spaces and functional ranks, derive an exact decomposition of model-supported variation into directions retained and lost by a chosen representation, and introduce a model-relative notion of local completeness. We further distinguish intrinsic model capacity from the variation actually activated by covariates. These results motivate a structured extension of AFT time scaling through a positive-affine deformation on the log-time scale, yielding a power-warp mechanism with an additional temporal deformation direction. Combined with a log-logistic reference hazard, this gives a parsimonious likelihood-based working specification for which peak timing and peak height provide complete coordinates over the unimodal regime. We also establish plug-in recovery and asymptotic inference for hazard functionals. Simulations and a lung-cancer application illustrate how model-induced restrictions propagate to hazard-functional representations.

papers.title: What Inverse Problems Can Be Solved Using Neural Networks?
papers.abstract: The relationship between classical methods for solving inverse problems and neural network methods is examined. An answer is provided to the question of what inverse problems can be solved using neural networks. The answer is that neural network algorithms can solve only conditionally well-posed problems (well-posed according to Tikhonov). The reason is that the design of standard neural network algorithms violates the well-known Bakushinsky veto from the theory of ill-posed problems. It requires that any method theoretically guaranteeing a stable solution to an ill-posed problem must depend explicitly on the error level of data. The article highlights the distinction between the concept of regularization (RA) in the theory of ill-posed problems and regularization as understood in neural network training, where Bakushinsky's veto is violated. Due to this violation, any changes to the neural network architecture, regularization during training, or training dataset augmentation cannot alter the answer specified above. It is theoretically demonstrated that an ill-posed inverse problem can be solved only by using a parametric set of neural networks that explicitly depend on the known error levels (as parameters) of data. Accordingly, as an alternative to standard neural network algorithms, \neural network based regularization algorithms (NNBRAs) are proposed to solve ill-posed inverse problems. One approach to their construction involves using a regularized dataset. Such a dataset can be generated from perturbed inverse-problem data using a specific base RA explicitly depended on the error level of the data. Test solving the simplest finite-dimensional ill-posed inverse problem demonstrate that the accuracy of the NNBRA approximate solutions is comparable to that of the base RA. At the same time, errors of conventional neural network methods may be unacceptable.

papers.title: Sharp $L^q$ estimate of adjoint problem and Pucci conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $L$ be a linear second-order elliptic operator satisfying a nondegeneracy condition. We establish sharp $L^q$ estimates for solutions of the adjoint problem associated with $L$ and, by duality, derive sharp $L^p$ estimates for solutions of $Lu = f$. In particular, this confirms a conjecture of Carlo Pucci.

papers.title: Isometries of Unit Spheres of SFS-Spaces and a Geometric Approach to Tingley's Problem
papers.abstract: We investigate surjective isometries between the unit spheres of facially symmetric spaces and their interaction with the underlying facial structure. It is shown that such isometries preserve the essential geometric relations associated with symmetric faces, orthogonality, and geometric tripotents. In particular, a surjective sphere isometry induces a natural correspondence between the geometric tripotents of the underlying spaces and preserves the principal structural features determined by the Peirce decomposition. These results provide a geometric framework for studying linear extension problems for sphere isometries. As an application, we establish a positive solution of Tingley's problem for finite-dimensional real neutral strongly facially symmetric spaces satisfying the joint Peirce property. We also obtain an extension result for a wider class of real neutral strongly facially symmetric spaces admitting an appropriate approximation by finite-dimensional Peirce subspaces. In these settings, every surjective isometry between unit spheres extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry of the ambient spaces. The results demonstrate that the facial and tripotent structures play a decisive role in the rigidity of spherical isometries.

papers.title: Percolative MDLA: phase transition and critical behaviour
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce the model of Percolative MDLA (PMDLA) on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ which engulfs the entire occupied percolation component of each particle that reaches the aggregate. We prove a phase transition of finite time explosion, as a function of the particle density $λ$, where the critical value equals $λ_c=-\log(1-p_c^{\rm site}(\mathbb{Z}^2))$. Below $λ_c$, the process is nonexplosive and has a linear upper bound on its radius. For $2/3<λ<λ_c$, it also has a linear lower bound on the growth rate. Above $λ_c$, an infinite component is swallowed in finite time a.s. At $λ_c$, every update is finite, but the updates accumulate in finite time, causing a blowup. Excluding criticality, the results are generalized to all higher dimensions.

papers.title: Sharp Constants, Threshold, and Failure of Uncertainty Principles on Non-trivial Flat Finsler Manifolds
papers.abstract: By uncertainty principles we mean the generalized Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg (CKN) inequality and the Heisenberg--Pauli--Weyl (HPW) uncertainty principle, with the latter being an endpoint case and the Hardy inequality a further limiting case. We study these \(L^p\)-type inequalities \((1<p<n)\) on \(n\)-dimensional non-trivial flat Finsler manifolds, which arise from Hilbert's fourth problem. These manifolds are forward complete but not backward complete, projectively flat, with zero flag curvature, and have infinite reversibility, making them highly asymmetric. They are the simplest non-Riemannian, non-Minkowskian solutions to Hilbert's fourth problem, providing a natural framework in which classical inequalities exhibit new behavior. For the full class, we establish a sharp threshold at the parameter value \(s=2\): the generalized CKN inequality and the HPW uncertainty principle hold for \(s>2\) but fail completely for \(s\le2\). When the generating Minkowski norm is reversible (while the Finsler metric itself remains irreversible with infinite reversibility), we determine the sharp constants for \(s>2\), which were previously unknown. These constants are approached in the limit by compactly supported radial functions. As a corollary, our results cover Berwald's metric space and resolve the open questions on its sharp constants. These findings reveal that the threshold phenomenon is structural for the entire class and is a genuinely non-Riemannian feature with no analogue in the Riemannian flat case.

papers.title: The $RO(C_2)$-graded Hurewicz image of Atiyah's Real K-theory
papers.abstract: We determine the $RO(C_2)$-graded $k\mathbb R$-Hurewicz image, where $k \mathbb R$ denotes the connective Atiyah's Real $K$-theory spectrum. As a consequence, we obtain four infinite families in the $RO(C_2)$-graded equivariant stable stems that are $C_2$-equivariant refinements of the classical $μ$-families. Using a $C_2$-equivariant $v_{1,0}$-self map, we explicitly construct an equivariant Adams periodicity operator $P_{C_2}$ that captures these $v_1$-periodicity phenomena in the $C_2$-stable stems.

papers.title: Cryogenic Multiplexing Control Chip for Superconducting Quantum Processor
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a scheme and design of cryogenic multiplexing control chip (MCC) which enables one microwave cable to control many superconducting qubits. Designed based on adjustable inductor, MCC is a non-reciprocal device which generates microwave signals between 4 and 8 GHz and constructs XY control circuit to operate qubits. The effects of filters, isolators, power splitters, qubits and load impedance on MCC are analyzed in the frequency-domain simulation. And in time-domain simulation, the response time, Gaussian pulses, single-sideband, amplitude and frequency compensation of MCC are examined. The MCC can be integrated with the superconducting qubits on the same package at 20 mK temperature stage, and output specific microwave pulses used to drive the superconducting qubits without crosstalks. The MCC can greatly reduce the number of microwave control lines and is beneficial to the development of large-scale superconducting quantum processor.

papers.title: On the Erdős--Odlyzko--Sárközy conjecture for prime-power moduli
papers.abstract: Erdős, Odlyzko and Sárközy conjectured that every reduced residue class modulo $q$ contains a product of two primes not exceeding $q$. O. Klurman, A. P. Mangerel and J. Teräväinen (2023) have shown that three primes suffice when $q$ is sufficiently smooth. We study the moduli $q=p^γ$ that are powers of a fixed prime $p$ and we show that the third prime can be taken subpolynomially small. For any $q_\bullet\le q$ for which $q_\bullet\ge\exp\bigl(C(\log q)^{2/3}(\log\log q)^{4/3}\bigr)$, we give an asymptotic formula for the weighted number of representations of each reduced class as a product of two primes not exceeding $q$ and a third not exceeding~$q_\bullet$. We also show that the conjecture holds for all but a proportion $\exp\bigl(-c(\log q)^{1/3}(\log\log q)^{-1/3}\bigr)$ of the reduced classes. Here $C$ and $c$ are positive constants that depend only on $p$. Both results are unconditional and they rely on a wide zero-free region with no exceptional zeros for the Dirichlet $L$-functions attached to characters modulo $p^γ$.We also present conditional versions of these results for arbitrary $q$ under a quasi-Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: On the Isomorphism of Semicircular Algebras
papers.abstract: Building on OpenAI's proof of isomorphism of free group factors, we give a self-contained proof of a corresponding result for $C^{*}$-algebras generated by free semicircular systems: the isomorphism class of a $C^{*}$-algebra generated by a semicircular $n$-tuple does not depend on $n\in\{2,3,\dots,+\infty\}$. Similarly, reduced free products of $n$ copies of the Jiang--Su algebra are isomorphic for different $n$ in this range. While reduced free group $C^{*}$-algebras of different ranks are not isomorphic (by a result of Pimsner--Voiculescu), we show that they have strong free absorption properties. At the heart of the proof is an automorphism approximation property for inclusions of $C^{*}$- and $W^{*}$-algebras; a relative version of that property was previously used to derive free complementation results.

papers.title: A short open space curve of unit width
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a curve to be a minimum of length among rectifiable, continuous curves of unit width in three-dimensional Euclidean space. We show that a previously conjectured minimizer of that problem is not of unit width, give the numerical derivation of a candidate family of unit width curves, prove that it admits a strict local minimum within that candidate family and that this minimum is of unit width and length $3.905124162243593\ldots$. The curve consists of eight straight segments, two cone geodesics, and three circular helices. Its parameters are specified by a uniquely isolated solution of the joining and stationarity equations. To establish unit width in every direction, we combine analytic estimates with interval arithmetic on a finite covering of the remaining directions. We conjecture that the curve is globally minimizing. We supplement this work with the programs used to identify the candidates, replicate the computer-assisted parts of our proof, as well as a formalization of our proof in Lean.

papers.title: Maximizing Reaction via Spatial Localization: A PDE-Constrained Variational Approach
papers.abstract: We study a PDE-constrained variational problem for the optimal spatial distribution of a catalytic material reacting with a substrate in a biological or materials system. With a given catalyst concentration, the substrate concentration is determined by a reaction-diffusion equation. The reaction functional for the catalyst concentrations is defined to be the total reaction output, which is the product of catalyst and substrate concentrations. Both the linear and Michaelis-Menten reaction kinetics are considered. We construct reaction-maximizing sequences through the localization of catalysts using barrier functions and show the non-existence of a global maximizer. We also derive the first and second variations of the reaction functional. By constructing a competing catalyst concentration, we show the non-existence of a local maximizer. Based on our analysis, we propose a regularized variational model and prove the existence of its global maximizer.

papers.title: The Density and Quantitative Upper Bound of Integers Not Expressible as the Sum of a Prime and a Zumkeller Number
papers.abstract: A Zumkeller number is a positive integer whose set of positive divisors can be partitioned into two disjoint subsets of equal sums. In this paper, we investigate the additive properties of these numbers in conjunction with prime numbers. Specifically, we study the natural density of the exceptional set \(\mathcal{E}\) consisting of all positive integers not expressible as the sum of a prime and a Zumkeller number. Let $α(x) = \#\{n \le x : n \in \mathcal{E}\}$ denote its counting function. We establish a quantitative upper bound for $α(x)$, demonstrating that $α(x) \ll x(\log \log x)^{-A}$, where $A = \log_2\left(\frac{2π^2}{2π^2-3}\right) \approx 0.2378$, thereby proving that the natural density of this exceptional set is $0$.

papers.title: A Reconstruction of Michelson Interference from On--Off Detection Statistics
papers.abstract: This paper reconstructs the Michelson interference phenomenon based solely on the binary (on-off) statistics of a single-photon counter and macroscopic path-difference data, without the a priori assumptions of complex wave superposition or prior spectral information. In contrast to the conventional approach that assumes light as a continuous complex wave function and considers interference between them, this study focuses on the algebraic properties inherent in discrete detection statistics. We verify that the discrete response data collected across various path differences form a positive semi-definite matrix, and apply Herglotz's theorem to this result. Consequently, we show that the harmonic form of the interference fringe is not a consequence of adopting a wave model as an axiom, but rather it is uniquely decomposed into a cosine average of wavenumbers dictated by testable algebraic constraints satisfied by the statistical data. Through this approach, the logical basis of the interference phenomenon can be described by the characteristics of the binary data itself, perfectly aligning with the modern optical experimental environment that relies entirely on discrete event statistics.

papers.title: The Two-Level Poset Game is PSPACE-Complete
papers.abstract: Poset games form a fundamental class of combinatorial games that includes classical games such as Nim and Chomp. Determining the outcome of a poset game is known to be PSPACE-complete even for posets of height at most three. However, the exact computational complexity of Two-Level Poset Game, played on posets of height at most two, has remained an open problem for over a decade. We resolve this problem by proving that Two-Level Poset Game is PSPACE-complete via a polynomial-time reduction from Avoid True on positive CNF formulas.

papers.title: Continuous Narayana Interpolations: Hankel Total Positivity and Log-Convexity Preservation
papers.abstract: We study a continuous interpolation between the type $B$ and shifted type $A$ Narayana triangles and its extension through affine moments of the continuous $q$-ultraspherical (Rogers) measure. For every fixed $0<q<1$ and $-1<β<1$, these affine moments form a coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive sequence in the polynomial variable $t$. The proof rests on a general continuant criterion: decreasing nonnegative off-diagonal weights and coefficientwise positivity of the leading continuants imply total positivity of the full tridiagonal matrix. A telescoping identity gives positive certificates for shifted continuants and stability under coordinatewise decreases of the weights. We determine the exact power of $t$, palindromicity, and extreme coefficients of arbitrary Hankel minors. Classical limits recover the continuous Narayana family, including its moment representation and gamma positivity. We further prove that the continuous Narayana transformations preserve strong $t$-log-convexity for every real $θ\ge0$, and that the $d$-Hoggatt transformations have the same preservation property for every integer $d\ge1$. The preservation proofs use the Zhu--Sun criterion and a mixed-minor one-sign-change argument whose local ingredient is a hypergeometric hitting-probability inequality.

papers.title: Shrinking targets versus recurrence: A survey on the Hausdorff dimension theory
papers.abstract: This survey reviews results on the Hausdorff dimension of shrinking target sets and recurrence sets in dynamical systems. In their basic formulations, shrinking target sets concern orbits approaching a prescribed centre, whereas recurrence sets concern orbits returning close to their initial points. A central theme is the comparison of the Hausdorff dimensions of these two classes of limsup sets. The dynamical systems considered include expanding conformal systems, irrational rotations, affine iterated function systems, and matrix transformations. Related results on Hausdorff measure are also included when they provide natural refinements of the dimension theory. Finally, we review results on badly approximating orbits and non-recurrent sets, with particular attention to winning properties and intersections with self-conformal and self-affine sets.

papers.title: Normalized Orbit Frames and Essential Spectrum, II
papers.abstract: Given $0<r_{j}<1$ with $r_{j}\to1$, there exist a normal operator $T$ on $\ell^{2}$ with eigenvalues $λ_{j}$ satisfying $|λ_{j}|=r_{j}$ and $g\in\ell^{2}$ such that \[ \left\{ \frac{T^{n}g}{\left\Vert T^{n}g\right\Vert }\right\} _{n\geq0}\text{is a frame}\:\Longleftrightarrow\:\sum_{j\geq1}\left(1-r^{2}_{j}\right)=\infty. \] Whenever this condition holds, the frame bounds can be chosen with ratio arbitrarily close to one.

papers.title: Shot- and Noise-Aware Pauli Correlation Encoding for Max-Cut Experiments on IBM Heron Quantum Processor
papers.abstract: Pauli correlation encoding (PCE) encodes $m$ binary variables in the signs of $k$-body Pauli correlators of $n=O(m^{1/k})$ qubits, and trains a parameterized circuit on a relaxed loss of sharpness $α$. The strongest published schedules sharpen this loss aggressively and are benchmarked with exact expectation values, whereas a quantum computer estimates correlators from a finite number of shots. We show that the sharpness is a hidden shot budget. Since the expected sign of a correlator estimated from $S$ shots, $\mathrm{erf}(c\sqrt{S/2})$, agrees with $\tanh(0.851\sqrt{S}\,c)$ to within $0.019$, the edge term of the relaxed loss at $α=0.851\sqrt{S}$ approximately equals, up to a constant, minus twice the cut expected from decoding $S$ shots. This explains why schedules tuned with exact expectation values lose their advantage at realistic budgets, and yields a shot-aware schedule whose final sharpness is set by the shot budget. On five G-set graphs with $800$ variables on $13$ qubits, this schedule outperforms every published schedule at its target budget in all $150$ paired comparisons of the decoded circuit output, owing to the sharpness at $1.6\times10^4$ shots and mostly to switching off the regularization at $10^3$; after a classical bit-swap search, it remains the best on average at $1.6\times10^4$ shots. Device noise damps the correlators by a factor $s$, which amounts to a smaller shot budget $s^2S$.
