We also establish properness and growth estimates for holonomy, including a relative version for smooth marked families, and derive finiteness results for spherical conical metrics and ramification divisors of stable extensions.

papers.title: The majority of a cactus is prickly
papers.abstract: We characterise all (undirected) cacti graphs, and forests of cacti, with an edge-preserving near-unanimity operation, by means of forbidden induced subgraphs. Indeed all such graphs also have an edge-preserving majority operation. We show that said majority can be chosen to be symmetric and explicitly construct it for all forests of cacti without the forbidden induced subgraphs.

papers.title: A Composite Representation Theorem for Solution Mappings in Regularized Composite Optimization with Applications to Hausdorff Lipschitz Stability
papers.abstract: We study the geometry and stability of solution mappings in regularized composite optimization, allowing multiple minimizers. We establish a composite representation that separates optimal linear images from their corresponding primal solutions through an image mapping and a generalized basis pursuit mapping. Under a fiber-attainment condition, the image mapping admits a reduced optimization formulation; neither representation requires convexity. For convex regularizers, suitable qualification conditions yield a Fenchel-conjugate representation of the reduced value function and a geometric characterization of the generalized basis pursuit mapping through affine fibers and a fixed lifting set. Using these representations, we establish sufficient conditions for local Hausdorff Lipschitz continuity of possibly set-valued solution mappings. We further show that the primal-space sufficient conditions imply the corresponding image-space conditions, with an additional injectivity requirement arising in the former. The results cover $\ell_1$-type and structured piecewise linear-quadratic regularizers under suitable assumptions. For classical $\ell_1$ regularization, our approach recovers an existing stability result without a finite sign-pattern decomposition. Numerical examples illustrate the recovery of complete solution sets, including a case with a nonpolyhedral graph of the generalized basis pursuit mapping.

papers.title: Local Turnpike Stability for Two-Population Second-Order Mean-Field Game Systems
papers.abstract: This paper establishes a local turnpike property for a two-population, second-order mean-field game system with a quadratic Hamiltonian, in which the running cost for each population may depend on both population densities. In the case of two populations, imposing a scalar stability condition separately on each species is not sufficient because it neglects cross-interaction effects. The appropriate requirement is instead a matrix-valued coercivity condition on vector perturbations $(μ_1,μ_2)$, which involves the symmetric part of the linearized interaction matrix together with weighted Poincaré inequalities associated with the two stationary measures. Consequently, in the multi-population framework, diffusion still acts independently on each population, but the interactions are controlled by the full coupling matrix. A naive scalar energy functional fails to capture mixed second-variation terms arising from costs that depend on both densities. We prove that matrix coercivity is precisely equivalent to the strict positivity of this second variation, and we provide a spectral characterization in terms of the principal spectral value of the coupled stationary linearized operator. For linear models with cross-interactions, this yields explicit algebraic conditions that separate stable parameter ranges from unstable ones. In the non-potential framework, the skew-symmetric part of the interaction matrix leaves the coercivity threshold unchanged, but it can induce transient oscillatory dynamics. Moreover, the scalar turnpike theory extends in a natural, though nontrivial, manner to multi-population systems, where stability is governed by the positivity of a coupled matrix-valued second variation that encodes both self-interactions and cross-interactions.

papers.title: A Feasible Direction Method with Active-Set Identification for Derivative-Free Optimization
papers.abstract: We propose a model-based trust region method for derivative-free optimization with simulation-based inequality constraints. We are motivated by settings of simulation optimization in which both function evaluations at infeasible points may be unreliable and constraint evaluations are expensive. Our method maintains feasible incumbents and computes steps from a subproblem suitable for a feasible-direction method in order to encourage generation of feasible trial points. To reduce the computational cost of modeling the constraints, we describe an active-set estimation scheme that permits modeling with only a subset of constraints in each subproblem, as opposed to maintaining models of all constraints. We show that every limit point of the incumbents generated by our method is a Fritz-John point, and is additionally a KKT point under the Mangasarian-Fromovitz constraint qualification. Under standard nondegeneracy conditions, the active-set estimate identifies, within finite time, all constraints active at the limit point of the incumbents. Experiments on CUTEst problems show that our method generates feasible trial points far more often than a comparable SQP-based approach and solves more problems within a given budget with fewer function evaluations.

papers.title: Block Sensitivity and Certificate Complexity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions
papers.abstract: We study block sensitivity and certificate complexity of rotation symmetric Boolean functions, with particular emphasis on monomial rotation symmetric Boolean functions. We first show that every odd-degree monomial rotation symmetric Boolean function on $n$ variables satisfies $s=bs=C=n$. We then determine sensitivity, block sensitivity, and certificate complexity for every quadratic monomial rotation symmetric Boolean function. For the quadratic function $Q_{n,k}$ generated by $x_0x_k$, we prove, outside the short-orbit case, that \[ C(Q_{n,k})= \begin{cases} n,&4\mid n/\gcd(n,k),\\ n-\gcd(n,k),&4\nmid n/\gcd(n,k). \end{cases} \] Moreover, \(bs(Q_{n,k})=C(Q_{n,k})\) for every quadratic MRS function, and outside the short-orbit case, strict separation \(s<bs=C\) occurs exactly when \[ \frac{n}{\gcd(n,k)}\equiv2\pmod4. \] Finally, for the consecutive quartic family \[ R_n(x)=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z_n}x_ix_{i+1}x_{i+2}x_{i+3}, \] we determine all three measures in every residue class modulo $6$, using the sensitivity formulas and, in one residue class, finite-state results established in our companion preprint~\cite{LiZhangRSBFSensitivity}. In particular, for $r=2,3$ and $6q+r\ge5$ we obtain strict separation, \[ \boxed{s(R_{6q+r})=6q<bs(R_{6q+r})=C(R_{6q+r})=6q+1,\qquad r=2,3.} \] Thus this family gives an infinite collection of rotation symmetric Boolean functions for which sensitivity is strictly smaller than block sensitivity, while block sensitivity and certificate complexity coincide.

papers.title: What the Machine Invented: Mining New Mathematical Instruments from OpenAI's October 2026 Release of AI-Generated Mathematics
papers.abstract: On 6 October 2026 OpenAI published an initial 722 AI-written mathematical manuscripts, organized into 372 problem families, in the public repository github.com/openai/math. The release includes claimed solutions to many prominent open problems. We approach this collection as a treasure mine of mathematical ideas. Our aim is to extract new lemmas, constructions, inequalities and proof mechanisms introduced in the source arguments, and to distinguish them from established tools and new combinations of those tools. We call these mathematical instruments. Extraction comes first; their validity, novelty and possible reuse then become subjects for further study. The resulting descriptions also help readers understand the selected papers without having to reconstruct every argument at the outset. We examine 38 families in two groups of 17 and 21, spanning number theory, geometry, analysis, combinatorics, complexity, algebra, operator algebras, topology and mathematical physics. Each entry records the claim, extracted instruments, antecedents and caveats. Eleven cross-cutting patterns connect the entries, and a scoreboard records formalization status and dependencies. Novelty assessments are provisional and sometimes mixed. Selected source comparisons correct mathematical statements, hypotheses and counts; they do not independently establish priority or certify the underlying proofs. No Lean development was compiled or kernel-checked for this survey. We also briefly describe a subsequent application of the signed restriction lemma from family 112 to circuit lower bounds at every fixed depth.

papers.title: The index of conformal Hopf maps
papers.abstract: We compute the index and nullity of any harmonic morphism from $S^3$ to $S^2$.

papers.title: An explicit construction of a limit variety of groups
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit countable group \(G_*=N(R)\rtimes A\) whose generated variety is a limit variety of groups: it has no finite identity basis, whereas every proper subvariety is finitely based. Here \(A\) is relatively free in the variety of groups of nilpotency class at most two and exponent dividing four, and \(R\) is an explicitly defined quotient of the group algebra \(\mathbb F_2[A]\). The proof establishes an ascending chain condition for coefficient spaces indexed by six ordered commutator entries and reduces every proper subvariety to a hereditarily finitely based approximation. Non-finite basability is obtained by transferring independent identities from the constructions of Gupta and Krasilnikov. The resulting variety is contained in \(\mathfrak B_4\mathfrak B_2\). This construction provides the first example of such a variety in which both the generators and a basis are explicitly given.

papers.title: Sustainable trees
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a connected graph and let $λ_1(X)$ denote the spectral radius of its adjacency matrix. An edge $e$ of $X$ is sustainable if it can be deleted and replaced by a non-edge so that the resulting graph is connected and its spectral radius does not decrease; $X$ is sustainable if every edge is. We study this edgewise notion of spectral robustness for trees, where each replacement is an elementary exchange between trees on the same vertex set. We establish basic properties of sustainability and exhibit infinite families of sustainable and non-sustainable trees. Our main results concern trees with a vertex of large degree: if $T$ is a tree on $n$ vertices with $Δ(T)\geq n/2$, then every vertex of maximum degree is a principal vertex, that is, a vertex at which the Perron vector is maximal. Building on this, we prove that every tree with $Δ(T)\geq n/2+1$ is non-sustainable, and we classify the sustainable trees in the boundary case $Δ(T)=n/2$: for $n\geq 4$, the only such trees are the double broom $B(2,n/2,n/2-1)$ and one exceptional tree on eight vertices. We conclude with open problems on the generalized tree-shift order and the asymptotic proportion of sustainable trees.

papers.title: Matching Randomized First-Order Bounds for Higher-Order Smooth Nonconvex Optimization
papers.abstract: Does randomization improve the worst-case first-order complexity of nonconvex optimization when the objective is very smooth? We prove that, for every fixed finite integer $p\ge3$, finding an $\eps$-stationary point requires $Ω_p(\eps^{-5/3})$ exact value-and-gradient queries, even for $C^\infty$ objectives with initial gap at most one and simultaneous global Lipschitz budgets of one for derivatives of orders $1,\ldots,p$. Together with the known deterministic upper bound, this determines the accuracy exponent up to a single logarithmic factor. The lower bound holds for unrestricted adaptive randomized algorithms, unbounded query locations, and outputs that need not have been queried. One algorithm-independent hard distribution suffices in dimension $O_p(\eps^{-47/3})$. The construction combines a block-chain potential with an exact quartic core, repeated quadratic spectra, and two static Gaussian tensor perturbations. A scheduled Haar argument controls the entire adaptive query span. An innovation-only Gaussian comparison then bounds exact transcript information without assuming finite precision or a minimum query separation. This establishes the $5/3$ randomized accuracy barrier under every prescribed finite smoothness order, extending the previously matched third-order case.

papers.title: $E$-symmetric algebras I
papers.abstract: We study various symmetry conditions related to the Auslander-Reiten formula for finite-dimensional algebras. In particular, we define a new class of algebras which we call $E$-symmetric. A theorem by Derksen-Weyman-Zelevinksy implies that all Jacobian algebras are $E$-symmetric. We prove the converse for the class of monomial algebras.

papers.title: An accurate parallel finite difference method for the variable-order fractional Laplacian in heterogeneous media
papers.abstract: Anomalous diffusion in heterogeneous media is ubiquitous across physical and biological systems, where spatially varying microstructures give rise to distinct transport regimes. Variable-order nonlocal operators provide a natural modeling framework for describing heterogeneity and transitions between diffusion regimes. However, the position-dependent long-range interactions inherent in these operators impose prohibitive memory costs and make numerical methods developed for constant-order operators computationally impractical. Consequently, accurate and computationally efficient numerical methods for variable-order nonlocal operators remain scarce. In this paper, we propose accurate finite difference discretizations for the variable-order fractional Laplacian $(-Δ)^{α(\mathbf{x})/2}$ and develop a fast Fourier transform (FFT)-accelerated scheme for their efficient implementation. The computational and memory costs are $O\!\big(MN\log(2N)\big)$ and $O(MN)$, respectively, where $N$ is the total number of spatial points and $M \ll N$. The method is also naturally parallelizable. We establish its consistency and accuracy through a rigorous error analysis that quantifies the local interplay between solution regularity and the spatially varying order $α(\mathbf{x})$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to quantify how these two factors jointly determine convergence rates, with numerical experiments demonstrating this dependence. Extensive numerical experiments confirm the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method. Applications to anomalous diffusion in composite materials further demonstrate its ability to capture the effects of material heterogeneity.

papers.title: A higher categorical approach to graded bivariant $K$-theories for Real $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We present an $\infty$-categorical refinement of classical $KK$-theory and $E$-theory for graded, $G$-equivariant for a locally compact second countable group $G$, Real $C^*$-algebras. As a consequence, we obtain a couple of fiber sequences connecting the different $K$-theory spectra, and explicitly analyse the induced endomorphisms on $K_0$-groups. We also answer precisely some folklore questions in the area. Among other things, we show that graded $KK$- and $E$-categories are not a Dwyer-Kan localization of graded $C^*$-algebras.

papers.title: Architecting Instruction Execution for Scalable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
papers.abstract: Scaling fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires orchestrating millions of operations continuously across a tightly coupled classical-quantum control stack. A critical challenge in this orchestration is determining the optimal hardware-software boundary, i.e., the Quantum Instruction Set Architecture (QISA). We focus on cryogenic, fixed-connectivity qubit platforms, such as superconducting and topological Majorana qubits. For these, existing QISA choices either operate at too low a level, violating cryogenic thermal budgets at scale, or at too high a level, imposing unrealizable complexity on the control engine. To reason about these tradeoffs, we introduce the ARIES instruction set hierarchy, which categorizes QISAs into distinct abstraction levels. To systematically evaluate these levels, we develop an end-to-end evaluation toolflow featuring a cycle-accurate classical driver and hardware engine simulator. Using eight quantum applications across superconducting and topological qubit platforms, we measure instruction bandwidth, transceiver power dissipation, and measurement processing overheads. We demonstrate that while physical-level abstractions exceed the thermal limits of dilution refrigerators by orders of magnitude, canonical-level abstractions significantly underestimate hardware routing congestion and execution runtimes. Our Level 4 QISA (local logical operations) offers an optimal architectural balance. As quantum hardware platforms scale toward FTQC in the coming years, our findings provide concrete architectural guidance for the design of their classical control stacks and instruction interfaces.

papers.title: Construction of Regular Fat Linear Sets and Non-Representable q-Matroids
papers.abstract: Let $q$ be a prime power. An $(r, i)$-regular fat $\mathbb F_q$-linear set has exactly $r$ points of weight $i\ge2$, called fat points. All of its remaining points have weight one, and at least one such point occurs. We solve two open problems posed by three of the authors of this paper. First, we derive divisibility constraints on the point weights using the scalar stabilizer of the defining subspace. Consequently, a regular fat linear set of rank $2i$ in $\operatorname {PG}(1,q^n)$ has at most two or exactly $q + 1$ fat points. In the latter case, the fat points form an $\mathbb F_q$-subline. Second, we construct higher-dimensional regular fat linear sets whose fat points do not form an $\mathbb F_q$-subgeometry. In particular, for every $k\geq 3$ we obtain examples of rank $2k$ whose fat locus consists of an $\mathbb F_q$-subgeometry $\operatorname {PG}(k-2,q)$ in $\operatorname {PG}(k-1,q^4)$ together with one external point. This construction is then generalized further. Finally, we apply our projective-line results to $q$-matroid representability and present an infinite family of non-representable rank-two $q$-matroids arising from partial spreads.

papers.title: Optical Detection of Coherent Nuclear Spin Control in a Molecular System at Room Temperature
papers.abstract: Molecular systems with optically addressable electron spins are emerging as versatile quantum sensing platforms, offering tunable qubit properties and molecular-scale spatial control. Owing to their longer lifetimes, coupled nuclear spins provide an attractive resource for enhancing sensing performance. For molecular spin systems, the ability to initialise, coherently control and readout nuclear spins at room temperature is crucial for realising such benefits. Here, we present the first optical detection of nuclear magnetic resonance and coherent nuclear spin control with a molecular system at room temperature. Specifically, we demonstrate optically detected Rabi oscillations of $^{14}$N nuclear spins in the photoexcited triplet state of the organic chromophore 6,13-diazapentacene. The strong hyperfine coupling between the electronic spin and $^{14}$N nuclei enhances the nuclear Rabi frequency, enabling fast coherent nuclear-spin rotations. This work lays the foundation for leveraging nuclear spins as memories for enhanced molecular-based quantum sensing.

papers.title: On the foundations of logic and probability, II. Modal probability spaces
papers.abstract: A class of models which brings to the fore the inner logic of the calculus of probability instead of assigning probabilities to sentences is introduced and investigated.

papers.title: On digit-appending walks along linear recurrences
papers.abstract: We study digit-appending walks in base $b\geq 2$ along integer linear recurrences with minimal characteristic polynomials having a unique simple dominant root $α$ that lies outside the unit circle. We prove that if $α$ and $b$ are multiplicatively independent, then no infinite walk can have uniformly bounded appended digit lengths. In contrast, we show that when the appended digit length can be unbounded, the same independence hypothesis implies the existence of infinite walks.

papers.title: Short Proofs for the Minimum Number of Determined Circles
papers.abstract: We present short proofs for the main parts of the recently completed solution of Erdős Problem 506, which asks for the minimum number of distinct circles determined by a finite planar point set that is neither collinear nor concyclic. An inversion argument and a seven-point line lemma show that eight points determine at least $17$ circles, and an explicit configuration attains this bound. A single argument combining Melchior's inequality with Langer's incidence bound establishes the sharp formula for every $n\ge15$. The proofs give concise alternatives to longer arguments in the recent literature; the remaining finite cases are cited separately.

papers.title: Enhanced Quantum Metrology via Saddle-Point Scrambling in Phase Space
papers.abstract: Nonlinear effects are widely utilized in quantum metrology to enhance measurement precision by leveraging complex dynamical behaviors. Here, we propose a quantum scrambling-integrated scheme that optimizes the selection of initial states and parameter encoding by exploiting the nonlinear dynamical trajectories and their geometric properties in phase space. We consider a two-mode Bose-Einstein condensate as a typical example. Within a certain parameter range, using uncorrelated spin coherent states located at saddle points and separatrices enables the measurement precision to reach the Heisenberg scaling. An analytical expression for the quantum Fisher information under long-time evolution is provided, and our analysis further reveals that the enhancement mechanism is governed by the sensitivity of the energy spectrum to parameter variations. Compared to the criticality-enhanced protocol that requires parameters to approach the critical point, our scheme offers a distinct advantage in its applicability over a broader range of parameters. Moreover, this scheme can also be applied to models that include one- and two-axis countertwisting interactions and chaotic dynamics. This Letter offers a new perspective for advancing the application of nonlinear dynamics to enhance the parameter estimation precision in quantum systems.

papers.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 2: variance under the uniform null
papers.abstract: For the counts $(X_1,\dots,X_n)\sim\mathrm{Mult}(N;1/n,\dots,1/n)$ of $N$ observations in $n$ ordered bins we study the variance of the discrete total variation $d=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}|X_{i+1}-X_i|$. An exact decomposition splits $\mathrm{Var}(d)$ into per-edge, adjacent-pair and disjoint-pair terms and yields, for fixed $n$ as $N\to\infty$, $\mathrm{Var}(d)/N=α(n)-β(n)/N+γ(n)/N^2+o(N^{-2})$. For every $n\ge 2$, $Nα(n)$ is the classical normal-theory variance (Hoel, Kamat) of the sum of absolute successive differences of $n$ independent $N(0,N/n)$ variables; the correction $β(n)$ is obtained in closed form for $n\ge 3$ (the case $n=2$ is treated separately). Two disjoint edge differences $D_1=X_2-X_1$ and $D_3=X_4-X_3$ are exactly uncorrelated and asymptotically independent, yet $\mathrm{Cov}(|D_1|,|D_3|)=-1/(πn)+O(1/N)$: a correlation of relative order $1/N$, invisible in the Gaussian limit and absent under Poissonized sampling, whose constant is proportional to the exact joint fourth cumulant $κ_{2,2}(D_1,D_3)=-4N/n^2$ and is proved here on the lattice. The adjacent pair contributes the lattice-Edgeworth constant $a_*=-2\sqrt{3}/(9π)$, of which one quarter is a smooth Edgeworth term and three quarters a lattice-corner term; the disjoint skeleton $h(m)$ is closed through a Bessel generating function; and $γ(n)$ ($n\ge 5$) is expressed through a single triangular-lattice constant whose closed form we conjecture. Together with the mean of Part 1, the variance supplies the two moments used by moment-matched approximations to the null law of $d$. This is Part 2 of a series; the cyclic statistic $d^{c}$ will be treated in Part 5.

papers.title: Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations for Finsler metrics on symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations are random tessellations that arise as limits of Voronoi diagrams for Poisson point processes as their intensity tends to zero. For the Riemannian metric on a symmetric space of higher rank, Frączyk, Mellick, and Wilkens (arXiv:2307.01194) proved that the corresponding ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellation is almost surely completely connected, with an unbounded side between any two cells. This contrasts sharply with the geometry of ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces studied by D'Achille, Curien, Enriquez, Lyons, and Ünel (arXiv:2303.16831). In this paper we introduce and study ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations for Finsler metrics on higher rank symmetric spaces. We show that ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with respect to polyhedral Finsler metrics can exhibit either behavior seen in these previous works: generically they resemble the hyperbolic case, where almost surely all cells have bounded sides. We further introduce the ideal Selberg--Poisson--Voronoi tessellation of the space of positive definite symmetric matrices, which has particularly nice properties.

papers.title: Oka realizations, fundamental groups, and holomorphic cofibrations
papers.abstract: The homotopy types of Oka manifolds are exactly those of countable finite-dimensional CW complexes. We construct realizations as open subsets of complex Euclidean spaces with explicit dimension bounds. Other realizations have good open covers by sets biholomorphic to $\C^N$, with prescribed finite nerves, or are unions of Fatou--Bieberbach domains whose nonempty finite intersections are again Fatou--Bieberbach domains. Every nonempty Stein manifold admits a proper holomorphic embedding into an Oka open subset of some $\C^N$, and this embedding is a homotopy equivalence. We obtain holomorphic representatives of ordinary and generalized cohomology classes, and realize every countable group as the fundamental group of an Oka domain in $\C^5$. The fundamental groups of algebraically elliptic manifolds are precisely the finite groups, and every virtually abelian Kähler group is the fundamental group of a projective Oka manifold. Finally, we classify holomorphic cofibrations in Lárusson's intermediate model structures and establish factorizations over aspherical targets into proper holomorphic embeddings and holomorphic fibre bundles with Oka fibre.

papers.title: Profinite recognition of uniformity
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a semisimple Lie group that is not isogenous to the isometry group of real or complex hyperbolic $n$-space. We show that the rational rank is a profinite invariant for irreducible lattices in $G$, unless $G$ has type $D_{2n}$ which forms a genuine exception. In particular, profinitely isomorphic lattices in $G$ of type $D_{2n}$ can have differing virtual cohomological dimension. As another corollary, uniformity is a profinite property for irreducible lattices in $G$ outside type $D_4$. Assuming CSP, the existence of triality symmetries gives uniform and non-uniform profinitely isomorphic lattices in type $D_4$.

papers.title: Analysis of a zeroth-order multiscale sampler: strong convergence, convergence of ergodic averages and weak convergence
papers.abstract: In many practical applications of Bayesian inference, it is difficult or undesirable to compute the gradient of the negative log-posterior, motivating the study of derivative-free samplers, also called zeroth-order samplers. The aim of this paper is to generalize and rigorously analyze a multiscale derivative-free sampler recently proposed in the literature by Pavliotis, Stuart and Vaes (2022). In the discrete-time setting, the multiscale sampler we study bears a strong resemblance to other recently proposed methods, such as the so-called zeroth-order perturbed stochastic gradient descent algorithm (Jin et al., 2018) and the zeroth-order Langevin Monte Carlo algorithm by Roy et al. (2022). We present error estimates with respect to all the parameters of the problem, both in the continuous-time and discrete-time settings. The error estimates are in three different metrics: strong convergence, convergence of ergodic averages, and uniform-in-time weak convergence.

papers.title: Identifiability and Consistent Recovery for the Unnormalized Graph Laplace Operators
papers.abstract: We study whether an unnormalized graph Laplace operator can determine both the geometry of a manifold and its sampling density. On a fixed compact smooth manifold without boundary, we use a known positive, continuous, strictly decreasing radial kernel at a fixed positive bandwidth. For positive sampling densities, the operator built from geodesic distances determines the Riemannian metric and identifies the density up to equality almost everywhere. When the metric is induced by a Euclidean embedding, the operator built from ambient distances also determines the embedding up to rotations, reflections and translations, and the density. On compact parameter classes with positive continuous densities, minimizing the distance between empirical and popula- tion operators gives estimates that converge to the true parameters under independent, identically distributed sampling. This recovery result assumes that the empirical operator can be evaluated at arbitrary points of the manifold.

papers.title: A Fully Discrete, Mass-Conservative Adaptive Discontinuous Spectral-Element Method for the One-Dimensional Richards Equation in Mixed Form
papers.abstract: We present and analyze a spatially and temporally adaptive high-order method for the one-dimensional Richards equation describing vertical water transport in unsaturated soil, with an emphasis on resolving sharp wetting fronts while satisfying a fully discrete water mass balance. The spatial discretization uses an arbitrary-order local discontinuous Galerkin spectral-element formulation with collocated Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto quadrature, and the time integration is based on a high-order Rosenbrock-Wanner method. We focus primarily on the mixed formulation of the Richards equation, which advances water content as the conserved variable while evaluating the nonlinear diffusion operator in terms of pressure head; the resulting fully discrete scheme satisfies the water mass balance in exact arithmetic, independent of spatial resolution and time step size, including under spatial and temporal adaptivity. In contrast, the pressure-head formulation advances pressure head through a nonlinear capacity function and satisfies the corresponding conservation identity only at the semi-discrete level. Numerical experiments examine convergence through spatial and temporal refinement studies, with mass conservation assessed under spatial and temporal adaptivity using the solver flux output method (SFOM). The SFOM results confirm machine-precision mass conservation for the mixed formulation, whereas the pressure-head formulation exhibits mass balance errors above roundoff. Moreover, in the temporal refinement studies, the mixed formulation yields more accurate solutions than the pressure-head formulation for a prescribed time step size. The combination of high-order accuracy, spatial and temporal adaptivity, and fully discrete mass conservation makes the proposed mixed-form discontinuous spectral-element method a promising approach for simulating unsaturated flow in next-generation land models.

papers.title: Universality of $\mathsf{CohFT}$ of $\mathsf{Hilb}_n(S)$
papers.abstract: By virtue of their relation to Fulton--MacPherson compactifications, the cohomological field theory of Hilbert schemes of points on a surface, in extremal curve classes, is universally and effectively determined by the characteristic numbers of the surface and by the corresponding theory of Hilbert schemes of the affine plane. As a consequence, we compute the extremal genus 1 Gromov--Witten invariants of Hilbert schemes of all surfaces.

papers.title: A cell problem for the boundary density and approximation of boundary correctors in homogenization theory
papers.abstract: We study the boundary corrector $θ_ε$ in the two-scale expansion for periodic elliptic problems with Dirichlet conditions. By results of Gérard-Varet--Masmoudi and Prange, on smooth uniformly convex domains $θ_ε$ converges to the solution $θ^*$ of a homogenized problem with boundary data given by the boundary layer tail $d(n)$, which is determined by a half-space problem for each normal $n$. In the lifted form of Gérard-Varet and Masmoudi, $d(n)$ is given explicitly by the cell correctors and the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator $N_n$ of this half-space problem. Our main result is that $N_n$ satisfies a nonlinear equation on the period cell alone, so that $d(n)$ and the boundary density that represents it can be computed on the cell. This equation is a Riccati equation in which the derivative in depth is replaced by a commutator with the derivative along $n$. This cell problem can therefore be solved by a Riccati doubling algorithm, and we can compute $d(n)$ at irrational normals without rational approximation. Dropping the commutator term in the cell equation gives an operator square root approximation for $N_n$ that captures the leading term of $d(n)$ for small contrast, for the truncated problem. Finally, we approximate $θ_ε$ at finite $ε$ by the sum of two solutions of constant coefficient problems, one with oscillatory boundary data and the other $θ^*$, and test it on the disk.

papers.title: Edge-preserving Bayesian neural networks via hierarchical sparsity-promoting priors
papers.abstract: Recovering piecewise-smooth functions with jump discontinuities from noisy, indirect, and incomplete data is a central task in computational inverse problems. Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) with heavy-tailed weight priors have emerged as effective edge-preserving priors for such problems. However, posterior inference for these models remains computationally challenging, and existing approaches settle for point estimates obtained by directly optimizing heavy-tailed log-densities. We propose GSBL-BNNs, which model the neural network parameters hierarchically using sparsity-promoting priors from generalized sparse Bayesian learning (GSBL). The hierarchical formulation recovers several popular marginal priors, including Laplace and Student's $t$ (including Cauchy). A key modeling ingredient, novel among edge-preserving BNNs and native to the hierarchical formulation, couples each neuron's bias to its weights through a shared hyperparameter, so that the induced jump discontinuities are free to occur anywhere in the domain while the conditionally Gaussian structure underlying efficient inference is preserved. Furthermore, we develop a block-coordinate descent (BCD) algorithm for maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation. This BCD approach alternates between standard network training with iteratively reweighted $\ell^2$-regularization and exact, closed-form hyperparameter updates for gamma and inverse gamma hyperpriors. Building on the BCD algorithm, we perform approximate Bayesian inference and uncertainty quantification (UQ) using deep ensembles. Computational experiments---including signal denoising, deblurring, and inverting a two-dimensional hyperbolic conservation law--- show that GSBL-BNNs deliver accurate, edge-preserving reconstructions with built-in UQ. Compared with Gaussian- and Cauchy-BNNs, they yield more accurate predictive means and avoid overconfident uncertainty estimates.

papers.title: Photon-stimulated decay of $χ$-matched ancillas causes unheralded bit flips in bosonic codes
papers.abstract: Bosonic codes often read out their syndrome with a transmon ancilla whose computational levels $g$ and $f$ have equal parity and matched dispersive shifts: a decay $f\to e$ is then heralded and leaves the code intact, while the direct $f\to g$ is forbidden by parity. We show that the photons of the code open this decay at first order in the ancilla's decay rate. Dressing by the code mode lets the charge noise that limits the ancilla's $T_1$ drive a photon-stimulated Raman decay $|f,n\rangle\to|g,n+1\rangle$, at $(n+1)(χ_{ge}/2g_{01})^2$ times the $f\to e$ rate for a smooth noise spectrum. When the matching is set by the detuning, the decay costs $\approxΓ_{fe}/α$ per gate and photon, whatever the coupling strength; a deliberate mismatch or matching by a drive lowers this cost, and a qubit ancilla has no such channel. The opened decay is unheralded and flips a cat with probability $\approx 1/2$; being first order, it overtakes the second-order double decay $f\to e\to g$ as the ancilla improves. In a microscopic model of the Ocelot repetition cat code, it makes the bit-flip floor of the gates grow linearly with the cat size, by a factor 1.2-1.7 from four to ten photons, which would limit the noise bias to $\sim 10^3$. The published gate data end at four photons and do not yet test this growth.

papers.title: Transformed Convexity for Lane--Emden Equations and Torsion on Spherical Domains
papers.abstract: We study the geometry of positive Dirichlet solutions on smooth, uniformly geodesically convex domains $Ω\subsetneq\mathbb S^n$, $n\ge2$. Set $p_n^*=2n/(2n-3)$. For the Lane--Emden equation $-Δ_g u=u^p$, $1<p\le p_n^*$, we prove that the set of positive solution pairs $(p,u)$ has a connected component containing the near-linear solution curve and projecting onto $(1,p_n^*]$. Every pair on this component satisfies $\nabla_g^2(u^{-(p-1)/3})>0$ in $Ω$. For the torsion equation $-Δ_g u=1$, we establish $\nabla_g^2\sqrt{u}<0$ for its unique Dirichlet solution in all dimensions $n\ge2$, without an additional diameter or circumradius assumption. In both settings, the solutions specified above have a unique nondegenerate maximum and strictly geodesically convex positive superlevel sets. For the non-power reaction $f(s)=s^p/(1+λs^δ)$, with $1<p\le p_n^*$, $λ>0$, and $0<δ\le(p-1)/3$, we also prove the existence of at least one positive solution $u$ for which the transform $\left(\int_u^\infty ds/f(s)\right)^{1/3}$ has positive definite Hessian. The proofs combine a spherical Schur-complement estimate with a priori bounds and continuation.

papers.title: Sensitivity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions via Binary Necklaces
papers.abstract: Rotation symmetric Boolean functions are Boolean functions invariant under cyclic permutation of their variables and can be represented by binary necklaces. We express local sensitivity as a weighted bichromatic degree in the necklace quotient and derive an exact formula for the multiplicities between neighboring necklaces. For an odd prime number of variables, we obtain explicit sensitivity formulas and show that multiplicity corrections occur only on an asymptotically negligible family of necklaces. For monomial rotation symmetric Boolean functions, we prove that every odd-degree function has maximum sensitivity, determine the sensitivity of every quadratic function, and determine the sensitivity of the consecutive quartic family. We also determine exactly the sensitivity of cyclic run-threshold functions for arbitrary length and threshold.

papers.title: On Sums of "Small" Cantor Sets
papers.abstract: We provide several results showing that sums of ``small'' Cantor sets can turn into an interval or a finite union of intervals. Specifically, we show that 1) There exists a Cantor set $C\subset [0,1]$ of zero logarithmic capacity such that $C+C=[0,2]$. 2) For any $n\ge 2$ there exists a Cantor set $C\subset [0,1]$ of zero logarithmic capacity such that a Minkowski sum of $n$ copies of $C$ is an interval $[0,n]$, while a sum of any smaller number of copies of $C$ is still a Cantor set. 3) For any $n\ge 2$ there exists a collection of Cantor sets $C_1, C_2, \ldots, C_n\subset [0,1]$ of zero lower box-counting dimension such that a Minkowski sum of any $n-1$ sets from this collection is a Cantor set of zero lower box-counting dimension, while the sum of all $n$ sets is an interval $[0,n]$. 4) There is an uncountable family of Cantor sets of zero lower box-counting dimension such that the sum of any two different sets from this family is a finite union of intervals. 5) For each of the properties above, there are examples of Cantor sets with the same property having zero Hausdorff $h$-measure for an arbitrary given gauge function $h$.

papers.title: Intrinsic Rigidity of Bar-and-Joint Frameworks on Riemannian Manifolds
papers.abstract: We develop an intrinsic rigidity theory for bar-and-joint frameworks whose vertices are constrained to a Riemannian manifold and whose edges are given by minimizing geodesic arcs. Such frameworks are called rigid if they cannot be deformed beyond the ambient isometries, while preserving the geodesic edge lengths. For admissible placements, for which adjacent vertices are joined by unique minimizing geodesics, we define a coordinate-free rigidity operator as the differential of the squared geodesic distance of the edges. By the first-variation formula, its edge rows are expressed in terms of the Riemannian logarithm, providing an intrinsic analogue of the classical Euclidean rigidity matrix. Trivial motions are characterized by orbits of the diagonal action of the isometry group, leading to notions of infinitesimal and local rigidity. We further develop a covariant second-order rigidity theory using the Riemannian Hessians of the edge constraints and characterize second-order rigidity through self-stresses and associated quadratic forms. Finally, we show that infinitesimal and second-order rigidity can be used as sufficient conditions for the local rigidity of an intrinsic framework. Our overarching goal is to provide a unified differential-geometric formulation of intrinsic framework rigidity on smooth manifolds.

papers.title: Stably ergodic endomorphisms with positive Lyapunov exponents
papers.abstract: We introduce a new criterion which guarantees that a conservative local diffeomorphism is both non-uniformly expanding (in particular has all its Lyapunov exponents positive) and stably ergodic. The criterion involves averaging expansion rates over preimages and allows us to construct explicit examples in a variety of homotopy classes, including those represented by linear endomorphisms with contracting directions.

papers.title: Spectral Measure and Tail Process for Multivariate Dynamical Extremes
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of extreme events in multivariate stationary sequences, with particular emphasis on stochastic processes generated by dynamical systems. We develop a general framework for describing the dependence structure of extremes through two complementary objects: the tail process and the spectral measure. We first extend the enriched point-process convergence of the univariate theory to the multivariate setting, proving that the decorated point process of exceedances converges to a marked Poisson cluster process whose marks retain the componentwise and temporal structure of extreme clusters. We then construct a spectral measure for stationary sequences, which assigns weight to distinct extremal profiles and characterizes the asymptotic dependence between components, and establish a de Haan-Resnick type representation. We also relate the spectral measure to the tail process, showing that its normalized profile distribution is recovered from the angular component of the tail process. Finally, we recover the classical univariate and multivariate exceedance processes as special cases. We illustrate the theory through applications to dynamical systems, using examples in which different dynamical mechanisms give rise to distinct extremal clustering patterns and cross-dependence structures. These applications demonstrate the ability of the proposed framework to capture genuinely multivariate features of extreme events and to extract information about the underlying dynamics that is not accessible through classical exceedance processes.

papers.title: A new family of constant width bodies obtained from Reuleaux polyhedra
papers.abstract: We give a construction of a body of constant width from a unit Reuleaux polyhedron that preserves all its symmetries. As opposed to the Meissner surgery, our construction modifies both edges of each dual pair and requires no choice between them. For the Reuleaux tetrahedron it recovers a previously known body of constant width with six elliptic edges and tetrahedral symmetry.

papers.title: Intrinsic Geometry Matching: learning observation-equivariant process geometry
papers.abstract: Real data are often arbitrary, indirect observations of an unknown underlying process, and those observations can distort its geometry. Existing geometric methods equip data with the induced geometry of the ambient space, but this entangles the true geometry of the process with the distortion of the observation. To address this, we introduce Intrinsic Geometry Matching (IGM): a scalable approach to learn the intrinsic geometry of the underlying process. Specifically, we learn the carré du champ operator of the process, allowing us to recover its diffusion geometry. Our method uses the fact that data often come with natural perturbations, like steps in a time series, to recover the intrinsic carré du champ while transforming naturally with changes in observation: it is observation-equivariant. Furthermore, since this equivariance relates the geometry of different spaces, we can train a model using additional sources of data, even when that data lies in another space. We evaluate IGM on molecular dynamics, image, and video data and find better performance and scaling than existing neural and graph-based geometric tools.

papers.title: Matching Randomized Bounds for Finite-Sum Nonconvex-Concave Optimization
papers.abstract: We characterize the randomized component-oracle complexity of finite-sum nonconvex-concave optimization with a bounded dual domain. For $Φ(x)=\max_{y\in Y}n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x,y)$, the goal is to find an $\varepsilon$-stationary point of the Moreau envelope $Φ_{1/(2L)}$ with probability at least $2/3$ and a fixed query budget. Let $A=LΔ/\varepsilon^2$, $B=LD_Y/\varepsilon$, and $\bar B=\max\{1,B\}$, where $Δ$ bounds the initial primal gap and $D_Y$ bounds the dual diameter. For $A$ above a universal constant, the worst-case complexity is \[ \widetildeΘ\!\left(n+A\min\left\{ \sqrt n\,\bar B+\bar B^4,\ n^{3/4}\bar B\right\}\right). \] The bounds agree within constants for $B\le n^{1/4}$ and within one logarithm for larger $B$. Upper bounds require only mean-squared averaged smoothness and concavity of the average in the dual variable; lower bounds already hold under individual smoothness. The lower constructions cover adaptive component selection, arbitrary query norms, private randomization, and outputs that were never queried. A cone construction gives the small-diameter bound, while a serial branch construction and balanced replication give the remaining two regimes. On the upper side, a persistent estimator with primal averaging complements accelerated proximal dual steps equipped with an explicit primal certificate. The characterization takes the worst case over admissible known dual domains and finite dimensions.

papers.title: Half-space polynuclear growth: a multipoint Fredholm--Pfaffian formula
papers.abstract: We derive a Fredholm-Pfaffian formula for the one-time multi-point transition probabilities of half-space polynuclear growth with any nonnegative boundary nucleation rate and general deterministic upper semi-continuous initial profiles. We prove the formula by showing that it satisfies an integral Kolmogorov equation with a unique bounded solution. We also discuss the formal 1:2:3 scaling limit of the kernel and its relation to the half-space KPZ fixed point.

papers.title: A quantitative CLT for the zeros of random trigonometric polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $X_N(t)$, $t\in[0,π]$, be a stationary Gaussian trigonometric polynomial, and let $\mathcal Z_N$ denote the number of zeros of the rescaled process $X_N(t/N)$ on $[0,Nπ]$. We establish the quantitative central limit theorem \[ d_{\mathrm W}\left( \frac{\mathcal Z_N-\mathbb E[\mathcal Z_N]} {\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(\mathcal Z_N)}},Z\right) \le C\frac{(\log N)^2}{\sqrt N}, \] where $Z$ is standard Gaussian and $d_{\mathrm W}$ denotes the Wasserstein-1 distance. The proof combines Ornstein--Uhlenbeck regularization of the singular Kac representation with direct estimates of the covariance between the Malliavin--Stein factor and Stein test functions. A lattice lower bound of order $N^{-1/2}$ shows that the convergence rate is optimal up to logarithmic factors.

papers.title: Vortex structures in momentum distributions from multi-pair production
papers.abstract: The vortex structures in the momentum distributions of multiple particle-antiparticle pairs produced from the vacuum by a spatially uniform, time-varying electric field with arbitrary polarization are investigated using the Bogoliubov transformation. For linearly polarized fields, as the field strength increases, the nodal lines in the multi-pair momentum distribution break up into vortex-antivortex pairs in both the bosonic and fermionic cases. Each vortex carries a topological charge that is an integer multiple of the single-pair vortex topological charge. For circular polarization, a central vortex appears at all field strengths. For bosons, its topological charge is an integer multiple of the single-pair vortex topological charge; for fermions, it is an integer multiple of the vortex topological charge for single-pair production with zero total spin projection along the field propagation direction. For elliptical polarization with suitable ellipticity, discrete vortices coexist with a central vortex. In this case, however, the integer-multiple relation for fermions generally fails because the two-pair production amplitude is a determinant and spin-channel contributions are separated in momentum space. These results provide a theoretical basis for understanding the vortex topology of multi-pair production in strong-field QED and for its potential control.

papers.title: Spectral and Nodal Properties of Static Manifolds with Boundary
papers.abstract: We study compact static manifolds with boundary from a spectral point of view, with particular emphasis on the relation between Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin spectra and the nodal structure of static potentials. We establish comparison inequalities linking Dirichlet and Neumann eigenvalues with the scalar curvature and derive sufficient spectral conditions ensuring that a static potential changes sign. We also obtain bounds on the number of connected components of the zero set, sufficient conditions for its connectedness, and sufficient conditions ensuring that its components intersect the boundary. Finally, we study variational properties of Robin static triples and characterize compact Robin static triples whose metrics are critical for the first mixed Robin--Dirichlet eigenvalue under admissible volume-preserving deformations.

papers.title: Asymptotic analysis of the confluent Dotsenko-Fateev system
papers.abstract: The Dotsenko-Fateev equation is a third-order linear ordinary differential equation studied in two-dimensional conformal field theory. We study the confluent Dotsenko-Fateev system, a rank-three system of linear ordinary differential equations obtained by confluence from a first-order system equivalent to the Dotsenko-Fateev equation. It has an irregular singular point at infinity, and its solutions admit double integral representations of confluent Selberg type. Using these representations, we construct sectorial fundamental solution matrices around infinity, establish their asymptotic expansions, and determine the associated Stokes matrices explicitly. We further study three aspects of the confluent Dotsenko-Fateev system: its equivalence to the degree-two polynomial reduction of the Schrödinger equation for the quantum Painlevé equation of type V, its realization as a restriction of a confluent version of the linear Pfaffian system associated with Appell's hypergeometric function $F_4$, and its reduction to the trivial rank-one equation via integral transforms and a quadratic change of the independent variable.

papers.title: Optimal Monte Carlo integration on matrix manifolds
papers.abstract: This article develops optimal order (up to logarithmic factors) weighted cubature rules for Monte Carlo numerical integration in Sobolev reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces over common matrix manifolds. Specifically, we consider matrix models of the Stiefel, Grassmann, flag, and Lagrangian Grassmann manifolds each over either real numbers $\mathbb{R}$, complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$, or quaternions $\mathbb{H}$. The proposed cubature rules use evaluation points which are independent and identically distributed uniform on the manifold. The weights are chosen to be optimal with respect to the reproducing kernel Hilbert space worst-case error, under the constraint that the weights sum to one. Crucially, this constraint ensures optimal weights may be found without having to evaluate the kernel mean embedding (the integral of the kernel), which is often difficult to compute. We consider computable Matérn kernels of Frobenius distances between matrices which reproduce the Sobolev reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces with equivalent norms. Open-source numerical experiments validate our theoretical development, including an application to simultaneous approximation of intrinsic volumes in the Cauchy--Kubota formula. We also present preliminary empirical results beyond independent points including transformations of low-discrepancy quasi-Monte Carlo points from the unit cube and jointly optimized points and weights.

papers.title: Determinantal linear spanning forests
papers.abstract: We introduce a determinantal linear process on the space of $1$-forms over a weighted graph endowed with a unitary local system, which we call the determinantal linear spanning forest (DLSF). This process is the analog of the uniform spanning tree in the presence of an arbitrary rank $n$ quenched gauge field in ${\rm U}(n)$ (or ${\rm O}(n)$, ${\rm SO}(n)$, ${\rm SU}(n)$, ${\rm Sp}(n)$), and generalizes the determinantal random cycle-rooted spanning forest which corresponds to the case of ${\rm U}(1)$ and ${\rm SU}(2)$. We describe the support of this process by means of a polymatroid which is described in terms of the circular and bicircular matroids. We also explain how the DLSF relates to the computation of currents in an electrical network in the presence of a gauge field. The partition function of the DLSF is shown to be the determinant of the twisted Laplacian, for which we also give a matrix-tree type theorem that computes its characteristic polynomial. We initiate the study of the twisted Laplacian determinant as a functional on the space of connections, and give a first order expansion of it in a neighborhood of the trivial connection, for which we provide a probabilistic interpretation. We extend the construction to infinite graphs, exhibiting the analogs of the classical wired and free distributions on spanning forests. We give a sufficient geometric condition on the local spectral gap for the existence of a Poincaré inequality as well as the uniqueness of the infinite volume measure, and the exponential decay of correlations. We show that on any recurrent graph, the wired and free DLSF coincide. We construct examples where they do not, for example, unlike in the classical case, on $\mathbb Z^d$ for $d\geq 3$.

papers.title: Crepant resolutions of four-dimensional finite quotients
papers.abstract: We give counterexamples to the conjecture of Dais-Henk-Ziegler on projective crepant resolutions of complete-intersection quotient singularities. For finite $G\subset\operatorname{SL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$, we determine whether $\mathbb{C}^4/G$ admits a projective crepant resolution, with the representations considered up to conjugacy in $\operatorname{SL}_4(\mathbb{C})$. Ten explicit criteria decide all cases. The examples also show that the Molien series and the age polynomial do not determine existence. We also discuss questions of Ito-Reid on maximal cyclic subgroups and the generation of cohomology in degree two.

papers.title: Certifying non-existence of integer points on curves
papers.abstract: We present an elementary but powerful method for proving that a two-variable equation has no integer solutions. The method produces quadratic identities which every integer solution must satisfy. Once these identities are established, a standard quadratic reciprocity argument finishes the proof. We illustrate the power of the method by resolving $25$ out of $30$ two-variable equations of size up to $34$ for which the problem of integer solubility remained open. We also resolve the remaining $5$ equations by deeper methods, and further determine the integer solubility of all two-variable equations of size up to $35$ and of length up to $12$, with two exceptions. Before this work, there were $211$ equations in this category that resisted the previously known methods, and we proved that $209$ of them have no integer solutions, with all proofs formalized in Lean. In addition, we show that our method can be used to solve certain two-variable equations whose integer solution set is non-empty.

papers.title: A finite coefficient theory for shape identification in tilted generalized gamma families
papers.abstract: A continuous shape parameter enters both a radial density and the normalization of its transform coefficients. This coupling allows changes in shape to be compensated by changes in scale and exponential tilt. We study the coefficients b_k=e^a E[Y^k ]/[k!(d)_k ] for densities proportional to y^(d-1) exp(-αy^q+\b{eta}y), with known integer q>=2, d,α>0, and unrestricted real a,\b{eta}. For q=2, the first four coefficients determine all parameters globally, whereas three coefficients leave an analytic curve of solutions. We characterize the exact image of the two shape ratios and prove that two alternating corners decide whether an entire coefficient box is realizable and give its exact shape range. For every fixed q, the first q(q+1) coefficients give global identification and an everywhere full-rank map. A finite-difference criterion yields generic identification from 2q+1 coefficients, including every zero-tilt model against the full tilted family. For q=3, an exact rational certificate constructs two distinct shapes with identical first four coefficients and separated fifth coefficients. The results distinguish exact identification, realizability, and sensitivity for a parameter-dependent coefficient normalization.

papers.title: On the Stability of the Independence Number of the Distance Graph G(n,r,<s) for Growing r and s
papers.abstract: We consider a random subgraph G_p(n,r,<s) of the complete distance graph G(n,r,<s) whose vertices are the r-element subsets of the set {1,...,n} and whose edges join pairs of subsets that intersect in fewer than s elements; each edge survives independently of the others with probability p. The stability of the Erdos-Ko-Rado theorem is the event that the independence number of the random subgraph equals that of the original graph, N = C_{n-s}^{r-s}. For fixed r and s, two-sided bounds for the critical probability, whose ratio depends on r and s, were obtained by P. A. Ogarok and A. M. Raigorodskii. In this paper we establish the order of the critical probability for growing r=r(n) and s=s(n): if min{C_r^s r^2, s r^3} = o(n), then the upper and lower bounds differ only by an absolute constant factor. The proof is elementary; only one of the two branches of the growth condition uses the complete nontrivial-intersection theorem of Ahlswede-Khachatrian.

papers.title: CM fibers of Shimura parametrizations and thirteen proofs of the class number one theorem
papers.abstract: We determine thirteen entirely CM identity fibers of Shimura parametrizations attached to elliptic curves of rank two and conductor below $2000$. Each yields a proof of the imaginary quadratic class number one theorem. The argument combines the Gross--Zagier formula with the Ribet--Takahashi degree comparison to show that the fiber is completely explained by known CM points.

papers.title: Solomon--Terao Algebras: Top Degree, Dimension, and Homology
papers.abstract: We study the Solomon--Terao algebra and the Solomon--Terao complex of a central hyperplane arrangement $\mathcal A$ in $\mathbb C^\ell$. Let $η$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $d\geq2$ whose restriction to every flat of $\mathcal A$ has no critical point away from the origin. We prove that the Solomon--Terao algebra $\mathrm{ST}(\mathcal A,η)$ has top degree $|\mathcal A|+\ell(d-2)$ and a one-dimensional top graded component with an explicit generator, solving a conjecture of Abe, Maeno, Murai, and Numata. For $d=2$, we show that the total dimension of $\mathrm{ST}(\mathcal A,η)$ is bounded below by that of the Orlik--Solomon algebra. Both results hold without assuming that the arrangement $\mathcal A$ is tame. Finally, we prove that $\mathcal A$ is tame if and only if all positive-degree homology groups of the Solomon--Terao complex associated with $η$ vanish.

papers.title: On Intersection Hypergraph of Finite Non-Cyclic Abelian Groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study various structural properties like girth, chromatic num ber, etc. of the intersection hypergraph on the subgroups of nite non-cyclic abelian group and we characterize for the star and hypertree structures. Fur thermore, we characterize hypergraphs which are embeddable on plane, torus and projective plane.

papers.title: Foundations for a Lens of Quantum Governance
papers.abstract: The second quantum revolution is a revolution of information. Advances in quantum computation, communication, and sensing offer new capabilities while raising questions about how quantum infrastructures will be organised, accessed, and governed. We argue that their significance for governance lies not in transforming political principles, but in how their technical and infrastructural requirements may affect existing relationships of authority, responsibility, legitimacy, and power. This paper develops a quantum governance lens that connects governance scholarship with quantum information science, examining interactions between technical design, institutional arrangements, and infrastructural dependencies. We apply this lens to five areas: quantum computation, quantum key distribution, Quantum Byzantine Agreement, blind quantum computation, and dual-use quantum sensing. These applications illustrate how technical capabilities may influence access, trust, privacy, oversight, and accountability, while demonstrating that technical guarantees cannot resolve institutional questions independently. We conclude that quantum technologies do not necessarily introduce unique governance challenges or require entirely new governance frameworks. Rather, they provide a context in which established questions of legitimacy, accountability, and equity must be reconsidered in relation to emerging technological capabilities and institutional choices.

papers.title: The Adiabatic b-Calculus and the Global Anomaly Formula on Manifolds with Boundary
papers.abstract: We study the determinant line bundle for a family of elliptic operators on compact manifolds with boundary with the associated Quillen metric and Bismut-Freed connection, and we prove the global anomaly formula in this context. This extends Witten's holonomy theorem to manifolds with boundary. Witten studied the limiting behavior of the eta invariant of a Dirac operator on the total space of a fibration over $\mathbb{S}^1$ when the metric in the base $\mathbb{S}^1$ is blown up in a certain manner, a process known as taking the adiabatic limit. In this paper, we construct the calculus of adiabatic $b$-pseudodifferential operators, which naturally synthesizes the $b$-calculus and the adiabatic calculus of pseudodifferential operators. Using this calculus, and assuming the fiber operators to be invertible, we compute the adiabatic limit of the natural eta invariant in this setting and relate it to the integral of the Bismut-Freed connection and new correction terms coming from the boundary of the fibers.

papers.title: Microlocal Arthur packets as a quasi-canonical basis of stable distributions
papers.abstract: We show that microlocal Arthur packets can be reconstructed from an otherwise underdetermined system of linear equations arising from Kashiwara's local index theorem. The key is a geometric rigidity property of Arthur orbits which, together with Fourier symmetry, uniquely determines the microlocal multiplicities defining these packets. This realizes the associated Arthur distribution as the unique normalized element in the intersection of two filtered spaces of standard stable distributions related by Fourier transform. Under standard enhanced local Langlands hypotheses and Aubert compatibility, this gives an alternative representation-theoretic definition of microlocal Arthur packets for general connected reductive $p$-adic groups that does not use twisted endoscopy and ensures stability through the stability of tempered packet distributions. In the unipotent setting, we use this characterization to prove agreement between endoscopic and microlocal Arthur packets for split $\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ when the residue characteristic is at least $6n+4$. We further use this characterization to compute all unipotent Arthur packets with unramified real infinitesimal character for inner-to-split adjoint exceptional $p$-adic groups. In this exceptional setting, we prove the microlocal weak Arthur packet conjecture and give counterexamples to the microlocal analogues of the least- and greatest-parameter conjectures.

papers.title: The quarter-point theorem for Gromov hyperbolic graphs
papers.abstract: Gromov hyperbolicity measures the geometric complexity of metric spaces and metric graphs through geodesic triangles and four-point conditions. While calculating the exact continuous hyperbolicity constant $δ^*(G)$ of a graph $G$ typically requires evaluating quadruples of points over an infinite metric continuum, discretizing this domain is a fundamental challenge in metric graph theory. In this paper, we study the continuous Gromov hyperbolicity constant via the Gromov product. Our main result, the Quarter-Point Theorem, establishes that the search space for quadruples $(x,y,z,w)$ attaining the exact hyperbolicity constant $δ^*(G)$ can be reduced from the entire metric graph to a finite or discrete subset $J'(G)$, comprising solely the vertices, edge midpoints, and quarter-points of $G$. This result holds for every graph, finite or infinite. This theoretical result provides a considerably simplified combinatorial framework for calculating hyperbolicity in complex networks and metric graphs. Furthermore, we exploit this discretization to significantly improve classical results by establishing and structural bounds relating the global hyperbolicity constant $δ^*(G)$ with its restrictions to vertices ($δ_V^*(G)$) and midpoints ($δ_J^*(G)$).

papers.title: Decision-Making in Digital Twins: Optimization, Control, and Learning
papers.abstract: A digital twin is a virtual representation of a physical system, continuously updated with data from the physical system, enabling dynamic information exchange and decision-making. This bidirectional interaction, which distinguishes digital twins from conventional simulation models, introduces new challenges to simulation-based optimization, control, and learning. This paper reviews recent developments in decision-making methodologies motivated by digital twins. We focus on three interconnected areas: simulation optimization, sequential decision making, and risk-aware decision making. For simulation optimization, we discuss data-driven simulation optimization under input uncertainty, streaming input data, decision-dependent observations, and limited computational and data-collection resources. For sequential decision making, we review the connections among digital twins, stochastic optimal control, and reinforcement learning, with emphasis on Bayesian approaches that update models and policies as new information becomes available. For risk-aware decision making, we discuss distributionally robust and Bayesian risk formulations as alternative approaches for addressing model uncertainty. Throughout the paper, we emphasize the common problem of making decisions while the underlying model is being updated. We conclude by identifying research challenges and opportunities.

papers.title: Graph Distortion Distances, Gromov-Hausdorff and the Hardness of Gromov-Wasserstein
papers.abstract: We study the computational complexity of graph distortion distances, a family of graph metrics measuring how vertex distances differ between two graphs. Formally, these distances are defined in terms of standard matrix norms on the difference of distance matrices under an optimal vertex alignment. The resulting metrics have natural interpretations, corresponding to three ways of measuring the distortion of shortest-path distances: the maximum distortion among all vertex pairs (entrywise maximum norm), global aggregation (entrywise $p$-norms), and local aggregation (operator $p$-norms) of distortions. For maximum distortion, we show that approximation below a factor of two is NP-hard even for highly restricted trees. Due to the close connection to the Gromov-Hausdorff distance, we obtain a similar hardness result for the latter. In both cases, we show essentially optimal additive inapproximability. On the algorithmic side, we give a subcubic-time algorithm for optimal embeddings of connected graphs into paths, based on a structural decomposition along a diametral path. Additionally, we give a simple approximation algorithm when one input graph has a "relatively path-like" metric structure, i.e. has bounded pathlength. For local and global distortion, we derive various hardness results even for restricted inputs. Making use of a close connection between the global distortion distances and Gromov-Wasserstein distances, we give the first formal proof of NP-hardness of the latter, which has been claimed in the literature many times but has, to the best of our knowledge, never been correctly proven.

papers.title: Semiclassical Moser--Trudinger type inequalities for orthonormal families in $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: For $H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$-orthonormal families $\{u_n\}_{n=1}^N$ with one-body density $ρ=\sum_{n=1}^N |u_n|^2$, we prove the whole-space endpoint Moser--Trudinger inequality $$ \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}\frac{e^{4πρ(x)}-1-4πρ(x)}{ρ(x)}\,dx \le C\left(N-1+\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}ρ(x)\,dx\right), $$ where the integrand on the left-hand side is defined to be zero on $\{x: ρ(x)=0\}$. We develop a heat-semigroup refinement of Rumin's density method to treat both the endpoint coefficient $4π$ and the whole-space setting. Our inequality is sharp in two respects: the optimality of the coefficient $4π$ and the linear growth in the rank $N$. Moreover, through a semiclassical analysis of the density generated by normalized Dirichlet eigenfunctions, we establish the collective asymptotic behaviors of the quantities appearing in the inequality in various regimes. These semiclassical behaviors show that the rank-dependent term $N-1$ on the right-hand side is indispensable.

papers.title: Mutual information across the commensurate--incommensurate crossover and near the Kosterlitz--Thouless point of the spin-$\tfrac12$ $J_1$--$J_2$ Heisenberg chain
papers.abstract: What quantum mutual information adds to conventional correlation functions is often unclear. We study the spin-1/2 $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg chain, using DMRG on infinite chains and periodic rings and an SU(2) decomposition of the mutual information into correlation channels. For singlet ground states the two-site mutual information is an exact function of the spin correlator, so any additional content must come from blocks. In the dimerized phase, blocks resolve bond-energy correlations in the SU(2)-scalar channel without an independent asymptotic length: singlet and triplet correlation lengths agree to about 1%. The scalar channel dominates block mutual information at large distances in the commensurate regime up to $J_2/J_1=0.40$, but falls to a few percent beyond the disorder point, which coincides numerically with the Majumdar-Ghosh point $J_2/J_1=1/2$; the structure-factor peak splits only at the Lifshitz point $J_2/J_1=0.520622(2)$. On the gapless side we compare block mutual information on rings extrapolated to infinite size with the two-interval prediction of SU(2)$_1$ conformal field theory across the Kosterlitz-Thouless point $J_2/J_1=0.241167$. There, for block lengths $l\le6$, the correction decays as $l^{-p}$ with $p=1.96$-$2.07$, and any logarithmic term is at least 60 times smaller than in the Heisenberg chain. Expanding in the marginal coupling (from level spectroscopy) the first-order coefficient is consistent with $l^{-2}$ scaling and the second-order coefficient is positive for $x\le1/4$, suggesting that the mutual information relative to the field-theory value becomes stationary at the KT point for large blocks. The scalar-channel share approaches 1/4 at small cross ratio $x$, as expected from SO(4) symmetry; under two stated assumptions its first-order response to the coupling is $(3/8)\ln x-5/8$ at small $x$, matched by the $l=4$ data within 1-3% at $x\le1/9$.

papers.title: Simultaneous Matrix-Free HSS Compression and Factorization with Adaptive Ranks
papers.abstract: Many dense matrices in scientific computing have hierarchically low-rank off-diagonal structure but are accessible only through routines that apply the matrix and, in general, its transpose or adjoint to vectors, that is, through matrix--vector products (matvecs). We present a fully matrix-free algorithm that compresses such a matrix into Hierarchically Semi-Separable (HSS) form and factorizes it simultaneously with the off-diagonal ranks chosen adaptively from a prescribed tolerance. The method uses $\mathcal{O}(k)$ matvecs with each operator, where $k$ is the largest off-diagonal rank found. Building on fixed-rank block nullification, it samples the matrix in small random batches and enlarges each local basis until a randomized error estimate falls below the tolerance. Unitary nullspace updates give $\mathcal{O}(k^3)$ local dense work, the same asymptotic cost as when the ranks are known in advance. Because compression and elimination proceed together, no separate factorization step is required. Excluding the matvecs, the factorization uses $\mathcal{O}(N)$ arithmetic and storage when the off-diagonal ranks are bounded, and its inverse is applied in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time. Experiments on Poisson and Helmholtz Schur complements, Matérn covariance matrices, and a complex Lippmann--Schwinger equation demonstrate the factorization as both a direct solver and a preconditioner on problems with up to millions of unknowns.

papers.title: Sequence spaces of Baire-one functions and their porosity
papers.abstract: We consider several families of sequences of Baire-one self-maps of $[0,1]$ investigated by A. Alikhani-Koopaei. They form a chain of inclusions where each space is closed and nowhere dense in the next one. We prove that each space is lower $2/3$-porous in the next one. If one modifies these families where sequences of Baire-one functions are real-valued uniformly bounded, then they are Banach spaces and each space of the respective chain is c-porous in the next one.

papers.title: Exponential profiles for the intrinsic volumes of Orlicz balls
papers.abstract: An Orlicz ball is the set of points where the sum of a fixed even convex function of the coordinates does not exceed a given radius, here proportional to the dimension. For a broad class of such functions, including non-homogeneous ones, we find the exponential rate of the intrinsic volumes whose order is proportional to the dimension and express it by a two-parameter variational formula involving only one-dimensional integrals. As a function of the order-to-dimension ratio, this rate is concave and continuous on the closed unit interval, and the convergence is uniform in the order. This proves the exponential-profile conjecture of Kabluchko, Marynych, and Prochno for these bodies and recovers their result for $\ell_p$ balls with $p>1$. The proof relies on the theory of large deviations. An exact formula for the Laplace transform of the intrinsic volumes in the radius, extending theirs for $\ell_p$ balls, plays the role of a moment generating function, and a Laplace method gives its exponential rate. An exponential change of measure, analogous to that used in Cramér's theorem, then recovers the intrinsic volumes. The key step is a lower bound on the tilted density at its mean, obtained from log-concavity rather than a law of large numbers.

papers.title: Solution Set Dimensions in Convex Optimization and Primal-Polar Facial Signatures
papers.abstract: We study the possible dimensions of solution sets in linearly perturbed convex optimization problems and their behavior under convex duality. The dimensions of solution sets and inverse solution sets capture two complementary forms of nonuniqueness: that of optimal solutions for a given perturbation, and that of perturbations for which a given point is optimal. Although these two families are linked by Fenchel conjugacy, we show that their collections of dimensions can be prescribed independently for finite supercoercive convex functions. As a geometric consequence, we prove that the facial dimension signatures of a convex body and its polar can be prescribed independently. The connection between these two realization results is obtained by homogenizing the epigraphs of a function and its conjugate. In contrast, under simultaneous facial exposedness, we establish a dimensional obstruction relating the smallest positive proper face dimensions of the body and its polar. These results resolve two open questions posed by Roshchina and Tunçel.

papers.title: Borderline double phase functionals with powers of the logarithm: regularity in the vectorial case
papers.abstract: We study vector-valued local minimizers of the borderline double phase functional whose integrand is $|D\mathbf{w}|^p+a(x)|D\mathbf{w}|^p\log^γ(e+|D\mathbf{w}|)$, where $p>1$, $γ>0$ and the coefficient $a(\cdot)$ is nonnegative and bounded. If the modulus of continuity $ω(\cdot)$ of $a(\cdot)$ satisfies $ω(r)\log^γ(1/r)\to0$ as $r\to0$, then minimizers are locally Hölder continuous for every exponent less than one.
