papers.abstract: Resampling is the standard remedy against weight degeneracy in particle filters, yet its effect on the spectrum of the particle second-moment matrix is poorly understood. We study a single resampling step for a d-dimensional ensemble of N particles with d/N -> c. For any unbiased scheme, the resampled empirical second-moment matrix dominates its pre-resampling counterpart in conditional convex order, while the conditional mean is preserved; the excess second spectral moment equals the Frobenius energy of the resampling perturbation. For multinomial resampling, the empirical count law converges to the mixed-Poisson law determined by the limiting weight law. For residual resampling, the count law is determined by the joint limit of floor-fraction pairs: we classify all residual limits of weight sequences converging to delta_1 in law as a one-parameter family between the deterministic identity and the full multinomial count law. Each count law feeds a common covariance-side spectral map, yielding exact consequences: a closed-form zero-eigenvalue mass, a rank-and-spectral-gap transition with a universal lower edge benchmark, computable regular edges, unbounded right support, and scheme-specific second-moment costs. The effective sample size determines one bulk statistic but cannot determine the limiting spectrum. Pre-registered numerical experiments confirm the theory at every level.

papers.title: Preconditioned Latent Variable Proximal Point Method for Optimal Control Problems with Control Constraints
papers.abstract: The latent variable proximal point (LVPP) method solves optimization problems in function spaces with pointwise constraints by a sequence of smooth subproblems whose iterates are strictly feasible. We apply it to linear-quadratic elliptic optimal control problems. Control and observation are distributed but may be restricted to subdomains. We prove that the LVPP subproblems are well posed in appropriate function spaces, that the iteration converges for every sequence of proximity parameters with divergent sum, and that it delivers the Lagrange multiplier of the constraint as a by-product. We interpret the Newton step for the LVPP subproblem as a linear-quadratic optimal control problem with a spatially varying control cost, and we show that Newton's method converges locally quadratically. The Newton systems are solved by the minimal residual method with a block-diagonal preconditioner. We prove that the spectrum of the Newton operator with respect to the inner product defined by the preconditioner is bounded independently of the proximity parameter, the iterate, the mesh and the observation and control domains. The results are combined into a complete algorithm, and tested in numerical experiments.

papers.title: Graphon Hawkes Processes: Sparse Estimation and Network Recovery
papers.abstract: Learning interaction structures from spatiotemporal event data is a key statistical problem in fields such as neuroscience, epidemiology, and seismology. We study this problem for Hawkes processes on a continuous spatial domain, where events may trigger future events at different locations. Following the framework developed in ``Spatiotemporal Hawkes processes with a graphon-induced connectivity structure'' by Baars, Laeven, and Mandjes (2026), we model the spatial interaction mechanism using an underlying graphon that characterizes how the intensities' excitation strength varies across locations. By expanding the baseline intensity, temporal excitation kernel and graphon in orthogonal bases, we represent the problem as a high-dimensional parametric inference problem. We propose a sparse penalized least-squares estimator that recovers the effective interaction structure while controlling model complexity. Our analysis establishes non-asymptotic error bounds in a high-dimensional regime where the number of parameters may grow with the observation horizon, without requiring the conditional intensity to be almost surely bounded. We further establish sparsistency results, showing that the latent interaction network can be consistently recovered. Simulation studies demonstrate the good finite sample performance of the proposed method and an application to large-scale neuronal spike data, comprising 1.81 million events, showcases its practical effectiveness.

papers.title: Graph Matching in Random Geometric Graphs I: Efficient Algorithms
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of the hidden vertex correspondence between two correlated dense random geometric graphs. Each graph is generated from $n$ latent unit vectors in $\mathbb R^d$; the vectors $u_i^A$ and $u_i^B$ of corresponding vertices satisfy $\langle u_i^A,u_i^B\rangle=ρ$, and the vertex labels of the second graph are permuted by an unknown permutation $π$. For every fixed correlation $ρ\in(0,1]$ and every edge density bounded away from zero and one, we give a randomized polynomial time algorithm that recovers $π$ exactly with probability tending to one whenever $d\ge(\log n)^L$, where $L$ depends only on the correlation and the density bounds. The algorithm assigns to each vertex a signature formed by counting decorated paths with a constant number of seeds. The number of such seeded templates grows exponentially with the path length, with an arbitrarily large constant base, so the resulting statistics amplify an arbitrarily small constant correlation. We control the dependencies created by the latent geometry in two ways: when $d$ is larger than $n/(\log n)^{L_0}$ for a suitable constant $L_0$, by comparing local moments with those of correlated Erdős--Rényi graphs; for smaller $d$, by spectral estimation of the latent geometry combined with a harmonic correction. We also provide low-degree evidence for a tradeoff between the correlation and the computational cost.

papers.title: Euler's thirty-six officers need not all be entangled: real AME(4,6), families and classification
papers.abstract: Absolutely maximally entangled states of four six-level systems, AME$(4,6)$, are the quantum solutions of Euler's problem of the thirty-six officers. Until recently all reported solutions were complex, and it was conjectured that no real orthogonal 2-unitary matrix of order $36$ exists. We give real AME$(4,6)$ states with $60$ non-zero coefficients in $\{\pm1,\sqrt2\}/\sqrt{72}$. Of their thirty-six officers, $12$ are classical, as some must be whenever fewer than $72$ coefficients are non-zero. They lie in the $-1$ eigenspace of an order-$4$ local symmetry, and on their support the AME conditions become linear. We derive two closed-form families of AME$(4,6)$ states that meet at one of these states: a $10$-parameter family that is supported on $72$ basis states, and an $11$-parameter family on $60$ basis states. At each of its two ends the first family loses $12$ coefficients, and the AME states on the remaining $60$ basis states form an $11$-parameter family: the second family at one end, and an analogous family at the other. These two $60$-term families contain $4096$ real AME states up to diagonal local unitaries, $1024$ of which are limits of the first family. They fall into exactly $20$ classes under local unitaries and permutations of the parties, and we certify their separation with interval arithmetic.

papers.title: Tight $σ$-filtrations and the BFPP of $C(ω^*)$
papers.abstract: Assuming that $\mathcal{P}(ω)$ is tightly $σ$-filtered, we prove that $C(ω^*)$ fails the ball fixed point property. This axiom holds under the continuum hypothesis and in the $\aleph_2$-Cohen model. The proof shows that the Stone space of the countable--cocountable algebra $\operatorname{Cc}(ω_1)$ is a continuous retract of $ω^*$ and uses the equivalence between tight $σ$-filteredness of $\operatorname{Cc}(ω_1)$ and of $\mathcal{P}(ω)$. We also prove that the quotient of a tightly $σ$-filtered Boolean algebra $B$ with the countable separation property by an $\aleph_1$-generated $P$-ideal is a Boolean retract of $B$.

papers.title: Semigroup properties of Schrödinger operators with complex singular potentials
papers.abstract: In the complex Hilbert space $L_2(\mathbb{R}_+)$ on the half-line $\mathbb{R}_+ = [0, \infty)$, we investigate non-symmetric Schrödinger operators \[ Su = -u'' + qu, \qquad u(0) = 0, \] with complex-valued, highly singular distributional potentials \[ q = s + Q' \in H_{\mathrm{loc}}^{-1}(\mathbb{R}_+), \qquad s \in L_{1,\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}_+), \quad Q \in L_{2,\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}_+), \] where the derivative $Q'$ is understood in the sense of Schwartz distributions. A rigorous operator-theoretic setting is established within the framework of Shin--Zettl quasi-derivatives. We prove that every accretive operator $S$ of this class is automatically $m$-accretive in $L_2(\mathbb{R}_+)$ and $C$-self-adjoint with respect to the complex conjugation involution $C : u \mapsto \bar{u}$. In particular, no additional boundary conditions at infinity are needed, meaning that a Weyl limit-point type situation always prevails for accretive realizations. Constructive local conditions on the coefficients $s$ and $Q$ are found under which the generated strongly continuous semigroup $\{e^{-tS}\}_{t \ge 0}$ is contractive or holomorphic in a sector of the complex plane.

papers.title: Pointwise improvement of the error term in the higher rank hyperbolic lattice counting problem
papers.abstract: We prove an upper bound for the error term in the higher rank hyperbolic lattice counting problem for ${\hbox{SL}(n, \mathbb{Z})}$. Blomer and Lutsko achieved recently a significant improvement of previous known results by Duke--Rudnick--Sarnak and Gorodnik--Nevo--Yehoshua. We deduce an improved upper bound for the error which holds for almost all pairs $z,w \in {\hbox{SL}(n, \mathbb{R})}$. We also derive a $Ω$-result for the error term, in the spirit of Rudnick--Phillips.

papers.title: On the Drinfeld doubles of Laistrygonian algebras in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: In this work, we study restricted Laistrygonian algebras over a field of positive characteristic $p$. We compute their Drinfeld double $\mathtt{D_p(q,a)}$ and give explicit presentations by generators and relations. We prove that $\mathtt{D_p(q,a)}$ is a pointed Hopf algebra. For $\mathtt{D_p(1,a)}$, we describe an abelian exact sequence of Hopf algebras and identify one of its quotients as a restricted enveloping Lie algebra. This exact sequence enables us to classify the finite-dimensional simple $\mathtt{D_p(1,a)}$-modules. We also introduce an infinite-dimensional Hopf algebra covering the restricted Drinfeld double and study its relation with the corresponding finite-dimensional case. Using this covering together with a Frobenius map, we construct a $3\times 3$ commutative diagram whose rows and columns are exact sequences of Hopf algebras. In particular, our approach provides a unified treatment of the Drinfeld doubles associated with restricted Laistrygonian algebras in arbitrary positive characteristic.

papers.title: On the non-existence of certain maximizing curves of degree 7
papers.abstract: In this paper we show there does not exist any arrangement of degree $7$ consisting of $k\geq 1$ conics and $d\geq 1$ lines admitting certain naturally chosen ${\rm ADE}$-singularities.

papers.title: On disjointness of 3-IETs from mixing and lightly mixing systems
papers.abstract: In this note we show that all interval exchange transformations of three intervals (3-IETs) are spectrally disjoint from all mixing and disjoint from lightly mixing systems. Until now, it was known that almost every 3-IET is rigid, which implies this property. However, not all 3-IETs are rigid, hence our result is a strict improvement of current knowledge. We then use this result, among many others, to prove that although some 3-IETs are mildly mixing, they are always disjoint in the sense of Furstenberg from lightly mixing systems.

papers.title: Globally Convergent Jacobi-Type Algorithms for Robust Approximate Diagonalization of Higher-Order Cumulant Tensors
papers.abstract: The sums of the absolute values of higher-order cumulants are classical contrast functions for independent component analysis (ICA) and lead naturally to robust approximate diagonalization of higher-order cumulant tensors using $\ell_1$-based diagonalization over the orthogonal or unitary group. We propose Jacobi-SubG, a Jacobi-type framework that selects index pairs using Riemannian subdifferential information and performs plane rotations with a refinement step that preserves nonzero diagonal contractions. For the general tensor model, we prove global convergence of the entire iterate sequence from any initialization with nonzero diagonal contractions, provided that the subproblem solvers satisfy a uniform sufficient-ascent estimate. For real and complex third- and fourth-order cumulant tensors, which are widely used in ICA, we develop specialized subproblem solvers satisfying these conditions. The resulting algorithms thus enjoy global convergence under the simple initialization condition that all diagonal contractions are nonzero. Numerical experiments on ICA and tensor diagonalization show that the proposed Jacobi-SubG variants achieve better source recovery and higher final objective values in several settings, particularly at the higher tested noise levels.

papers.title: Perfect matchings in planar 3-connected graphs: girth five and minimum degree five
papers.abstract: Let $Φ(G)$ denote the number of perfect matchings of a graph $G$. Goedgebeur et al. posted two questions about the perfect matchings of planar 3-connected graphs: does there exist an infinite family of matchable planar 3-connected graphs of girth 5 with a constant number of perfect matchings? Whether there exist infinitely many planar 3-connected graphs with minimum degree 5 which have a constant number of perfect matchings. We present answers to those questions. First, we construct, for every even $n\ge196$, a simple planar 3-connected graph of order $n$ and girth five with exactly $c$ perfect matchings, where $c$ is a fixed positive integer. Second, for a simple planar 3-connected graph $G$ with a perfect matching and minimum degree at least five, we show that $Φ(G)\ge2^{\lceil(|V(G)|+20)/22\rceil}$. This implies that, for each positive integer $t$, only finitely many such graphs, up to isomorphism, have at most $t$ perfect matchings.

papers.title: Analytic Liouville Integrable Geodesic Flow Has Zero Entropy
papers.abstract: This paper studies the topological entropy of real-analytic Liouville integrable Hamiltonian systems. We prove that the Hamiltonian flow on a compact connected regular energy hypersurface has zero topological entropy whenever a complete family of commuting real-analytic first integrals is generically independent in a connected neighborhood of that hypersurface. The proof uses finite normal expansions along minimal analytic carriers and an ergodic version of Ziglin's leading-term argument to obtain independent invariant normal polynomials, whose Poisson geometry makes all tangent Lyapunov exponents of the carriers vanish. In particular, we prove that a real-analytic Liouville integrable geodesic flow on a closed real-analytic Riemannian manifold has zero topological entropy, giving a positive answer to the conjecture proposed by Paternain in 1992.

papers.title: Reverse quantum aging: Restoring rhythmicity from quantum aging state
papers.abstract: Quantum aging transition has recently been reported, whereby the oscillatory dynamics of a network of globally coupled quantum self-sustained oscillators is degraded sharply when the fraction of inactive nodes exceeds a critical value. Here we explore the reverse process: the revival of rhythmic dynamics from an aged state in a quantum oscillator network by introducing a controlled incoherent single-boson pumping channel. Using a self-consistent quantum master equation in the Lindblad form for globally coupled active--inactive quantum Stuart--Landau oscillators, we show that increasing the pumping strength progressively suppresses the aging transition and eventually eliminates it, restoring rhythmicity even when all oscillators are inactive. Remarkably, complete compensation of the coupling-induced dissipative loss is not required; a substantially weaker pumping strength is sufficient to eliminate the aging transition. We show that the revival is governed by a redistribution of the Fock-state population of the inactive oscillators toward higher-occupation states. Our results establish controlled incoherent pumping as an effective mechanism for restoring dynamical robustness in quantum oscillator networks.

papers.title: The relation between non-exchangeability and radial asymmetry of copulas
papers.abstract: Non-exchangeability and radial asymmetry have got substantial attention in the literature, but relation between the two has not been studied yet. We propose the question: if a copula has a given degree of radial asymmetry, what is the range of possible values of the measure of non-exhangeability. We determine the set of all points whose first coordinate is the radial asymmetry of a copula and the second coordinate is its non-exchangeability. We show that this set is a non-convex hexagon.

papers.title: Bosonic Quantum Conditional Mutual Information and Bose-Einstein Condensation
papers.abstract: This article aims to introduce the bosonic asymmetric quantum conditional mutual information (QCMI), $I_{B}(A; B|C)$, as a rigorously defined information-theoretic quantity for continuous-variable (bosonic) systems. After defining $I_{B}(A; B|C)$ through quantum instruments on infinite-dimensional Fock spaces, we prove that Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC) induces a logarithmic divergence $ I_{B}(A; B|C) \geq α\log_2 (N_{0}^C+1)$, which further establishes $I_{B}(A; B|C)$ as a quantum-information order parameter for BEC with power-law scaling near the critical point. We provide the complete five-step proof of this result, connecting measurement back-action, off-diagonal long-range order, and Jensen's inequality. In the condensed phase, the effective causal propagation velocity is set by the Bogoliubov sound speed $c_s$ in the long-wavelength limit, and vanishes continuously at the superfluid--Mott-insulator transition. Applications to composite bosons, the BEC--BCS crossover, and a quantum-gas-microscope measurement protocol are presented. Finally, we demonstrate how the reduced bosonic QCMI serves as a finite-size scaling probe analogous to the Binder cumulant.

papers.title: Sparse Lifts of q-Linearized Permutation Polynomials with Explicit Inverses
papers.abstract: We give a higher unit-torus lift from q-linearized permutation polynomials over Fqn to generally nonlinear sparse permutation polynomials over Fqns. The construction preserves compositional inverses: if a linearized polynomials and its inverse have coefficients (ai) and (Ai), then the lifted polynomial and its inverse have the same coefficients. As a consequence, we obtain nonlinear binomial lifts whose inverses are again binomials in the two-dimensional case, including an explicit inverse for a binomial family over Fq4. The three dimensional specialization yields permutation trinomials whose compositional inverses are again trinomials, together with explicit involution criteria and examples.

papers.title: Closed-form construction of exceptional points in a two-parametric PT-symmetric large-matrix model
papers.abstract: Stable bound states living on a discrete one-dimensional N-point lattice are assumed generated by a certain two-parametric PT symmetric potential $V=V(A,B)$. At any $N$, the coordinates $A=A^{(EP)}$ and $B=B^{(EP)}$ of the Kato's exceptional point (marking the phase-transition instant of the loss of stability) are defined, exactly, via roots of a certain elementary quartic polynomial.

papers.title: On the singular set of the geodesic flow on nonpositively curved surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that the singular locus of the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle of a nonpositively curved surface enjoys an additional regularity property: its characteristic function belongs to the geometric anisotropic Sobolev space $H^{5/8-}_xH^{-13/16}_θ$. In particular, this implies that if the geodesic flow is not ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure, then the zero set of the curvature must be thick in the sense that it supports a nonzero, nonnegative function in $H^{5/8-}$. The proof relies on semiclassical analysis and a new radial estimate for parabolic flows.

papers.title: The periodic Airy line ensembles
papers.abstract: In this paper we construct a one-parameter family of periodic Airy line ensembles $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{per},R}$ for $R>0$ as weak scaling limits of Borodin's periodic Schur processes. We establish several properties of $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{per},R}$, including a determinantal point process structure with an explicit correlation kernel. We also show that, after a parabolic shift and normalization, $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{per},R}$ satisfies, on its domain $[-R/2,R/2]$, the same Brownian Gibbs property enjoyed by the usual Airy line ensemble. A main technical contribution of the paper is a general tightness criterion for determinantal line ensembles, which extends the argument used by Johansson in [Comm. Math. Phys. 242 (2003), 277-329] to prove a functional limit theorem for the discrete polynuclear growth model.

papers.title: How Mobile Oscillators Reshape Dynamical Robustness in Complex Networks
papers.abstract: While the robustness of collective dynamics in static networks is well established, how agent mobility and network topology jointly shape dynamical robustness remains largely unexplored. In this letter, we investigate the robustness of mobile Stuart-Landau oscillators performing random walks on networks and interacting diffusively when co-located. In the rapid-mobility regime, we reduce the dynamics to a mean-field framework linking network degree statistics to an effective global coupling strength. We show analytically that increased degree heterogeneity in the network enhances the effective coupling strength, and strictly lowers the critical threshold of functional degradation for amplitude death. Numerical simulations confirm the predicted heterogeneity-dependent ordering of the transition thresholds, showing an earlier collective collapse in scale-free networks than in random or regular networks. Our results establish mobility and network heterogeneity as key determinants of robustness in mobile oscillator populations, with implications for resilient biological and engineered collectives.

papers.title: Homotopy Self-Equivalences of $\mathbb{R}P^2\times S^2$ and a Braid for non-orientable $4$-Manifolds
papers.abstract: We compute the group of based homotopy classes of self-homotopy equivalences of the non-orientable $4$-manifold $\RP^2\times S^2$. It is an elementary abelian $2$-group of rank $5$. The subgroup of classes whose based lift to the universal cover $S^2\times S^2$ has degree $+1$ has rank $4$ and is isomorphic to the group of free homotopy classes. The group maps onto the group of self-equivalences of the algebraic $2$-type, which has order $8$, with kernel $π_4(\RP^2\times S^2)\cong(\Z/2)^2$ generated by pinch-fold maps; that these maps are independent is shown by an adjunction argument. We then construct a non-orientable analogue of the Hambleton--Kreck braid of exact sequences in dimension $4$, for non-orientable manifolds with spin universal cover, stated for finite fundamental group. We apply the braid to $\RP^2\times S^2$ and to $\RP^4$, and for the Hambleton--Hillman manifold with fundamental group $(\Z/2)^2$ we determine the normal $1$-type and show that self-equivalences act on $π_2$ through diagonal sign matrices. For $\RP^2\times S^2$ the pinch-fold maps are detected by twisted spin bordism, and, assuming facts from surgery theory stated as hypotheses, exactly one of the three non-trivial pinch-fold maps is homotopic to a homeomorphism.

papers.title: $2$-large sets are sets of nil-Bohr recurrence
papers.abstract: A set $S$ of positive integers is $2$-large if every two-coloring contains arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common difference in $S$. We prove that every such set meets every nil-Bohr neighborhood of $0$. This proves a conjecture of the first author and gives a sharp answer to a question of Host, Kra, and Maass. We also show that, for every fixed nil-Bohr neighborhood \(B\) of \(0\) and every \(\eps>0\), restricting the common difference to \(B\) increases the extremal number for \(k\)-term arithmetic progressions by at most a factor of \(1+\eps\), provided \(k\) is sufficiently large.

papers.title: The ring of values of $E$-functions is not a field
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{E}$ be the ring of values taken at algebraic points by $E$-functions. The exponential function and the Bessel function $J_0$ are classical examples of $E$-functions. We prove that $\mathbf{E}$ is not a field. More precisely, we prove that it is neither noetherian nor factorial, and construct non-units of $\mathbf{E}$ explicity, including $e+1$, $J_0(1)$, and ${}_1F_1(a;b;1)$ for rational parameters $a$ and $b$ such that $0

papers.title: The symmetry group of Turk's head knots
papers.abstract: For p, q >= 3 with gcd(p,q) = 1 we show that the symmetry group of the Turk's head knot Th(p,q), the closure of the braid (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1} sigma_3 sigma_4^{-1} ... sigma_{p-1}^{+-1})^q, is the dihedral group of order 4q. This proves Conjecture R of Di Prisa and Şavk for q >= 3; the case p = 3 is due to Sakuma and Weeks. The argument is diagrammatic: by the flyping theorem of Menasco and Thistlethwaite, the symmetries of a knot with a prime, reduced alternating diagram without non-trivial flypes are the symmetries of the diagram (we write out a proof for the diagrams at hand), and we show that the standard diagram of Th(p,q) has no non-trivial flypes and exactly 4q symmetries. The chirality of Th(p,q) for even p, which also follows from a theorem of Murasugi, is visible in the group. We compare the argument with the geometric one of Sakuma and Weeks for p = 3.

papers.title: There are only finitely many irregular Diophantine quadruples
papers.abstract: A set of $m$ distinct positive integers is called a Diophantine $m$-tuple if the product of any two distinct elements, increased by one, is a perfect square. A Diophantine quadruple $\{a,b,c,d\}$ with $a<b<c<d$ is called regular if $$d=a+b+c+2abc+2\sqrt{(ab+1)(ac+1)(bc+1)}.$$ We prove that every irregular Diophantine quadruple satisfies $c<10^{338}$ and $d<10^{10^{24}}$.

papers.title: Fatou Components of Attracting Skew Products: From Polynomial Classification to Transcendental Complexity
papers.abstract: We study the Fatou components of holomorphic skew products $F \colon \mathbb{C}^2 \to \mathbb{C}^2, F(z,w) = (f(z) + r(z,w), g(w))$ near an attracting invariant fiber, introducing a refined classification of components on the fiber: bulging, partial bulging, and nowhere bulging. For polynomial skew products, we give a complete characterization of when the basin at infinity is non-bulging, and show that in this case non-bulging implies nowhere bulging, ruling out partial bulging entirely. In the transcendental setting, the behavior is richer: we construct partially bulging wandering domains and Baker domains, show that any orbitally unbounded Fatou component can be made nowhere bulging by choosing an appropriate function $r$, and prove that for any nonconstant $r$ there exists an entire function $f$ with an escaping wandering domain that fails to be bulging. Bulging thus depends on the interplay between fiber dynamics and perturbation.

papers.title: Pointwise Ergodic Theorems Along Reiter Sequences on Locally Compact Groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a locally compact, second countable group admitting a Reiter sequence, and suppose that $G$ acts on a von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$ equipped with a semifinite trace $τ$ via trace-preserving automorphisms. In this paper, we prove a maximal inequality for ergodic averages along such Reiter sequences. Our approach relies on approximating the Reiter sequence by a linear combination of characteristic functions of Følner sequences using the layer-cake representation. Furthermore, we establish the bilateral almost uniform convergence of these ergodic averages. As an application, we deduce a non-commutative Wiener-Wintner type theorem along Reiter sequences.

papers.title: New tools for sparse graph embeddings: Hybrid expanders and application to nested cycles
papers.abstract: We introduce \emph{hybrid expanders}, sparse graphs which combine sublinear expansion across all scales with strong constant-factor expansion on smaller, polylogarithmic sets. We show that every $n$-vertex graph of average degree at least $2^{ω(\log^*n)}$ contains such a subgraph, and use this local expansion to bring into the sparse setting tree-embedding and rollback tools more commonly associated with random or pseudorandom graphs. As an application, for fixed $k\in\mathbb N$, we prove that every graph satisfying this average-degree condition contains $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint cycles with nested vertex sets and compatible cyclic orders, resolving up to a quasi-constant factor a problem of Thomassen, originating in work of Erdős.

papers.title: Minimal time for heat observability on almost-Riemannian surfaces
papers.abstract: We determine the minimal observation time for the heat equation on a closed almost-Riemannian surface, for a class of observation sets leaving sufficiently thin collars around simple Baouendi-Grushin circles. The structure and density are analytic near these circles, and the coefficients may depend on both variables. The formula is expressed through a complex phase describing concentration near the singular set and extends the thresholds known for separated models. Regular unobserved regions away from the circles do not change this time, provided all other singularities are observed. For singular circles of constant bracket step greater than two, local analyticity implies failure of observability at every time for observation sets at positive distance. We also construct quasimodes concentrated near simple singular circles, with exponentially small errors. Their superpositions give a lower bound for the Schrödinger observation time.

papers.title: Long-time asymptotics for the focusing coupled Kundu-Eckhaus equation
papers.abstract: The focusing coupled Kundu-Eckhaus (CKE) equation extends the coupled nonlinear Schrödinger (CNLS) equation by adding quintic and derivative nonlinearities. We study the Cauchy problem for the focusing CKE equation with Schwartz initial data under the assumption of no discrete spectrum and no spectral singularities on the real axis. Based on the gauge equivalence between the focusing CKE and CNLS equations, we analyze the associated $3\times3$ matrix Riemann-Hilbert problem by the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method. By establishing joint error estimates for the CNLS solution and the gauge phase, we obtain a uniform long-time asymptotic formula for the dispersive radiation of the CKE equation with an $O(t^{-1}\log t)$ remainder in bounded velocity cones.

papers.title: Ricci pinching on complete Kahler manifolds
papers.abstract: We study Ricci pinching problem on complete Kähler manifolds. For complete noncompact manifolds with Euclidean volume growth, we prove flatness under nonnegative bisectional curvature and Ricci pinching, and Ricci flatness under nonnegative Ricci curvature, quadratic curvature decay, and the same pinching condition. In both cases, the pinching constant may tend to zero at a logarithmic rate. Examples show that the logarithmic exponent is sharp in complex dimension two. Second part of the paper proves that a complete Kähler manifold of complex dimension at least two with positive holomorphic bisectional curvature is compact if its sectional curvature is nonnegative and its Ricci curvature is uniformly pinched outside a compact set. No volume-growth assumption or curvature upper bound is needed. Heat smoothing of the Busemann function supplies a strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustion with bounded gradient, so the general top Ricci-mass theorem of Datar--Pingali--Seshadri applies. The new ingridents are integral estimates for the Ricci form. The analytic arguments use scalar curvature gap theorems and a critical-$L^n$ vanishing theorem for closed real $(1,1)$-forms under nonnegative Ricci curvature and nonnegative quadratic orthogonal bisectional curvature. The Hodge-Laplace heat eqution deformation conserves the signed top-degree integral, including its initial value, while norm domination and scalar heat-semigroup decay force this integral to vanish. For semipositive initial forms this gives pointwise vanishing of the top wedge power.

papers.title: The Davenport constant of low-dimensional boxes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the maximal length of a minimal zero-sum sequence over $\left[\!\left[ -m,m \right]\!\right]^d$ having a support of size $d+1$. When $d=2$, we find the exact value of this maximal length for all $m \ge 2$, as well as the exact structure of all extremal sequences for this problem. When $d=3$, we obtain lower and upper bounds that asymptotically match each other as $m$ tends to infinity. This allows us to improve on the best known lower bounds for the Davenport constant of low-dimensional boxes.

papers.title: Period Piece: NEXPTIME-complete problems on digraphs via Boolean network dynamics
papers.abstract: The central object in this work is the Boolean network, a function $f:\{0,1\}^V \to \{0,1\}^V$. Often identified with $f$ is its dynamics $D_f$, the digraph with exactly $\{x \to y : f(x)=y\}$ as its arcs. The interaction graph of $f$ is the digraph $G$ on $V$ which can be thought of as representing the dependencies of the components of $f$ on one another. On the other hand, model-checking is a major field of study in graph algorithms and complexity. We consider problems at the intersection of these paradigms: for a given property $φ$, we say that a digraph $G$ is $φ$-dynamic if $G$ is the interaction graph of some Boolean network $f$ such that $D_f \models φ$. The corresponding decision problem $φ$-DYNAMIC asks whether $G$ is $φ$-dynamic. Problems of this form are well-studied in the Boolean networks community. For example, it is a well-known result that, letting $φ$ be 'No fixed points' (i.e. $\nexists x:x\to x$), $φ$-DYNAMIC is equivalent to the structural digraph problem NON-ACYCLIC, which is solvable in linear time. We establish, for the first time, properties $φ$ for which $φ$-DYNAMIC is computationally hard. These include the 'Unique fixed point' property $\exists!x:x\to x$, and a range of properties concerning the periodic points of $f$ (i.e. vertices of $D_f$ which lie on a cycle). More widely, we exhibit an infinite family of natural properties $φ$ such that $φ$-DYNAMIC is $\mathrm{NEXPTIME}$-complete, which we call PERIOD PIECE. As a special case, these include all properties of the form 'Unique cycle of length $k$' and 'Exactly $k$ fixed points' for any $k \ge 1$. On the other hand, we show that if the input digraph has bounded in-degree, then for those same problems $φ$-DYNAMIC collapses down to $\mathrm{NP}^{\mathrm{NP}}$, the second level of the polynomial hierarchy, though it remains $\mathrm{NP}^{\mathrm{NP}}$-complete.

papers.title: Scalable Identification of Physics-Based and Neural Dynamics from Partial Measurements
papers.abstract: We present a scalable method for identifying nonlinear dynamics from partial measurements, supporting physics-based, neural-network, and gray-box models. We use the Prediction Error Method (PEM) coupled with state estimation performed by a Moving Horizon Estimation (MHE) scheme, which can account directly for general nonlinear dynamics. This results in a bi-level optimization problem that scales poorly with increasing model parameters. To improve computational efficiency, we derive a reformulation that avoids explicit parameter-wide sensitivity matrices and exploits the temporal structure of the underlying optimization problem. Numerical comparisons show up to a $215\times$ speedup in hypergradient evaluation. Racing-vehicle simulations demonstrate accurate prediction and physical-parameter recovery in tire-force identification. Real-world data show that the gray-box model improves prediction accuracy with a neural residual while retaining physical interpretability.

papers.title: AI Discovery in Combinatorics: From Problems to Solutions and Back to Bigger Problems
papers.abstract: We introduce $qt$Bench, a benchmark of 29 open problems in algebraic combinatorics. These problems ask for a simple combinatorial algorithm that explains given polynomial coefficients or identities. To help AI agents search for such algorithms, we provide a scaffold for playing with combinatorial objects, countering cheating attempts, and testing candidate solutions. To explore how far frontier AI systems can go on these problems, we collaborated with OpenAI, whose researchers obtained proposed solutions to several of them. This highlights bigger meta-problems: is AI discovery at scale ethical? How should these results be released? How should proof digestion be organized? We discuss these questions and give our views.

papers.title: Order convergence in ordered vector spaces: compactness, atoms, pervasiveness, and ice cream spaces
papers.abstract: We study order convergence in ordered vector spaces that are not necessarily lattices. In this setting, we consider two generalizations of order convergence on vector lattices, a directed and an undirected variant. We show that these notions agree for the class of pervasive spaces and extend several results concerning atomicity and order convergence in vector lattices to this class. In particular, we prove that a pervasive JB-algebra is associative, which strengthens a result of Sherman for C*-algebras. We also establish a number of new characterizations of pervasive spaces. Additionally, we systematically study a class of order unit spaces associated to Banach spaces, called ice cream spaces. We provide descriptions of both directed and undirected order convergences in these spaces, yielding examples where the two notions differ. We also consider other order-theoretic aspects of ice cream spaces, such as atoms and lattice operations, relating them to the geometry of the underlying Banach spaces. We demonstrate that ice cream spaces exhibit behavior very different from vector lattices and can serve as a rich source of counterexamples in the theory of ordered vector spaces.

papers.title: Neural Network Preconditioning: A Case Study for the Solution of the Parametric Helmholtz Equation
papers.abstract: This work presents a hybrid numerical approach for solving linear systems arising from the discretization of the two-dimensional parametric Helmholtz equation. A convolutional neural network based on the U-Net architecture is trained in an self-supervised manner (i.e., without explicitly generating reference solutions) to approximate the inverse of the discretized Helmholtz operator, using a loss function involving the residual norm of the linear system. The trained network is used as a nonlinear preconditioner within the flexible GMRES (FGMRES) algorithm. Numerical experiments show that while the neural network is not accurate enough to act as a standalone solver, it significantly improves the convergence of FGMRES when employed as a preconditioner. The neural preconditioner demonstrates robust performance and generalization capabilities with respect to variations in the velocity field and the domain size. Comparisons with algebraic preconditioners, based on LU factorizations of approximations of the original system matrices, indicate the superior efficiency of the neural approach under equivalent conditions. We believe that the proposed method is not tied to a specific neural architecture and can be extended to other parametric PDEs.

papers.title: Spectra and Support Theory for Wide Subcategories in $n$-Abelian Categories
papers.abstract: We develop a support theory for wide subcategories of essentially small Krull--Schmidt \(n\)-abelian categories. We construct spectra associated with families of wide subcategories and establish the corresponding support and radical theories. In particular, we characterize prime wide subcategories as the completely meet-irreducible elements of the lattice of wide subcategories and prove that every wide subcategory is recovered from the prime wide subcategories containing it. We further show that any classifying support datum is recovered, together with its object supports, from the canonical prime spectrum. Finally, we provide a \(2\)-abelian example admitting no classifying support datum.

papers.title: Closed-form evaluation of the cumulative distribution function and absolute moments of the variance-gamma distribution
papers.abstract: Closed-form formulas are derived for the cumulative distribution function and odd-order absolute moments of the variance-gamma distribution. As a special case, closed-form expressions are deduced for the cumulative distribution function and odd-order absolute central moments of the product of two correlated zero-mean normal random variables.

papers.title: Knot Floer homology of fibered positive links
papers.abstract: We determine the Maslov-graded next-to-top term of knot Floer homology for fibered positive links. Its rank in Maslov grading (-1) is the number of nontrivial prime connected-sum factors plus the number of components minus one, and the remaining summand is supported in Maslov grading zero. For a knot, the dimension of this remaining summand is determined by its Alexander polynomial. The proof combines a preferred-crossing construction with reductions of generalized Seifert surfaces to planar pretzel surfaces and a graded skein induction. We also obtain bounds on the fixed points of monodromies for fibered positive knots.

papers.title: Bounded continued fractions and quadratic orders in $\Q(\sqrt{127})$
papers.abstract: We study the least periods and multiplier orders in two constructions of Mercat for continued fractions with bounded partial quotients. Our main explicit result concerns a family in $\Q(\sqrt{127})$ with partial quotients at most $4$. For every integer $j\geq1$, we prove that its primitive period has length $92j+2$ and its multiplier order has conductor $y_{4j}/4$, where $(4730624+419775\sqrt{127})^k=x_k+y_k\sqrt{127}$. The totally positive unit group of this order has index $4j$ in that of the maximal order. These exact formulas give divisor-sum lower bounds at fixed traces and a lower bound of order $(\log X)^2$ for the number of bounded continued fractions with discriminant at most $X$. We also prove a primitive-period refinement of Mercat's palindromic construction. Combining this refinement with Hensley's counting theorem gives, for every $m\geq2$ and $η>0$, at least $X^{δ_m/2-η}$ quadratic fields, up to a positive constant, that admit infinitely many purely periodic continued fractions with partial quotients at most $m$. Here $δ_m$ is the Hausdorff dimension of the corresponding continued fraction Cantor set.

papers.title: Asymptotic stability and sharp decay near homogeneous solutions of a nonlinearly damped Schrödinger equation on the torus
papers.abstract: We study the one-dimensional periodic nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a power-type nonlinear damping, both in the focusing and the defocusing regime. For a sufficiently small damping parameter and initial data close in relative $H^1$ norm to a nonzero spatially homogeneous state, we prove global existence and asymptotic convergence, after a constant phase adjustment, to an explicit homogeneous solution. The \(L^2\) and \(H^1\) norms follow the explicit adiabatic decay law, with the same leading coefficient as the homogeneous solution. We obtain explicit convergence rates, including a \(t^{-1/2}\) bound for the relative spatial perturbation. For every nonconstant initial datum in a small neighborhood of the homogeneous solution, the kinetic energy has a strictly positive leading coefficient and decays one power of time faster than the squared \(L^2\) norm.

papers.title: Towards learning-enhanced solvers for multi-parametric optimization
papers.abstract: Neural networks (NNs) have been employed in various ways to accelerate the solution of multi-parametric optimization problems (OPs), which prominently arise in model predictive control (MPC). Early approaches focused on approximating the parametric solution (e.g., the optimal control law) directly by NNs. More recently, learning-based techniques have been used to emulate or enhance solver iterations. For the direct approximation of the parametric solution, it has been demonstrated that exploiting structural properties of the underlying OP facilitates the design of suitable NN architectures. In this paper, we show that structural analysis can also be leveraged to systematically integrate learning into classical optimization algorithms, thereby enhancing their performance. We formalize our concept for the case of multi-parametric quadratic programs (mpQPs), which frequently arise in linear-quadratic MPC, as a representative application. More precisely, we demonstrate that tailored NNs enable a parameter-dependent fine-tuning of the step sizes in a standard dual projected gradient scheme. The design of the NNs is guided by the observation that optimal step sizes, which permit obtaining the exact optimal solution in finitely many iterations, are piecewise constant functions over the parameter space (e.g., the state space in MPC). We establish key theoretical properties of the proposed approach and illustrate its effectiveness in a numerical case study.

papers.title: Asymptotic Risk of Learning-Rate Schedules for Least-Squares Regression with Discretely Distributed Features
papers.abstract: We study the last iterate of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on streaming least squares with discretely distributed features (Slock's model), which decouples the dynamics across eigendirections. Under power-law source and capacity conditions, we derive the exact finite-time risk and asymptotic equivalents of constant and Warmup-Stable-Decay (WSD) schedules. With a tuned base learning-rate, the resulting scaling law decays as $Θ(T^{-q})$, where $T$ is the horizon, and $q$ is independent of the cooldown length $c \in (0,1]$ but is strictly smaller for the constant schedule: any cooldown of fixed relative length $c > 0$, however short, improves the risk by a polynomial factor, while its length only affects the constant, which is minimized by linear decay ($c = 1$). Finally, we show that the optimal risk depends on the batch size $b$ and horizon $T$ only through $bT$, up to a critical batch size.

papers.title: An Algebraic Matching Algorithm for the Genus of Grid Diagrams
papers.abstract: Grid diagrams encode knots and links combinatorially through an (n,n) winding matrix W(G). A fundamental invariant of the grid diagram is its genus g(G), which records essential topological information about the underlying knot. We give an algebraic algorithm that computes g(G) directly from W(G). The method repurposes the Hungarian algorithm ,after a column normalization that makes the matrix non-negative, it applies row-column reductions and minimum-vertex-cover corrections until the zero entries admit a perfect matching, equivalently until the minimum marking number equals n. By Konig's theorem the resulting permutation defines a distinguished grid state, and g(G) is then read from this matrix via the classical grid homology formula (Ozsvath-Stipsicz-Szabo). The novelty of this paper is the algorithm and its strongly polynomial analysis; the underlying invariant is known grid-homology theory. We illustrate the method on the trefoil and additional examples, and discuss extensions to (m,n) matrices and grid-move navigation toward the knot genus g(K).

papers.title: Towards the Geometry of Quantum Optical Measurements: Kraus Trajectories in the Instrumental Weyl-Heisenberg Group Manifold
papers.abstract: Since ancient Greek times, geometry has been a method by which humans can make inferences, by the use of similar triangles, about the world far beyond their immediate senses. Similarity plays an equally important role in quantum measurement, except that instead of triangles, the similarity is between the infinitesimal generators of rotation, canonical transformation, or some other virtual symmetry. For many quantum optical measurements of a single mode, these generators produce Kraus operators that are contained within a twelve-dimensional Lie group: the Instrumental Weyl-Heisenberg group manifold ($\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$). In particular, $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ is general enough to include all diffusively generated 'dyne measurements. In this paper, $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ will be used to develop two more general classes of 'dyne measurement: one that interpolates between diffusive homodyne and diffusive heterodyne (``slomodyne'') and one that adds to 'dyne measurements adaptive squeezing and displacement. Our analysis uses an approach known as the Instrument Manifold Program (IMP). In particular, a Harish-Chandra-like decomposition of $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ is used to calculate the vielbein transformation from a right-invariant basis to the corresponding coordinate basis, allowing us to universally and autonomously navigate $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ and locate the Kraus-operator of whatever selective process is being considered as it evolves in time according to the measurement record.

papers.title: Dudley-type bound for stationary Bernoulli processes
papers.abstract: This is preliminary, AI-generated note on the Dudley-type bound for stationary Bernoulli processes postulated by M. Talagrand based on the unpublished notes of the authors and the recent note \cite{invariant} which in turn is an alternative proof of the result by Hu, Wang, Wu.

papers.title: Hecke modules associated to certain even ternary lattices of half-discriminant $\mathbf{N^2}$
papers.abstract: We consider Hecke modules of orthogonal modular forms attached to definite even ternary lattices of half-discriminant $N^2$, where $N > 1$ is odd and square-free. We prove explicit Jacquet-Langlands style correspondences with spaces of classical modular forms (in the spirit of Birch and Hein-Tornaria-Voight). This is done by applying sequences of Watson-style transformations that reduce the discriminant while preserving the adelic orthogonal group.

papers.title: Quantum integrals II: Dominated and almost uniform convergence
papers.abstract: One main aim of our paper is to formulate noncommutative versions of the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem in the setting of quantum integration theory on von Neumann algebras. Our starting point is a reformulation of classical dominated convergence in terms of weak* convergence. Using our recent sequential-continuity theorem, we obtain dominated convergence formulations for sequentially normal states and, under domination by a fixed bounded integrable majorant, for sequentially normal weights. Integrable, possibly unbounded, majorants are treated first in the tracial setting, then for arbitrary von Neumann algebras using Haagerup's L1 space, and finally using normal semifinite weights and their GNS representations. For any faithful normal semifinite weight $φ$, weak* convergence of norm-bounded sequences is characterized by `integrating against' bounded positive integrable majorants. We also study noncommutative almost uniform and local almost uniform convergence. In particular, for norm-bounded sequences, local $φ$-bilaterally almost uniform convergence implies weak* convergence and L1 convergence to 0 of $h^{1/2}(x_n-x)h^{1/2}$ for every positive Haagerup L1 density h, without assuming sigma-finiteness. We also prove a dominated convergence theorem in the predual: fixed positive order domination and Petz's almost uniform convergence imply convergence in the predual norm. We establish implications and equivalences among these convergence notions, connecting dominated convergence with tracial and nontracial integration.

papers.title: Bell's go theorem: regaining local causality with a new notion of realism
papers.abstract: Bell's theorem is popularly stated as the inconsistency of quantum theory with local realism. Realism is here formalized by the ontological models framework, where elements of reality are points of a measurable space and probabilities obey the Kolmogorov axioms. In the Bell scenario, locally causal ontological models posit a common cause supporting a global valuation, a joint assignment of outcomes to all measurements at once, across incompatible contexts. Within this notion of realism, Bell's theorem makes any realist explanation of the quantum predictions conspiratorial: any mechanism, whether superluminal, superdeterministic, or retrocausal, must be finely tuned so as never to manifest operationally. We redefine realism through a new ontological framework that generalizes the standard one. The elements of reality, which we call records, are no longer points but relational parts of a point-free generalization of a topological space (sublocales of a locale). A record shared by two incompatible contexts establishes the sameness of a measurement across them, without such pairwise identities composing into a global valuation, and the common cause is then a web of such records. Within this framework, Bell's no-go theorem becomes a go theorem: local causality, restated for records, is no longer at odds with the quantum statistics. This is possible because modularity, the inclusion-exclusion law of classical probability, fails across incompatible contexts, so that the probability theory generalizes Kolmogorov's. We exhibit explicit models reproducing several quantum strategies, including the optimal CHSH violation. More broadly, locally causal models of this kind attain every Bell-CHSH value up to the algebraic maximum. A realist explanation of the quantum predictions need not be conspiratorial; every causal influence posited by these models is reflected in the operational predictions.

papers.title: On the cyclic limiting behavior of the restarted Arnoldi algorithm for real symmetric matrices with restart length $s=2$
papers.abstract: We prove that the restarted Arnoldi algorithm for real symmetric matrices with restart length $s=2$ has a cyclic limiting behavior. In the terminology established in (arXiv:2209.14579), this is a proof of the ACI($s$) conjecture for $A=A^T\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and $s=2$. As explained in (arXiv:2209.14579), this also proves the Forsythe conjecture (Numerische Mathematik, 11 (1968), pp. 57-76) about the limiting behavior of the conjugate gradient method and positive definite $A=A^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ for $s=2$. The proof we give is an extensively rewritten and simplified version of a proof found using Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol. At the end of this paper, we discuss its origin and evolution, as well as related recent developments around the Forsythe conjecture. Our motivation is to present a proof that is instructive and transparent, so that it can enhance the knowledge of interested human readers.

papers.title: A Multipatch Model for Evaluating Interdivisional Connectivity and Vaccination Dynamics in the 2026 Bangladesh Measles Outbreak
papers.abstract: The 2026 measles resurgence in Bangladesh motivates a spatial modelling framework that accounts for heterogeneous local transmission, vaccination activity, and interdivisional connectivity. We formulate a multipatch susceptible-vaccinated-infectious-recovered model for the eight administrative divisions of Bangladesh. Division-specific parameters are estimated from reported measles cases \cite{DGHS} and smoothed vaccination data using bounded nonlinear least squares, with uncertainty quantified through 1000 parametric bootstrap replicates. The fitted divisional systems are then connected through compartment-specific movement and cross-patch infection coefficients adjusted for connectivity and the source division's relative reproduction number. The fitted model captures the main division-specific epidemic patterns. Estimated local reproduction numbers range from \(1.1386\) in Khulna (95\% CI:\(0.5703\)--\(1.3834\)) to \(4.3491\) in Dhaka (95\% CI: \(1.4449\)--\(5.6307\)), while Chattogram also exhibits high transmission potential (\(\mathcal{R}_0^i=4.2275\); 95\% CI: \(4.0019\)--\(4.3185\)). Baseline spatial coupling increases the network-wide epidemic peak from \(190.96\) to \(313.20\) infectious individuals and more than doubles cumulative infections from \(1086.42\) to \(2345.35\). Relative to baseline coupling, 50\% and 80\% restrictions reduce the epidemic peak by \(26.69\%\) and \(34.37\%\), and cumulative infections by \(25.07\%\) and \(41.48\%\), respectively. Conversely, a 50\% increase in spatial coupling raises the peak by \(30.14\%\) and cumulative infections by \(23.54\%\). Although local transmission remains dominant in every division, cross-patch infection accounts for \(28.83\%\) of new infections in Rajshahi at the baseline epidemic peak. Source-sink analysis identifies Dhaka as the dominant cross-patch source and Chattogram as a smaller secondary source.

papers.title: The triangular metric on projective surfaces
papers.abstract: In \cite{ThurstonStretch} Thurston introduced stretch paths and stretch maps between hyperbolic surfaces. In this paper we extend similar constructions to the space of convex real projective structures on surfaces. Using Fock-Goncharov-like parameters, we introduce stretch paths and construct explicit stretch maps between the projective surface. We show that stretch maps are $e^t$--Lipschitz with respect to a triangular metric we introduce on the projective surface. This allows us to gain control on several length functions on an open set of the space of convex real projective structures (those where there is no ``local back--tracking"). As an application we obtain pointwise upper bounds for the Hilbert entropy of some convex real projective structures in terms of Fock-Goncharov-like parameters.

papers.title: Poincaré inequalities, logarithmic growth and doubling
papers.abstract: We investigate when a Poincaré inequality forces the underlying measure to be doubling, with particular attention to the space \(X\) controlling the oscillation. We identify \(L\log L\) as the sharp threshold: under a natural local growth condition on the measure, doubling is forced precisely when \(L\log L(0,1)\not\hookrightarrow X\). We also obtain a doubling criterion under a weaker geometric assumption when the oscillation norm is sufficiently stronger than \(L\log L\). We show that this threshold is sharp in every fixed Euclidean dimension, using a dimension-free local \(L\log L\)-Poincaré inequality for log-concave measures and non-doubling Gaussian examples. We then turn to infinite-dimensional spaces, where doubling is impossible for the measures under consideration. Nevertheless, the \(L\log L\)-Poincaré inequality continues to hold, and we establish sharp characterizations for infinite product models, Gaussian measures on Hilbert spaces under power-type small-ball estimates, and Wiener measure with the uniform norm.

papers.title: A geometric lower bound for the clamped plate eigenvalue problem in low dimensions and extensions
papers.abstract: We show that the spectrum of the Dirichlet-biLaplacian can be quantitatively bounded from below in terms of the inradius only, for a general open set in dimensions $2$ and $3$. For the same dimensions, we also extend this result to fractional powers $s$ of the Laplacian, with $N/2<s<2$. The resulting estimate comes with a constant having the correct asymptotic behavior as $s$ approaches the two endpoints $N/2$ and $2$. The proofs exploit capacitary techniques in the vein of Maz'ya.

papers.title: Quantum state texture of maximal-resource Fourier states under Hawking radiation
papers.abstract: Quantum state texture (QST) is a recently proposed quantum resource that characterizes the nonuniformity of a density matrix in a given computational basis. In the resource theory of QST, the Fourier states f_k are maximally resourceful states, attaining the maximum QST measure. We study the QST behavior of three maximally resourceful states in a two-mode Dirac field under Hawking radiation from a Schwarzschild black hole, using a fidelity-based measure. We consider three cases: only mode B undergoes radiation, only mode A undergoes radiation, and both modes undergo radiation simultaneously. Our results show that for single-mode radiation, if the mode unaffected by radiation is orthogonal to the single-mode textureless state, the QST of the overall output state remains maximal and is independent of the Hawking temperature; we call this phenomenon orthogonality protection. When both modes undergo radiation simultaneously, orthogonality protection vanishes, and the QST of all three Fourier states decreases with increasing Hawking temperature. Notably, the QST measure of f_3 under two-mode radiation is higher than that under only mode B radiation, indicating that QST can be redistributed among modes: QST gained by one mode under radiation can partially compensate for QST lost by the other. We further provide a general resource-theoretic explanation of orthogonality protection, showing that this phenomenon is independent of the specific form of the QST measure. These results reveal how QST degrades under Hawking radiation and provide a new perspective on the redistribution of quantum resources in black hole backgrounds.

papers.title: Schatten--Lorentz properties of commutators with matrix weights
papers.abstract: We study the membership of commutators $[b,T]$ of Calderón--Zygmund operators in the Schatten--Lorentz classes in the matrix-weighted setting. Working on a space of homogeneous type $(X,ρ,μ)$ with a matrix $A_2$ weight $W$, we characterise, for $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $q\in[1,\infty)$, the Schatten--Lorentz norm $\|[b,T]\|_{S^{p,q}(L^2(W))}$ in terms of an oscillation (Besov-type) norm $\|b\|_{\mathrm{Osc}^{p,q}}$ of the symbol: for all $p\in(1,\infty)$, finiteness of $\|b\|_{\mathrm{Osc}^{p,q}}$ is necessary; and for $p>p(η)$, where $p(η)$ depends on the regularity of the kernel of $T$ and a dimensional parameter of the space, the two-sided estimate $\|[b,T]\|_{S^{p,q}(L^2(W))}\approx\|b\|_{\mathrm{Osc}^{p,q}}$ holds. Extending a recent unified framework for unweighted and scalar-weighted versions of such results by one of us to the matrix-weighted setting, our approach combines the dyadic representation of singular integral operators with the nearly weakly orthogonal (NWO) sequences of Rochberg and Semmes.

papers.title: Remarks on ultrafilters exponentiation
papers.abstract: Recently, two exponentiations of ultrafilters have been introduced in [7]. We rephrase them in nonstandard terms, and use the nonstandard formulations to characterize some of their properties. We also study their relations with divisibility by introducing factor-picking functions and highly exponential ultrafilters.

papers.title: Some complete $ω$-powers of a one-counter language in the difference hierarchy
papers.abstract: Fix a finite alphabet $Σ$ having at least two letters, and natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$. We denote by $D_n(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$ the class of differences of $n$ subsets of the Cantor space $Σ^ω$ in $\mathbfΠ^0_k$, and by $\checked{D}_n(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$ the class of complements of sets in $D_n(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$. We prove, for any natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$, the existence of a finite alphabet $Σ$ having at least two letters and a finitary language $U_{n,k}$ over $Σ$ accepted by a one-counter automaton such that the $ω$-power $$U_{n,k}^\infty:=\{ w_0w_1\cdots\inΣ^ω\mid\forall i\inω~~w_i\in U_{n,k}\}$$ is $D_{2n-1}(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$-complete. We also prove a conditional result for the dual classes $\checked{D}\_{2n}(\mathbfΠ^0\_k)$: under the assumption that there exists a finitary language $V_{n,3}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $ω$-power $V_{n,3}^\infty$ is $\checked{D}_{2n}(\mathbfΠ^0_3)$-complete, there would also exist, for any integer $k>3$, a finitary language $V_{n,k}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $ω$-power $V_{n,k}^\infty$ is $\checked{D}_{2n}(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$-complete. Finally we add another conditionnal result about Wadge degrees of rational $\mathbfΔ^0_2$ omega powers, which completes the recent results of [FGL26].

papers.title: On the Weyl tube formula for nonlocal perimeters
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the nonlocal perimeter of tubular neighbourhoods. For a closed $C^{1,1}$ submanifold of Euclidean space, we show that a suitable rescaling of the nonlocal perimeter of its tube converges to an explicit constant times the Hausdorff measure of the submanifold. The constant is the fractional perimeter of the unit ball in the codimension of the submanifold. For finite point sets, we obtain an exact tube formula in terms of a generalised hypergeometric function. In contrast with the classical Weyl formula, this expansion has infinitely many terms, contains both noninteger and integer powers of the tubular radius, and has coefficients that depend on the relative positions of the points rather than only on their intrinsic geometry. We also establish a point-set expansion for general analytic kernels.

papers.title: Edge and spectral conditions for rainbow bipancyclicity in bipartite graph collections
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{G}=\{G_1,\dots,G_{2n}\}$ be a collection of not necessarily distinct balanced bipartite graphs of order $2n$ with a common bipartition $V=(X,Y)$. A cycle $C$ with $V(C)\subseteq V$ and $|E(C)|\leq 2n$ is called \emph{rainbow} in $\mathbf{G}$, if there exists an injection $φ\colon E(C)\to [2n]$ such that $e\in E(G_{φ(e)})$ for each $e\in E(C)$. The graph collection $\mathbf{G}$ is said to be \emph{rainbow bipancyclic} if it contains a rainbow cycle of every even length from 4 to $2n$. In this paper, we show that if $e(G_i)\ge n^2-n+1$ for each $i\in[2n]$, then $\mathbf{G}$ is rainbow bipancyclic unless $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{2n}\cong B_{n}^1$, where $B_{n}^1$ is the graph obtained from $K_{n,n}$ by deleting all edges in its one subgraph $K_{n-1,1}$. As a corollary, we obtain that if $ρ(G_i)\ge ρ(B_{n}^1)>\sqrt{n(n-1)}$ for each $i\in[2n]$, then $\mathbf{G}$ is rainbow bipancyclic unless $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{2n}\cong B_{n}^1$, which strengthens Theorem $5$ of [Electron. J. Combin., \textbf{33}(3)(2026), \#P3.29] and Theorem $1.6$ of [Linear Algebra Appl., \textbf{743}(2026), 250--270] from rainbow Hamiltonicity to rainbow bipancyclicity. We also characterize all bipartite graph collections that are not rainbow bipancyclic under the condition $ρ(G_i)\ge \sqrt{n(n-1)}$ for each $i\in[2n]$

papers.title: Axioms and internal rigidity of spectral duality structures
papers.abstract: Spectral duality structures (SDS) explain why a distinguished family of initial distributions makes the absorption probabilities of resetting processes insensitive to the resetting mechanism. Here we study their axioms. We prove that the six defining conditions are mutually independent and determine what each one contributes. The key tool is a structure theorem valid for an arbitrary permutation and an arbitrary positive weight: every insensitive distribution is supported on a union of cycles balanced at a common level, and the level of a cycle is fixed by the geometric mean of the weight on it. From it, positivity selects the admissible root, the constant orbit product is equivalent to the existence of an insensitive distribution of full support, and the involution is equivalent to the response rank being equal to the number of free weight parameters. Without the duality relation, insensitivity of a single distribution is cheap and generically isolated; duality turns it into structural neutrality of the separatrix. The full-rank condition splits into two layers: a weaker condition is equivalent to maximal response rank, while full rank also excludes insensitivity at any other level. We then show that a single SDS is internally rigid: compatible semigroup structures force a constant weight, compatible abelian group structures obey a precise arithmetic condition, congruences form a simple lattice, and the automorphism group is computed explicitly. Finally, the axioms do not determine the orientation of the response; in the two-site case we give the exact condition under which the geometric and analytic sign criteria agree.

papers.title: The rich-neighbor chromatic index is linear in the maximum degree
papers.abstract: An edge of a multigraph is rich with respect to a proper edge-coloring if all the edges adjacent to it receive mutually distinct colors, and a proper edge-coloring is a rich-neighbor coloring if every non-isolated edge has a rich edge adjacent to it. The least number of colors in such a coloring is the rich-neighbor chromatic index chi'_rn(G). So far it was studied for subcubic graphs only, and multigraphs of larger maximum degree are considered here for the first time. The only upper bound valid in general was the quadratic one inherited from the strong chromatic index, while a single rich edge already requires 2D-1 colors in a D-regular graph, where D denotes the maximum degree. We give an upper linear bound chi'_rn(G) <= 6D-8 which holds for every loopless multigraph G with D >= 3, and we show that a coloring realizing this bound can be found in polynomial time. Consequently chi'_rn(G) = Theta(D). For D-regular graphs with D >= 3 the lower bound is 2D-1, and the upper bound is 5D-8. The bound 5D-8 holds more generally for every multigraph with D >= 3 which has a dominating P_{>=3}-system, and we characterize these multigraphs: such a system exists if and only if k_2(G-T) <= 2|T| holds for every set T of vertices, where k_2 counts the components on two vertices. In particular the bound holds for every graph with 3 <= D <= 4d-4, where d denotes the minimum degree. The paper is concluded with a conjecture on the tight upper bound on chi'_rn(G).

papers.title: Depth-zero local Langlands via shtukas in mixed characteristic
papers.abstract: Assuming a smoothness property for mixed-characteristic shtuka spaces and hyperbolic localization for twisted sheaves, we determine the inertial restriction of the Fargues-Scholze $L$-parameter for irreducible depth-zero representations. Let $E$ be a non-archimedean local field of residue characteristic $p$, let $G$ be an unramified connected reductive group over $E$, and let $π$ be an irreducible smooth depth-zero representation of $G(E)$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{\ell}$ where $\ell$ is a prime number which does not divide $p|π_0Z(G)|$. Let $\varphi_π^{\operatorname{FS}}$ be the Fargues-Scholze $L$-parameter associated to $π$. We describe the restriction of $\varphi_π^{\operatorname{FS}}$ to the inertia subgroup in terms of Deligne-Lusztig theory. We prove this by computing the inertia action on the cohomology of shtuka spaces with depth-zero level structure. As an application, we prove that the Fargues--Scholze $L$-parameters agree with DeBacker--Reeder $L$-parameters over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{\ell}$.

papers.title: Tempered fractional Laplacian: Boundary regularity
papers.abstract: We study the boundary regularity of solutions for the tempered fractional Laplacian \[ (-Δ)^s_λu=f \quad \text{in }Ω, \qquad u=0 \quad \text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ, \] where \(0<s<1\), \(λ>0\), and \(Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a bounded Lipschitz domain satisfying the exterior ball condition. The tempered operator is defined by \[ (-Δ)^s_λu(x) = c_{n,s}\operatorname{P.V.} \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \frac{u(x)-u(y)}{|x-y|^{n+2s}} e^{-λ|x-y|}\,dy, \] which was originally proposed in [Koponen, Phys. Rev. E (1995), 1197-1199]. % Exponential tempering preserves the leading singularity of % the kernel but destroys its homogeneity, preventing a direct % application of classical boundary regularity estimates. % Extending these estimates [Ros-Oton and Serra, J. Math. Pures Appl. (2014), 275--302] to the tempered setting therefore % requires overcoming the difficulties caused by the loss % of scale invariance. By decomposing the operator into the classical fractional Laplacian and the correction operator \(\mathcal Q_λ^s\), and combining approximation, localization, and iterative arguments with interpolation inequalities, we establish the global estimate \[ \|u\|_{C^s(\mathbb{R}^n)} \le C\|f\|_{L^\infty(Ω)}. \] For more regular data, we derive interior and boundary-weighted Schauder estimates. In particular, under suitable regularity assumptions on \(f\), these estimates yield \[ |D^νu(x)| \le C\,δ(x)^{s-|ν|}, \quad |ν| > 0, \] where \(ν\) is a multi-index and \(δ(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,\partialΩ)\). These bounds quantify the possible growth of higher-order derivatives near the boundary and provide a regularity foundation for numerical error analysis of the tempered problem.

papers.title: Radial pressureless Euler flow: structure and stability of absorption at the origin
papers.abstract: We study absorption at the origin in radial pressureless Euler flow in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq2$. For rotation-invariant nonnegative locally finite initial mass and bounded radial initial velocity vanishing at the origin, we prove global existence and uniqueness in a full-space radial entropy class with a one-sided Lipschitz bound and an initial kinetic-energy trace. Absorption is permanent, including retention of any initial origin atom. For finite positive mass with finite second moment, a Lagrangian projection representation characterizes the absorbed mass and its left limits at positive times through extreme minimizers of a free-position primitive. We derive a radial scalar momentum balance with a nonnegative Stieltjes boundary impulse measure. The minimum value of the same primitive yields a weighted Stieltjes identity equating accumulated time-weighted impulse with the integral of initial radii over absorbed labels, valid also for jumps and singular continuous absorption; the boundary impulse measure and the absorption measure are mutually absolutely continuous on $(0,\infty)$. For such finite-mass data with common total mass, strong $L^2$ convergence of initial quantiles and Lagrangian velocities, together with convergence of initial origin masses, yields convergence of absorbed mass at continuity times of the limiting absorption and local weak convergence of absorption measures on $(0,\infty)$. Finally, even with a fixed smooth initial radial probability density, every probability measure compactly supported in $(0,\infty)$ can be realized as the absorption measure by choosing a bounded radial initial velocity; in particular, purely singular continuous absorption occurs.

papers.title: Biconservative hypersurfaces in Euclidean Spaces
papers.abstract: An isometric immersion $X: Σ^n \longrightarrow \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ is biharmonic (BHH) if $Δ^2 X = 0$, i.e., if $ΔH =0$, where $Δ$ and $H$ are the metric Laplacian and the mean curvature vector field of $Σ^n$ respectively. More generally, biconservative hypersurfaces (BCHs) are isometric immersions for which only the tangential part of the biharmonic equation vanishes. BCHs are first described and then constructed.

papers.title: Lens spaces that cannot be obtained by two integral surgeries
papers.abstract: In this article, we demonstrate that there exists an infinite family of lens spaces L(p,q) that cannot be obtained from the 3-sphere by two integral surgeries. The first such lens space in our family is L(177,29).

papers.title: Taming Nonconvexity with Epigraph Lifting
papers.abstract: We consider inverse problems regularized by a trained neural network with \emph{convex activations} and \emph{unrestricted weights}. The resulting optimization problem is generally nonconvex, and gradient-based methods may converge to poor local minima. We introduce a \emph{penalized epigraph lifting} of the network and show that the lifted problem admits a \emph{difference-of-convex (DC) decomposition}. For Lipschitz continuous activations, we establish \emph{finite exactness}: the original objective is recovered exactly at a finite and explicitly computable penalty threshold $\barρ$. Building on this structure, we propose \emph{H-DC} (Homotopic DC), a homotopic scheme that solves a sequence of DC subproblems with increasing $ρ$, warm-starting each level from the previous solution. Numerical experiments on synthetic problems, a manifold denoiser regularizer, and image inpainting with a learned Mumford--Shah regularizer show that H-DC consistently escapes poor local minima and reaches solutions with lower objective values than gradient-based methods from the same initialization.

papers.title: The Inviscid Limit of Viscous Burgers through Shock Formation and Development
papers.abstract: We study the inviscid limit of the one-dimensional viscous Burgers equation from smooth initial data through nondegenerate shock formation and subsequent shock development. Chaturvedi and Graham \cite{CG} obtained sharp estimates of order $ν^{1/4}$ up to the shock-formation time. We extend their analysis beyond this time, comparing the viscous solution with the inviscid entropy solution evolving from the same initial data. With the shock-formation time normalized to $t=0$, we prove a pointwise error bound on a fixed interval $0\leq t \leq \bar{\varepsilon}$, where $\bar{\varepsilon}>0$ is independent of the viscosity $ν$. The bound consists of a term of order $ν^{1/4}$ and an exponentially localized contribution originating from the viscous shock layer. The proof is based on matching an outer expansion, an inner expansion near the formation point, and a viscous shock-profile expansion. Combined with the results of Chaturvedi and Graham, this yields a quantitative description of the inviscid limit from the initial time through the development of the young shock.

papers.title: Classification of Projective Models of $K3$-surfaces
papers.abstract: Extending the methods previously established for plane sextics and quartic surfaces, we develop a unified and systematic framework for the equisingular deformation classification of projective models of $K3$-surfaces of arbitrary polarization. We treat all polarizations of degree $2n$ with $n\le 4$, including the higher-degree cases of sextic surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^{4}$ and octic surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^{5}$. The computational machinery developed here is degree-independent and provides a complete tool for enumerating and distinguishing the deformation classes arising from singular projective models of $K3$-surfaces. This framework lays the foundation for future investigations in higher degrees, particularly the geometry of equisingular strata, extremal configurations, real structures.

papers.title: Stable reduction and large Nielsen orbits on generalized Markoff surfaces
papers.abstract: We establish lower bounds on the orbit cardinalities of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ on the $\mathbb{F}_p$-points of the generalized Markoff surfaces given by $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xyz = τ+2$. We show that outside of the reductions of a certain exceptional finite set of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$-points found by Dubrovin and Mazzocco, every orbit has cardinality $\ge p$.
