Together with a recent result of Nathaniel Kingsbury-Neuschotz, this establishes, for all but finitely many primes $p$, the classification conjectures of McCullough-Wanderley (2013), and gives a complete classification of the connected components of the Hurwitz stack of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of elliptic curves, only branched above the origin. This extends earlier work of Bourgain-Gamburd-Sarnak and the author in the Markoff case $τ= -2$. Our method studies certain noncongruence modular curves attached to a $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$-orbit. These modular curves parametrize elliptic curves with a $\text{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-cover. We use this moduli interpretation to show that the noncongruence modular curves involved have bad reduction, as a cover of the $j$-line, at some place above $p$. This implies that the degree of the cover is $\ge p$, which translates into the desired bound on orbits. Key inputs include a result of Bouw-Wewers on bad reduction of three-point $\text{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of the projective line, and the general stable reduction theory of Henrio, Obus, Raynaud, and Wewers.

papers.title: Equilibria and consensus in discrete-time opinion dynamics with mixed weighted-averaging and weighted-median mechanisms
papers.abstract: Opinion dynamics models relate interpersonal influence to consensus or persistent disagreement. We study a discrete-time model combining weighted-average and weighted-median updates on a fixed directed network. Individuals update synchronously with possibly different adjustment coefficients. We characterize equilibria through local balance conditions and opinion level sets, and establish convergence to a Lyapunov-stable equilibrium using nonexpansiveness and Krasnosel'skii--Mann theory. We define type-dependent cohesive sets: each weighted-average member assigns all its weight to the set, whereas each weighted-median member assigns at least one half. Consensus is reached from every initial condition if and only if no two such sets are disjoint. Otherwise, an open set of initial conditions leads to persistent disagreement. Replacing weighted-median individuals by weighted-average individuals preserves consensus whenever it is already guaranteed for all initial conditions. Four numerical studies examine the number and locations of weighted-average individuals. The frequency of reaching a prescribed consensus tolerance is nondecreasing with their fraction in the sampled ensembles, but individual realizations need not follow this trend.

papers.title: Reverse Hölder Class and Two-Parameter Good-$λ$ Inequality over Hausdorff Content
papers.abstract: Classical harmonic analysis is built upon Lebesgue (or more general) measure. Such a framework is remarkably successful for sets of full ambient dimension, but becomes intrinsically insensitive to lower-dimensional geometry: curves, surfaces, and more generally fractal subsets of \(\mathbb R^n\) with zero \(n\)-dimensional Lebesgue measure. In contrast, Hausdorff content provides a dimension-sensitive notion of size for lower-dimensional sets or fractal sets, but harmonic analysis in this setting is still largely limited to maximal operators. In this paper, we establish a weighted two-parameter good-\(λ\) inequality under Hausdorff content setting, providing a route toward other general operators from maximal operators over Hausdorff content. To do this, we firstly identify an appropriate reverse Hölder class $\mathcal R\mathcal H_{q,δ}$ associated with Hausdorff content, and then prove the self-improving property of $\mathcal R\mathcal H_{q,δ}$ by establishing the fundamental equivalence between reverse Hölder weights and capacitary Muckenhoupt weights. As direct applications, we obtain weighted Fefferman--Stein inequality and some boundedness on general operators over Hausdorff content. The methodology developed in this paper, even when reduced to the Lebesgue measure case, also provide novel insights, which shows that the good-\(λ\) principle is not intrinsically tied to an underlying measure, but can extended to a non-additive framework.

papers.title: Effective shadowing of transition maps for a Hamiltonian saddle-center-center equilibrium
papers.abstract: We introduce a general methodology to construct globally unstable trajectories near the normally hyperbolic invariant manifold (NHIM) of a saddle-center-center Hamiltonian equilibrium. The proposed approach builds upon the classical geometric mechanism of searching for trajectories near heteroclinic connections between invariant tori of the NHIM. The main ingredient is the Birkhoff normal form near the NHIM, which allows us to control the dynamics of the hyperbolic and center components. We construct transition maps on the NHIM that encode the dynamics along heteroclinic connections. By combining the transition maps with the inner dynamics, given by the restriction of the Hamiltonian flow to the NHIM, we show that these connections can be efficiently (in terms of the travel time) shadowed by true trajectories of the full Hamiltonian system. Finally, the efficiency of this methodology is illustrated in the case of the NHIM associated to the libration point $L_1$ of the Spatial Restricted 3-Body Problem (SR3BP) for the Sun-Earth system.

papers.title: Ideal quotients of $n$-exact categories
papers.abstract: In this paper, we extend the notion of a removable subcategory to $n$-exact categories, and prove that an ideal quotient by a subcategory of projective-injectives inherits an $n$-exact structure from the original category if and only if the subcategory is removable. In the Frobenius case, the quotient remains Frobenius, and the stable $(n+2)$-angulated categories are equivalent. We give a sufficient condition for a subcategory of projective-injectives to be removable. We also show that the ideal quotient construction is compatible with cluster tilting. Finally, we apply the construction to $2$-cluster tilting subcategories of the category of ACM bundles on a Geigle--Lenzing projective plane, obtaining quotients for both natural and relative $2$-exact structures.

papers.title: Boundedness and exponential stabilization in a degenerate migration-consumption system with logistic damping
papers.abstract: We study the no-flux problem for a taxis-type migration-consumption system with logistic damping in a bounded planar domain, where the motility function \(φ\) vanishes at zero and degenerates algebraically of order \(α\ge1\). We prove uniform boundedness in \(L^\infty(Ω)\times W^{1,\infty}(Ω)\) for every fixed damping coefficient \(b>0\), without any smallness assumption on the initial data, thus improving the previous \(L^2\)-boundedness results. For \(α>1\), we further prove that the solution converges exponentially to the spatially homogeneous state \((a/b,0)\), with an explicit admissible rate. The proof combines a weighted Gagliardo--Nirenberg type inequality adapted to the degeneracy with the dissipative structure of the signal equation. Therefore logistic damping drives the system toward homogeneity, despite the loss of uniform elliptic regularization.

papers.title: Dynamical generalizations of the two-point Chowla conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the values of the Liouville function become asymptotically uncorrelated at consecutive natural numbers. Recently, the two-point case is resolved by OpenAI. In 2026, Charamaras and Richter conjectured a generalization of the Chowla conjecture to the asymptotic independence of the consecutive prime Omega functions. In this article, we prove the two-point case of their conjecture. As a consequence, we obtain a dynamical generalization of the two-point Chowla conjecture.

papers.title: QBFF: Deep Quantum Bottleneck for Automatic Speaker Verification Anti-Spoofing
papers.abstract: A central goal of quantum machine learning is to identify applications in which small quantum circuits can improve task performance while remaining executable on real hardware. We investigate deepfake (synthetic) speech detection, a largely unexplored application in this area, where reliable confidence scores are as important as discrimination performance because deployment decisions are made at fixed thresholds and overconfident errors can be costly. We introduce QBFF, which routes a compressed speech representation through a small 8-qubit variational circuit (VQC) used as a drop-in bottleneck, with a matched classical bottleneck as the control. The quantum circuit yields better-calibrated confidence in most matched comparisons, including out-of-distribution evaluation, though the downstream deployment-cost benefit is model-dependent. We then run the same circuit on a real IBM quantum processor. To our knowledge, this is the first anti-spoofing pipeline to run on a QPU; hardware execution demonstrates feasibility, with lower subset EER and $C_{llr}$ but higher mean actDCF than the matched classical reference. Together, these results show that hardware-executable quantum bottlenecks can improve score reliability, with gains that vary by evaluation setting.

papers.title: $\mathcal{D}$-Pullback Measure Attractors of McKean-Vlasov Stochastic Lattice Wave Equations
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the pullback measure attractor for a non-autonomous distribution-dependent stochastic lattice wave equation with nonlinear noise on $\mathbb{Z}$. We establish well-posedness in the energy space $\ell^{2}\times\ell^{2}$ and show that the solution generates a continuous non-autonomous dynamical system on $\mathcal{P}_{4}(\ell^{2}\times\ell^{2})$, which possesses a unique pullback measure attractor $\mathcal{A}$. Furthermore, we prove the convergence of the attractor $\mathcal{A}^{\varepsilon}$ as $\varepsilon\to 0^{+}$ to the attractor of the corresponding distribution-independent limit system.

papers.title: Persistence diagrams of finite topological spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we apply persistent homology to study finite topological spaces by associating persistence diagrams with their elements through the furtherness function. This approach enables us to classify elements according to their topological evolution within the space. We further establish a bottleneck stability theorem showing that the bottleneck distance between the persistence diagrams associated with two elements is bounded above by their mutual furtherness.

papers.title: Large deviation principles for 2D stochastic $g$-Navier--Stokes equations on unbounded channel-like domains
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the large deviation principle for 2D stochastic $g$-Navier--Stokes equations driven by multiplicative noise and defined on an unbounded channel-like domain. We first prove the existence and uniqueness of probabilistically strong solutions for the stochastic equation under small noise perturbations by means of the local monotonicity method. Subsequently, we show the well-posedness of solutions to the corresponding control equation and the convergence in distribution of the solutions for the stochastic equation as the noise intensity tends to zero. Finally, we establish the Freidlin-Wentzell type large deviation principle for the solutions of the stochastic equation by using the weak convergence method. To overcome the lack of compactness of Sobolev embedding on unbounded domains, we employ a scalar stream function together with a truncation technique to derive uniform tail estimates for the solutions of the control equation.

papers.title: Benchmarking a randomized quantum algorithm for estimating expectation values of molecular observables
papers.abstract: Randomized quantum algorithms for the estimation of expectation values of molecular observables offer a promising route to early fault-tolerant quantum advantage by trading circuit depth for an increased number of samples. However, this begs the question whether the resulting measurement overhead remains feasible for industrially relevant molecular systems. In this work, we benchmark the randomized sampling algorithm of Wang et al. [1] through numerical simulations on a hydrogen molecule and resource estimates for various active spaces of the cytochrome P450, an industry-relevant system in the pharmaceutical industry. Our numerical simulations reveal that the analytical error bounds significantly overestimate the actual sampling error, whereas the analytical bound on the required imaginary evolution time is comparatively tight, exceeding a direct DMRG estimate by roughly 44% for the active space where the comparison is feasible. The measurement overhead nevertheless remains prohibitively high: even for the smallest active spaces, the expectation-value estimation alone requires around 1010 samples, scaling to beyond 1015 for the largest active spaces considered. These results suggest that substantial improvements in measurement strategies or algorithmic scaling are necessary before randomized early-fault-tolerant algorithms become competitive for industrial quantum chemistry applications.

papers.title: Spectral stability of resonant Y-solitons for the KP-II equation
papers.abstract: The KP-II equation was introduced by Kadomtsev and Petviashvili to explain the transverse stability of line solitary waves in shallow water. Using Darboux transformations, we prove the spectral stability of Y-shaped line solitons in an exponentially weighted space that captures the amount of waves receding behind the line solitons. We show that the spectrum of the linearized operator consists of the continuous spectrum of the zero background together with three residual spectral domains whose boundaries contain continuous spectra associated with the constituent line solitons. Exploiting the analytic dependence of the pairings with adjoint eigenfunctions on the spectral parameters, we prove that the orthogonality conditions associated with all adjoint eigenfunctions can be reduced to orthogonality conditions against three families of adjoint continuous eigenfunctions. Moreover, we investigate linear stability of Y-solitons in a subspace satisfying orthogonality conditions against adjoint continuous eigenfunctions associated with outgoing modulations along each line soliton constituting the Y-soliton.

papers.title: Four-dimensional almost-Einstein manifolds with circulant structures
papers.abstract: This paper considers a four-dimensional Riemannian manifold with an additional circulant tensor structure $Q$. We prove that such a manifold is almost-Einstein if the curvature tensor preserves the action of the structure on the last two arguments. Additionally, we examine an associated Riemannian product manifold $(M, g, Q)$ where $P=Q^{2}$, deriving explicit expressions for the curvature tensor in terms of the metric and the product structure. The sectional and Ricci curvatures of these manifolds are determined using special bases generated by the images of a given vector under the structure $Q$. Finally, we construct a non-trivial example of a four-dimensional locally product manifold by embedding a four-dimensional hypersurface into a ten-dimensional Euclidean space.

papers.title: Track objects in cubical presheaf automata
papers.abstract: Using the formalism of presheaf automata, we introduce new classes of automata for modelling concurrency that extend higher-dimensional automata and symmetric higher-dimensional automata. We study their languages and characterise these languages in terms of posetal cospans.

papers.title: Pathfinder-BP: A Low-Latency Recursive Decoder for Topological Codes
papers.abstract: We propose Pathfinder-BP, a recursive decoder for topological quantum codes that combines belief propagation with controlled bit-flipping. An initial BP pass identifies and permanently fixes high-confidence errors. Upon convergence failure, the decoder recursively explores alternative error patterns by tentatively flipping low-confidence variables. On surface codes, Pathfinder-BP achieves a noise threshold and logical error rate comparable to minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM). A crucial advantage of Pathfinder-BP is its highly parallelizable structure, which yields a worst-case decoding latency quasi-linear in the code distance, making it a suitable candidate for low-latency hardware implementation.

papers.title: Double Bruhat cells in symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: This paper studies the closures of the double Bruhat cells of symmetric spacess in its equivariant embeddings. We call them large double Bruhat varieties. Our aim is to establish the double Bruhat stratification as a natural setting for extending the geometry of Richardson varieties to symmetric spaces. For the wonderful compactification of the associated adjoint symmetric space, we show their scheme-theoretic intersections with the unique closed orbit are reduced unions of projected Richardson varieties. This connection with Richardson geometry on partial flag varieties supports large double Bruhat varieties as a natural class of subvarieties in symmetric-space embeddings. In positive characteristic, we prove that every equivariant embedding admits a Frobenius splitting compatible with all large double Bruhat varieties and all boundary divisors. These varieties are strongly F-regular, and globally F-regular when the ambient embedding is projective. In characteristic zero, they are of strongly F-regular type, and of globally F-regular type in the projective case; in particular, they are normal, Cohen-Macaulay, and have rational singularities.

papers.title: An algebraic multiscale framework for two-level overlapping Schwarz preconditioners
papers.abstract: The robustness of two-level overlapping additive Schwarz (OAS) preconditioners for highly heterogeneous elliptic problems hinges on the choice of the coarse space. We propose an algebraic multiscale (AM) coarse space built from the system matrix alone through an algebraic formulation of the multiscale finite element method (MsFEM). The coarse basis functions are energy-minimizing extensions of the solutions of reduced boundary condition (RBC) problems on the subdomain interface, so that coefficient variations along the interface enter the coarse space. By posing the RBC problems on slabs that extend the interface, the construction also applies to general unstructured domain decompositions. Embedding the AM formulation in an energy-minimizing framework extends it to linear elasticity, and we show that existing condition number bounds for OAS with MsFEM coarse spaces carry over to the algebraic setting. For problems with high coefficient inclusions on the coarse nodes, the AM iteration count and condition number are unaffected by increasing the contrast. In 3D scalar diffusion with log-normal coefficients, AM needs about as many iterations as the generalized Dryja--Smith--Widlund (GDSW) coarse space, while solving a coarse problem ten times smaller. For linear elasticity, omitting the coarse basis functions associated with the rotational rigid body modes yields a fully algebraic coarse space that still scales well for homogeneous problems.

papers.title: NP-hardness of additive approximation for generalized Turán problems
papers.abstract: For a fixed graph $T$ and a fixed nonempty family $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs, let $\operatorname{ex}(G, T, \mathcal{F})$ denote the maximum number of copies of $T$ in an $\mathcal{F}$-free subgraph of a graph $G$. Alon and Shikhelman~[Algorithmica, 2022] conjectured that if $e(T)> 0$ and no member of $\mathcal{F}$ is a subgraph of a blow-up of $T$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$, approximating $\operatorname{ex}(G, T, \mathcal{F})$ within an additive error $n^{v(T)-\varepsilon}$ is NP-hard for an input graph $G$ on $n$ vertices. The previously established general cases for this conjecture include $\operatorname{ex}(G, K_2, \mathcal{F})$ by Alon, Shapira and Sudakov~[Ann. of Math., 2009], and $\operatorname{ex}(G, K_m, K_k)$ by Alon and Shikhelman. In this paper, we confirm this conjecture for every bipartite graph $T$ and every clique $T$. Our reductions use iterative leaf additions, symmetric rooted extensions and random transversals to encode the maximum number of edges in a $(k-1)$-colorable subgraph of $G$, where $k=\min_{F\in \mathcal{F}}χ(F)$.

papers.title: The $(km,kn)$-square paths theorem
papers.abstract: For positive integers $k,m,n$ with $\gcd(m,n)=1$, we prove a $(km,kn)$-square paths theorem: the symmetric function $(-1)^{k-1}\frac{[km]_q}{[k]_q}p_k[-MX^{m,n}]\cdot1$ is a weighted sum over $(km,kn)$-preference functions. This proves a corrected form of the conjecture of Iraci, Pagaria, Paolini, and Vanden Wyngaerd and generalizes the square paths theorem of Sergel. We encode preference functions by row strict tableaux and closed walks on a set of states, compare them with parking functions for each value of the touch statistic, and apply Mellit's compositional $(km,kn)$-shuffle theorem. Finally, we establish a fall Delta square theorem conjectured by Iraci, Pagaria, and Paolini.

papers.title: Cyclic Kronecker Fourier Transforms, Weber Norms, and Rogers-Ramanujan Singular Values
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be an imaginary quadratic field with fundamental discriminant $D=-5n$, where $n>0$ is odd, and cyclic ideal class group $\text{Cl}(K)=\langle g\rangle\simeq C_{4M}$. Assume that the ramified prime class above $5$ is the unique involution $g^{2M}$. For the Kronecker eta invariant \[ F(A)=\frac{|η(z_A)|^2}{\sqrt{a_A}}, \] where $z_A$ and $a_A$ arise from a positive definite quadratic form representing the ideal class $A$, we show that the logarithms of the mirror ratios \[ R_j=\frac{F(g^{2M-j})}{F(g^j)},\qquad 0\le j<M, \] are related by an explicit discrete cosine transform to the odd class-character Hecke $L(1)$-values. A single level-$5$ generalized-Weber orbit realizes all of these mirrors. Combining Fourier nonvanishing, lower-power Weber class invariants and a ray-class cancellation argument, we prove \[ \mathbb{Q}(R_j)=H^{\langle c\rangle},\qquad R_j^{σ^{2M}}=R_j^{-1},\qquad \mathbb{Q}(R_j+R_j^{-1})=H^{\langle c,σ^{2M}\rangle}. \] Here $H$ is the Hilbert class field, $c$ denotes complex conjugation, and $σ$ corresponds to $g$ under the Artin map. Consequently \[ [\mathbb{Q}(R_j):\mathbb{Q}]=4M,\qquad [\mathbb{Q}(R_j+R_j^{-1}):\mathbb{Q}]=2M, \] and the latter degree becomes $M$ over the real genus field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt5)$. Thus the degree pattern $2^r,2^{r-1},2^{r-2}$ in the cyclic $2$-power hierarchy is a specialization of a uniform $C_{4M}$ theorem. We give exact low-class-number evaluations and certified computations at $D=-895,-3295,-8495$, separating respectively four, eight and sixteen non-genus Hecke $L(1)$-values and producing corresponding alternating Rogers-Ramanujan singular values. Classical mixed modular equations then give ordinary Rogers--Ramanujan companions at the same arguments.

papers.title: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
papers.abstract: An isolated quantum system evolves reversibly, yet a small subsystem can lose nearly all information about its initial state. Conserved quantities may retain some of this information, depending on how strongly they overlap with local observables. Here we consider a subsystem in an arbitrary initial state coupled to a maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square equilibration error, maximised over window origins, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation, with the stationary part subtracted. A correlation record over a finite interval therefore controls the equilibration error in every interval of the same length. The result allows arbitrary degeneracies of energies and gaps. We apply it to two static Hamiltonian families. For fixed spin subsystems in the one-particle sector of a bounded-range periodic clock, fixed-accuracy thermalisation is guaranteed on windows that grow only slightly faster than linearly with system size, despite exponentially small positive energies. A random commuting model with logarithmic interaction range retains an extensive set of conserved observables. Its expected mean-square error is bounded by a finite-size term and an inverse-time term. The inverse-time dependence is unavoidable because of the initial transient. These examples show how local relaxation can coexist with exact conservation laws and a finely spaced spectrum.

papers.title: Generalizing Green's Syzygy Theorems to Symmetric Products of Curves
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$, and let $T_{n,L}$ denote the tautological line bundle on its $n$-th symmetric product $C_n$. We prove effective vanishing criteria for Koszul cohomology $K_{p,q}(C_n,T_{n,B};T_{n,L})$, extending two classical theorems of Mark Green. The main ingredient is a weight-one vanishing theorem proved by induction on $n$, using a filtration of the kernel bundle of $T_{n,L}$ to reduce the required cohomological vanishings to lower symmetric products. As a consequence, when $g\geq1$ and $n\geq2$, $T_{n,L}$ satisfies property $(N_p)$ for $\mathrm{deg}(L)\geq(n+1)g+p$. This bound is sharp for elliptic symmetric squares and also gives evidence for a folklore conjecture on adjoint syzygies.

papers.title: One-dimensional pressureless flow with a nonlinear velocity law: Bregman variational construction and well-posedness
papers.abstract: We establish global existence, uniqueness and quantitative stability for one-dimensional pressureless flow governed by \[ \partial_tρ+\partial_x\bigl(ρf(u)\bigr)=0, \qquad \partial_t(ρu)+\partial_x\bigl(ρu f(u)\bigr)=0, \] where $ρ$ is the mass density, possibly measure-valued, $u$ is the physical velocity, and $f\in C^1(\mathbb R)$, with $f'>0$, determines the transport velocity $f(u)$. The initial mass has finite positive mass and finite second moment, allowing atoms and unbounded support, and the initial physical velocity is bounded. The difficulty at a cluster collision is that mass and momentum conservation determine a mass-weighted average of physical velocity, whereas transport is governed by the nonlinear law $f$ applied to that average. We construct global entropy solutions by a Bregman variational time discretization whose cost is chosen to reproduce the transport velocity determined by this mass-weighted average, coupled with conditional-expectation updates of physical velocity. For every entropy solution satisfying the Oleinik condition on the transport velocity and initial weak continuity of the kinetic energy measure, we establish a Lagrangian representation and prove uniqueness within this class by comparing flows with possibly different cluster intervals. For two such solutions with the same velocity law and common mass, we obtain a $W_\infty$ estimate for the normalized mass measures in terms of the initial position and physical-velocity discrepancies in mass coordinates, whenever the initial $W_\infty$ distance is finite. The Lagrangian evolution has the semigroup property.

papers.title: Translational self-affine tiles in $\mathbb{R}^n$
papers.abstract: Two basic problems in the theory of integral self-affine tiles are to characterize the digit sets that generate translational tiles and to understand whether such tiles admit periodic translational tilings. We give a complete solution to the first problem: for an expanding integer matrix $\mathbf{A}$ and a digit set $\mathcal{D}\subset\mathbb{Z}^n$ with $\#\mathcal{D}=|\det\mathbf{A}|$, the self-affine set $T(\mathbf{A},\mathcal{D})$ is a tile if and only if, for some $N\geq1$, the iterated digit set $\mathcal{D}_{\mathbf{A},N}$ is of skew-product form with respect to $\mathbf{A}^N$. As a consequence, every integral self-affine tile admits a fully periodic self-replicating $q$-fold tiling. Moreover, $q$ divides $|T(\mathbf{A},\mathcal{D})|$. In dimension two we prove more: every integral self-affine tile admits a fully periodic tiling. In particular, the periodic tiling conjecture holds for integral self-affine tiles in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

papers.title: Distinguishing sets and measures from their planar Brownian images
papers.abstract: Motivated by a question of Hochman, we investigate whether two deterministic time measures or time sets can be distinguished almost surely from a single planar Brownian image. Using rescaled correlation integrals, we give a criterion for mutual singularity of the laws of the image measures, even when the time measures have the same dimension. For self-similar time sets satisfying the open set condition, we also recover the natural occupation measure from the compact image. Together, these results allow us to distinguish lattice and non-lattice self-similar sets and their natural measures within this class. For a naturally parametrised family with two contractions, with fixed dimension, each parameter can be distinguished from all but finitely many others. If the dimension is sufficiently small, every distinct parameter can be distinguished.

papers.title: Multiplicative Gradient Method for Log-Homogeneous Optimization: A Unified Mirror-Descent Framework
papers.abstract: Consider the problems of computing $\ell_p$-Lewis weights, Kelly portfolios, D-optimal designs, general equilibria in Fisher markets, and optimal error exponents for channel coding in information theory. All of them can be formulated as optimization problems over the probability simplex, but except for the last one, the associated objective functions are neither Lipschitz continuous nor smooth, rendering existing first-order optimization algorithms and their guarantees not directly applicable. Nevertheless, first-order algorithms for solving these problems do exist in the literature and, perhaps surprisingly, look very similar, even though their interpretations, derivations, and analyses mostly appear unrelated. In this paper, we develop a framework unifying these results that captures their common problem structure through log-homogeneity and a novel second-order condition on the objective function, and identifies their common algorithmic pattern as multiplicative gradient methods. The framework recovers known algorithms and their optimization error guarantees for computing Kelly portfolios, D-optimal designs, optimal error exponents for channel coding in classical communication, $\ell_p$-Lewis weights with $p < 2$, and general equilibria in Fisher markets. To illustrate the insights provided by the framework, we further show that multiplicative gradient methods yield state-of-the-art performance guarantees for computing $\ell_p$-Lewis weights with $p > 2$ and optimal error exponents in classical-quantum communication. Both results are novel to the best of our knowledge.

papers.title: Regularity of Totally Nonnegative Wonderful Compactification
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split real semisimple group of adjoint type. We prove that the cellular decomposition of the totally nonnegative part of its wonderful compactification is a regular CW complex, confirming a conjecture of Galashin, Karp, and Lam. In particular, the closure of every cell is homeomorphic to a closed ball. The proof combines a Bruhat atlas compatible with total positivity and a CL-labeling of the augmented face poset. The atlas models the strata locally with open Richardson varieties in the flag variety of a larger Kac-Moody group and identifies their totally nonnegative cells.

papers.title: A Lean formalisation of the disproof of Ramaekers's conjecture
papers.abstract: We describe Redhill, a Lean formalisation of the major results in Hölzl, Kleine and Stephan's "Improved Lower Bounds for Strong $n$-Conjectures" (arXiv:2409.13439). Design decisions regarding types and data structures are justified as enabling canonical versions of the paper's claims, and from there the most direct proofs of said claims. The formalisation process also uncovered many errors, omissions and optimisation opportunities in the informal proof, all of which are addressed in the final library. Although Redhill is meant to stand alone, a few lemmas were upstreamed to the primary Lean mathematics library mathlib. We discuss the tension between upstreaming and leaving lemmas in separate libraries. Unlike many other contemporary formalisation projects, Redhill was completed without any assistance from large language models (LLMs). We compare our work with LLM-assisted projects, in particular an extension of arXiv:2409.13439 to $n=4$, aiming to establish design and style guidelines that define good Lean formalisations.

papers.title: Optimal information loss for Liouville spectral responses
papers.abstract: We study Fisher information about the amplitude of a known smooth mean shift from the first Dirichlet eigenvalue and spatial responses of a Liouville random medium. The complete response record determines the speed measure and the Gaussian free field, whereas every finite record strictly loses information; an optimal design exists in each finite-dimensional probe space. We quantify this gap as the known Liouville parameter $γ$ tends to zero. If the probe space contains an explicit matching probe, the minimum loss equals $γ^2$ times a positive compression error for a deterministic second-chaos operator, up to $o(γ^2)$, with designs allowed to depend on $γ$. After enlarging the probe dictionary, the optimal $m$-response coefficient is asymptotic to $\|Lg\|_{L^1(D)}^2/(8m)$, where $L=-(2π)^{-1}Δ_D$ on the unit disk $D$. A quadratic correction of the readouts attains the same fixed-design loss to second order.

papers.title: Nested polynomial algebras and the exact spectrum of a three-dimensional two-spin oscillator
papers.abstract: We construct representations of the symmetry algebra and derive the exact spectrum of a three-dimensional oscillator with two spin-$\tfrac12$ degrees of freedom. The Hamiltonian and its first-order scalar and pseudo-scalar integrals were obtained in earlier classifications. Here we determine their action on the complete spectral basis. At fixed total angular momentum, a quadratic algebra acts on the three triplet orbital channels and admits a three-dimensional deformed-oscillator representation, while an overlapping two-state exchange algebra joins the middle triplet to the singlet. These finite modules determine angular--spin multiplicities but do not quantize the radial energy. A separate positive-discrete-series $su(1,1)$ representation of the common radial Hamiltonian generates the energy sequence. We give the finite matrices, Casimir and structure functions, normalized eigenfunctions, radial ladder actions, the exceptional $j=0$ sector, complete energy-shell multiplicities, and the effect of particle interchange.

papers.title: The Fekete-Szegö problem for starlike mappings of order $α$ and quasi-convex mappings of type $B$ in the unit balls of complex Banach spaces
papers.abstract: We establish sharp estimates for the generalized Zalcman functional corresponding to the index $n=2$ for normalized starlike mappings of order $α$ and normalized quasi-convex mappings of type $B$ in the unit ball of a complex Banach space and on the unit polydisk in $\mathbb{C}^n$. We also derive sharp Fekete-Szegö inequalities for normalized starlike mappings of order $α$ and normalized quasi-convex mappings of type $B$ in the unit ball of a complex Banach space. Our results extend classical coefficient estimates to higher-dimensional holomorphic mappings and provide a partial confirmation of the generalized Zalcman conjecture in higher dimensions.

papers.title: Logarithmic Kunz and Radu--André Theorems
papers.abstract: Frobenius morphisms play a crucial role in algebraic geometry and commutative algebra in positive characteristic. In particular, \textit{the Kunz theorem}, characterizing non-singularity via Frobenius morphisms, is a monumental work and has a relative version, called \textit{the Radu--André theorem}. In this paper, we extend the Kunz theorem and the Radu--André theorem to logarithmic algebraic geometry in positive characteristic.

papers.title: Some remarks on nonexistence in the Gamow liquid drop model
papers.abstract: In this paper we deal with the celebrated Gamow liquid drop model, namely, for $m>0$, $N\geq 2$ and $α\in (0,N)$, we study the problem \[ \min\Big\{P(Ω)+ V_α(Ω) : Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^N,\;|Ω|=m\Big\}\,, \] and focus mostly on the nonexistence of minimizers for large masses. First we show that any possible minimizer in the asymptotic regime must satisfy an optimal thickness property. Eventually, in the simplified setting of sets made up as a tiling of cubes, we show that nonexistence occurs for large masses for the whole range of parameters $N\geq 2$ and $α\in (0,N)$.

papers.title: Derivation based noncommutative geometry of quiver path algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study derivation based noncommutative geometry of path algebras arising from quivers by identifying a Lie algebra of derivations from which a differential calculus is constructed. We show that properties of the differential calculus are intimately connected with the structure of the quiver. In particular, by introducing the notion of a separating quiver, we find a condition on the quiver which is equivalent to the module of differential forms being a projective bimodule. For such quivers, one can construct bimodule connections, as well as bimodule forms which serve as noncommutative analogues of the Riemannian metric. As an illustration of the above concepts, we present a class of quivers for which one can construct Levi-Civita connections, i.e. torsion free connections compatible with a bimodule form.

papers.title: $L^p$-weighted cone restriction estimates
papers.abstract: We study Fourier extension estimates for the truncated cone in $\R^{n+1}$ with weights satisfying an $m$-dimensional ball condition only at radii between $1$ and $R^{1/2}$, where $0<m\le n-1$. Within the discrete induction framework of Du--Li--Wang--Zhang, we obtain a family of bounds by combining multilinear refined Strichartz inequalities, narrow decoupling, and Lorentz rescaling. We also give lightplank, lattice, and hybrid lattice--Knapp examples.

papers.title: Nonarchimedean discrete groups and quasi-isometric doubles of free groups
papers.abstract: For any nonarchimedean local field $k$, we exhibit the first examples of Zariski-dense, discrete subgroups of special linear groups over $k$, which are not commensurable to any lattice in the points of a semisimple group over a local field, and contain an infinite index subgroup isomorphic to a lattice in the $k$-points of a higher rank $k$-semisimple group. We prove that any Gromov-hyperbolic double of a non-elementary free group along a cyclic subgroup embeds as a quasi-isometrically embedded subgroup of $\mathsf{SL}_5(k')\times \mathsf{SL}_5(k')$, where $k'$ is a discretely valued field. More precisely, $k'$ is the field of rational functions $k(t)$ equipped with the Gauss valuation and $k$ is any nonarchimedean local field of characteristic not equal to $2$ or $3$.

papers.title: Weighted and Sobolev Estimates for Fractional Schrödinger Operators with Reverse Hölder Potentials
papers.abstract: We study weighted and Sobolev estimates for two fractional Schrödinger operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$, where $n\geq3$ and $0<s<1$. For the additive operator $L=(-Δ)^s+V$, with a nonnegative, nontrivial potential $V$ belonging to a suitable reverse Hölder class, $RH_q$, we establish a critical-radius form inequality and decay estimates for the semigroup mass. These yield a heat-kernel bound combining polynomial off-diagonal decay with a fixed positive exponent of decay relative to the fractional critical radius $ρ_s$. A decomposition at this scale gives weighted strong-type estimates for the semigroup maximal operator and weighted Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev estimates for $L^{-α/2}$, $0<αs<n$, together with the corresponding endpoint weak-type estimates. The admissible weights satisfy explicit growth restrictions determined by the kernel decay, and the fractional integration order is $αs$. We also consider the spectral operator $Q=(-Δ+V)^s$. Assuming $V\in RH_{q_1}$ with $n/(1+s)\leq q_1<n$ and classical critical radius $ρ_1(x)\geq1$, we prove that $\nabla Q^{-1/2}$ maps $H^{1-s,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ into $L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for $1<p\leq p_0$, where $1/p_0=1/q_1-1/n$. By duality, its adjoint maps $L^{p^{'}}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ into $H^{s-1,p^{'}}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for $p_0^{'}\leq p^{'}<\infty$.

papers.title: Quantitative upper bounds for certain quantum channel divergences
papers.abstract: We show that completely positive maps can be decomposed into sums of submaps which are close in completely bounded trace norm but as far apart as possible in terms of geometric channel fidelity. We then show that this kind of behavior extends to a large class of quantum channel divergences. We construct quantitative norm estimates for quantum channel divergences in terms of the Arveson-Radon-Nikodym theorem.

papers.title: Classical and Quantum Information Measures Characterizing Convertibility: An Axiomatic Approach
papers.abstract: In this PhD thesis, we take an axiomatic approach to studying multivariate divergences, which are measures of the information content of a tuple of classical or quantum states. These divergences are studied in the context of large-sample and catalytic convertibility of tuples of states. This type of convertibility is characterized by the ordering of an axiomatically defined family of divergences. In this thesis, we identify this family of divergences explicitly for two scenarios, one classical and one quantum. In the classical setting, we show that the relevant divergences are certain generalizations of the bivariate Rényi divergences. Unlike previous studies, we do not require the distributions to have the same support, yielding interesting new divergences. In the quantum setting, we consider pairs of classical-quantum states with pure component states, and find that majorization is characterized by all $α$-$z$ relative entropies for $α<1$. This demonstrates the first operational interpretation of these relative entropies.

papers.title: Towards a Sum-of-Squares Proof for the Nonexistence of Conway's 99-graph
papers.abstract: Conway's $99$-graph is a strongly regular graph with parameters $(v,k,λ,μ) = (99,14,1,2)$ and whose existence has long been an open problem. We use both a sum-of-squares program and the fact that a strongly regular graph with $λ= 1, μ= 2$ has no diamond or $K_{2,3}$ subgraph to derive a loose upper bound for the number of triangles that such a graph could contain. This bound is less than the number of triangles that the graph's spectrum asserts, implying that it does not exist.

papers.title: Well-Posedness and Strong Convergence of Infinite-Dimensional Port-Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Gradient Dynamics
papers.abstract: We establish a functional-analytic framework that justifies the LaSalle convergence argument outlined in [van der Schaft, 2026] on port-Hamiltonian primal-dual gradient dynamics for finite-horizon optimal control of linear systems. In addition to strict convexity of the running cost as in \cite{vanderSchaft2026PDGJuly}, our analysis requires global Lipschitz continuity of the cost gradient. This ensures that the nonlinear gradient operator is well-defined and Lipschitz on the entire underlying space. We establish global well-posedness of the optimizer dynamics: every initial value determines a unique global mild solution, and the associated solution operators form a contraction semigroup. Similar to [Gernandtand Schaller, 2025], this is proved using tools from maximal monotone operator theory. Assuming existence of an optimal solution, we combine a dissipation inequality with an infinite-dimensional LaSalle invariance principle to prove strong convergence of every trajectory with a relatively compact positive orbit to the unique optimal state, control, and costate. Moreover, we present a sufficient condition for compactness through uniform control regularity and show that convergence holds for all initial states. Finally, we present an example with a strictly but not strongly convex running cost for which every mild solution converges strongly to the unique equilibrium, while no global exponential estimate uniformly over initial values can be obtained.

papers.title: Elementary graphs are chromatic-choosable
papers.abstract: A graph is \emph{elementary} if its edges can be coloured with two colours so that the two edges of every induced path on three vertices receive different colours. Elementary graphs are one of the two basic classes in the Chvátal--Sbihi decomposition of claw-free perfect graphs; they include all line graphs of bipartite multigraphs and all complements of bipartite graphs. We prove that every elementary graph $G$ satisfies $\ch(G)=χ(G)=ω(G)$, confirming for this class the conjecture of Gravier and Maffray that claw-free graphs are chromatic-choosable. The proof combines the Maffray--Reed description of elementary graphs as augmentations of line graphs of bipartite multigraphs, Galvin's theorem, an extremal (edge-maximal) choice of counterexample, and a Hall-type lemma describing how list colourings of a complete graph minus a matching can fail.

papers.title: $H_2$-optimal model order reduction using hyperbolic geometry
papers.abstract: We revisit the problem of approximating a linear time-invariant LTI model by a reduced-order model (ROM) in an $H_2$-optimal sense. A widely used method for computing such ROMs is the iterative rational Krylov algorithm (IRKA). However, in practice, the stability of the resulting ROM is not generally guaranteed. In this work, we develop a novel framework that can be used to obtain $H_2$-optimal models of single-input single-output LTI systems while enforcing stability of the ROM. We use Malmquist-Takenaka orthogonal expansions in the corresponding $H_2$-spaces and their connection to hyperbolic geometry to develop an equilibrium function. We show that the poles of an $H_2$-optimal ROM transfer function are defined by the zeros of this equilibrium function. The resulting nonlinear root-finding problem is solved using a Newton-type method formulated on the products of Poincaré disk manifolds, where updates are performed along hyperbolic geodesics ensuring that the stability constraint is satisfied at every iteration. We present numerical experiments on benchmark systems for both discrete- and continuous-time LTI MOR problems, including examples where IRKA produces unstable reduced models while the proposed method preserves stability throughout the iteration.

papers.title: Reflected Proximal Dynamics for Accelerated High-Accuracy Log-Concave Sampling
papers.abstract: We study sampling from $π(x)\propto\mathrm{e}^{-V(x)}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $V$ is $α$-strongly convex and $β$-smooth with condition number $κ=β/α$. For this problem, the proximal sampler preserves the target exactly and recovers overdamped Langevin dynamics in the small-step limit, but its Gaussian resampling step discards directional information. Underdamped Langevin dynamics retains such information through momentum to accelerate exploration, motivating a proximal construction that combines target preservation with directional persistence. We introduce \textit{reflected proximal dynamics}, which combines proximal sampling with an exact reflection of the auxiliary variable, conditional kinetic motion, and controlled refreshment. We develop two realizations: a flux-resampled underdamped half-turn and a persistent-momentum quarter-turn. From a warm start with constant $χ^2$ divergence, both methods achieve total variation error $\varepsilon$ using $\widetilde O(\sqrtκd^{1/4})$ expected oracle queries. We further remove the supplied warm-start assumption by combining either sampler with existing posterior samplers in a proximal initialization stage with an optimized coarse step size. Accounting for both initialization and sampling yields $\widetilde O(κ^{6/7}d^{1/4})$ expected oracle queries. In both regimes, the dependence on the target accuracy $\varepsilon$ is $\mathrm{polylog}(1/\varepsilon)$, making reflected proximal dynamics a promising framework for accelerated high-accuracy log-concave sampling.

papers.title: Tournaments with many Hamilton cycles
papers.abstract: The object of interest is the maximum number, $h(n)$, of Hamilton cycles in an $n$-tournament. By considering the expected number of Hamilton cycles in various classes of random tournaments, we obtain new asymptotic lower bounds on $h(n)$. The best result so far is approximately $ 2.85584...$ times the expected number $g(n)$ of Hamilton cycles in a random $n$-tournament, and it is conjectured that $h(n)\sim cg(n)$ where $c\approx 2.855958$. The same statements hold for Hamilton paths.

papers.title: A non-nilpotent localization of a finite p-group
papers.abstract: We give negative answers to two questions of Farjoun about localizations of groups. For every odd prime $p$, we construct a finite $p$-group $G$, an infinite non-nilpotent group $H$, and a local embedding $f\colon G\hookrightarrow H$. The associated localization satisfies $L_f(G)\cong H$, showing that localizations need not preserve nilpotence and that the localization map $G\to L(G)$ need not be surjective when $G$ is a finite $p$-group.

papers.title: Subgroup Perfect Codes in Bi-Cayley Graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study perfect codes in bi-Cayley graphs, focusing on when two subgroups $H$ and $K$ of a group G can form a perfect code of the form $H_0 \cup K_1$. We first consider the problem for a general group G and then examine what happens for special classes of groups, particularly abelian groups. Along the way, we obtain several results, including a necessary and sufficient condition for normal subgroups to form a perfect code, as well as an equivalent condition for abelian groups in terms of their Sylow 2-subgroups. Finally, we study the same problem for dihedral groups, providing results for this important class of non-abelian groups.

papers.title: Mixed Hodge structure in the cohomology of moment-angle complexes
papers.abstract: This work studies the relationship between the multigrading in the cohomology of moment-angle complexes, introduced by V. Buchstaber and T. Panov in their computation of these cohomology groups, and the multigrading in the cohomology of the corresponding complements of coordinate subspace arrangements, arising from the mixed Hodge structure. It is shown that these multigradings coincide. This result refines a theorem from Yu. Eliyashev's 2013 dissertation. Furthermore, results on the mixed Hodge structure in the cohomology of complements of coordinate subspace arrangements are applied to the study of the same varieties over finite fields. In particular, various formulas are obtained for the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points and for the associated global $ζ$-functions.

papers.title: Sharp decay characterization for the Oldroyd-B system with only velocity dissipation
papers.abstract: We study the incompressible Oldroyd-B system on $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, in the regime in which the velocity is the only dissipated quantity: the stress tensor undergoes neither relaxation nor diffusion. In this regime the operator $\mathbb P\operatorname{div}$ acting on symmetric stresses has an infinite-dimensional kernel consisting of exact stationary states, so no decay estimate can hold for the full stress tensor and the existing sharp-decay theory for dissipative systems does not apply. We identify the active pair $U=(u,Λ^{-1}\mathbb P\operatorname{div}τ)$ as the correct decaying observable and establish, in a critical hybrid Besov framework, a complete characterization of its large-time behavior. For $-d/2<σ_1<σ\le d/2-1$ we prove that $\|U(t)\|_{\mathcal H^σ}=O(t^{-(σ-σ_1)/2})$ holds if and only if the low-frequency part of $U_0$ belongs to $\dot B^{σ_1}_{2,\infty}$, and, for $σ<d/2-1$, that the two-sided estimate $\|U(t)\|_{\mathcal H^σ}\simeq t^{-(σ-σ_1)/2}$ holds if and only if the low-frequency part of $U_0$ belongs to a nondegenerate subclass $\mathfrak B^{σ_1}_{2,\infty}$ of $\dot B^{σ_1}_{2,\infty}$.

papers.title: Contractivity of Rudin's diagonal restriction operator for $H^p$ of the polydisc
papers.abstract: We establish that Rudin's diagonal restriction operator is contractive from the Hardy space $H^p$ of the bidisc to the Bergman space $A^p$ of the disc for $2\leq p<\infty$, and characterize all cases of equality. We extend the result to polydiscs and obtain applications to polynomial point evaluation among others. The proof relies on an explicit formula, deduced from certain Green's formulas, for the defect between the $p$th powers of the two $L^p$ norms.

papers.title: Irreducible components of crystabelline deformation rings: the wildly ramified case
papers.abstract: Let $p\geq11$ be a prime, and let $\barρ:\Gal(\bar\QQ_p/\QQ_p)\rightarrow\GL_2(\bar\FF_p)$ be a reducible and very generic representation. In this paper, we use ghost series \cite{Lghost2} to study the irreducible components of Kisin's potentially crystalline deformation rings of $\barρ$. For wildly ramified principal series inertial types and arbitrary regular Hodge--Tate weights, we distinguish the components by the crystabelline slopes on their generic fibers and determine the total number of irreducible components. Combining this with an explicit formula for the total Hilbert--Samuel multiplicity of the special fiber obtained from the Breuil--Mézard conjecture, we compute the Hilbert--Samuel multiplicity of the special fiber of each component. Every such multiplicity is one when $\barρ$ is non-split, and is either one or two when $\barρ$ is split, according to whether the generic fiber of the corresponding component parametrizes reducible or irreducible Galois representations.

papers.title: Optimal Synthesis on the Special Linear Group
papers.abstract: We study the exponential map on the group of real two-by-two matrices with determinant one, endowed with a left-invariant Riemannian metric. Using the Euler-Poincaré equation and its linearization, we determine the conjugate and Maxwell times and identify a domain on which the exponential map is a global diffeomorphism onto the complement of the Maxwell stratum. This provides an alternative proof that the first Maxwell time coincides with the cut time. We obtain an explicit matrix description of the cut locus and characterize the globally minimizing geodesics. Furthermore, we analyze the first Maxwell-time function, determine its unique global minimum, and show that the injectivity radius is $\frac{π\sqrt{14}}{4}$. Finally, we characterize the intersection of the cut and conjugate loci and prove that every geodesic is equi-optimal.

papers.title: Higher order isoperimetric inequalities and rigidity for surfaces in $\R^n$
papers.abstract: We establish a family of sharp higher order isoperimetric type inequalities for smooth compact surfaces in Euclidean spaces of arbitrary codimension. These inequalities involve arbitrarily high derivatives of the boundary curve, together with the mean curvature vector of the surface. For example, the first and second order inequalities yield the sharp two-sided estimate for the isoperimetric deficit: \begin{align*} & \fracπ{R}\int_{\partial M}|x-Rν|^2\, ds +2π\int_M x\cdot H\, dA \le L^2-4πA\\ \le& \fracπ{R}\int_{\partial M}|x-Rν|^2\, ds +2π\int_M x\cdot H\, dA +\fracπ{3R}\int_{\partial M}|x+R^2κ|^2\, ds, \end{align*} where $R=\frac{L}{2π}$ and the origin is chosen to be the centroid of the boundary. For minimal surfaces, equality in the lower bound holds precisely for flat disks, whereas the second inequality admits non-round equality cases. Our results extend that of Carleman, Sachs, Chakerian, and Li-Schoen-Yau. A distinctive feature of our work is the unexpected rigidity structure arising at higher orders. At the first and second orders, equality curves admit decompositions into circular Fourier modes supported in mutually orthogonal planes. Remarkably, this phenomenon fails at higher orders. We establish a multiplicative factorization of the unit tangent map into elementary planar rotations acting on a fixed unit vector, providing a characterization of equality cases at arbitrary order. As a result, we construct a third order equality curve in $\mathbb R^3$ whose Fourier modes cannot be decomposed into mutually orthogonal circular modes.

papers.title: Limiting distributions of the rightmost eigenvalue of the truncated circular Unitary ensemble across all truncation regimes
papers.abstract: We study the limiting distribution of the largest real part of the eigenvalues of truncated unitary matrices. Let \(U_m\) be an \(m\times m\) Haar-distributed unitary matrix, and let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) be the eigenvalues of its upper-left \(n\times n\) principal submatrix. We determine the limiting distribution of \(\max_{1\le i\le n}\Re Z_i\) under a unified normalization: the limiting law is Gumbel when $q:=m-n\to\infty$ and is of Weibull type when $q$ is fixed. The fixed-\(q\) limiting laws converge to the Gumbel law as \(q\to\infty\). We also give a unified formulation of the normalizing constants for the spectral radius that recovers the previously known limiting laws.

papers.title: Representation Type and Schurian Finiteness of Tits Algebras
papers.abstract: We determine the representation type and Schurian finiteness of the Tits algebra of a finite central real hyperplane arrangement over an algebraically closed field. The algebra is representation-finite when the arrangement has at most two hyperplanes, tame when it has three, and wild when it has at least four. Moreover, it is Schurian-finite if and only if the arrangement has at most two hyperplanes. Both classifications hold over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. The proof combines Saliola's bound-quiver presentation with explicit module constructions, convex subquivers, essentialization, and deletion. In the $\mathbb{R}^2$ case, we describe all eleven indecomposable modules for two lines and construct a full exact embedding of modules over a free algebra for at least four lines.

papers.title: C^(sigma+alpha) regularity for fractional Hamilton-Jacobi equations, and rates of convergence in periodic homogenization
papers.abstract: We study two related questions for nonlocal equations of Bellman type: the regularity of solutions when the set of controls depends on the state variable, and the periodic homogenization of stationary nonlocal Hamilton-Jacobi equations driven by uniformly elliptic integro-differential operators of order $σ\in(0,2)$, whose kernels depend simultaneously on the slow variable, the fast periodic variable and the control. The effective equation is again a nonlocal Bellman equation, but its supremum runs over a set of viscosity Mather measures that varies with the space variable, in a merely Hölder continuous way. We first develop a $C^{σ+α}$ regularity theory for nonlocal Bellman equations with Hölder continuous, state-dependent index sets, extending the Schauder estimates of Caffarelli-Silvestre and Serra, in a general framework independent of homogenization. We then use these estimates as a source of compactness to construct a classical solution of the effective problem, unique among bounded classical solutions. Finally, combining this regularity with discounted approximate correctors, we make the perturbed test function method quantitative, and prove that the whole family of solutions converges to the effective solution, with the explicit rate $ε^{σα/(2+α)}$, where $α$ is the Hölder exponent of the data.

papers.title: Collective Floquet engineering between two distant superconducting artificial atoms
papers.abstract: A one-dimensional waveguide is a crucial medium for transferring propagating quantum information between remote qubits, yet the photon-mediated interaction is typically fixed by the static device geometry, qubit parameters, and their couplings to the transmission line. Such an interaction can be engineered to be coherent or dissipative via virtual- or real-photon exchange, respectively, yet its effective strength remains fixed in either case. Here we demonstrate dynamical control over this interaction by applying Floquet engineering to two superconducting qubits coupled to a waveguide terminated by a capacitive mirror. By positioning one qubit at an antinode and the other qubit at a node or an antinode of the resonant standing wave, we realize a Hermitian or non-Hermitian coupling between the two qubits. A periodic flux drive of the qubit frequencies then enables on-demand control of the coherent energy splitting and the collective decay. Our results establish Floquet engineering as a route to dynamically reshape both coherent and dissipative photon-mediated interactions between remote quantum emitters.

papers.title: Bootstrapping Classical and Quantum Query Lower Bounds for Finding Tarski Fixed Points
papers.abstract: The Tarski fixed-point problem asks for a fixed point of a monotone map on a $k$-dimensional grid lattice of width $n$ and has applications in game theory, economics, and verification. Substantial gaps remain between the known upper and lower bounds on its quantum query complexity. We prove two hardness bootstrapping theorems for quantum query lower bounds. Starting from a hard instance family whose instances have pair-wise incomparable unique fixed points, and a lower bound established by the nonnegative adversary method, we bootstrap this lower bound by (i) a factor of $Ω(t)$ when the dimension is multiplied by $t$ and the width remains unchanged, and (ii) a factor of $Ω(\log m)$ when the width is multiplied by $m$ and the dimension is doubled. Applying these theorems, we obtain three consequences: (i) an $Ω(k\log^2 n)$ lower bound for $k\geq 4$, improving previously best-known classical and quantum lower bounds; (ii) for every fixed constant $α>0$, there exists a constant $δ(α)>0$ such that $Q_ε(\text{Tarski}(n,k))=Ω(kn^{δ(α)})$ whenever $k>n^α$, and in particular, an $Ω(kn^{0.0072})$ lower bound for $k>n^{2/203}$, the first lower bound with simultaneous linear dependence on the dimension and polynomial dependence on the width; and (iii) a superpolynomial lower bound of $(k/\log k)^{Ω(\log k)}$ for exponentially wide grids, where $n=2^{Θ(k)}$. The last result rules out a route to polynomial-time algorithms for simple stochastic games and ARRIVAL through generic polynomial-query black-box Tarski solvers.

papers.title: Deterministic preparation of squeezed and non-Gaussian states in coupled qubit-boson systems
papers.abstract: Deterministic preparation of bosonic resource states is a central task in continuous-variable quantum information processing and quantum metrology. Here we develop a measurement-based imaginary time evolution (MITE) protocol for preparing squeezed and non-Gaussian states. The protocol combines ancilla-mediated weak measurements of the Hamiltonian with a conditional phase rotation that suppresses excited state trapping and stabilizes convergence toward the ground state. The method is potentially applicable in hybrid discrete variable-continuous variable (DV-CV) platforms, where the qubit acts as the measurement readout. We demonstrate deterministic convergence over a broad range of parameters and show that the performance degradation near the stability boundary is governed by the shrinking Bogoliubov quasiparticle gap. The same framework also extends to non-Gaussian bosonic resource states, including Schrödinger cat states and excited states of the single-mode squeezing Hamiltonian, which display Wigner negativity. The squeezed states remain robust under bosonic loss over experimentally relevant regimes.

papers.title: Stein degree over fields of characteristic zero
papers.abstract: We show that the Stein degree of horizontal divisors on generalised log Calabi-Yau fibrations or certain vertical divisors of Fano type fibrations over arbitrary fields of characteristic zero is bounded by constants that are independent on the ground field.

papers.title: A Proof of the Erdős Matching Conjecture for Large Matchings via Sharp Tail Probability for Sums of i.i.d. Nonnegative Random Variables
papers.abstract: We resolve a conjecture of Łuczak, Mieczkowska and Šileikis on the maximal tail probability of sums of independent and identically distributed nonnegative random variables. Specifically, for every integer $k\ge1$ and every $0\le x\le1/k$, we prove \[ \sup_{\mathbb E X_1\le x}\mathbb{P}(X_1+\cdots+X_k\ge1) =\max\{1-(1-x)^k,(kx)^k\}, \] where the supremum is over nonnegative i.i.d.\ random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_k$. We also characterize all maximizing distributions. Using this result, we prove the Erdős Matching Conjecture for every fixed $k\ge3$, all sufficiently large $s$, and every $n\ge k(s+1)$. More specifically, we show that in this range, the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph containing no $s+1$ pairwise disjoint edges is \[ \max\left\{ \binom{k(s+1)-1}{k}, \binom nk-\binom{n-s}{k} \right\}. \] Moreover, every extremal family consists either of all $k$-sets meeting a fixed $s$-set or of all $k$-sets contained in a fixed $(k(s+1)-1)$-set.

papers.title: Repairing covariance functions on metric trees through a Hausdorff-type distance
papers.abstract: A compact metric tree is the natural domain of spatial data recorded along a river network, a root system, or the branched processes of a cell, and a suitable distance between two points is the length of the path joining them. That distance admits almost none of the covariance models of spatial statistics, since only the roughest members of each family stay nonnegative definite, and the resulting fields are nowhere mean square differentiable. The repair proposed here is a change of metric. Comparing two points through their distances to the leaves gives a Hausdorff-type metric built from the shortest-path one. The new metric has a closed form, agrees with the shortest-path one inside every edge, and is strictly smaller across branching points. Any correlation function valid in a Euclidean space of dimension equal to the number of leaves may then be composed with it, returning the Matérn, powered exponential, and generalized Cauchy families at every degree of smoothness, and, on trees with few leaves, also correlations that change sign or have compact support. The same construction yields the multivariate Matérn and space-time models of the Gneiting class. In simulations covering a range of smoothness and of spatial scale, maximum likelihood provides estimates without appreciable bias, and on a reconstructed microglial cell the smooth models reduce the cross-validated prediction error by half.

papers.title: Exploration strategies for Gaussian process bandit optimization with inference regret guarantees
papers.abstract: Existing cumulative regret guarantees for Bayesian optimization (BO) do not necessarily characterize the quality of the algorithm's final output. This gap is critical under noisy evaluations, where the goal is to return a single high-quality recommendation. To address it, we introduce efficient exploration strategies that can be incorporated into any BO procedure by occasionally replacing the acquisition query with an exploration query. To validate this approach, we bound the Gaussian process posterior standard deviation over the search space via the fill distance of the queries, which measures the largest region left unexplored. We then use this result to derive upper bounds on the inference regret, i.e., the gap between the global optimum and the function value at the algorithm's returned point. Empirically, these exploration strategies improve the final recommendations of existing BO algorithms on synthetic benchmarks, hyperparameter optimization, and a control task.

papers.title: Regularity of the Price of Anarchy in Routing Games over the Multivariate Demand Space
papers.abstract: We study the price of anarchy (PoA) in nonatomic routing games as a function of the full vector of origin--destination demands. We show that the Beckmann value function is continuously differentiable on the positive demand cone, with gradient equal to the equilibrium origin--destination cost vector; hence the PoA is continuously differentiable on the regular demand region. We prove that the nondifferentiability set has Lebesgue measure zero and, when every edge cost is strictly increasing or constant, is covered by countably many codimension-one submanifolds. Under the same cost structure, all equilibrium objects are cellwise as smooth as the edge costs. For affine costs, the exceptional sets become finite unions of lower-dimensional polyhedral cells linked by an exact scaling law, and the maximum of the PoA over a cell closure is attained on the cell boundary, generalizing the one-dimensional endpoint result. The theory is illustrated on the Sioux Falls benchmark network.

papers.title: Regularity lemma for Gaussian polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove a regularity lemma for polynomials with fixed degree $d$ and any number of standard Gaussian input variables. Following modern approaches to the Szemer{é}di regularity lemma, we deduce our results from a general formulation of the regularity lemma using ultraproducts. Along the way, we give a direct combinatorial proof of the celebrated ``fourth moment theorem'' of Nualart and Peccati, which characterizes the asymptotically Gaussian polynomials inside degree-$d$ Gaussian chaos as those such that $\mathbb{E} p^2 \to 1$ and $\mathbb{E} p^4 \to 3$.

papers.title: On Z-Noetherian Rings
papers.abstract: In this paper, introduce a new finiteness condition for commutative rings, called $Z$-Noetherian, under which every ideal contained in the set of zero-divisors $Z(R)$ is finitely generated. This condition lies properly between Noetherian and $Nil_{*}$-Noetherian. We establish intrinsic characterizations of $Z$-Noetherian rings and investigate their stability under nilpotent quotients and localizations. Under the assumption that $Z(R)$ is an ideal, we obtain a primary decomposition theorem for ideals contained in $Z(R)$. For $ZD$-rings, we prove a Cohen-type criterion characterizing $Z$-Noetherian in terms of the finite generation of prime ideals contained in $Z(R)$. We further establish $Z$-Noetherian analogues of the Hilbert Basis Theorem and Krull's Intersection Theorem. Finally, we establish a principal ideal theorem for $Z$-Noetherian rings. Collectively, these results show that several fundamental finiteness and structural properties of Noetherian rings extend to the broader class of $Z$-Noetherian rings.

papers.title: A Dimension Estimate for Polynomial Growth Holomorphic Functions
papers.abstract: On a complete noncompact Kähler manifold $M^n$ of complex dimension $n$ with nonnegative Ricci curvature, we prove that polynomial growth holomorphic functions of degree $d$ ($d\geq 0$) have an dimension upper bound $C(n)(1+d)^n$. In particular, $\dim_{\C}\OO_d(M)\leq C'(n)d^n,$ for $d\geq1$, and the estimate is sharp.

papers.title: Wasserstein rates of all orders for the Sato-Tate law of Kloosterman sums
papers.abstract: Let $μ_q$ be the distribution of the normalized Kloosterman sums $\mathrm{Kl}(a;q)$, $a\in\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and let $μ_{\mathrm{ST}}$ be the Sato--Tate law. We prove $W_s(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/3}$ for $1\le s\le2$, $W_s(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/6-1/(3s)}$ for $2\le s<\infty$, and $W_\infty(μ_q,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/6}$, answering a question of Kowalski and Untrau. More generally, we bound $W_s(μ,μ_{\mathrm{ST}})$ for all $s$ whenever the Chebyshev moments of $μ$ satisfy bounds of Katz type. For $s=2$ the bound also follows from a smoothing inequality of Borda and Cuenin; for $s>2$ and $s=\infty$ our bounds are stronger. The proof uses the quantile coupling, which arises from Stieltjes sums over two different intervals whose cells are paired so as to balance two measures, and which is optimal for all $s$ simultaneously; an explicit $W_2$ smoothing inequality relative to $μ_{\mathrm{ST}}$; and a sharp comparison between $W_s$ and the Kolmogorov distance for laws with square-root edges. The last result shows that $q^{-1/6}$ is the best rate for $W_\infty$ obtainable from Niederreiter's discrepancy bound. Numerically, for primes $10^3<p<10^6$, all these distances appear to decay like $p^{-1/2}$.

papers.title: A characterization of the finite model property for $ω$-categorical theories
papers.abstract: A first-order theory $T$ has the {\em finite model property} if every first-order sentence that is implied by $T$ has a finite model. We give a characterization of when a complete $ω$-categorical theory $T$ has the finite model property. The characterization makes it possible to transfer stability theoretic results in [29] to certain classes of finite structures. This approach also gives information concerning properties that a sequence of finite ``base structures'' of ever larger size must have in order for its random expansions to a larger vocabulary to have a chance to satisfy a convergence law for first-order logic.

papers.title: A counterexample to integral Aleksandrov-Bakelman-Pucci estimates for a nonlocal operator
papers.abstract: We construct a counterexample to integral Aleksandrov-Bakelman-Pucci estimates for nonlocal inequalities of the form \begin{equation*} L_au(x):=\int_{\mathbb R^n}δ_yu(x) \frac{a(x,y)}{|y|^{n+σ}}\,dy \ge-f(x)\quad\text{in }B_1, \end{equation*} with $u\le0$ in $\mathbb R^n\setminus B_1$, where $δ_yu(x)=u(x+y)+u(x-y)-2u(x)$, and the measurable coefficient satisfies \begin{equation}\tag{C} λ\le a(x,y)\leΛ,\qquad a(x,y)=a(x,-y),\qquad x\in\mathbb R^n,\quad y\ne0. \end{equation} More precisely, for every $n\ge1$, $0<σ<2$, and $0<λ<Λ$, there exist a fixed coefficient $a(x,y)$ satisfying \textup{(C)}, a constant $d>0$, and nonnegative functions $u_j,f_j\in C_c^\infty(B_1)$ such that $L_au_j\ge-f_j$ in $B_1$, $0\le f_j\le1$, and $|\operatorname{supp}f_j|\to0$ as $j\to\infty$, while $u_j\ge d$ on $B_{1/4}$ for every $j$. Consequently, this fixed operator admits no $L^p$ maximum estimate for any $1\le p<\infty$.

papers.title: Cubic moments of eigenfunctions on surfaces
papers.abstract: We identify Gaussian curvature as a local mechanism for cubic cancellation of Laplace eigenfunctions on Riemannian surfaces, without arithmetic or dynamical assumptions. For $L^2$-normalized local solutions at frequency $λ$, cubic integrals against smooth compactly supported weights tend to zero whenever the curvature is nonzero almost everywhere where the weight is nonzero. Finite-order nondegeneracy yields sharp polynomial decay rates. In particular, on closed surfaces with nowhere-vanishing curvature, we obtain the rate $O(λ^{-1/6})$, attained by spherical harmonics on the round sphere. This proves the cubic case of the Gaussian moment conjecture for all normalized real eigenfunctions on closed negatively curved surfaces. The local proof rests on an exact identity relating the reduced phase at a Fermat point to Gaussian curvature. On complete hyperbolic surfaces with positive systole, we also prove global $O((\logλ)^{-3/2})$ decay for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions and smooth weights with bounded covariant derivatives through order two, without assuming finite area.

papers.title: Architectural Robustness to Label Noise Using Variational Quantum Circuits for Medical Image Classification
papers.abstract: Label noise is prevalent in medical image datasets, arising from observer disagreement and ambiguous cases and deep networks memorize the mislabeled examples at the cost of generalization. Current solutions such as loss correction and sample selection add training complexity and generally assume the noise rate is known or estimable. This paper investigates whether robustness can be obtained architecturally, by routing a frozen backbone's features through a low-dimensional bounded bottleneck and classifying them with a head whose function class is intrinsically smooth. Variational quantum circuits with angle encoding and a linear cost function realise exactly such a class. Their use in medical imaging, however, has been limited by the small number of qubits available on noisy intermediate-scale devices, which typically restricts inputs to low-resolution grayscale images. We therefore couple a frozen ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B/16 backbone to a trainable linear bottleneck and an eight-qubit variational quantum circuit, allowing 224x224 RGB inputs to be processed. Under clean labels the model leads five of six MedMNISTv2 benchmarks against published hybrid quantum-classical models, with margins of 17.4 and 15.7 percentages on BloodMNIST and PathMNIST. The advantage emerges under corrupted labels. At symmetric noise rates of 30% and 50% the model outperforms many published quantum and noise-robust classical baselines on all six datasets without any explicit noise-handling component. Against a control that shares the backbone, bottleneck, parameter count and optimizer and replaces only the circuit with a ReLU layer, it retains 89.75% accuracy on PathMNIST at 50% noise where the control falls to 78.96%. Direct measurement of training dynamics shows that this advantage is not an inability to fit corrupted labels, which the circuit retains, but greater stability under prolonged training on them.

papers.title: Device-to-protocol simulation of spectrally-resolved quantum photonic circuits
papers.abstract: Predicting quantum-photonic circuit performance requires retaining source and device physics without making photon-counting calculations prohibitively expensive. Here we present PhoQuS, a framework that combines frequency-resolved source models, electromagnetic compact models and spatially correlated fabrication variation to simulate quantum photonic circuits. Covariance-Gram reduction after full-resolution Gaussian propagation lowers readout cost while retaining dominant spectral correlations. For continuous-variable state preparation, spectral reduction accelerates photon counting by 60.4-fold in an approximate Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill circuit. Frequency-resolved modeling guides the use of cascaded squeezing with temporal walk-off compensation, yielding 0.99 fidelity to the single-mode circuit reference and 0.98 conditional purity in lossless simulations. For discrete-variable state preparation, simulations of three-photon Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger circuits across a virtual wafer show that component robustness alone does not predict circuit fidelity, which depends jointly on source spectra, circuit architecture and control. PhoQuS connects device physics to protocol-level performance through a unified workflow that retains spectral detail while reducing readout cost.

papers.title: A ghost-cell immersed boundary method for the shallow water equations on Cartesian grids: mass conservation and wetting and drying over variable topography
papers.abstract: A ghost-cell immersed boundary method is proposed for the two-dimensional shallow water equations with a variable bed (topography), solved with an explicit Godunov-type finite volume scheme (unsplit second-order MUSCL, HLLC flux, hydrostatic reconstruction) on Cartesian grids. Ghost-cell methods leak mass through the wall. To find a robust and conservative treatment, eight constructions of the ghost values and a cut-cell form of the continuity equation were applied to seven test problems, which include wetting and drying on sloping beds and a laboratory dam break.
