As an application, we construct the first examples of completely $S_p$-bounded Herz-Schur multipliers in the free group that are unbounded as Fourier multipliers. This result disproves Fourier-Schur transference---a longstanding open problem since the work of Neuwirth and Ricard in 2011. In line with this, our main result also implies the surprising fact that free balls Schur multipliers are uniformly $S_p$-bounded, in sharp contrast to their Fourier behavior. In addition, we disprove Fourier-Schur transference over the algebraic groups $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbf{Q}_q)$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbf{R})$ with $\mathrm{K}$-biinvariant counterexamples, the latter involving additional geometric and probabilistic techniques.

papers.title: Quantum Localization in Geometric Complex Networks
papers.abstract: Quantum localization, the phenomenon by which wave diffusion is halted, here understood as the superposition of propagating waves, can have many different origins, such as onsite random potentials in Anderson localization. However, some systems exhibit complex geometries and could potentially reproduce similar results without external potentials. In this work, we study how localization of single particle states is affected by the underlying topology of a simple but highly predictive complex network model: the geometric soft configuration model $\mathbb S^1$. By tuning the model's temperature and heterogeneity parameters, we are able to generate different structural patterns and focus on the transition from a small-world to a non-small-world regime. Our study suggests that small-world networks tend to have extended states, which spread the whole system's size, in contrast to non-small-world networks which tend to localize, showing how complex connectivity can play the role assigned to random energetic disorder.

papers.title: Entropy-Regularized Mean-Field Games with Average-Reward Criterion: Span-Seminorm Contractions and Model-Free Learning
papers.abstract: We study stationary discrete-time mean-field games with finite state and action spaces under the average-reward criterion, with an entropy-regularized objective and population-dependent dynamics and rewards. Under a minorization condition, the soft Q-operator is a span-seminorm contraction for the full transition kernel, so relative value iteration does not require the minorizing measure. When the Lipschitz constant of the kernel is below the minorization mass and the temperature exceeds an explicit threshold, the equilibrium fixed-point operator is a contraction: an equilibrium exists, its population distribution is unique, and a fixed-point iteration converges to it geometrically. We then learn the equilibrium model-free from a simulator, combining soft Q-learning at a fixed population distribution with an empirical transition kernel. We prove a finite-sample bound for soft Q-learning in the span seminorm, with temperature-independent constants, and derive convergence rates for the learned population distribution and policy. A congestion-aware routing game illustrates the results.

papers.title: Semiprime and real submodules of arbitrary modules are intersections of prime and real prime submodules
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A submodule $N$ of an $R$-module $M$ is semiprime if $m\in(N:m)M$ implies $m\in N$. It is known that every semiprime submodule of $R^n$ is an intersection of prime submodules, and Aryapoor extended this to finitely generated modules. We show that no finiteness assumption is needed: every semiprime submodule of an \emph{arbitrary} $R$-module is the intersection of the prime submodules containing it. The proof is short and uses neither coordinates nor presentations; its key step is that a nonzero element $q$ of a semiprime module $Q$ satisfies $sq\notin\p Q$ for all $s\notin\p$, where $\p$ is any minimal prime over the annihilator of $q$. We define an $R$-module $M$ to be real if $\sum_i m_i\otimes m_i=0$ in $M\otimes_RM$ implies $m_i=0$ for all $i$, and a submodule $N\subseteq M$ real if the module $M/N$ is real. We prove the corresponding result for real submodules: every real submodule of an arbitrary module is the intersection of the real prime submodules containing it. On $R^n$ our notion of realness coincides with the coordinate definition used in earlier work on real Nullstellensätze for free modules.

papers.title: Higher-order nonhomomorphicity under affine restrictions
papers.abstract: We study the behavior of the $k$-th-order nonhomomorphicity of Boolean functions under restriction to affine subspaces. For odd $k\ge3$ and $0\le t<n$, we introduce the $t$-restriction $k$-th-order nonhomomorphicity $P_{k,t}(f)$, defined as the minimum of $P_k(f_{\mid A})$ over affine spaces of codimension at most $t$. For a direct sum of $m$ monomials of degrees at least two, we determine $P_{k,t}$ exactly. When $t<m$, a minimum is obtained by setting one variable equal to zero in each of the $t$ monomials of lowest degree. When $m\le t<n$, the minimum is zero. The proof combines multiplicativity of even Walsh moments with a contraction argument for affine restrictions. We establish a general formula for the Walsh transform of a Boolean function restricted to an affine subspace of arbitrary codimension, yielding an exact spectral characterization of the $t$-restriction normalized nonlinearity $\rnnl_t(f)$. As odd $k$ tends to infinity, $(1-2P_{k,t}(f))^{1/(k+1)}$ converges to $1-2\rnnl_t(f)$. We further prove that every non-affine function has a hyperplane restriction with strictly smaller odd-order nonhomomorphicity. Finally, we determine $\rnnl_1(T_{d,n})$ exactly for all threshold functions with $n\ge3$. This proves the two threshold-function conjectures left open in~\cite{SergeAnaPante2025}, including the previously unresolved odd-majority case, where a minimizing hyperplane is $x_1+x_2=0$.

papers.title: Auxiliary Hessian Equations
papers.abstract: We propose k-Hessian equations as auxiliary equations for degenera- tions of Kähler classes to nef classes of numerical dimension k. As proof-of-concept results, we provide a uniform mean-value inequality and uniform à priori estimates for Hessian equa- tions.

papers.title: A note on the Slater$\unicode{x2013}$Vélez permutation
papers.abstract: We study the greedy sequence of positive integers introduced by Slater and Vélez. They proved that it is a permutation of the positive integers but left open whether its sequence of consecutive absolute differences is also a permutation. We prove that it is.

papers.title: The operad of anti-pre-Lie algebras and its Lie elements
papers.abstract: We initiate a systematic operadic approach to anti-pre-Lie algebras. We study the operad controlling anti-pre-Lie algebras, its relationship to the operad of Novikov algebras and its cyclic structure. We establish that the Lie bracket of an anti-pre-Lie algebra satisfies the standard identity of degree five. We also establish a quadratic maximality property of the anti-pre-Lie operad with respect to this identity. We then show that the anti-pre-Lie operad and its Koszul dual are not Koszul and give a full description of the latter. Finally, we identify the Lie elements in the Koszul dual operad with the operad of metabelian Lie algebras.

papers.title: Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for singular $L^k$ interaction kernels with rates
papers.abstract: Based on a semigroup approach, we prove quantitative uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for two systems of interacting particles with singular interaction kernels $K$ of type $L^k$, $k>d$, and a contractive Lipschitz confinement force field. First, we consider a system with moderate interaction, which means that the particles interact through the mollified kernel $K\ast V^N$, for some approximation of identity $V^N = N^{dα} V(N^α\cdot),\, α>0$. Assuming that $\|K\|_{L^k}$ is sufficiently small, we obtain that for any $\varepsilon>0$ the uniform-in-time rate is of order $N^{-\min\left(α,\frac12-\frac{dα}{2}-\varepsilon\right)}$, plus an exponentially small in time contribution of the initial condition. Second, for the classical, non-mollified particle system we establish uniform-in-time propagation of chaos with rate $N^{-\min\left(α,\frac12-\frac{dα}{2}-\varepsilon\right)} + \|K-K\ast V^N\|_{L^{k}}$, plus an exponentially small in time contribution of the initial condition. The method relies on the regularity properties of the solution of the associated nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation combined with estimates of the Duhamel formulation of the mollified empirical measure, together with partial Girsanov transforms for the non-mollified system of particles.

papers.title: Unrectifiable surfaces with intrinsic regularity in Carnot groups
papers.abstract: In any noncommutative Carnot group, for every $0\le α<1$, we show the existence of a $C^{1,α}_\mathrm H$ surface that is unrectifiable with respect to the Euclidean distance. Precisely, the surface has Euclidean Hausdorff dimension higher than its topological dimension. We show that in step-2 Carnot groups the construction gives hypersurfaces of maximal Euclidean Hausdorff dimension, equal to $q-\frac{1+α}{2}$, where $q$ is the topological dimension of the group. Here the range of unrectifiability is sharp, since for $α=1$ the surface is rectifiable in the classical sense. In step-2 Carnot groups, it is also possible to prove that the $(q-\frac12)$-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure of every $C^1_\mathrm H$ hypersurface is zero. These results extend the seminal work by Kirchheim and Serra Cassano in the first Heisenberg group.

papers.title: Universal Shift Congruences for Weighted Permutation Sequences
papers.abstract: The involution numbers $1,1,2,4,10,26,\ldots$ repeat modulo $3$, $5$ and $7$. We explain this, and many similar patterns, by one rule. Many sequences count permutations in which every cycle of length $m$ carries a weight $w_m$ (involutions, derangements, "sets of lists", and many others in the OEIS). Writing $A(n)$ for such a count, the rule is $A(n+k)\equiv A(n)A(k)$ modulo $\mathrm{lcm}(n,k)$. It generalizes our earlier proof of the case modulo $k$ for one such sequence, but now it holds for all weights at once, as a coefficientwise congruence between universal polynomials, and we find the largest modulus that works for the universal polynomials, $nk/\mathrm{rad}(\gcd(n,k))$, and show that nothing larger does. We then show that passing from $k$ to $pk$ behaves like raising to the $p$-th power modulo a high power of $p$, with a sharp exponent for the polynomials, which gives $A(p^r)\equiv(w_1+(p-1)w_p)^{p^{r-1}}$ modulo $p^r$ for odd $p$, and explains why the prime $2$ is special. A family of sequences defined by Lagrange inversion fits the same framework, which proves Bala's conjecture for the whole family (the single sequence A278070 had been proved earlier by an automated system) and the divisibility observed in the entries A251568 and A251569. As further applications we prove OEIS conjectures of Richman, Hanna, van Hoeij and Bala (A227937), and the theorems apply to 101 OEIS sequences, whose congruences are recorded in a supplementary catalogue. Higher-order versions of the content formula are treated in a separate paper.

papers.title: Iwasawa cohomology of pseudorigid families of $(\varphi,Γ)$-modules
papers.abstract: We study the Iwasawa cohomology complex attached to a pseudorigid family of $(\varphi, Γ)$-modules and prove coadmissibility of its cohomology groups, perfectness and compatibility with base change. We apply this result to give another proof of perfectness of the Herr complex in pseudorigid family. We also use it to prove perfectness of Selmer complexes and obtain a result on variation of ranks of Selmer groups in analytic family.

papers.title: Regularity for Minimizers of Mixed-Smoothness Variational Integrals
papers.abstract: We establish the first partial regularity results for minimizers of a class of suitably quasiconvex variational integrals defined on anisotropic Sobolev spaces. These variational integrals are related to higher gradient continuum models for pantographic metamaterials.

papers.title: Eigenstate transitions and critical transport in 3D Aubry-André model
papers.abstract: We numerically study spectral and wave-function properties, as well as time evolution, in finite-size commensurate approximations of the 3D Aubry-André model. We explicitly show, through scaling analysis, the existence of two critical points. One of the critical points is a localization-delocalization transition in real-space, similar to the critical point in the 3D Anderson model. The other is a localization-delocalization transition in a dual momentum space, which does not have any analog in the 3D Anderson model. We estimate their values from spectral measures, such as the gap ratio and the spectral form factor, as well as from wave-function measures, such as the inverse participation ratio and the participation entropy. Additionally, we demonstrate that both critical points exhibit hallmarks of critical points between quantum ergodicity and localization. First, the eigenstates and the eigenspectrum at the critical point fulfill the mutual universal relation between the eigenspectrum compressibility $χ$ and the eigenstate fractal dimension $d^{(1)}$ [S. Jiricek et al., Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. 123, e2518027123 (2026)]. Second, the dynamics of the wave packet at the critical point is governed by the critical dynamical exponent $z$, characterized by the spectral fractal dimension and the dimensionality of the lattice [M. Hopjan and L. Vidmar, Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 060401 (2025)]. Thus, similarly to the 3D Anderson model, the critical dynamical exponent is sub-diffusive with the value of $z=3$.

papers.title: Finite Length of Locally Analytic Vectors for $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ and $D_F^\times$
papers.abstract: Let $F/\mathbf Q_p$ and $E/\mathbf Q_p$ be finite extensions, and let $G=\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ or $D_F^\times$, where $D_F$ is the quaternion division algebra over $F$. Let $Π$ be an admissible Banach $E$-representation of $G$ whose locally $\mathbf Q_p$-analytic vectors $Π^{\mathrm{an}}$ have an infinitesimal character. If $p>2$ or $F=\mathbf Q_p$, we prove that $Π^{\mathrm{an}}$ and $Π$ have finite length in their respective admissible categories.

papers.title: Open substacks preserving moduli spaces: classification and bounds
papers.abstract: For a smooth locally reductive stack admitting an adequate moduli space, we show that there are finitely many open substacks preserving the adequate moduli space, and give a complete classification of such opens. For $\mathbb{G}_m$-actions, this becomes an explicit description in terms of the codimension-one Bialynicki-Birula strata. Moreover, for a stable adequate moduli space, we show that the number of preserving opens are bounded by 3 raised to the relative Picard rank. As an application, the number of fixed components for $\mathbb{G}_m$-actions is at least the relative Picard rank.

papers.title: The theory of $(λ,μ)$-fold factorizations of groups
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent study of $λ$-fold near-factorizations of finite groups by Kreher, Li, and Stinson (Designs, Codes and Cryptography, 2026), we introduce and systematically investigate $(λ,μ)$-fold factorizations of finite groups, with particular emphasis on the abelian case. These structures form a natural relaxation of $λ$-fold near-factorizations and encompass several related families that have previously been studied in different contexts. We establish the foundational theory of $(λ,μ)$-fold factorizations, provide two general constructions, and prove several nonexistence results for finite abelian groups.

papers.title: Separating Statistical Inference from Experimental Runtime: An Architecture for Sequential Scientific Analysis
papers.abstract: Sequential statistical procedures are increasingly embedded in scientific systems in which observations arrive incrementally from heterogeneous sources. In such systems the statistical update is only one part of the computation: observations must also be acquired, aligned across inputs, ordered, delivered, persisted, and replayed, and results must be passed to systems that display them or act on them. Sequential methods are nevertheless missing from the general software toolkit. They run inside proprietary experimentation platforms and commercial statistical packages, or exist as offline functions over complete data, and the batch fit interface that dominates machine-learning libraries has no place for a procedure that listens, keeps state, and decides when to stop. We propose an architecture that separates statistical inference from data topology, execution runtime, run lifecycle, persistence, and external action. Its central abstraction is the Sequential Procedure: a state-transition function that maps an inferential state, a valid statistical input, and a statistical random state to a new state and a scientific output. The procedure does not define how observations are acquired, paired, scheduled, stored, or acted upon. We specify the architecture semantically rather than through an object model, derive seven conformance invariants that any implementation can be tested against (among them synchronous/asynchronous, checkpoint, replay, and batch equivalence), and describe a dependency-free reference implementation in which all seven hold bitwise. Lorden's 2-SPRT for the Kiefer-Weiss problem serves as the reference procedure; the same contract accommodates sequential estimators, Bayesian filters, change-point detectors, and stateful predictive models.

papers.title: Equivariant formality for rational $\C_{p^k}$-spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss equivariant formality for spaces equipped with a primary cyclic group action. We study the behavior of equivariant formality with some topological constructions. The algebraic complexity needs to deal with injectivity. In the end, we discuss equivariant intrinsic formality.

papers.title: Weak type (1,1) bound criterion for maximal truncated singular integral operators with rough kernels
papers.abstract: This paper proves the weak type (1,1) boundedness for maximal truncated singular integral operators with rough non-convolution kernels of the form $Ω(x-y) K(x,y)$, where $Ω$ is homogeneous of degree zero with $Ω\in L\log L(\sS^{d-1})$ and $K$ is a standard Calderón-Zygmund kernel. This extends the recent resolution of the classical convolution case by Lai \cite{Lai2025weak} to a wider class of operators.

papers.title: Koszul Duality in an Equivariant Context
papers.abstract: This article takes steps to show that an equivariant version of the well known phenomena of Koszul Duality can be formulated in a manner not considered prior: via dg (co)algebra valued functors on the orbit category. As such techniques used in this article mix traditional and modern categorical methods in homotopy theory.

papers.title: The Diagonal of a Regular Pentagon
papers.abstract: We demonstrate the well-known fact that the diagonal of a unit regular pentagon has length the golden ratio. While similar to other proofs, we provide a novel figure that we believe is particularly well-suited to achieve full understanding at a glance.

papers.title: A note on the $p$-adic inhomogeneous Littlewood conjecture
papers.abstract: Bugeaud, Haynes and Velani (2011) resolved a metric version of the $p$-adic Littlewood conjecture. We establish a fully inhomogeneous generalisation of their result, as well as a partially inhomogeneous generalisation of a result of Harrap and Haynes (2013) in the more general mixed setting.

papers.title: Failure of dimension drop for harmonic measure on Ahlfors regular flat boundaries
papers.abstract: We develop an $N$-adic modification of the construction of David-Jeznach-Julia for compact subsets of the real line $\mathbb{R}\subset\mathbb{C}$ for which harmonic measure for the complementary domains has no dimension drop. In particular, we show that for every $s\in(0,1/2)$, there exists an $s$-Ahlfors regular compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}\subset\mathbb{C}$ such that $\mathrm{dim}ω^\infty=s$, where $ω^\infty$ denotes harmonic measure for $\mathbb{C}\setminus K$ with pole at infinity. Combined with a result of the third author, this shows that the threshold $1/2$ is sharp.

papers.title: A Sharp Bound for the Second Betti Number of Hyperkähler Sixfolds
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth compact irreducible hyperkähler manifold of dimension six. We prove that the second Betti number satisfies $b_2(X) \le 23$. Furthermore, we show that the third cohomology vanishes whenever $b_2(X) \ge 19$, and that all odd cohomology vanishes when $b_2(X) = 23$. If the second Chern class lies in the subalgebra generated by $H^2(X,\mathbb{Q})$, then $b_2(X) \in \{5,8,23\}$. The proof uses the Looijenga--Lunts--Verbitsky decomposition, curvature inequalities for Segre classes, and the Hodge--Riemann bilinear relations on the projective cotangent bundle.

papers.title: Sub-Gaussian Confidence Intervals for Heavy-Tailed Data: Characterizing the Limits of Inference
papers.abstract: We investigate the problem of uncertainty quantification in the mean estimation framework. Given an i.i.d. sample from a distribution with unknown mean $μ$ and variance $σ^2$, we want to construct an estimator $\whμ_n$ and provide a computable and size-optimal upper bound for the error $|\wh μ_n - μ|$. While estimators possessing strong deviation guarantees are well known, no data-dependent non-asymptotic upper bounds for their performance exist in general. We show that this gap can be bridged by introducing a parameter that characterizes the ``effective sample size'' available for uncertainty quantification. This parameter captures the difficulty of the problem, interpolating between ``easy'' cases where sub-Gaussian confidence intervals exist and ``hard" cases where their construction is impossible. Using this characterization, we design confidence intervals of optimal length that are fully adaptive to the unknown variance. Numerical experiments confirm that our approach maintains nominal coverage even in asymmetric and heavy-tailed regimes where other existing methods fail.

papers.title: A Multiplicative Horn Obstruction to the Unitary Categorification of a Rank-Twelve Modular Datum
papers.abstract: We study the rank-twelve potential modular datum denoted $12^{39,406}_{4,1276.}$ in the low-rank classification tables. Its global dimension is $(1287+351\sqrt{13})/2$, and its fusion ring agrees with that of the known rank-twelve Haagerup modular category. The datum satisfies the modular relations, has nonnegative integral Verlinde coefficients, and passes several familiar genus-one necessary tests. We prove, nevertheless, that it cannot be realized by a unitary modular tensor category. The obstruction already occurs in the representation of the three-strand braid group on $\operatorname{Hom}(C_{[10]},B^{\otimes3})$. Generalized Frobenius--Schur indicators determine the eigenvalues of the two-strand generator on this twelve-dimensional space. The central relation in $B_3$ then reduces the problem to a product of three prescribed unitary conjugacy classes. A sixfold symmetry reduces the $1302$ determinant-compatible cases to $217$ representatives. Rank-one inequalities leave only $17$ of these, and ten explicitly displayed degree-zero rank-two Schubert inequalities exclude the remaining cases. A violated inequality with gap $2/117$ is worked out explicitly. All calculations used in the obstruction are exact. The argument uses unitarity essentially and leaves non-unitary categorification open.

papers.title: Quantum ordinal optimization under a fixed comparison budget
papers.abstract: Ordinal optimization selects designs that are good enough rather than optimal when evaluation is expensive and the budget is small. The alignment probability measures the chance that the selected set contains at least a prescribed number of truly good designs. We formulate quantum ordinal optimization as a class of problems that maximize this probability under a fixed oracle budget. We study exact, coherent pairwise comparisons with one selected design as a first instance, with the budget counted in comparison queries. For every classical comparison budget smaller than the number of designs, we prove that a knockout among uniformly sampled designs attains the optimum. The sample is drawn without replacement and contains one more design than the number of comparisons. For a uniformly random order, the selected design's rank has a polynomial probability law. At the same comparison budget, the maximum quantum degree is at most twice the classical maximum, a factor attained whenever there are more than twice as many designs as comparisons, so a quantum algorithm can realize rank laws that no classical algorithm with the same budget can. We determine the exact quantum optimum with one comparison for every number of designs and every good-enough set. For selecting the best of n designs, the optimal success probability with one quantum comparison is approximately 3.30/n for large n, compared with 2/n for one classical comparison. When the best design is sought, one quantum comparison gives a higher alignment probability than two classical comparisons whenever there are more than nine designs.

papers.title: Inference on the Value of Policy Improvement in Adaptive Experiments
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop an asymptotically normal estimator for the value of policy improvement (VPI) under adaptively collected data. This value, which is defined as the gap between the value of the best treatment policy in a class and that of a baseline policy, gauges whether or not it is worth deploying a personalized treatment policy. Building an estimator for the VPI is naturally more difficult than estimating the value of a fixed policy. This is because, in addition to contending with the correlated data and decaying propensities associated with adaptive experiments, any estimator must also handle the non-regularity, or lack of pathwise differentiability, of the underlying estimand when the optimal policy is non-unique. Our proposed estimator works by sequentially fitting a weighted empirical welfare maximizing policy on historical data and then evaluating it using inverse propensity weighting on future samples. We neither assume that the optimal policy is unique nor make a margin assumption on the underlying heterogeneous treatment effects. A key difficulty in analyzing our estimator is showing that the regret incurred through policy learning is asymptotically smaller than the standard error of the estimator. We accomplish this by showing faster regret rates for policy learning under decaying propensities, which may be of independent interest. We not only evaluate the coverage of our estimator on a mix of synthetic and semi-synthetic data, but also employ it to estimate the VPI in an adaptive experiment evaluating the efficacy of job assistance programs in Jordan due to Caria et al. Although our estimates are generally more conservative than their hierarchical Bayesian analysis, which assumes that the optimal policy is unique, we still corroborate the benefits of personalization amongst Syrian refugees.

papers.title: Explicit counterexamples to Frank-Loss optimizer conjectures for critical Dirac and vector Sobolev inequalities
papers.abstract: Frank and Loss proposed critical Sobolev inequalities for the Dirac operator and for vector fields. They conjectured optimality of their spinorial family and wrote that it is conceivable that the higher-dimensional Loss-Yau potential is an optimizer. Wang and Zhang recently disproved both optimizer claims using direct comparison and instability arguments. We compute closed-form quotients for two elementary families of explicit competitors with strictly smaller quotients. For every $d\geq2$, the spinorial competitor is a constant spinor multiplied by a scalar Aubin-Talenti optimizer. For every $d\geq3$, the vector competitor is the planar azimuthal field \[ A_d(x)=\frac{d}{(1+\lvert x\rvert^2)^2} (-x_2,x_1,0,\ldots,0). \] It lies in the nonlinear gauge and its quotient is computed in closed form. For every odd $d\geq3$, it gives an explicit proof of nonoptimality of the higher-dimensional Loss-Yau-Dunne-Min potential. In dimension three, this field is a specific member of the competitor family of Wang and Zhang: it is a linear combination of the Loss-Yau potential and its reflected twin. Its axisymmetry gives a negative answer to their question about minimization within the $\mathrm{SO}(2)\times 1$-invariant class.

papers.title: Translational tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets
papers.abstract: The periodic tiling conjecture asserts that if a bounded set $Ω\subset \mathbb R^d$ of finite measure tiles $\mathbb R^d$ by translations, then it admits at least one fully periodic tiling. This conjecture was proved to hold in $\mathbb R$ by Lagarias and Wang, and was recently disproved by Greenfeld and Tao in sufficiently high dimensions. Its discrete analogue in $\mathbb Z^2$ was proved by Bhattacharya, whereas the conjecture in $\mathbb R^2$ remains open. In this paper, we analyze the structure of tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets: bounded open sets in $\mathbb R^2$ whose boundary is a finite union of line segments parallel to the axes. We prove that every such tiling that is topologically minimal is weakly periodic. Moreover, we show that if an axis-parallel polygonal set $Ω$ tiles $\mathbb{R}^2$ then it admits a quasi-periodic tiling (i.e., a finite union of translated lattices). The proofs combine geometric decompositions of tilings with rational approximation and discrete tiling theory. As a consequence, we obtain that the translational tiling problem for axis-parallel polygonal sets with real algebraic vertex coordinates is decidable.

papers.title: $6$ powers of $2$ in the Linnik--Goldbach problem
papers.abstract: Linnik's approximation to Goldbach's conjecture concerns the representation of sufficiently large even integers as the sum of two primes and a bounded number of powers of two. We prove that $6$ powers of $2$ suffice unconditionally and that $5$ suffice under the GRH, improving previous works.

papers.title: Violation of Bell-type Inequality in the Hanbury Brown-Twiss (HBT) Toy-Model: Quantum Correlations beyond Local-Realism
papers.abstract: The Hanbury Brown-Twiss (HBT) effect marked a significant milestone in quantum optics by illustrating that intensity correlations can reveal inherently quantum features of light. Motivated by the structure of the original 8-mode HBT interferometer, we develop a simplified 4-mode toy-model that captures its essential physical ingredients while significantly reducing analytical complexity. Our toy-model provides an intuitive and well-structured framework for examining the desired correlation functions. We investigate whether our toy-model can exhibit genuinely non-classical behaviour by formulating and applying a Bell-type inequality tailored to its specific measurement configuration. Our analysis shows that the correlations generated by the toy-model violate the inequality, indicating the presence of non-local features that are incompatible with any classical hidden-variable description. The results highlight the power of simplified models in uncovering fundamental aspects of non-classicality in optical systems.

papers.title: Minimal Product Sets in Finite Metacyclic Groups
papers.abstract: Minimum product-set problems ask how small a product of two subsets of prescribed cardinalities can be in a finite group. Although the problem is completely understood for finite abelian groups, exact results in the nonabelian setting are available only for particular classes. We determine the minimum product-set function $μ_G$ for every finite metacyclic group, without assuming that the relevant cyclic extension splits. Our proof converts the extremal problem into a finite recursive arithmetic description of the feasible cardinality vectors of subset trios. The recursion combines the subgroup structure of finite metacyclic groups with the structural classification of maximal critical subset trios. The resulting characterization recovers the previously known formulas for abelian and nilpotent groups, dihedral groups, and nonabelian groups of order $pq$. It also yields metacyclic examples in which the minimum product-set size lies strictly between the classical lower and upper arithmetic bounds for finite solvable groups. For faithful split metacyclic groups, we further show that requiring one factor to be symmetric, contain the identity, and generate the whole group can force a strictly larger product set than the unrestricted minimum. The latter constraint admits a vertex-isoperimetric interpretation on connected Cayley graphs.

papers.title: GPU-Accelerated Nested Schur-Complement Solvers for Atmospheric Flow Simulations Using Horizontally-Explicit, Vertically-Implicit Schemes and Discontinuous Galerkin Methods
papers.abstract: Horizontally explicit, vertically implicit (HEVI) time integration removes the acoustic time-step restriction imposed by fine vertical grids in nonhydrostatic atmospheric models, but requires fast solvers for the resulting vertical linear systems, especially on GPUs. We present GPU-accelerated nested Schur-complement solvers for these systems for a split-form discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method on Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto (LGL) nodes applied to the compressible Euler equations with gravity. In time, we use a Rosenbrock-W method, a linearly implicit Runge-Kutta scheme that retains its order and stability with approximate Jacobians. This allows a sparse vertical Jacobian that captures vertical acoustic waves and gravity on curvilinear meshes with orography and decouples into independent column systems. The solvers are nested: a global Schur complement (static condensation) exploits the LGL sparsity to condense each column onto a few element-edge unknowns, and a local Schur complement eliminates all variables but the vertical momentum within each element, exploiting that the pressure depends only on the potential-temperature density. We propose and analyze two condensation strategies, which lead to banded and block-tridiagonal reduced systems. The resulting HEVI schemes conserve total mass and potential-temperature density to round-off. The solvers are implemented for CPUs and GPUs in TrixiAtmo.jl, the atmospheric extension of Trixi.jl. We verify high-order convergence with linear inertia-gravity waves in a 2D channel and demonstrate robustness on the sphere with the baroclinic instability, a mountain-induced baroclinic instability, and the DCMIP-2025 gap-flow and vortex-shedding cases. For the baroclinic instability without orography, the scheme achieves 18.8 and 2.9 simulated years per day at 100 and 50 km resolution on one NVIDIA GH200 GPU in double precision.

papers.title: Two-axis twisting by two-photon exchange: rate, depth, and the self-Kerr constraint
papers.abstract: The coherent exchange of pairs of quanta between two bosonic modes is equivalent, up to a numerical factor, to the generator of two-axis twisting, which attains Heisenberg scaling of the squeezing; we determine how much of that equivalence survives in a realistic nonlinear medium. In any such medium the exchange term is accompanied by a local Kerr nonlinearity, and within a sector of fixed particle number the Hamiltonian depends on a single dimensionless ratio of the effective Kerr strength to the exchange strength. We derive two criteria governing this ratio and show that they are independent. The first is the rate at which squeezing is generated: the exponential rate follows in closed form, vanishes exactly when the two strengths are equal in magnitude, and recovers as the square root of the detuning from that point. The second is the depth to which squeezing can be driven: at fixed particle number the attainable depth is a function of the anisotropy of the mean-field saddle alone, reaches the full two-axis-twisting value only for the isotropic saddle, and is independent of the rate, parameter sets sharing the same anisotropy but differing in rate by a sizeable factor giving depths that agree to every printed digit. The closed-form Gaussian dynamics reveals a pitfall: extracting rates from short-time data overestimates them by more than a factor of two unless the saddle is isotropic. An isotropic cubic nonlinearity imposes the value of the ratio where the rate vanishes, so realizing two-axis twisting by pair exchange requires detuning it; a moderate mismatch already recovers almost all of the optimal depth. We also explain why the constraint has not surfaced before: at two quanta the self-Kerr shifts the two coupled states equally, so the two twisting Hamiltonians are rigorously indistinguishable, the degeneracy being lifted only from four quanta.

papers.title: An optimization problem for $δ'$ leaky stars
papers.abstract: We consider singular Schrödinger operators with an attractive $δ'$ interaction of strength $β$ supported by a star graph and prove that the ground-state eigenvalue is uniquely maximized by stars of the maximum symmetry. Two different proofs are presented, one for an even number of edges using a comparison to the $δ$ interaction star, the other general based on Birman-Schwinger technique.

papers.title: Tribonacci numbers that are palindromic concatenations of two distinct repdigits
papers.abstract: Let $(T_n)_{n\ge1}$ be the Tribonacci sequence, defined by $T_1=T_2=1$, $T_3=2$, and $T_n=T_{n-1}+T_{n-2}+T_{n-3}$ for $n\ge4$. In this paper, we study the Tribonacci numbers whose decimal representation is a palindromic concatenation of two distinct repdigits, that is, numbers of the shape $\overline{d_1\cdots d_1\,d_2\cdots d_2\,d_1\cdots d_1}$ with $1\le d_1\le9$, $0\le d_2\le9$, $d_1\ne d_2$. We prove that no Tribonacci number is a palindromic concatenation of two distinct repdigits. The proof combines lower bounds for linear forms in logarithms, the Baker-Davenport reduction method, and a finite computational verification.

papers.title: Parabolically induced representations of $GL_n(O_l)$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be the ring of integers of a non-Archimedean local field with uniformizer $\varpi$, and let $\mathcal O_\ell=\mathcal O/\varpi^\ell\mathcal O$ for $\ell\geq1$. In this article, we study representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_\ell)$ parabolically induced from characters of the Borel subgroup $\mathrm{B}_n(\mathcal O_\ell)$. For $n=3$, we establish a criterion for the irreducibility of these induced representations in terms of the relative conductors of the inducing characters. Motivated by this result, we formulate a conjecture characterizing the irreducibility of such representations for arbitrary $n$. We further show that when all inducing characters are equal, the resulting induced representation is not multiplicity-free, implying that the corresponding triple $(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_\ell),\mathrm{B}_n(\mathcal O_\ell),χ)$ is not a Gelfand pair. Finally, we study the irreducible decomposition of these representations for $\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathcal O_\ell)$ when two relative conductors attain their maximal values. Using the decomposition theory for $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathcal O_\ell)$, we describe the irreducible constituents and determine their dimensions.

papers.title: Failure of dimension drop for harmonic measure on Ahlfors regular boundaries of dimension close to $1$
papers.abstract: For every $0<s<1$ we construct a compact $s$-Ahlfors regular set $K\subset\mathbb C$ for which harmonic measure of $\mathbb C\setminus K$ with pole at infinity is comparable to $\mathcal H^s|_K$. In particular, there is no dimension drop for any dimension $s<1$. The construction is $N$-adic and based on configurations close to the $N$-th roots of unity. We adjust the positions of the children by small polynomial deformations so that the logarithmic potential of the natural Bernoulli measure becomes constant in the limit. A first-mode correction gives the range $s<2/3$, while corrections of arbitrary finite order yield the full range $0<s<1$.

papers.title: On the inverse Goldbach problem
papers.abstract: We establish two quantitative results concerning additive decompositions of the set $\mathbb{P}$ of primes. First, we prove that, if $A,B\subseteq\mathbb N$ have at least two elements and $A+B$ differs from the primes by only finitely many elements, then $$ \frac{\sqrt{x}}{\log x}\ll A(x),B(x) \ll \sqrt{x}. $$ Second, we show that, if $A,B,C\subseteq\mathbb N$ have at least two elements each, then $$ ((A+B+C)\mathbin{\bigtriangleup}\mathbb P)(x) \gg \frac{\sqrt{x}}{(\log x)^2}. $$ An analogous estimate is obtained for sumsets of $k\ge 3$ sets. The proofs use Montgomery's large sieve, Gallagher's larger sieve, a mean-value argument for a certain multiplicative function, and a submultiplicative sumset inequality.

papers.title: Small-speed solitary-wave stability and global well-posedness for a Bessel-regularized Airy equation
papers.abstract: We prove orbital stability of minimizing solitary waves at sufficiently small positive speeds for an Airy equation with a quadratic interaction filtered by a Bessel potential of order one. The stability hypotheses are verified: constrained minimization gives one negative direction, the small-speed KdV limit and operator-norm perturbation of the profile resolvent give a one-dimensional translation kernel, and a differentiable rescaled branch with uniformly bounded derivative gives a positive slope of the quadratic invariant. A conserved Lyapunov functional then proves orbital stability in the three-halves-derivative energy space and the perturbation also gives uniqueness of centered minimizers at small speed. The dynamical framework is supplied by a direct Bourgain-space bilinear estimate, local well-posedness in the square-integrable class, unconditional uniqueness from one-quarter derivative onward, and global well-posedness in the half-derivative energy space. For every prescribed positive speed, constrained minimization constructs smooth positive profiles that are symmetric, strictly monotone away from their center, and exponentially localized. At general positive speeds the stability criterion remains conditional on nondegeneracy and the slope condition.

papers.title: Nonperturbative optomechanics with thin, weakly reflective intracavity dielectrics
papers.abstract: Levitated dielectric sensors are often treated as perturbative probes of a pre-existing optical field. We show that this picture fails for a novel sensor geometry: a dielectric plate whose transverse extent captures the full optical mode. Even an optically thin sensor with modest refractive index can heavily restructure the intracavity fields, effectively partitioning a cavity into two subcavities with substantial cross-coupling and producing new optical resonances and trapping sites with properties which deviate from the standard intuition. Conventional perturbative expressions for the cavity frequency shift and optomechanical coupling depart from the exact solution at thicknesses as small as $\simλ/(10n)$. Furthermore, cavity locking decreases the coupling and increases the trap stiffness by orders of magnitude, and the coupled subcavity structure permits appreciable optical cooling at zero detuning, a distinct behavior unique to this nonperturbative regime. These effects, sharing a common origin, establish a distinct regime of cavity optomechanics in which the sensor is no longer merely a probe of the cavity field, but an element that helps define it.

papers.title: Variational Minimization of Almost Strong Zero Modes in Parafermionic Wires
papers.abstract: Strongly interacting fermionic chains obeying a $Z_n$ symmetry can host topological phases with highly degenerate ground-state manifolds. The different ground states are connected by strongly bound fractionalized edge modes called parafermionic zero modes. While exactly preserved under time evolution at zero temperature, interactions lead to a destabilization of these modes at finite energy densities, and, given a generic Hamiltonian, obtaining the lifetime of these modes is often impossible as it requires knowledge of the full spectrum of the Hamiltonian or long time evolutions. Here, we propose a novel quantum-inspired algorithm that can be used to variationally search for these almost strong zero modes in generic parafermionic chain models. We demonstrate analytically and numerically that our ansatz faithfully reproduces the exact results and finds strongly bound parafermionic operators in the non-integrable Kitaev-Hubbard chain and chiral Potts model. Our results further allow us to verify the existence of a true strong zero mode in the symmetrical limit of the chiral Potts model for $Z_3$-parafermions.

papers.title: Spatial interference changes the symmetry class of a Josephson element
papers.abstract: Spatial interference can break the inversion symmetry of an effective Josephson potential even in a laterally homogeneous junction with inversion-symmetric local energy. We derive a general criterion based on harmonic-dependent complex spatial form factors: a single local harmonic remains a shifted cosine, whereas multiple harmonics can acquire phases incompatible with any common inversion center, permitting cubic interactions and three-wave mixing. Phase reflection reverses all odd-order expansion coefficients about corresponding minima while preserving the even-order ones. For a capacitively shunted junction at fixed charging energy and arbitrary offset charge, it also preserves the complete quantum spectrum, enabling reversal of the odd nonlinear sector without spectral retuning. A centered cross junction with multiple local harmonics is one concrete example. Within the imposed-field model, a three-component magnetic field can generate an inversion-asymmetric effective potential, and reversing an odd number of field components exactly reflects it without changing the quantum spectrum of the capacitively shunted junction.

papers.title: Fractional symplectic Fourier transforms and their actions on function and distribution spaces
papers.abstract: We consider symplectic analogues of the fractional Fourier transforms and obtain convenient representations in terms of Bargmann transforms and Wigner distributions. We show that they act as homeomorphisms on Schwartz spaces, the space of square integrable functions, the space of tempered distributions, and on Fourier-invariant Gelfand-Shilov spaces and their corresponding distribution spaces. More generally, we establish their homeomorphism properties on a broad class of spaces defined through (Wigner-)Hermite expansions. In addition, we prove that these transforms preserve norms on Schatten-von Neumann symbol classes associated with the Weyl calculus.

papers.title: Molecular Vibronic Complexity as a Quantum Resource for Optimal Control: Nonadiabatic Mixing Creates Protected Coherence Subspaces in Dissipative Environments
papers.abstract: In molecules, electronic coherence typically decays within a few hundred femtoseconds, a timescale usually attributed to the environment. We show that it is set to a large extent by which coherences are excited: the molecule can host coherences that the bath barely sees, and optimal control can find and exploit them. Using gradient-based optimal control (GRAPE) with Redfield dynamics, we maximize the total vibronic coherence between the electronic ground and an optically bright electronic excited state in a three-state model with nonadiabatic features, in two regimes of low and high nonadiabatic mixing and for different system-bath coupling strengths. The Liouvillian spectrum reveals, in both regimes, a well-separated coherence mode with substantial ground-bright character that decays on a picosecond timescale. This mode is protected by mixing with the dark state, which brings the geometry of the optically accessible excited state close to that of the ground state and thus weakens its coupling to the bath. Without prior information, GRAPE finds this mode and keeps the photoexcited wave packet near the Franck-Condon region. At equal fluence, it increases the coherence at 800 fs by more than two orders of magnitude over a Gaussian pulse at the weakest coupling, and by many more at stronger coupling. The Liouvillian predicts the bath dependence of the long-lived coherence to within 1\%, and a Gaussian pulse tuned to the mode frequency comes within 10\% of the best pulse found. Beyond two-level and spin systems, our study puts forward the vibronic structure of molecules as a route to protected coherence subspaces, identifying a dark-state protection mechanism and a design criterion based on molecular parameters. These results lay the groundwork for our goal of using vibronic molecular systems as a resource for long-lived, controllable coherences in molecular quantum information science.

papers.title: Remarks on the disjoint minimal graphs conjecture
papers.abstract: It is known that there can be at most 3 disjoint nontrivial minimal graphs in R^3 with 0 boundary values, and conjectured that there can be at most 2. We explore properties that the graphs would have if there were 3.

papers.title: Lie Algebras of Locally Finite Derivations over Fields of Positive Characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a field of positive characteristic, and let $A$ be a finitely generated commutative associative $F$-algebra. We study Lie subalgebras of $Der \, A$ generated by locally finite derivations. We prove that if all commutators of the generators satisfy a natural local finiteness condition, then the associative subalgebra of $End_{F}\, A$ generated by these derivations is finite-dimensional.

papers.title: Adaptive Robust Confidence Sets in High Dimensions
papers.abstract: We study adaptive confidence sets for mean vectors of multivariate Gaussians with identity covariance under Huber contamination when the contamination proportion is unknown. We show that an information-theoretically optimal adaptive confidence set can be constructed by simultaneously quantifying uncertainty across all one-dimensional projections. The resulting confidence set achieves the optimal diameter and reveals a substantial adaptation cost compared with the minimax estimation error. Although statistically optimal, this construction is computationally infeasible. We establish a Statistical Query (SQ) lower bound showing that achieving diameter $O(m^{-1/2})$ requires either exponentially many queries or query tolerance $d^{-Ω(m)}$. Thus, in contrast to robust mean estimation, adaptation to the unknown contamination proportion incurs both a statistical cost and a computational barrier within the SQ framework. Finally, we give a low-degree moment-matching algorithm that constructs an adaptive confidence set using $d^{O(m)}$ samples and time. Its diameter bound contains an additional $O(m^{-1/2})$ term beyond the information-theoretic rate, matching the dependence on $m$ in the SQ lower bound. Together, these results characterize the statistical limits of adaptive robust confidence sets under Huber contamination and quantify a computational barrier within the SQ framework.

papers.title: Multivariate stable mixing local limit theorem for intermittent diffeomorphisms and flows
papers.abstract: We prove mixing local limit theorems for dynamical systems in the superdiffusive regime where there is convergence to a multivariate stable law (including the nonstandard domain of the central limit theorem). We apply our results to d-dimensional observables for intermittent maps and solenoids, as well as intermittent semiflows and flows.

papers.title: A Smooth Autonomous Flow with Exponential Mixing on the Three-Torus
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth autonomous divergence-free vector field on $\mathbb{T}^3$ whose flow is exponentially mixing with respect to Lebesgue measure. This answers an open question about smooth autonomous exponential mixing in three dimensions. Starting from an exponentially mixing Anosov suspension flow, we perform surgery near four periodic orbits and show that the resulting manifold is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{T}^3$. The resulting vector field has exactly sixteen hyperbolic equilibria. We also prove a general transfer theorem that preserves exponential mixing under certain singular changes of coordinates.

papers.title: Sharp Rogers--Shephard Inequalities for Rényi Entropy
papers.abstract: We establish sharp weighted Rogers--Shephard inequalities for Rényi differential entropy. For independent copies $X,X'$ of a log-concave random vector in $\R^n$, we prove $h_p(aX-bX')\le h_p(X)+n\log(a+b)$ for all $a,b>0$ and $1\le p\le\infty$, where orders $1$ and $\infty$ correspond to Shannon entropy and min-entropy, respectively. The Shannon case settles the entropic Rogers--Shephard conjecture of Madiman and Kontoyiannis and its higher-dimensional formulation. For $1\le p<\infty$, equality holds precisely for invertible affine images of random vectors with independent exponential coordinates. At $p=\infty$, the larger equality class is characterized by possibly extended-valued convex potentials that are positively homogeneous of degree one. For every $0<p<1$, uniform laws on sufficiently high-dimensional simplices violate the unweighted bound. Thus $p=1$ is the critical order for this bound to hold in every dimension. The proof combines weighted convex intersections with an exponential lift to a log-affine probability density. At the Shannon endpoint, this lift yields an exact deficit decomposition with a conditional mutual information term for an additive channel with asymmetric Laplace noise.

papers.title: Solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with small $x_3$: a spectral approach
papers.abstract: We count the integral solutions of x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D weighted by Phi(x_3/M), for M smaller than sqrt(D). Such solutions correspond to binary quadratic forms of discriminant D, and the count becomes a sum, over the geodesics of discriminant D, of a function of their distance to the point i, which we evaluate by the spectral theory of automorphic forms. For square D=n^2 the geodesics run from cusp to cusp, and Hecke theory reduces them to a single geodesic. For every n and both parities of x_3 we obtain an asymptotic formula with error O(n^{1+theta+eps} M^{-1/2}), theta=7/64, using the Kim-Sarnak bound and the large sieve of Deshouillers and Iwaniec; it is non-trivial for M >= n^{71/96+eps}. This improves the range n^{5/6+eps} of the elementary method and confirms the corrected main term of the author's earlier work. For non-square D=f^2 D_0 the geodesics are closed, and a Hecke relation for their traces reduces everything to the fundamental discriminant D_0. For odd D_0 we obtain an error O(D^eps f^{1+theta} D_0^{2/3} M^{-1/2}), using the formulas of Duke-Imamoglu-Toth and Baruch-Mao together with Young's cubic moment. For D = 5 mod 8 this counts all solutions, and the range M >= D^{1/2-1/1332} of Friedlander and Iwaniec improves to M >= D^{4/9+eps}. This paper was written in collaboration with Claude (Opus 5.5, High), an AI model developed by Anthropic.

papers.title: Poissonian Pair Correlation for Bernoulli Orbits
papers.abstract: Let \(α, β\in \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}\), and let \((ξ_n)_{n \ge 1}\) be independent random variables taking the values \(α\) and \(β\) with equal probability. We study the random walk \[X_n = ξ_1 + \cdots + ξ_n \pmod 1\] and present a deterministic Diophantine condition on \((α, β)\) that implies almost sure Poisson pair correlation. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result providing explicit examples in this framework where the increment measure is purely discrete. The classical Fourier contraction method fails in this setting; a different approach is required. Our proof uses the parabolic geometry of returns to \(1\) and an exact covariance formula for overlapping blocks.

papers.title: Symplectic four-manifolds and hyperbolic $π$-orbifolds
papers.abstract: We construct closed symplectic 4-manifolds admitting the structure of hyperbolic $π$-orbifold, addressing LeBrun's conjecture. Our simplest example has Euler characteristic $304$, is tessellated by $64$ copies of the right-angled hyperbolic $120$-cell and admits a four-fold branched covering over a product of two surfaces of genus $4$.

papers.title: Sharp conditions for fully nonlinear equations with $(n-1)$-Hessian matrix: Part II. $k$-Hessian case
papers.abstract: We study admissible entire subsolutions and radial boundary blow-up solutions of $S_k^{\frac1k}[ΔuI-D^2u]=f(u)+g(u)|Du|^q$ for $1\leq k<n$, continuing our study of the determinant case $k=n$ in Part I. Under structural assumptions on the continuous, non-decreasing coefficients $f$ and $g$, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of entire subsolutions when $q<2$. Our results cover the non-Lipschitz case $0<q<1$ with a possibly vanishing zero-order term, the gradient-singular case $q<0$, and sign-changing gradient coefficients. We also characterize finite-radius blow-up of radial solutions and derive two-sided estimates for the blow-up radius, as well as pointwise upper bounds for their profiles in terms of inverse Keller--Osserman functions.

papers.title: Counting subspaces with prescribed Welch sums
papers.abstract: Let $q=2^n$ with $n=2m+1$ for an integer $m\ge1$, and let ${\mathbb F}_q$ be the finite field with $q$ elements. Let $W_n(x)=x^{2^m+3}$ be the Welch function on ${\mathbb F}_q$. For $1\le k\le n$ and $b\in{\mathbb F}_q$, denote by $N_{n,k}(b)$ the number of $k$-dimensional ${\mathbb F}_2$-subspaces $E$ of $\mathbb F}_q$ such that \[ \sum_{x\in E}W_n(x)=b. \] In this paper, we determine $N_{n,k}(b)$ for all $k$. The only nontrivial case is $k=3$, for which the answer is given in terms of a binary Kloosterman sum. As a consequence, we prove a recent conjecture of Hou and Zhao on the third-order sum-freedom of the Welch function.

papers.title: Sharp conditions for fully nonlinear equations with $(n-1)$-Hessian matrix: Part I. Monge--Ampère case
papers.abstract: We study positive $(n-1)$-convex entire subsolutions of the normalized real $(n-1)$ Monge--Ampère equation $\operatorname{det}^{\frac1n}\bigl(ΔuI-D^2u\bigr)=f(u)+g(u)|Du|^q$ in $\mathbb R^n$. Under two sets of structural assumptions on the continuous, non-decreasing coefficients $f$ and $g$, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of entire subsolutions when $q<2-\frac1n$. Our results cover the pure-gradient degenerate case $f\equiv0$ with $0<q<1$, the gradient-singular case $q<0$, and the case where $g$ changes sign. For $q=2-\frac1n$, we recover the Keller--Osserman condition for the gradient-independent equation, prove nonexistence when $g$ is eventually positive, and obtain an exponentially weighted condition when $g$ has a nonpositive limit at infinity. This is the first of two companion papers and treats the determinant case.

papers.title: Notes on Uniform Policy Score Bounds and Lipschitz Continuity for Truncated Gaussian, Product Cauchy, Boltzmann, and Softmax Policies
papers.abstract: We establish uniform score bounds and Lipschitz continuity for truncated Gaussian, Cauchy, Boltzmann, and softmax policies under explicitly stated parameterizations.

papers.title: When do explicit penalties improve flow matching?
papers.abstract: Flow matching can learn structure directly from data, raising the question of when additional constraints improve generation. We study penalties that encode such constraints, with physics-informed flow matching as a motivating example. Satisfying a constraint more closely need not make the generated distribution more accurate. We therefore compare penalised and unpenalised generative modelling through their expected squared $2$-Wasserstein error. Our analysis covers both vector-valued and functional data in a Hilbert-space setting. We first derive geometric criteria that account for constraint violations and the distribution of samples after projection onto the constraint set. We then solve the statistical comparison explicitly for specific velocity-field classes and constraints via flow matching. In this model, penalisation improves accuracy exactly when the reduction in estimation variance outweighs the increase in squared bias. The resulting formula shows how this trade-off depends on sample size, the model class, the noise schedule, and the penalty weight.

papers.title: Total Cohomology of Hilbert schemes of Orbisurfaces I: Reduction to Stacky Loci
papers.abstract: We generalize Nakajima's theory of Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces to Hilbert schemes of points on \textit{orbisurfaces}, and obtain initial factorization based on stratification by stabilizers. While the usual formula is retained for the trivial stabilizer stratum and for those strata of codimension $1$, genuine difficulties arise with stacky points strata. In the local picture of an isolated stacky point, the theory reduce to the study of $\Quot^\bfv[\CC^2/G]$ for a \textit{small} finite subgroup of $GL_2(\CC)$. The generating series for their total cohomology is a geometric correction of the generating series for total cohomology of ordinary smooth surface schemes. In addition, we obtain an action of the Borel-Moore homology of the punctual fibre stacks on the total Hilbert cohomology by virtual correspondences, in analogy with the Fock space description in Nakajima's theory. The punctual fibre stacks are genuinely different from the symmetric stack, and has natural realizations via motivic integration.

papers.title: **Winding number forces universal synchronisation**
papers.abstract: We prove that two completely different oscillators synchronise through arbitrarily weak reciprocal impulses. Any two planar oscillators with hyperbolic attracting limit cycles and equal natural periods lock stably one-to-one under translation impulses with generic directions and a suitable range of positive strength ratios, whatever their vector fields, limit cycles and transverse contraction rates. The mechanism is topological: the winding of the asymptotic phase gradient forces phase advances and delays, and the relative winding number of an effective impulse field gives lower bounds on attracting and unstable locked states. Equal periods are not essential: locking persists under small nonzero mismatches, with persistence and loss governed by a shifted phase balance. The analysis covers the full state-dependent impulsive dynamics, including transverse stability. Nearly simultaneous emissions may make the return discontinuous; under an explicit regularity condition the global return has a normally attracting Lipschitz invariant circle with topologically Morse--Smale dynamics.

papers.title: Teams, Truthmakers, Translations
papers.abstract: We present a faithful translation from Aloni's logic BSL into a classical modal logic over semilattices combining ideas from earlier modal translations of truthmaker semantics with algebraic representation theory. We show how our method can also be made to work for other current hyperintensional logics. Finally, we place our results in a broader setting of translating hyperintensional logics into classical modal ones, and discuss applications and new challenges that arise for both areas of philosophical logic connected in this way.

papers.title: Bipartite edge frustration of nut graphs: proofs and constructions
papers.abstract: The bipartite edge frustration of a graph $G$, $\varphi(G)$, is the minimum number of edges that must be removed from $G$ to obtain a graph that is bipartite. Core graphs are singular graphs on $2$ or more vertices, for which the kernel of the adjacency matrix contains a full eigenvector. A nut graph is a core graph of nullity one. Nut graphs $G$ are non-bipartite. It is proved here that $\varphi(G) \geq 2$ if $G$ is a nut graph, i.e. every nut graph requires deletion of at least two edges to produce a bipartite graph. In addition, we give a constructive proof that for every integer $k \geq 2$ there exist infinitely many chemical nut graphs $G$ with $\varphi(G) = k$. Furthermore, for $3 \leq d \leq 8$, the values $k$, for which a $d$-regular nut graph $G$ with $\varphi(G) = k$ exists, are characterised. It is shown here that for every integer $k \geq 2$ there exist infinitely many cubic polyhedral nut graphs $G$ with $\varphi(G) = k$. Two ways of producing larger nut graphs from smaller are described: the cut and frustration constructions. One straightforward consequence is that total double subdivision of a nut graph (i.e. simultaneous insertion of two degree-$2$ vertices into every edge) yields a nut graph.

papers.title: A greedy double-block nonlinear Bregman-Kaczmarz method for nonlinear equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a greedy double-block nonlinear Bregman-Kaczmarz method to efficiently find sparse solutions of nonlinear equations. The theoretical convergence rate of the proposed method is established under certain assumptions. Numerical experiments illustrate the competitive performance and superiority of the proposed method.

papers.title: Coprime pairs with equal sum of divisors, assuming smooth shifted primes
papers.abstract: Let $h(x)$ be the number of pairs $1\le a<b<x$ with $\gcd(a,b)=1$ and $σ(a)=σ(b)$. Erdős Problem #824 asks whether $h(x)>x^{2-o(1)}$. By an argument of Pollack and Pomerance, this follows if for every fixed $δ>0$ there are $y^{1-o(1)}$ primes $p\le5y$ with $p+1$ free of prime factors exceeding $y^δ$. We write this implication out with explicit parameters and formalize it in Lean 4. We then check that the argument of the recent OpenAI preprint "Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers", which claims the corresponding statement for $p-1$, applies to $p+1$ after a change of sign in two of its sections. Consequently $h(x)=x^{2-o(1)}$, conditionally on the correctness of that preprint, which has not been refereed and whose main new estimates we have not independently verified.

papers.title: Blow-down and immediate onset of positivity in the Neumann problem for (super-)fast diffusion equations
papers.abstract: For the degenerate parabolic equation $u_t=\nabla\cdot (u^{m-1}\nabla u)$, the homogeneous Neumann problem in smoothly bounded domains $Ω\subset {\mathbb{R}}^n$ is considered in the (super-fast) diffusion range when $m\in (-\infty,1)$. Upper and lower estimates for solutions are inferred by means of two Moser-type iterations, and optimality properties of these bounds are derived using comparison arguments. On the basis of the accordingly obtained information on regularization into spaces of bounded and uniformly positive functions, a result on global solvability in an associated initial-boundary value problem is achieved for all nonnegative and nontrivial initial data belonging to $L^1(Ω) \cap \bigcup_{s>n(1-m)/2} L^s(Ω)$.

papers.title: The entry-exit function and nilpotent corrections in multidimensional slow-fast systems
papers.abstract: We study multidimensional entry-exit phenomena in slow-fast systems whose fast linearization contains a nilpotent component. We show that the classical spectral balance still determines the exit point as $\varepsilon \to 0$, however the nilpotent component induces an algebraic amplification invisible to the spectrum, producing a $\varepsilon|\log\varepsilon|$-shift of the exit point for $0 <\varepsilon \ll 1$. We further extend the analysis to systems with several spectral branches and show that mode dominance follows a hierarchical, lexicographic selection principle: accumulated spectral growth determines the leading order, while the nilpotent component resolves degeneracies between spectrally equivalent modes.

papers.title: Geodesic Models for Loop Spaces on Riemannian Manifolds
papers.abstract: A topological group, defined in terms of ``composable minimal geodesics'' is constructed and shown to be homotopy equivalent to the pointed loop space of a path-connected, simply connected Riemannian manifold $M$ of positive convexity radius. This construction is analogous to John Milnor's free group model for the pointed loop space of a connected simplicial complex. Related models built from composable minimal geodesics are also obtained for the free loop space of $M$ and for the space of maps from any finite two-dimensional CW-complex into $M$.

papers.title: Non-Stationary Quantum Systems Associated with Stationary Scattering in One Dimension
papers.abstract: Stationary scattering admits a dynamical formulation in which the scattering data are extracted from the evolution operator for an effective non-stationary and non-unitary quantum system. This provides a mathematical method of solving scattering problems. We consider the possibility of realizing such a quantum system and relating the scattering information to outcomes of quantum measurements performed on it. To this end, we examine stationary scattering problems in one dimension where the scattering data consist of reflection and transmission amplitudes and the corresponding effective quantum system is a non-unitary two-level system. The states of this system identify points in a Bloch sphere $S^2$ and their evolution yields trajectories in $S^2$. Quantum measurements turn out to be capable of providing information about the reflection amplitudes. We identify configurations displaying reflectionlessness with situations where one or both of the poles of $S^2$ undergo cyclic evolutions. Spectral singularities and coherent perfect absorption correspond to dynamical spin flips which map one of the poles of $S^2$ to the other.

papers.title: Uniform adjacency-degree probes from differential rigidity
papers.abstract: We construct a fixed triangular family of noncommutative polynomials that spans the joint cyclic module of a real symmetric pair from any prescribed vector. In dimension at most $N$, when the second matrix has spectral diameter at most $N-1$, the family has $N(N+1)/2$ members, degree at most $N-1$, and a shared arithmetic circuit of size $O(N^2)$. No rank-dependent choice of coefficients is made. The proof uses a rational differential connection with a small self-adjoint residue: a primitive polynomial exterior vector for an invariant subspace must have an integer degree smaller than one. For connected trees, the probes and the pointed adjacency--degree reconstruction theorem give one explicit self-adjoint polynomial $p_N\in\mathbb{Z}\langle a,d\rangle$ whose trace separates all trees of order at most $N$. Its circuit has $O(N^2)$ gates, formal degree at most $3N-2$, and polynomial bit complexity. Only the original adjacency and degree matrices, the identity, and ordinary matrix arithmetic are used. A separate integer sum-of-squares construction gives a fixed positive semidefinite representative on which the all-one vector is cyclic; its degree is $O(N^2)$. A linear trace-degree lower bound shows that the first construction has the correct asymptotic degree scale.

papers.title: Continuum-many discontinuous actions of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on manifolds
papers.abstract: For any $n\geq 1$, we construct a continuum of non-conjugate actions by homeomorphisms of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on the $n$-sphere $S^{n}$ that do not extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{R})$. We do this by adapting a blow-up construction of Bowden and Mann. We motivate studying these actions and note down some related observations.

papers.title: Transport Polynomial Exactness for Direct ALE-DG Methods with Nonsmooth mesh motion: A Conservative Coefficient-Evolution Framework
papers.abstract: High-order direct arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian discontinuous Galerkin (ALE-DG) methods can suffer severe order reduction under nonsmooth mesh motion despite satisfying the geometric conservation law (GCL). To address this limitation, we propose a new ALE-DG framework applicable to moving triangular and quadrilateral meshes. This framework successfully overcomes the uniform Lipschitz constraint inherent in existing direct ALE-DG methods, retaining high-order accuracy even when the mesh-velocity gradients are unbounded. This capability is driven by transport polynomial exactness (TPE($k$)), which is a structural property stronger than the GCL. TPE($k$) ensures the exact transport of polynomials of degree at most $k$ under arbitrary mesh motion. To incorporate TPE($k$) into a direct ALE-DG method, we introduce a coefficient-evolution (CE) formulation. Reconciling strict local conservation, an indispensable requirement for accurate shock capturing, with the preservation of the TPE(\(k\)) property constitutes the principal technical challenge. We resolve this by evolving the coefficients using the third-order strong-stability-preserving Runge--Kutta method, paired with a conservative correction executed via Simpson's rule integration. Crucially, this correction strictly vanishes for exactly transported quadratic polynomials, thereby ensuring that our third-order scheme rigorously satisfies the TPE($2$) property. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed scheme retains third-order accuracy when the discrete mesh-velocity Lipschitz estimate grows as $\mathcal O(h^{-1})$, whereas a representative existing direct ALE-DG scheme exhibits order reduction under the same mesh motion. Tests with discontinuous solutions further demonstrate robust and high-resolution performance under random and Lagrangian mesh motions.

papers.title: Post-critically finite polynomials in characteristic $p$
papers.abstract: It follows from the compactness of the connectedness locus that the locus of PCF polynomials in the moduli space of polynomials of degree d (at least 2) over the complex number is a countable union of zero-dimensional subvarieties. Over fields of characteristic p the analogous claim is certainly false, so it is natural to ask how large the components of the PCF locus can be. We show that the components of the PCF locus in the moduli space of polynomials of degree d over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0 have dimension at most d/p and that this bound is sharp, in the strong sense that for every p and d there are infinitely many distinct PCF components whose dimension is the greatest integer no greater than this bound (except in the case $p=d=2$).

papers.title: Weighted Frames and the Douglas-Foias problem
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{T}=(T_1,\ldots,T_n)$ be a commuting tuple of bounded linear operators on a separable Hilbert space $\mathcal{K}$, and let $\{a_α\}_{α\in\mathbb{Z}_+^n}$ be strictly positive weights. Under mild assumptions on the weights, we characterize the weighted frame vectors and weighted Parseval frame vectors, that is, those vectors $ξ$ for which $\{a_α\mathbf{T}^αξ\}_{α\in\mathbb{Z}_+^n}$ is a frame or a Parseval frame. We reduce the problem to characterizing surjective module maps from the reproducing analytic Hilbert module associated with the weights onto the module $\mathcal{K}$, equipped with the module structure defined by $\mathbf{T}$. It is shown that weighted Parseval frame vectors differ by a unimodular scalar whenever they exist. If the kernel defined by the weights has the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property, then any two associated weighted frame vectors are similar whenever they exist. We also focus on the case of the Hardy kernel on the polydisc, that is, the case $a_α=1$ for all $α\in\mathbb{Z}^n_+$. This is related to the famous Douglas--Foias problem: whether two similar quotient modules of the Hardy spaces $H^2(\mathbb{D}^n)~(n>1)$ are equal. Our result shows that the answer is negative. This leads to the conclusion that frame vectors for representations of $\mathbb{Z}_+^n$ $(n>1)$ may fail to be similar. It means that, for the case $a_α=1$, there exists a tuple $\mathbf{T}=(T_1,\dots,T_n)$ with $n>1$ on $\mathcal{K}$ and two distinct frame vectors for $\mathbf{T}$ which are not similar.

papers.title: A trace lower bound for totally positive units in $\mathbb{Q}(ζ_p)^+$ and its application to fusion category
papers.abstract: Let $p = 4q + 1$ be a prime integer, where $q$ is an odd prime. Let $L = \mathbb{Q}(ζ_p)^+$ denote the maximal totally real subfield of the $p$-th cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(ζ_p)$. In this paper, we prove that if $U_L^+=U_L^2$ (i.e., every totally positive unit is a square in $L$), then for any non-trivial subfield $K \subseteq L$ and any non-trivial totally positive unit $\varepsilon \in U_K^+$, the absolute trace satisfies the sharp lower bound $\Tr_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\varepsilon) \ge p - 4$. As an application, we show that a spherical fusion category $\C$ with global dimension $\dim(\mathcal{C})=p=4q+1$ is pointed, where $2$ is a primitive root modulo $q$, or $p=4q+1<2^{22}$ and $p\neq 29$.

papers.title: On Mok's uniqueness problem of holomorphic isometries from complex unit balls of maximal dimension into classical domains
papers.abstract: We prove that every holomorphic isometric embedding, with respect to the Bergman metrics, from a complex unit ball of maximal dimension into irreducible classical bounded symmetric domain of rank at least two that is not biholomorphic to a Type IV domain is equivalent to Mok's embedding. This completely resolves a problem of Mok.

papers.title: Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs
papers.abstract: Let $C_n^k$ denote the $k$th power of the cycle $C_n$. The equivalence covering number $\operatorname{eq}(G)$, studied by Alon, is the minimum number of equivalence subgraphs needed to cover all edges of $G$. King conjectured that $\operatorname{eq}(C_n^k)=Ω(k)$ for sufficiently large $n$ relative to $k$. We study $\operatorname{eq}(C_n^k)$ and prove that, for every $n \geq 2k + 2$, we have $1 + \lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil \leq \operatorname{eq}(C_n^k) \leq 1 + 2\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil$. We further show that, whenever $n\ge(k+1)\max\{41,5\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil\}$, \begin{equation*} \operatorname{eq}(C_n^k)\in\left\{1+\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil,\,2+\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil\right\}. \end{equation*} Moreover, for every integer $n\ge \max\{2k+2,k^2(k+2)\}$, the following exact values hold in the indicated cases: \begin{equation*} \operatorname{eq}(C_n^k)=\begin{cases} 1+\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil, & k+1\neq2^{\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil} \text{ or }(k+1)\mid n,\\[3pt] 2+\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil, & k+1=2^{\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil} \text{ and }2\nmid n. \end{cases} \end{equation*}

papers.title: Weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for noncommutative rough homogeneous singular integrals
papers.abstract: We establish the weak type \((1,1)\) endpoint estimate for operator-valued rough homogeneous singular integrals with kernels satisfying the classical \(L\log L\) integrability and cancellation conditions. This extends Seeger's endpoint theorem [{J. Amer. Math. Soc.} \textbf{9} (1996)] to the noncommutative setting. A key ingredient is an off-diagonal analysis that controls interactions between different kernel scales and avoids an additional logarithmic loss.

papers.title: Maximum degree for random geometric graphs in the connectivity regime and beyond
papers.abstract: A random geometric graph is a random graph model whose vertex set is a binomial point process, where two vertices are connected by an edge if each lies within the ball of radius $r$ centered at the other. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic fluctuations of the threshold radius required for the maximum degree of the graph to reach a target value.
