Assuming this target value grows with the number of vertices $n$ at an order of at least $\log n$ but strictly less than $(\log n)^d$, we show that these fluctuations follow a Gumbel distribution. We also investigate the spatial configurations of vertices with extremely large degrees, and show that the point process marked by their degrees converges in distribution to a Poisson point process.

papers.title: Diagonal recovery from noisy Fourier--Hermite coefficients: exact orders of the error
papers.abstract: We consider the recovery of functions of the weighted Wiener classes $W_s^μ$ from perturbed Fourier--Hermite coefficients in the metric of $L_\infty(\mathbb R)$. For the summation methods of the class $\mathcal S^θ$ we find error estimates on $W_s^μ$. The estimates take into account the behaviour of the Hermite functions both in the oscillatory region and near the turning point: the maxima of functions with different indices are attained at different points, and the supremum of a sum over a block of indices is substantially smaller than the sum of the suprema. Owing to this, in particular, we establish a common lower bound for all finite diagonal methods; for $s\ne4/3$ and $p\ne4/3$ it matches the upper bound and gives the exact order of the error in this class, while at the critical points the gap between the bounds does not exceed $(\log(e/δ))^{1/4}$ up to a constant. If, in addition, $s>4/3$ or $p<4/3$, then this order is also optimal among all recovery operators that use the whole sequence of data.

papers.title: Proposal for a multi-ion optical clock with hundreds of ions
papers.abstract: Scaling trapped-ion optical clocks to hundreds of ions remains a major challenge due to inhomogeneous frequency shifts in large ion crystals. Here, we propose a circular surface-trap architecture for a multi-ion optical clock with hundreds of ions. The rotational symmetry of the ion crystal suppresses the main sources of inhomogeneity, quadrupole shift.We investigate the feasibility of a clock based on a ring crystal of 400 $^{40}\mathrm{Ca}^{+}$ ions and propose a suitable experimental setup configuration. We have shown that circular configuration of ions leads to suppression by two orders of magnitude of the quadrupole shift comparing to the linear trap. Combined with stray-field compensation and dynamical decoupling techniques, this architecture provides a pathway toward multi-ion optical clocks with fractional frequency uncertainty at the $10^{-18}$ level and an expected 20-fold improvement in frequency stability compared to single ion clocks.

papers.title: Beyond Harnack Amoeba Boundaries
papers.abstract: We construct smooth irreducible plane curves whose complete amoeba contour is a smooth embedded curve equal to the amoeba boundary, although the curves are not torically equivalent to simple Harnack curves. Finite monomial coverings yield explicit infinite families with higher logarithmic multiplicity and nonmaximal normalized amoeba area. We classify the Newton polygons admitting such covering constructions through their exponent lattices, give an exact connectedness criterion in terms of monodromy, and treat primitive polygons by a separate phase-sensitive construction. Exact triangular and trapezoidal families are complemented by positive-genus investigations exhibiting bounded amoeba-complement components. These results show that a perfectly exposed amoeba contour does not determine the real structure, logarithmic sheet number, or Harnack type of the underlying curve.

papers.title: A Quantum Analogue of the Covering Lemma: Limits of Exact Anonymous Computation
papers.abstract: Can quantum communication determine the size of an anonymous network when no size bound is known? Classical impossibility proofs rely on the covering lemma: an execution can be reproduced on a larger network with the same local structure. Quantum interference invalidates this argument - a measurement record possible on a network can become impossible on a cover. We show that the impossibility of exact counting nevertheless survives. Our main result is a quantum analogue of the covering lemma that preserves local possibilities rather than complete executions. Within a cyclic covering family, every local measurement outcome possible at a node remains possible at a corresponding node in every sufficiently large network. This holds even after information has travelled around the smaller network, beyond the reach of a simple locality argument. We extend the principle to the universal covering tree and finite covers with sufficiently long cycles. The proof combines tensor-network methods with graph coverings: a common representation across network sizes turns normalization into a constraint on which local outcomes can occur. For uniform synchronous protocols with independently prepared nodes, this support-lifting principle rules out zero-error counting and even the production of a guaranteed finite size bound on anonymous rings and the other cyclic covering families considered here. It also rules out exact leader election with termination in finite time with probability one on these families. Measurements, classical control, and local memory growing with time are allowed; no predetermined running-time bound is assumed. Quantum interference thus defeats execution lifting without enabling infallible certification of network size.

papers.title: Beyond Amoeba Boundaries
papers.abstract: We construct smooth plane curves whose logarithmic contours are smooth and embedded but strictly larger than their amoeba boundaries. The examples include connected irreducible curves, disconnected unions of nonlinear components with two-dimensional amoebas, nested families with arbitrarily many components, and a uniform construction realizing every positive genus. Exact critical-locus calculations distinguish the boundary-producing folds from compact or noncompact contour branches lying in the amoeba interior. These constructions show that smoothness of the complete contour does not force contour--boundary equality and that internal critical-value branches persist under monomial transformations, controlled perturbations, and finite monomial coverings.21 pages, 14 figures

papers.title: The CR Nirenberg Problem, Part II: Existence and Topological Degree
papers.abstract: This paper is a continuation of Part~I \cite{QTWPartI}, where blow-up analysis and compactness results for the CR Nirenberg problem were established. We prove some existence and degree results for the CR Nirenberg problem on the standard sphere. More precisely, we first prove existence results under antipodal and, more generally, finite-group symmetries. Without symmetry, we derive a Leray--Schauder degree formula under natural flatness conditions, yielding existence results for positive prescribed curvatures with certain homogeneous expansions at critical points. We also obtain Aubin-type inequalities under a vanishing first-moment condition, uniformly near the critical exponent.

papers.title: Negative Sobolev regularity and optimal decay for the fractional Navier--Stokes--Poisson system
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem in $\R^{3}$ for the repulsive compressible Navier-Stokes-Riesz system with Riesz exponent $0<s<1$ and viscosity $0<\varepsilon\leq1$, where the Riesz interaction $\nabla(-Δ)^{-s}(ρ-\barρ)$ is a generalization of the Coulomb interaction for electrons. For small perturbations of a constant equilibrium, with the solenoidal component of the initial velocity of order $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$, we prove the global existence and uniqueness of smooth solutions. We derive time-decay estimates in $L^{2}$ norms and $L^{\infty}$ norms that capture both uniform-in-$\varepsilon$ dispersive behavior and viscosity-dependent dissipation. We further establish a global-in-time inviscid limit to the irrotational global solution of the compressible Euler-Riesz system whose initial data consist of the same density and the curl-free component of the velocity, with an explicit convergence rate in $W^{k,p}$ norms. The proof combines viscosity-adapted dispersive estimates, normal-form analysis and nonlinear energy estimates with control of both negative and positive Sobolev norms.

papers.title: Topological extensions of elementary measurable spaces
papers.abstract: An elementary space is a pair $(X, \mathcal A)$, where $\mathcal A$ is an algebra of subsets of $X$. Every elementary space $(X, \mathcal A)$ is naturally a topological space when equipped with the topology $τ_{\mathcal A}$ generated by $\mathcal A$. Elementary mappings on elementary spaces are defined in a manner analogous to measurable mappings on measurable spaces. In addition, the notion of an {\it extension} of an elementary space is introduced. Let $M(X, \mathcal A)$, denote the ring of all real-valued elementary functions on $(X, \mathcal A)$. In this article, we study the ring $M(X, \mathcal A)$ and extensions of an elementary space. We show that, for any elementary space $(X, \mathcal A)$, there exists a unique compact elementary extension $(β_{\mathcal A}X, \bar{\mathcal A})$ of $X$, analogous to the Stone-$\check C$ech compactification, which contains every other extension of $X$. This extension has the property that every elementary map from $X$ into any compact topological space extends continuously to $β_{\mathcal A}X$. Next, we show that $β_{\mathcal A}X$ contains a realcompact extension $(\upsilon_{\mathcal A}X, \bar{\mathcal A}_R)$ of $X$, such that every elementary map from $X$ into any realcompact topological space extends continuously to $\upsilon_{\mathcal A}X$. Moreover, $\upsilon_{\mathcal A}X$ is the smallest realcompact extension of $X$ and $(X, \mathcal A)$ is realcompact if and only if $X=\upsilon_{\mathcal A}X$. Also, we see that, every metric space equipped with the $σ$-algebra of all Borel sets is realcompact. Finally, we observe that the maximal ring of quotients of $M(X, \mathcal A)$ is the direct limit of locally constant (continuous) functions on dense open subsets of $(X, τ_{\mathcal A})$. Some questions raised in the literature are also answered.

papers.title: The Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture after OpenAI
papers.abstract: We provide a simplified and more human-friendly version of the proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture recently given by OpenAI. No originality is claimed.

papers.title: Global solutions to the compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations in the half-space
papers.abstract: We study the initial boundary value problem for the compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations without damping in the three-dimensional half-space. The velocity satisfies the no-slip boundary condition, and the electric potential satisfies the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. For small perturbations of a constant state in $H^3$, with a small initial electric field in $L^2$, we establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. The uniform estimates combine density dissipation, tangential and normal derivative estimates, and a modified energy that accounts for the electric boundary contribution through the Helmholtz projection. We also prove algebraic decay under an additional low-frequency assumption on the initial data. If the density perturbation, velocity and electric field have finite tangential negative Sobolev norms of order $-s$, where $1/2\leq s<1$, then the solution decays at the rate $(1+t)^{-s/2}$ in the full energy norm. The decay estimate follows from the formulation in terms of the momentum $ρu$, uniform negative-order estimates and interpolation with the dissipation.

papers.title: Adjoint Transfer and Order-Lifting Dichotomies for 2 x 2 Matrices over Prime-Power Rings
papers.abstract: For an odd prime p, we study the change in matrix order under lifting from Z/p^k Z to Z/p^(k+1) Z. The first variation of the order defect is an affine translate of a cyclic adjoint transfer on sl_2(F_p). We classify the full-order transfer for every q in GL_2(F_p): its rank is 3 for scalar elements, 1 for nonscalar semisimple elements, 1 for nonscalar Jordan elements when p = 3, and 0 for nonscalar Jordan elements when p > 3. For a Jordan element q = lambda(I + U), U^2 = 0 and U != 0, the vanishing first-order transfer for p > 3 admits an exact higher-order refinement. Writing d = (p - 1)/2, the full-order perturbation has depth d when tr(UX) != 0, depth p - 1 when tr(UX) = 0 and X is not in the span of U, and vanishes identically for X in the span of U. For p = 3, among the 27 lifts of a nonscalar order-preserving parent with determinant fixed to +1 or -1, exactly 9 preserve its order and 18 triple it; after the first increase, every further lift triples the order. We also give a scalar obstruction criterion for order preservation among unrestricted Jordan lifts.

papers.title: Bloch torsion and modular combinations of Nahm sums
papers.abstract: We construct a positive-definite symmetric integral $12\times12$ matrix $A$ such that, for every solution $Q$ of Nahm's equations $1-Q=Q^A$ with $Q_i\ne0,1$ for all $i$, the associated element $\sum_i[Q_i]$ is torsion in the Bloch group of $\mathbb{Q}(Q_1,\ldots,Q_{12})$. However, the Nahm sum $F_{A,B,C}(τ)$ is nonmodular for every $B\in\mathbb{Q}^{12}$ and $C\in\mathbb{Q}$. Thus the torsion condition for all solutions in Nahm's conjecture is not sufficient for the existence of a modular Nahm sum.

papers.title: Riemannian Formulation of Sample-Based Quantum Krylov Solvers for Elliptic Problems: Energy-Norm Guarantees and Duct-Flow Applications
papers.abstract: Sample-based quantum linear solvers measure quantum Krylov states $e^{-iAT}|b\rangle$ and reconstruct the solution of $Ax=b$ classically on the observed basis states. We develop this approach for positive-definite systems that arise from elliptic partial differential equations. We show that the sampling guarantees hold in any fixed basis with an efficient transform. We then replace the variational reconstruction by a Galerkin solve on the sampled set. For this reconstruction we derive expected and high-probability energy-norm error bounds, a sample complexity in terms of the smallest sampling probability on an essential set, a computable residual certificate, and a support-completeness theorem for the dephased outcome law. We formulate the method for elliptic problems on Riemannian cross sections. In two dimensions the stiffness matrix is metric-independent in conformal coordinates, and curved vessels lead to the same matrix class. Killing symmetries of the cross section give selection rules for the measurement outcomes, and the Lie derivative of the metric gives first-order bounds for geometric perturbations. We separate operator approximations, whose effect we bound, from sampler approximations, which affect coverage but not the target. As examples we treat the implicit step of pulsatile flow in elliptic, lens-shaped, and curved ducts. In simulations of up to 12 qubits, the number of Fourier modes required for 1% error grows from 14 to 60 while the number of unknowns grows from 64 to 4096. A classical residual-greedy selection is nevertheless more efficient than quantum sampling in all cases studied, consistent with the low measured sampling efficiency. On a six-qubit trapped-ion processor, the measured outcome laws follow a replacement-noise model whose strength grows by about 0.6% per two-qubit gate, and a parity selection rule rejects shots at the predicted rate.

papers.title: Homogenization of an optimal control problem for a Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system in a 3D perforated domain
papers.abstract: We study the homogenization of an optimal control problem governed by a Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system in a periodically perforated three-dimensional domain. The obstacles are Lipschitz sets of size $\varepsilon^α$, $α>3$, where $\varepsilon$ is the period. The fluid satisfies the no-slip condition on the outer boundary and the free-slip condition on the obstacles, the phase-field equation contains a source term, and the convective term carries a pore-scale Reynolds number that tends to zero as $\varepsilon\to0$. The control is a distributed body force, and the cost functional tracks the velocity in $L^2$ and the order parameter in $H^1$. Since uniqueness of weak solutions of the state system is not known for fixed $\varepsilon$, the control-to-state relation is multivalued, and we pose the microscopic problems over control-state pairs. We prove the existence of microscopic optimal pairs and the sequential $Γ$-convergence of the cost functionals to the cost functional of a control problem governed by the unsteady Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system on the full domain. As a consequence, the optimal values converge, every cluster point of microscopic optimal pairs is optimal for the homogenized problem, and the optimal controls converge strongly along the corresponding subsequences. The $\liminf$ inequality follows from the homogenization of the state system, including the strong convergence of the gradients of the order parameter. Only the recovery sequence requires uniqueness of weak solutions of the homogenized system, which we prove when the outer boundary is of class $C^{2,1}$.

papers.title: Explicit Bounds for Restricted Invertibility with Prescribed Group Cardinalities
papers.abstract: We prove an explicit lower spectral bound for independent random vectors with prescribed group multiplicities. Let $v_{ij}\in\mathbb C^d$, $1\le i\le l$, $1\le j\le k_i$, be independent random vectors with finite support and $\mathbb E v_{ij}v_{ij}^*=A_i$, where $\sum_{i=1}^l A_i=I_d$ and $\operatorname{Tr}(A_i)\geε$. Set $k=\max_i k_i$, $n=\max_i\operatorname{rank}(A_i)$, and $K=\sum_{i=1}^l k_i$. If $n>(6+4\sqrt2)k$ and $2\sqrt{nk}-k<ε\le n/2$, then, with positive probability, \[ λ_K\left(\sum_{i=1}^l\sum_{j=1}^{k_i}v_{ij}v_{ij}^*\right) \ge n-(\sqrt{k}+\sqrt{n-ε})^2. \] As a consequence, we obtain a restricted invertibility result selecting exactly $k_i$ vectors from the $i$th group of a Parseval frame. The proof combines interlacing families, a reciprocal transformation of mixed characteristic polynomials, and a multivariate barrier estimate that accommodates repeated differentiation in the same variable.

papers.title: Synergistic Learning in Domain Adaptation with a Known Link: A Minimax Understanding
papers.abstract: When can combining source and target data yield much better performance than using either alone? From a minimax viewpoint, writing $R(n,n_T)$ for the minimax risk from $n$ source and $n_T$ target observations, we ask when $R(n,n_T)$ decays strictly faster than both $R(n,0)$ and $R(0,n_T)$. We call this the Synergistic Learning Phenomenon (SLP) and quantify it by the Synergistic Advantage Ratio $\mathrm{SAR}=\min(R(n,0),R(0,n_T))/R(n,n_T)$. We study domain adaptation with a known link: source regression $f$, target regression $g=\mathcal{A}f$ for a known operator $\mathcal{A}$, and possibly different designs. Three links---identity, integration, and differentiation---and the density ratio $ρ=h_T/h_S$ determine whether synergy is possible, at what rate, and in which sample-size window. For the identity link (covariate shift) with a Beta$(a,1)$ source and uniform target, a known necessary condition for SLP is $a\geq2+1/(2β)$, where $β$ is the smoothness of $f$ (Result I). An integral link $g(x)=\int_0^xf(t)\,dt$ can yield the joint rate $(nn_T)^{-1/2}$ even for a bounded ratio (Result II), and under a Beta$(a,1)$ source has a phase diagram with cuts at $a=2$ and $a=3$: integral SLP for $1<a<2$, an extra level-split rate $n_T^{-1}$ for $2<a<3$, and covariate-shift-type spatial SLP for $a>3$ (Result III). A derivative link $g=\dot f$ synergizes only under a stronger singularity (Result IV), giving a sharp integration--differentiation asymmetry under a bounded ratio. Across all three links, synergy arises from role separation: each dataset resolves a distinct bottleneck associated with the link and designs. We characterize the sample-size windows for synergy and how SAR varies with $n$ and $n_T$. Simulations support the predicted phase structure, and a mirrored integration--differentiation analysis of real vehicle and smartphone signals illustrates the asymmetry.

papers.title: Walk-on-Ambient-Patch: Solver-Adapted Isometric Embeddings for Projected Walk on Spheres
papers.abstract: Projected Walk on Spheres (PWoS) solves surface PDEs through ambient sampling and closest-point projection, but tightly folded embeddings can force short steps or ambiguous projections despite simple intrinsic geometry. We introduce Walk-on-Ambient-Patch (WoAP), which treats the embedding as a solver variable. Edge-isometry constraints and tangent-point repulsion separate intrinsically distant regions, optionally in higher codimension; patch states track residual projection branches without introducing PDE boundaries. We analyze the resulting geometry--sampling tradeoff: additional dimensions provide separation freedom but reduce uniform tangent progress, while strong tangent-biased proposals incur large importance-weight moments. Folded-surface experiments demonstrate reduced projection conflicts, a separate hard-constraint pilot verifies metric preservation, and an internal fixed-RMSE comparison favors higher dimensions at stricter accuracy targets. Together, these results motivate choosing the embedding and projection state jointly with the stochastic solver.

papers.title: The Goldbach exceptional set: an exponent 7/12 and conditional refinement
papers.abstract: Let \(E(X)\) count the even integers between \(4\) and \(X\) that are not sums of two primes. We combine Pintz's explicit formula for the major arcs with the exponential-sum estimate of Maynard, Pandey, and Radziwiłł to prove \(E(X)\ll_\varepsilon X^{7/12+\varepsilon}\) whenever all Dirichlet \(L\)-functions have a common fixed zero-free half-plane \(\Rea s>θ_0\), with \(θ_0<1\). The uniform \(7/8\) theorem reported in the OpenAI mathematics release supplies this input. Under the stronger hypothesis that every nontrivial Dirichlet zero has real part at most \(θ\), where \(1/2\leqθ\leq2/3\), we prove \[ E(X)\ll_{θ,\varepsilon}X^{g(θ)+\varepsilon}, \qquad g(θ)=\frac{θ(5-4θ)}{2(2-θ)}. \] Thus every fixed \(θ<2/3\) gives an exponent strictly below \(7/12\). The latter argument uses a classical fixed-modulus zero-density estimate and is independent of the new exponential-sum theorem.

papers.title: Rank-based Model Average Estimator for Average Treatment Effects
papers.abstract: Model averaging emerges as an attractive ensemble technique that strategically synthesizes all available information from potential candidate models to enhance estimation accuracy. Despite of having been widely practiced in various areas in biostatistics and economics, its application to causal inference is rather limited. We propose to estimate the average treatment effect (ATE) by forming the weighted combination of the robust rank-based estimators obtained from a series of candidate models, where the model weights, selected via the growing window cross-validation, dynamically adjust the importance of candidate models. The proposed robust rank-based model averaging ({\sf RRMA}) is not only robust to handle potential outliers and heavy-tailed error distributions but also capable to reduce the risk of model mis-specification and enhance the flexibility and the accuracy of estimation. Theoretically, we establish the desirable asymptotic properties of {\sf RRMA}, including the asymptotic optimality, consistency and asymptotic distribution. Moreover, motivated by the asymptotic distribution of {\sf RRMA}, an easy-to-implement confidence interval is also developed for the ATE. Simulation experiments and an empirical application demonstrate the superiority of {\sf RRMA} over existing competitors in estimation accuracy, coverage probabilities and widths of confidence intervals.

papers.title: K_1 of matroids
papers.abstract: Using the geometric realization spectral sequence and the Serre spectral sequence, we compute $K_1(\operatorname{Mat}_*)$, the first K-theory group of the proto-exact category of pointed matroids, answering a question of Jun, Sistko and Wright.

papers.title: Topological Classification of Univariate Sparse Polynomials via Tropical Geometry
papers.abstract: We give the topological classification of some simplest univariate complex fewnomials, and find tropical fans of the fewnomial strata with each topological type. Specifically, for the support $ A=\{d,d+1,d+2,d+3,d+4\},\quad d\geq3, $ we classify the topological equivalence classes of polynomials having two critical values of ramification type $(2,2)$. There is one class for odd $d$ and two classes for even $d$. We describe the branches at infinity of the corresponding one-dimensional stratum using Newton polytopes of certain complete intersection representations of the sought strata, and determine their tropicalizations. The combinatorial types of the obtained tropical polynomials distinguishes all three kinds of topological equivalence classes. These computations suggest a correspondence between topological equivalence classes of polynomials and combinatorial types of tropicalizations of their branches at infinity, as well as a possible periodicity phenomenon under translations of the support.

papers.title: KKT Residual Sliding Manifolds: A Projection-Free Structured Finite-Time Solver for Nonlinear Constrained Optimisation
papers.abstract: Nonlinear Constrained Optimisation (NCO) requires simultaneous satisfaction of the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions. Existing methods enforce these conditions through projections, penalties, barriers, or sequential approximations, potentially introducing computational complexity and convergence difficulties. For nonconvex problems, a KKT point need not be a local optimum. This paper reformulates NCO as stabilisation of a unified KKT sliding residual manifold and develops SM-KKT, a projection-free solver. Stationarity, equality feasibility, and regularised Fischer-Burmeister complementarity are integrated into a unified residual system, with complementarity encoding inequality feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementary slackness. The manifold's zero set is shown to be equivalent to the KKT conditions. The required Jacobian saddle-point inertia is characterised and shown, under stated assumptions, to be equivalent to the simultaneous satisfaction of the Linear Independence Constraint Qualification (LICQ) and Second-Order Sufficient Condition (SOSC). This characterisation establishes local stability of the structured correction algorithm under these conditions and distinguishes nondegenerate locally optimal KKT solutions from points failing second-order optimality. SM-KKT computes structured primal--dual corrections and applies a discrete sliding reaching law to drive the KKT residual into a prescribed boundary layer in finite time. Four nonlinear benchmarks show recovery of reference constrained optima with KKT residuals below $10^{-6}$, earlier boundary-layer reaching, and favourable KKT accuracy compared with projected primal-dual, augmented-Lagrangian, quadratic-penalty, and log-barrier baselines.

papers.title: Beyond Aggregate Drift: Optimal Client-Specific Windows in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: We study federated learning from continuously arriving data: each client samples from its own distribution, these distributions drift over time, and the server must track the minimizer of the clients' weighted average loss. Clients are not alike as they collect data at different rates, with different noise, and change at different speeds. The main question is how much history should each one keep? A single shared window must serve every client at once, and so makes a fast-changing client carry the sampling noise of a slow, nearly stationary one. We give each client a memory of its own, sized to that client's noise, arrival rate, and drift, and refresh it by restarted accelerated method that starts from a common point. The tracking error is then bounded by \[ R\left(\sum_m w_m^{3/2}\,σ_m\sqrt{γ_m/λ_m}\right)^{2/3}, \] for clients with weight $w_m$, noise $σ_m$, arrival rate $λ_m$, and drift rate $γ_m$ on a domain of diameter $R$. This is never worse than what any common window can achieve, and strictly better whenever noise and drift are spread unevenly across clients. A lower bound that puts different groups of clients on different drift clocks shows this quantity is the right one. The two bounds agree up to a constant whenever the clients occupy boundedly many refresh scales, and in general differ only by the sixth root of the number of scales. Experiments show the gain comes from the memory rather than from the solver: it persists across accelerated, stochastic-gradient, and one-step methods, and against a separately tuned common-memory baseline.

papers.title: Tuza's Conjecture under an Edge-Count Condition
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$, let $ν(G)$ denote the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles and let $τ(G)$ denote the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle. Tuza's conjecture asserts that $τ(G)\le 2ν(G)$ for every graph $G$. We first note that Tuza's conjecture is equivalent to the following statement: for every fixed $c\ge 0$, if $G$ is a sufficiently large $n$-vertex graph with $e(G)\ge n^2/4-cn$, then $τ(G)\le 2ν(G)$. In this paper, we prove this statement for every $c<2$.

papers.title: Hull Variation in Symplectic Linear Codes
papers.abstract: We study the variation of hull dimensions of symplectic linear codes under equivalence transformations preserving the symplectic distance. For a symplectic linear code $C$, we introduce an even-valued invariant $Δ(C)$, which depends only on the equivalence class of $C$. This invariant can be expressed as the generic rank of an associated space of alternating matrices and, equivalently, as twice a corresponding matroid matching number. If $C$ has dimension $k$, we prove that the minimum symplectic hull dimension among all codes equivalent to $C$ is $k-Δ(C)$. Consequently, $C$ is equivalent to a symplectic LCD code if and only if $Δ(C)=k$. We further show that every symplectic MDS code of even dimension is monomially equivalent to a symplectic LCD code. For a symplectic self-orthogonal code $C$, we determine all attainable hull dimensions: for every integer $r$ with $0\le r\le Δ(C)/2$, there exists a monomially equivalent code whose symplectic hull has dimension $k-2r$. We also refine a standard form for the generator matrix of a symplectic self-orthogonal code and derive the corresponding parity-check matrix and the Gram matrix of the dual code. In the self-dual case, we characterize $Δ(C)$ through minors of an associated symmetric matrix. Furthermore, we relate hull variation to graph matchings, establish a bound for $Δ(C)$, and give graph constructions producing symplectic self-dual MDS, optimal, and best-known codes.

papers.title: A chain theorem for planar PM-compact bricks
papers.abstract: A connected graph $G$ is matching covered if it contains at least one edge and every edge belongs to some perfect matching of $G$. A matching covered graph is a brick if it is 3-connected and after removing any two vertices, the resulting graph has a perfect matching. Bricks are the building blocks of matching covered graphs. A brick $G$ is extremal if the incidence vectors of all perfect matchings are linearly independent over $\mathbb{R}$. Zhou et al. [On planar extremal nonsolid bricks, J. Graph Theory, 2026] proved that for every planar extremal brick $G$, there exists a sequence of planar extremal bricks $G_0,G_1,\dots,G_n$ such that the underlying graph of $G_n$ is an odd wheel, $G_0=G$, and each $G_i$ $(0\leq i < n)$ has a triangle $T_i$ such that $G_i/T_i = G_{i+1}$, where $G_i/T_i$ means contracting the triangle $T_i$ into a single vertex. In this paper, the result of Zhou et al. is generalized to planar PM-compact bricks, a larger class of bricks including extremal bricks. We present a chain theorem for planar PM-compact bricks: for every planar PM-compact brick $G$, there exists a sequence of planar PM-compact bricks $G_0,G_1,\dots,G_n$ such that the underlying graph of $G_n$ is an odd wheel, $G_0=G$, and each $G_i$ $(0\leq i < n)$ contains a triangle $T_i$ such that $G_i/T_i = G_{i+1}$.

papers.title: A Viscoelastic Wave Equation with Nonlinear Damping and Supercritical Variable-Exponent Logarithmic Sources
papers.abstract: We investigate a viscoelastic wave equation with nonlinear variable-exponent damping and a variable-exponent logarithmic source, allowing supercritical growth. The main difficulties arise from the failure of the source to map the energy space into $L^2(Ω)$, the sign-changing logarithmic potential, and the lack of Sobolev control of the displacement for supercritical damping. Under an exponent condition linking the source and damping exponents, we prove local existence, an energy identity, and a continuation criterion. We prove finite-time blow-up for nontrivial solutions with nonpositive shifted initial energy. We also establish a blow-up criterion based on a sufficiently large initial displacement--velocity pairing, with a threshold depending on the positive part of the shifted initial energy, and derive an explicit upper bound for the lifespan. This criterion allows us to construct blow-up data at every prescribed level of the original energy. For initial data in a suitable stable region, solutions exist globally. For damping within the Sobolev range, a general relaxation condition yields energy decay estimates that include exponential and polynomial rates. Beyond this range, a time-weighted displacement estimate and a splitting of the memory integral give logarithmic decay.

papers.title: A Counterexample to Three Conjectures of Luo
papers.abstract: We give a single counterexample to Conjectures 1--3 as stated in Luo's paper: a minimal two-tetrahedron triangulation of the lens space L(3,1) with a null-homotopic loop edge. The proof uses quadrilateral matching equations, an explicit calculation of shape parameters, and known results on volume maximization.

papers.title: Quantum circuit representation and incomplete Bell measurements in Compton scattering
papers.abstract: We formulate massless tree-level Compton scattering as an effective two-qubit operation on electron and photon helicities. In the Bell basis, the scattering map separates into two parity sectors and admits a simple quantum circuit representation with one nonunitary filter. After Kraus normalization, this filter defines an unsharp incomplete Bell measurement that distinguishes the two Bell-parity sectors but not the relative Bell label within each sector. We further show that the incomplete measurement alone does not surpass the classical teleportation threshold, whereas a subsequent complete Bell-basis readout enables unit conditional teleportation fidelity.

papers.title: A linear independence criterion for $p$-adic Hurwitz zeta values at odd integers
papers.abstract: In this article, a new criterion is established to obtain the linear independence of some values of the $p$-adic Hurwitz zeta function at odd integers $s\geq 3$. We generalize a theorem of F.~Beukers, who gave, among others, an alternative proof---using Padé approximation theory---of a result originally due to F.~Calegari on the irrationality of the $p$-adic Riemann zeta value $ζ_p(3)$ for $p = 2, 3$. To prove our main theorem, we work in a general setting, where we construct and study new Padé approximants of Laurent series satisfying the functional equation $f(z) = f(1-z)$. This complements our previous work on the linear independence of $p$-adic polygamma values.

papers.title: Crystals and the parabolicity conjecture
papers.abstract: These notes introduce crystals and crystalline Dieudonné theory through the example of abelian varieties. After discussing $p$-divisible groups, $F$-isocrystals, slope filtrations, and overconvergence, we explain the parabolicity theorem for $F$-isocrystals and some of its applications to monodromy and Hecke orbits. Two appendices formulate research projects on isocrystals over formal schemes and on monodromy beyond the constant-slope setting. The exposition is intended for readers familiar with basic algebraic geometry and the étale and fppf topologies; prior knowledge of Witt vectors is helpful but not required.

papers.title: On a derived equivalence classification of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type
papers.abstract: We consider a family $(Λ_λ)_{λ\in \Bbbk^\times}$ of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type over an algebraically closed field $\Bbbk$, where $\Bbbk^\times:= \Bbbk\setminus \{0\}$, and for each $λ\in \Bbbk^\times$, $Λ_λ$ is socle equivalent to $Λ_1$, which is the trivial extension of a hereditary algebra of type $\tilde{A}$. We compute their Hochschild cohomologies, which shows that $Λ_λ$ is not derived equivalent to $Λ_1$ if $λ\neq 1$. This means that a derived equivalence classification of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type given by Bocian--Holm--Skowro{\' n}ski is not complete.

papers.title: The Brakke-BV structure of flat flows
papers.abstract: We show that, in ambient dimension at most seven, varifold limits of the minimizing movements scheme introduced by Almgren--Taylor--Wang and Luckhaus--Sturzenhecker are integral Brakke flows. As a consequence, we show that $L^1$-limit points of the scheme, usually known as flat flows, are generalized BV flows. The result is unconditional and, in particular, remains valid even in the absence of energy convergence and in the presence of fattening.

papers.title: From Product Evidence to Access Rights: Auditing and Routing Non-Firm Grid Connections
papers.abstract: Non-firm connection products can accelerate grid access while reinforcements are delayed, but their planning value depends on evidence supporting the contractual promise. We develop a one-way evidence-to-access framework for calendarized products. Stage A constructs and fixes directional restriction calendars from public residual-load and day-ahead price-timing signals. Stage B audits the submitted calendar and one bounded common repair, tests joint threshold attainability under the shared annual budget, and applies an aggregation-aware Power Transfer Distribution Factor (PTDF) certificate. Stage C treats the resulting ledger as fixed in queue-aware allocation and intervention planning. In the primary policy-package evaluation, the evidence-supported menu returns the same $2.119$~GW allocation as firm-only access, whereas authorizing the uniformly derated fallback raises awards to $6.442$~GW and reduces backlog from $136.076$ to $113.601$~GW-years; all $4.489$~GW of non-firm awards use the fallback. In a target-free matched control, evidence-routed and state-blind fallback menus attain primary objectives equivalent within EUR~1 and return the same accepted applicants, award years, routes, and intervention portfolio. Thus, in the reported testbed, fallback authorization rather than calendar-specific evidence support drives the access-volume effect.

papers.title: Orbital stability of solitary wave solutions of the derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation in the endpoint case
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the orbital stability of solitary waves for the derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation $$iq_t+q_{xx}+i\partial_x\bigl(|q|^2q\bigr)=0, \quad (t,x)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}.$$ For the endpoint solitary waves satisfying $c>0$ and $c^2=4ω$, we prove the orbital stability in $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ without any additional assumptions. The proof uses conservation of mass and the second Hamiltonian $\mathcal{H}_2$ to keep the Bäcklund-transformed solution small in $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ uniformly in time. We establish an inverse Bäcklund compactness result to reconstruct the algebraic solitary wave as the spectral zero approaches the negative real axis.

papers.title: Symmetric Bases and $\ell^p$ Embeddings in Musielak--Orlicz Sequence Spaces under $δ_2$
papers.abstract: We study isomorphic embeddings into Musielak-Orlicz sequence spaces \(\ell_Φ\), where the normalized generating sequence \(Φ=\{φ_n\}\) satisfies the \(δ_2\) condition. Using admissible normalized blocks, we construct an associated limiting family \(\mathcal C_{Φ,τ}\) of Orlicz functions. If a Banach space \(X\) with a symmetric basis embeds into \(\ell_Φ\), then there is a function \(ψ\in\mathcal C_{Φ,τ}\) such that the basis of \(X\) is equivalent to the canonical basis of \(\ell_ψ\). An Orlicz sequence space \(\ell_ψ\) embeds if and only if \(ψ\) is equivalent near zero to a member of \(\mathcal C_{Φ,τ}\); in particular, \(\ell^p\) embeds exactly when such a member is equivalent to \(t^p\). Assuming differentiability of the generators on a common interval near zero, we also derive the necessary bound \(p\leq b_{Φ,(c_n),δ}\), where the upper growth index incorporates the summable errors in the \(δ_2\) condition. The same index yields cotype \(q\) for every \(q\geq2\) with \(q>b_{Φ,(c_n),δ}\). Examples with nonuniform growth and lacunary weights illustrate this bound. For alternating Nakano exponents, the explicit limiting family gives a sharper restriction than the index alone. For general Nakano exponents, we recover the known exact cotype criterion, including attainment of the optimal exponent. For weighted Orlicz spaces, we express the cotype criterion through summable scalar errors and recover the formula using the global upper growth index when \(w\in\mathcal A\).

papers.title: Toeplitz determinants for starlike mappings of order α in several complex variables
papers.abstract: Let $F(z)=zf(z)$, where $f$ is a normalized scalar holomorphic function on the unit ball $\mathbb B$ of a complex Banach space $X$ or on the unit polydisk $\mathbb U^n$ of $\mathbb{C}^n$. We establish sharp bounds for two Toeplitz determinants involving the second, third and fourth Fréchet derivatives of $F$ when $F$ is starlike of order $α$, $0\leqα<1$. The first bound is sharp for the full range $0\leqα<1$, while the second is sharp for $0\leqα\leq 2/3$. The extremal mappings are explicitly identified, confirming the sharpness of the estimates.

papers.title: Hypersurfaces with constant sectional curvature of a product of two space forms
papers.abstract: We complete the classification of hypersurfaces with constant sectional curvature of dimension greater than or equal to three in the product of two space forms.

papers.title: Rationality of Kontsevich moduli of stable maps, and their Galois descents
papers.abstract: Let k be a field and X be a geometrically rational variety over k. We investigate the Kontsevich moduli spaces of genus zero, stable maps with curve classes of low degree on X over k, and define their twisted Galois descents. We study the k-rationality of these spaces in detail when X is a projective space/Severi Brauer variety and when X is moduli of genus zero n-marked points. When X is a homogeneous variety over the field of complex numbers, this is a well-known theorem of Kim-Pandharipande.

papers.title: Dimension of affine iterated function systems on $\mathbb{R}^d$
papers.abstract: Let $\{f_i(x)=M_ix+a_i\}_{i\in I}$ be an affine iterated function system on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with attractor $Λ$, and let $μ$ be an associated self-affine measure. Assume that the $M_i$ generate a Zariski dense subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb{R})$. Under the strong open set condition, we show that $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}Λ$ equals the affinity dimension and that $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}μ$ equals the Lyapunov dimension. The above results are consequences of the following projection theorem, which requires no separation condition. For every $1\leq n\leq d$ and for Furstenberg measure a.e. $(d-n)$-dimensional subspace $V$, \[ \dim_{\mathrm{H}} (P^V)_*μ=\min\{n,\,\dim_{\mathrm{H}}μ\}. \] This projection theorem in fact holds under hypotheses weaker than Zariski density: simplicity of the Lyapunov spectrum and a mild transversality condition (the Oseledets non-concentration property). The source of dimension increment in our proof is the positive dimension of the fiberwise conditional measures, exploited through Wu's one-dimensional entropy increase theorem. A key ingredient in reducing the higher-dimensional problem to this setting is a new structural result: a slab-filling property of the measure.

papers.title: On the OpenAI proof that Landau-Siegel zeros do not exist
papers.abstract: A recent manuscript of OpenAI asserts that Landau-Siegel zeros do not exist. Here, we give a detailed account of its argument, arranged as a direct proof with explicit constants. There are absolute constants $q_0$ and $δ_0>0$ such that, for every primitive real Dirichlet character $χ$ of conductor $q\ge q_0$, every real zero $β\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,χ)$ satisfies $(1-β)\log q\geδ_0$, and one can take $q_0=10^{10}$ and $δ_0=3.0\times 10^{-3}$. Combined with a recent computation of Lu, Zaman, and Zhao, this result yields the bound $(1-β)\log q\ge 3.0\times 10^{-3}$ for every conductor $q\ge 3$. The proof is an interpolation determinant argument in the biquadratic field generated by $\sqrt{2}$ over the quadratic field attached to $χ$. A real zero close to one forces $χ(p)=-1$ for most primes $p$, and the Frobenius congruence at these primes makes a certain nonzero determinant divisible by higher powers of these primes than its Archimedean size allows. The underlying ideas are those of the OpenAI manuscript. The explicit constants, and the presentation, are new.

papers.title: Whitney--Lagrange Decomposition for the First Family of Finite Element Differential Forms
papers.abstract: We derive polynomial bubble duality in barycentric coordinates and construct explicit nodal bases for the first family of finite element differential forms. Logarithmic coordinates give an elementary proof of the Whitney--bubble decomposition. The Hessian of negative entropy defines a metric whose normalized Hodge star maps bubble generators to complementary-degree polynomial forms. This gives a direct geometric description of the known dualities and proves nondegeneracy of their integral pairings. Combining Whitney forms with shifted Lagrange polynomials then gives bases dual to tangential point evaluations in every dimension and order. The construction extends to scalar nodes that are unisolvent on every face. The interpolant is independent of the roots and commutes with face restriction.

papers.title: A noetherian Hopf algebra has bijective antipode
papers.abstract: We prove that a Hopf algebra over an arbitrary field has a bijective antipode if either its left or right regular module has finite uniform dimension. In particular, this solves Skryabin's conjecture, posed in 2006, that every noetherian Hopf algebra has a bijective antipode. Starting from Skryabin's injectivity theorem for weakly finite Hopf algebras, we associate to each finite-dimensional subcoalgebra an essential left ideal of common denominators that is also a right coideal in the antipode image. An annihilator identity makes this image essential in the original algebra as a left module over the image, yielding finite left uniform dimension from finite right uniform dimension. A second denominator construction inside the antipode image, together with a restricted inverse-antipode identity, proves surjectivity.

papers.title: Schatten class membership of products of composition operators and their adjoints
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Schatten class membership of the product of a composition operator and the adjoint of another composition operator on the Hardy and Bergman spaces. We provide several sufficient conditions and necessary conditions for these operators to belong to the Schatten classes. Moreover, for some specific symbols including linear fractional maps, finite Blaschke products, and inner functions, we obtain necessary and sufficient conditions.

papers.title: Bimodule duality and Artin's problem for skew field extensions
papers.abstract: Emil Artin asked whether the left and right dimensions of an extension of skew fields must agree. Cohn and Schofield gave counterexamples through elaborate constructions. It has been a long-standing open question whether there is any division ring, infinite-dimensional over its center, for which the left and right indices agree whenever at least one is finite. We give the first such examples. Call a division ring index-symmetric if every division subring with at least one finite index has equal finite indices. Using a duality formula for bimodules over division algebras, we prove that every twisted Calabi--Yau division algebra is index-symmetric. The examples include the Weyl skew fields and, more generally, the quotient division rings of rings of differential operators on smooth affine varieties in characteristic zero. Further examples are the quotient division rings of enveloping algebras of finite-dimensional Lie algebras, Ore extensions of twisted Calabi--Yau noetherian domains, quantum affine spaces, and group algebras of torsion-free polycyclic-by-finite groups.

papers.title: FirstFit coloring process of random bipartite graphs and an online coloring lower bound in the random order model
papers.abstract: FirstFit colors each arriving vertex with the smallest positive integer absent from its previously colored neighborhood. We prove that this rule can require $n^{Ω(1)}$ many colors on certain bipartite graph of $n$ vertices even when the vertices arrive in a uniformly random order. This refutes the conjecture of Bosek, Gutowski, Lasoń, and Przybyło [BGLP24] that FirstFit uses a polylogarithmic expected number of colors on every bipartite graph in the random order model. We obtain the lower bound by analyzing the FirstFit coloring process on random bipartite graphs, where vertices arrive to either side with equal probability, and with an independent edge density $n^{-x}$ for some $0 < x < 1$. Our result can also be viewed as a qualitative strengthening of Kučera [Kuč91], who showed that, for every $ε> 0$, there are graphs with chromatic number at most $n^ε$ on which FirstFit uses $Ω(n/\log n)$ colors in expectation under a uniformly random order. Our result shows that such poor behavior of FirstFit already occurs for $χ(G) = 2$.

papers.title: Temporal invariance of evolutionary entropy and comparative demographic analysis
papers.abstract: Does evolutionary entropy depend on the width of the age classes used to describe a population? We show that the apparent dependence on temporal resolution is a consequence of the loss of information about reproductive timing within discrete classes. When this information is retained, corresponding continuous and discrete representations yield the same cycle entropy, generation time, evolutionary entropy, and reproductive potential in a common unit of time. When within-class timing is unknown, a uniform local reconstruction yields a logarithmic correction. For constant post-maturity hazard and fertility, continuous exponential and discrete geometric descriptions correspond exactly at every time scale. Thus, for a fixed reference duration, evolutionary entropy is a property of the reproductive process, not of its temporal partition. These results provide a mathematical basis for comparing demographic models across different temporal scales by identifying the information required to separate differences in reproductive organisation from effects of the chosen age-class representation.

papers.title: Boundary Vanishing Orders and Asymptotic Expansions for Planar Harmonic Functions with a Sublinear Robin Condition
papers.abstract: We study boundary vanishing orders and asymptotic expansions of planar harmonic functions satisfying the sublinear Robin condition $\partial_νu=λu-|u|^{p-1}u,$ with $λ\geq0$ and $0<p<1$. For nontrivial global solutions on bounded connected Lipschitz domains, we bound the number of nodal domains by the number of Steklov eigenvalues strictly below $λ$ and establish finite vanishing order at every boundary point. The boundary scaling gives the critical exponent $\frac{1}{1-p}$. On $C^1$ boundaries, every positive subcritical vanishing order is an integer, and the leading term is a unique homogeneous Neumann profile in conformal coordinates. At a noninteger critical order, the rescaled solution converges in normalized graph coordinates to an explicit homogeneous profile determined by $p$ up to sign. Every supercritical bulk vanishing order $m$ is an integer, with a unique homogeneous Dirichlet profile in conformal coordinates. The boundary trace has vanishing order $\frac{m-1}{p}>m$. Integer critical vanishing orders are excluded if the boundary is $C^1$ with Dini mean oscillation.

papers.title: Classification of minimal-mass blowup solutions to the mass-critical Hartree equation at the $L^2$-critical level
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the focusing mass-critical Hartree equation \[ iu_t+Δu=-\bigl(|x|^{-2}*|u|^2\bigr)u \] at the ground-state mass $M(Q)$. We prove that, up to the symmetries of the equation, every global minimal-mass non-scattering solution is a solitary wave, while every finite-time minimal-mass blowup solution is a pseudo-conformal image of a solitary wave. This extends the results of \cite{LZ28,Miao-Xu-Zhao3,Wang-Gao} to the scaling-critical space $L^2$ and removes the radial assumption in the global case.

papers.title: A new approach to interior estimates for fully nonlinear elliptic equations
papers.abstract: We give new, elementary proofs of interior second derivative estimates for the Monge-Ampère equation and the constant quadratic Hessian equation, based on the two-point maximum principle. The arguments require only one differentiation of the equation. For the Monge-Ampère equation, the inhomogeneous term is assumed to be positive and continuously differentiable. For the quadratic Hessian equation, the estimate holds in every dimension $n\ge2$.

papers.title: An overring characterization of Gorenstein Prüfer domains
papers.abstract: We prove that a commutative integral domain is Gorenstein Prüfer if and only if every overring is Gorenstein flat over the original domain. It is enough to test overrings that are finitely generated as algebras. The proof combines finite duality with a conductor-quotient argument. Under the overring hypothesis, the conductor quotient of a proper overring generated by two elements as a module is an IF-ring, and degree-one duality lifts first syzygies of finitely presented quotient modules to totally reflexive modules. This gives a bound of one for the Gorenstein flat dimension of every module annihilated elementwise by conductor powers. Quadratic integral elements provide such conductors at nonnormal localizations, while normal localizations give principal-ideal neighborhoods. Constructible compactness yields a finite cover, and a bounded complex of localizations combines these bounds over the original domain. Consequently every finitely generated ideal is Gorenstein flat and the domain is coherent. Examples distinguish finite-type from module-finite tests and Gorenstein flatness from ordinary flatness.

papers.title: The First Modular Zhu Algebra of $L(\frac12,0)_F$ in Characteristic Seven
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $7$, and let $V=L(\frac12,0)_F$. For the degree-four singular vector $q=(L(-2)^2-2L(-4))\mathbf1$ in the universal vacuum vertex operator algebra $\bar V$, set $V_q=\bar V/I(q)$. We prove that the natural quotient map induces an isomorphism $A_1(V_q)\cong A_1(V)\cong F[T]/(T(T-4)(T-5))\cong F^3$. Explicit $O_1(V_q)$-relations and four families of triangular PBW straightening relations give the upper bound, while three one-dimensional homogeneous subspaces give the matching lower bound.

papers.title: Turán Numbers of Linear Stars and Expanded Trees
papers.abstract: For an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$, let $\ex_r(n,\mathcal H)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph containing no copy of $\mathcal H$. The $r$-uniform expansion $T^{(r)}$ of a tree $T$ is obtained by adding $r-2$ new vertices to each edge, with the added sets pairwise disjoint and disjoint from $V(T)$. In particular, the expansion of $K_{1,k}$ is the linear star $\mathcal L_k^r$, whose $k$ edges intersect pairwise in a single common vertex. Chung and Frankl (1987) determined $\ex_3(n,\mathcal L_k^3)$ and all extremal hypergraphs for every $k\ge3$ and sufficiently large $n$. We extend the odd-$k$ part of their result to every $r\ge5$, determining the exact Turán number and the unique extremal hypergraph up to isomorphism for sufficiently large $n$. More generally, we extend this result to expansions of trees for which the minimum degree among the vertices in the smaller color class is odd and at least three. For every $r\ge5$ and sufficiently large $n$, we establish lower and upper bounds on their Turán numbers. When no two vertices attaining this minimum degree in that color class have a common neighbor, we determine the exact Turán number and the unique extremal hypergraph up to isomorphism. The proofs combine the delta-system method with stability arguments and a detailed analysis of extremal constructions.

papers.title: Gorenstein Prüfer domains with non-Prüfer integral closure
papers.abstract: There exists a one-dimensional local Gorenstein Prüfer domain whose integral closure is not Prüfer. We prove that the recently constructed coherent counterexample to the normalization problem has this stronger Gorenstein property. The argument establishes permanence of divisoriality of finitely generated ideals under ultraproducts and quotients by divided primes. It also supplies uniform matrix factorizations: in an ultraproduct of plane-curve domains, every nonzero ideal generated by $r$ elements is a cycle of a two-periodic totally acyclic complex with free terms of rank $r$. The divided prime defining the one-dimensional example is flat, so these complexes descend through the quotient and localization. A specified two-generated ideal remains noninvertible in every integral overring. Over the normalization, its associated Laurent overring has nonzero first Tor with every injective cogenerator, although both rings are Gorenstein flat over the original domain. Examples distinguish this failure from a nonnormal Gorenstein curve with Prüfer normalization and show that the periodicity conclusion is stronger than the Gorenstein Prüfer property alone.

papers.title: On modular vector invariant fields
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field of any characteristic and $\rm GL(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$ the general linear group over $\mathbb{F}_q$. Suppose $W$ denotes the standard representation of $\rm GL(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$ and $\rm GL(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$ acts diagonally on the direct sum of $W$ and its dual space $W^*$. Let $G$ be any subgroup of $\rm GL(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$. Suppose the invariant field $\mathbb{F}_q(W)^G=\mathbb{F}_q(f_1,f_2,\dots,f_k)$, where $f_1,f_2,\dots,f_k\in\mathbb{F}_q[W]^G$ are homogeneous invariant polynomials. We prove that there exist homogeneous polynomials $\ell_1,\ell_2,\dots,\ell_{n}$ in the invariant ring $\mathbb{F}_q[W\oplus W^*]^{G}$ such that the invariant field $\mathbb{F}_q(W\oplus W^*)^{G}$ is generated by $\{f_1,f_2,\dots,f_k,\ell_1,\ell_2,\dots,\ell_{n}\}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$.

papers.title: Spectral Gårding Elliptic Equations
papers.abstract: We study spectral Gårding elliptic equations on compact Kähler manifolds. Smooth solvability is equivalent to the existence of a smooth representative in the admissible domain. The concavity theorem for ideal Gårding polynomials gives a fixed concave formulation to which Székelyhidi's second-order argument applies in every degree $2\le d\le n$, extending Lin's top-degree solvability theorem. Combined with the numerical criteria of Fu--Li--Zhang--Zhang and Chen--Nie--Xu, this yields a Nakai--Moishezon type criterion for solvability on compact Kähler manifolds. A solution converts the local ideal Gårding structure into a global Lorentzian structure. Its mixed derivatives give a strict nonlinear Hodge--Riemann hierarchy from the degree of the equation down to degree two, and the homogenization of the intersection polynomial is Lorentzian in nef class directions. Numerical criteria then produce explicit Hodge--Riemann classes, Lefschetz isomorphisms in bidegree $(1,1)$, and weighted Hodge-index inequalities.

papers.title: Oka complements in algebraic tori and their logarithmic covers
papers.abstract: Suppose $n\ge2$ and $K\subset\C^n$ is compact and polynomially convex. Write $q(z)=(e^{-iz_1},\ldots,e^{-iz_n})$, $X_K=(\C^*)^n\setminus(K\cap(\C^*)^n)$, and $Y_K=\C^n\setminus q^{-1}(K)$. We prove that $X_K$ and its logarithmic covering $Y_K$ are Oka. More strongly, $Y_K$ admits normalized holomorphic families of entire embeddings through prescribed holomorphic sections. The proof combines polynomial pair Hamiltonian transport in multiplicative coordinates, compatible with the coordinate hyperplanes, with a fixed Fatou--Bieberbach model. Applications include Oka slab crosses over arbitrary nonempty connected planar domains, complements of periodic equal-radius Euclidean balls centered at products of planar lattices, and complements of sufficiently small closed metric balls in products of elliptic curves.

papers.title: A trace Paley-Wiener theorem for $\mathrm{GL}_{n}(F)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_{n}(E)$, with $E/F$ a quadratic extension of non-Archimedean local fields
papers.abstract: We extend the classical trace Paley-Wiener theorem for $p$-adic reductive groups, given by Bernstein, Deligne and Kazhdan in 1986, to a relative case. That is when $E/F$ is a quadratic extension of $p$-adic fields, the main result is a scalar Paley-Wiener theorem for relative Bessel distributions on $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$. These distributions are relative character of the form $$π\mapsto I_π(f), \ f\in C_c^\infty(\mathrm{GL}_n(E)),$$ as $π$ ranges over $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$-distinguished irreducible tempered representations, and are constructed from a $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$-invariant functional and a Whittaker functional. Using the local Langlands correspondence, and the base-change from a unitary group, we show that the relative characters can be described as elements of the "generic" Bernstein center of the unitary group $U(n)$.

papers.title: Genuine Information Backflow Requires Noncommuting Initial System States
papers.abstract: The Gorini-Kossakowski-Lindblad-Sudarshan (GKLS) equation, a cornerstone of open-system theory, describes Markovian semigroup dynamics in which information about the initial preparation cannot revive. Beyond this regime, information revivals are widely interpreted as backflow from a non-Markovian environment. However, a decrease followed by an increase in information retrievable from the system need not imply that information has returned from the environment [PRX Quantum 6, 020316 (2025)]. It may instead arise from noise correlations unrelated to the system's initial preparation, carried by inert degrees of freedom that never interact with the system and therefore cannot mediate backflow. Such revivals are called extrinsic; genuine backflow is reserved for revivals that cannot be explained this way. The framework developed in that work, however, assumes access to arbitrary initial system states, an assumption often incompatible with physical constraints or limited experimental control. This leaves open which properties of the available preparations are necessary for an information revival to certify genuine backflow. Here we extend the framework to allow the description of restricted families of initial states and show that genuine backflow is possible only if the family contains noncommuting states. If all available states commute, as in a classical stochastic process, every revival can be explained by a suitable inert extension and is therefore extrinsic. Noncommutativity of the available system states is thus necessary for information revivals to provide an operational signature of environmental memory.

papers.title: Every n points in the plane contain (m1 + o(1)) n points with no unit distance
papers.abstract: Let $f(n)$ be the largest integer such that every set of $n$ points in the plane contains $f(n)$ points no two at distance $1$, and let $m_1$ be the supremum of the upper densities of Lebesgue measurable planar sets with no two points at distance $1$. Larman and Rogers observed that $f(n) \ge m_1 n$. We prove that $f(n)/n \to m_1$; that is, $f(n) = (m_1 + o(1))n$. This is the first half of a conjecture of Dúcz and Varga, and with the bound $m_1 \le 0.247$ of Ambrus, Csiszárik, Matolcsi, Varga and Zsámboki it gives $f(n) \le (0.247 + o(1))n$. The proof builds a random independent subset of the algebraic plane, invariant under algebraic translations and rotations, whose probability of containing the origin is at least the worst finite independence ratio, and turns it into a measurable planar set of at least that upper density. Its only non-classical input is the Haar rigidity theorem for wild character laws from the OpenAI preprint The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable, which has a machine-checked Lean proof. The whole argument has been formalized in Lean 4 on top of it.

papers.title: General Constructions of Permutation-Fair Dice
papers.abstract: Suppose that each of $n$ players rolls a different die and the players are ordered by their rolls. Can the dice use disjoint labels such that ties are impossible, while all $n!$ orders remain equally likely? We give two general constructions of such dice and solve some related problems.

papers.title: A Berry--Esseen Bound of Order $(1+\log n)/\sqrt n$ for Peng's Central Limit Theorem
papers.abstract: We derive a quantitative central limit theorem under sublinear expectations from a spatial endpoint regularity estimate for the one-dimensional \(G\)-heat equation. For bounded Lipschitz initial data, the second spatial derivative and the time derivative of its solution are Lipschitz in space and \(1/2\)-Hölder in time away from the initial time. In particular, \([u_{xx}(t,\cdot)]_{\mathrm{Lip}}\le C_G\Lip(φ)/t\). Combining this estimate with the nonlinear Stein identity introduced in Song \cite{Song2020} and a replacement argument yields a bound of order \((1+\log n)/\sqrt n\) for bounded Lipschitz tests when the third absolute moment is finite and the lower variance is positive. The final replacement step is estimated directly, avoiding the nonintegrable singularity at time zero.

papers.title: On strongly minimal asymptotic bases of order $h$ generated by powers of $2$
papers.abstract: Let $h\geq2$ be an integer and let $\mathbb{N}_0=W_1\cup\cdots\cup W_h$ be a partition into infinite sets. For $W\subseteq\mathbb{N}_0$, let $A(W)$ denote the set of all finite nonempty sums of distinct powers $2^w$ with $w\in W$. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for $A=A(W_1)\cup\cdots\cup A(W_h)$ to be a strongly minimal asymptotic basis of order $h$. This provides a complete answer to a problem posed by Nathanson in 1988.

papers.title: Discrete intermediate dimensions: endpoints, spectra and quasi-isometric invariance
papers.abstract: We introduce upper and lower discrete intermediate dimensions for unbounded subsets of Euclidean space and extend them to metric spaces. The definitions restrict the covering radii within a scale-dependent range of dyadic shells and take a supremum over an auxiliary parameter. The resulting dimensions are monotone in the parameter and recover the Barlow--Taylor discrete Hausdorff dimension at zero. We prove continuity at every positive parameter, with a sharp quantitative bound, and give an example with a jump at zero. At the upper endpoint, the upper dimension equals upper mass dimension for uniformly discrete Euclidean sets; the analogous lower mass identity fails. We establish a mass distribution principle and prove quasi-isometric invariance under a uniform coarse packing condition. For spaces with uniform polynomial volume growth, we construct clustered subsets attaining the continuity bound. Independent thinning truncates these spectra at the resulting mass dimension, almost surely for all parameters simultaneously. Applications include the discrete Heisenberg group with its word metric and the ranges of simple symmetric random walks.

papers.title: One boundary, infinitely geometries
papers.abstract: Let $N$ be a 3-dimensional integral homology sphere. We prove the existence of a sequence of 4-dimensional topologically negatively curved manifolds $M_k$, $k=1,2,\dots$, satisfying the following: (1) all aspherical manifolds $M_k$ have the same universal cover $U_N$ depending only on $N$; (2) all fundamental groups $π_1(M_k)$ are hyperbolic and share the same Gromov boundary $X_N$ depending only on $N$; (3) the groups $π_1(M_k)$ represent infinitely many distinct quasi-isometry classes. The last conclusion, which represents the new feature, shows that negatively curved geometries in dimension 4 exhibit substantially richer structure than those in dimension 3.

papers.title: Uniqueness of prescribed-node radial bound states for a zero-mass double-power equation
papers.abstract: We study radial bound states of \[ Δu-\abs{u}^{q-1}u+\abs{u}^{p-1}u=0 \quad\text{in }\R^n, \qquad n\ge3,\qquad 1<q<p<\frac{n+2}{n-2}. \] For every integer $k\ge1$, we prove that there is exactly one radial bound state with $k$ simple zeros and $u(0)>0$. Its absolute maximum is attained at the origin. This confirms the zero-mass, Sobolev-subcritical case of Tang's double-power uniqueness conjecture. The proof adapts Tang's phase-transition analysis and combines it with a finite-level separation argument inspired by Cortázar--García-Huidobro--Yarur. Three main difficulties arise in the zero-mass double-power setting: the sign changes of key comparison quantities in the low-amplitude region, the possible failure of pointwise positivity of an auxiliary quantity when $n=3$ and $p+q<3$, and the absence of exponential decay at infinity. We overcome these difficulties by introducing bridge functionals to propagate the required sign information through low amplitudes, establishing a weighted integral positivity estimate in the exceptional three-dimensional range, and combining a radial-flux tail estimate with finite-level inverse-branch comparison. We also establish the strict ordering of the bound-state shooting heights and show that the shooting variation along the \(k\)-node state has exactly \(k+1\) simple zeros.

papers.title: On the convergence of doubly stochastic block gradient descent method for linear inverse problems
papers.abstract: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and randomized block coordinate descent (RBCD) belong to two fundamentally different classes of stochastic iterative regularization methods, and are promising and popular for solving large-scale inverse problems, due to their excellent scalability with respect to data size and signal size, respectively. In this work, we propose a doubly stochastic block gradient descent (DSBGD) method with early stopping, by integrating the updating strategies of both SGD and RBCD, for solving linear inverse problems in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. At each iteration, the method randomly selects one data pair to obtain a stochastic gradient estimate, and then uses it to update one randomly selected block coordinate. We prove the regularizing property of DSBGD under a priori stopping rules and then derive its convergence rates with the additional source condition and a condition on the forward operator. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first convergence rate results of randomized coordinate descent-type iterative methods for inverse problems from the perspective of regularization theory. We also prove that the DSBGD iteration can be stopped by the classical discrepancy principle in finitely many steps with high probability, and that the mean squared error decreases monotonically before stopping. Several numerical experiments are provided to complement the theoretical analysis.

papers.title: Construction and analysis of an explicit fourth-order symmetric low-regularity integrator for the semilinear Klein-Gordon equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose and analyse a novel explicit fourth-order symmetric low-regularity trigonometric integrator for the semilinear Klein-Gordon equation with non-smooth solution in the $d$-dimensional space, where $d=1,2,3$. The integrator is constructed based on the full use of Duhamel's formula, the employment of a twisted function tailored for trigonometric integrals and the symmetrization procedure of trigonometric integrators. Robust error analysis is conducted, demonstrating that the proposed scheme achieves fourth-order accuracy in the energy space under a weak regularity requirement in $H^{2+\max(μ,1)}(\mathbb{T}^d)\times H^{1+\max(μ,1)}(\mathbb{T}^d)$ with $μ> \frac{d}{2}$. A numerical experiment shows that the proposed low-regularity integrator is much more accurate than some well-known exponential integrators for approximating the Klein-Gordon equation with non-smooth solutions.

papers.title: Spectral geometry of saturated Fell bundles
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal B=(B_g)_{g\in G}$ be a saturated Fell bundle over a countable discrete group, equipped with a spectral triple. We give explicit sufficient conditions for lifting this triple to the reduced cross-sectional C\Star-algebra $C_r^*(\mathcal B)$. Using finite projective realizations of the homogeneous Morita equivalence $B_e$-bimodules, we transport the base Dirac operator to the individual fibres and assemble the resulting operators into a fibrewise Dirac operator. We introduce a spectral-regularity condition ensuring bounded commutators and give a sufficient criterion in terms of uniform derivative bounds on smooth factor-system data. Combining the fibrewise operator with a length operator associated with a proper translation-bounded matrix-valued length function yields the lifted spectral triple. When $B_e$ is separable, the lifted triple, with a suitable grading, represents the Kasparov product of the vertical class with the class of the unit-fibre triple. We also establish a summability criterion and sufficient conditions for stability under central cocycle twisting. A range of examples illustrates the scope of the construction, including twisted crossed products, free compact Abelian actions, and Fell bundles with nonfree homogeneous fibres.

papers.title: Impact of matrix topological properties on the convergence of the conjugate gradient method
papers.abstract: It is well known that the matrix structure affects the convergence of iterative methods, particularly those utilizing Krylov subspaces. The matrix structure, determined by its graph, dictates the propagation order of updates to the vector components that are recursively computed during the conjugate gradient method iterations. Along with the propagation of these component updates, round-off errors also propagate. We present a model for the propagation and accumulation of round-off errors and demonstrate that the larger the values of topological characteristics of the matrix graph, such as its diameter, effective diameter, and pseudodiameter, the slower the round-off error accumulates during the method's iterations, and the longer the propagation of round-off errors remains local when computing the components of the search direction, residual, and approximate solution vectors. Round-off errors arising during the computation of these components affect only those components whose corresponding vertices in the matrix graph are at a distance not exceeding the current iteration number. As the iteration number increases, the propagation of round-off errors between the vertices of the matrix graph becomes global, leading to the loss of orthogonality of residuals and conjugacy of search directions. In the context of mixed-precision computations, this implies that for a matrix with a larger graph diameter (or, more practically, effective diameter), a greater number of method iterations can be performed in a lower-precision mode before the onset of convergence stagnation.

papers.title: Cohen-Macaulay truncated path and Nakayama algebras
papers.abstract: This paper characterizes Cohen-Macaulay algebras in the sense of Auslander and Reiten [Progr. Math. 95(1991)] within the following two classes of finite dimensional algebras: (i) truncated path algebras and (ii) Nakayama algebras. For the former, our characterization in terms of ordinary quivers shows that if a Cohen-Macaulay truncated path algebra $Λ$ is connected, then $Λ$ or $D(Λ)$ gives a dualizing module, where $D$ denotes the standard duality. For the latter, we show that every Cohen-Macaulay Nakayama algebra $Λ$ is Iwanaga-Gorenstein. In particular, $Λ$ always gives a dualizing module. Consequently, there is no non-trivial Cohen-Macaulay algebra among truncated path and Nakayama algebras.

papers.title: Answer some Tkachenko's questions in factorizable semitopological groups
papers.abstract: We construct a Hausdorff quasitopological abelian group that is second-countable and semiregular, with a bounded continuous function that does not factor through any regular first-countable semitopological group. Its regular and Tychonoff reflections coincide, have a countable network, and fail even factorizability through arbitrary first-countable semitopological groups. This gives negative answers to \cite[Problems~6.1, 6.2, 6.4, and~6.5]{Tk2026} of Tkachenko. The construction starts with a countable cone group whose common separation reflection is not Fréchet--Urysohn, answering \cite[Problems~6.8 and~6.9]{Tk2026} negatively. In contrast, symmetrization gives affirmative answers to \cite[Problems~6.6 and~6.7]{Tk2026} without separation assumptions. We also show that every countable semitopological group admits simultaneous factorizations of countable families through second-countable Tychonoff semitopological groups.

papers.title: Maximum index of unbalanced signed graphs without a positive odd cycle
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}_{r}^+$ be the set of all balanced signed graphs with underlying graphs $C_r$. A signed graph is called $\mathcal{C}_{r}^+$-free if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to any member of $\mathcal{C}_{r}^+$. In this paper, we characterize the extremal graphs that achieve the maximum index among all $\mathcal{C}_{2k+1}^+$-free unbalanced signed graphs of order $n$ when $k\ge 2$ and $n\ge 187k$.

papers.title: The sharp constant in the Chang--Marshall inequality
papers.abstract: We prove that the optimal constant in the Chang--Marshall inequality is $e$, as conjectured by Andreev and Matheson. More precisely, if $f$ is analytic in the unit disk, vanishes to order $m\geq1$ at the origin, and has normalized Dirichlet integral $d\leq1$, then the boundary mean of $e^{|f|^2}$ is at most $e^{d/m}$. Equality holds precisely for monomials. The proof uses an auxiliary closed planar curve and the isoperimetric inequality to establish monotonicity of the exponential functional along normalized radial dilations.

papers.title: Monotonicity of Coefficients of Interpolated Multiple Zeta Values
papers.abstract: Let $ζ^t(\boldsymbol{k})=\sum_{d=1}^{r}S_d(\boldsymbol{k})t^{r-d}$ be the interpolated multiple zeta value of an admissible index $\boldsymbol{k}$ of depth $r$. We show the monotonicity property of coefficients $S_1(\boldsymbol{k})\ge\cdots\ge S_r(\boldsymbol{k})>0$.
