In the proof, we represent the coefficients as integrals over a common measure space and compares the integrands pointwise. As consequences, we determine the sign and vanishing of $ζ^{-1}(\boldsymbol{k})$ and locate the zeros of $ζ^t(\boldsymbol{k})$ in the closed unit disk.

papers.title: A Four-by-Four Obstruction to Polynomial Removal for Ordered Binary Matrices
papers.abstract: We exhibit a fixed $4\times 4$ binary matrix with no polynomial induced ordered removal bound. At depth $h\geq 1$, let $m=2^h$. Our explicit host has order $(14h+2)m$, exactly $2m^6+\frac{1}{2}(m-2)m^5$ induced copies, and exact editing distance $m^2$ cells. Its normalized editing distance is $Θ(h^{-2})$, while its induced-copy density is $Θ(4^{-h}h^{-8})$. The lower bound holds against arbitrary cell edits through an injective family of $m^2$ protected selections. An exhaustive arithmetic classification identifies every induced copy and proves that a matching canonical repair creates none. The original-copy transversal number is exactly $m$, yielding an unbounded gap between hitting existing copies and eliminating all copies. The identities and the obstruction at every depth are formalized in Lean, with verification sources included as ancillary files.

papers.title: Three Homoscedastic Gaussian Components Have at Most Four Modes
papers.abstract: Gaussian mixtures can have more modes than components. For three Gaussian components with a common covariance, four modes are attainable, whereas the best general upper bound was eight. We prove that four is the exact maximum in every dimension $d \ge 2$, for arbitrary means and positive weights. We further show that the sharp bound drops to three when the whitened means are collinear or form a right or obtuse triangle. The result covers degenerate modes without genericity or separate finiteness assumptions. Our proof maps modes to local minima of a separable free-energy functional on the probability simplex, reduces the problem to counting scalar inverse-function branches, and controls competing branches through curvature and stationary-height comparisons.

papers.title: pper and Lower Bounds for Blow-up Times in Coupled Reaction--Diffusion Systems with Nonlocal Sources
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the following reaction-diffusion system \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} u_t=Δu+F\bigl(x,t,u,v,V(t)\bigr), & (x,t)\in\Om\times(0,T), v_t=Δv+G\bigl(x,t,u,v,U(t)\bigr), & (x,t)\in\Om\times(0,T), \mathcal B u=\mathcal B v=0, & (x,t)\in\partial\Om\times(0,T), u(x,0)=u_0(x),\quad v(x,0)=v_0(x), & x\in\Om, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where \begin{equation*} U(t)=\int_{\Om}u(x,t)\dd x,\qquad V(t)=\int_{\Om}v(x,t)\dd x, \end{equation*} and the boundary operator $\mathcal B$ is either \[ \mathcal B_D w=w \qquad\text{or}\qquad \mathcal B_N w=\partial_νw, \] $\Om\subset\R^N$ be a bounded domain with sufficiently smooth boundary, $N\ge 1$, and $ν$ is the outward unit normal on $\partial\Om$. Under certain conditions, we obtain the upper and lower bounds for the blowup time of the solution to the system.

papers.title: Criticality Concentrates Extensive Sensing Information into a Local Readout
papers.abstract: We show that criticality concentrates extensive sensing information into a local trajectory. In the rapid-readout limit of an all-to-all dissipative feedback network, a single binary trajectory has a Fisher-information rate linear in $N$ for a common weak field, as does the full record. Critical slowing does not remove this gain because the local weight of the slow mode decreases with $N$. An analytic bound guarantees that the local record retains more than half of the full information across the entire channel-parameter range. We also identify how parameter drives and observation dynamics determine local access to collective information beyond permutation symmetry. Furthermore, our sparse-readout theorem establishes a $k^{-1}$ decay of fractional information loss: only $Θ(\varepsilon^{-1})$ trajectories are needed to retain a fraction $1-\varepsilon$ of the full information rate. Any growing readout set, even of vanishing density, asymptotically recovers the full common-field Fisher-information rate.

papers.title: Polynomial Bohnenblust--Hille Bounds and Hardy--Littlewood Inequalities for Finite Local Systems
papers.abstract: The complex polynomial Bohnenblust--Hille inequality states that, for a $d$-homogeneous polynomial $P:\mathbb C^N\to\mathbb C$, $P(z)=\sum_{|α|=d}c_αz^α$, the coefficient norm $(\sum_{|α|=d}|c_α|^{p_d})^{1/p_d}$ is bounded by $B_d^{\mathrm{pol}}\|P\|_\infty$, where $p_d=2d/(d+1)$ and $B_d^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is independent of $N$. Here $\|P\|_\infty$ is the supremum norm on the unit polydisc. This inequality has a Boolean analogue for the Fourier--Walsh coefficients of functions of degree at most $d$, with the supremum taken over $\{-1,1\}^N$. In this setting, Defant, Mastyło and Pérez obtained subexponential bounds, and Ivanisvili established polynomial growth. Further polynomial estimates were obtained by Slote, Tseng and Volberg in the Boolean setting and by Slote and Volberg for cyclic groups. We study these coefficient inequalities in a broader framework of finite systems of functions that encompasses and extends the Boolean and cyclic settings. This framework also admits a natural $\ell_p$ formulation, leading to Hardy--Littlewood-type inequalities. For orthonormal systems, we obtain polynomial bounds for the Bohnenblust--Hille constants and, for sufficiently large $p$, for the constants in these Hardy--Littlewood-type inequalities. In the Boolean case, the polynomial power is $5/2$, with a cubic logarithmic factor.

papers.title: Regular automorphisms of periodic $p'$-groups need not be splitting
papers.abstract: For a fixed prime $p$, a group is called a $p'$-group if the orders of all its elements are coprime to $p$. It is well known that in a finite $p'$-group an automorphism of order $p$ is regular if and only if it is a splitting automorphism of period $p$. In the Kourovka Notebook, V.\,D.~Mazurov asked whether these two notions coincide for periodic $p'$-groups. We answer this question in the negative by constructing a periodic group of prime period $q$ that admits a regular automorphism of order $p \neq q$ which is not splitting.

papers.title: Invariant Measures for Interacting Continuous-State Population Models
papers.abstract: We study invariant probabilities for nonlinear two-population branching systems with competition, cooperation, or predator--prey interaction, driven by Brownian noise and spectrally positive stable jumps. Without immigration, every invariant probability of a conservative competitive or predator--prey system is concentrated on the boundary under either boundary convention. With nontrivial axis dynamics, coordinatewise continuation admits only the point mass at the origin. For cooperative systems, we give criteria for boundary concentration and interior stationarity, including a sharp criterion for bilinear cooperation with a common relative noise exponent. With immigration, explicit parameter conditions yield existence and stationary moment bounds. For square-root diffusions with positive immigration, these conditions ensure interior concentration and full support on the closed quadrant. Further lower bounds on immigration rates give uniqueness and convergence of time-averaged transition laws.

papers.title: Supersaturation thresholds for expanded color-critical graphs
papers.abstract: For a $k$-uniform hypergraph $L$, let $h_L(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies of $L$ in an $n$-vertex $k$-graph with $\mathrm{ex}(n,L)+q$ edges. Let $t_L(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies obtained by adding $q$ edges to an extremal $L$-free $k$-graph. A graph is color-critical if deleting a suitable edge decreases its chromatic number. Let $\mathcal K_k(F)$ be the expanded graph obtained by adding $k-2$ new vertices to each edge of $F$, with disjoint sets of new vertices for distinct edges. Mubayi proved that, for every clique $K_r$ with $r\ge4$ and fixed $ q>0$, $ h_{\mathcal K_3(K_r)}(n,q)\ge qt_{\mathcal K_3(K_r)}(n,1)$ for every sufficiently large $n$. Pikhurko and Yilma later proved that, for every color-critical graph $F$, there is a constant $ε_F>0$ such that $h_{F}(n,q)=t_{F}(n,q)$ for every sufficiently large $n$ and $1\le q\leε_F n$. We extend this equality to expanded color-critical graphs. Let $d>k\ge3$. For every color-critical graph $F$ with $χ(F)=d+1$, there is a constant $ε>0$ such that $ h_{\mathcal K_k(F)}(n,q)=t_{\mathcal K_k(F)}(n,q)$ for every sufficiently large $n$ and $1\le q\leεn^{k-1}$. Let $q_L(n)$ be the largest integer $q$ such that $h_L(n,s)=t_L(n,s)$ for every integer $1\le s\le q$. We give a sufficient condition for $q_L(n)=Θ_L(n^{k-1})$ and an explicit family satisfying it. We also give a different sufficient condition under which $q_L(n)=Ω_L(n^{k-1/2})$. \noindent \emph{Keywords.} Supersaturation; extremal graph; color-critical graph; chromatic number; expanded graph; hypergraph.

papers.title: A categorical approach to the set-theoretic Yang-Baxter equation
papers.abstract: We investigate set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter equation from a categorical perspective. The paper has two main objectives. On the one hand, several existing constructions and classification results in the literature are recast in categorical terms, thereby showing that certain hypotheses previously imposed on such solutions are in fact superfluous. On the other hand, the categorical approach leads naturally to new classes of Yang-Baxter solutions. Our approach consists in identifying suitable subcategories of the category $\mathcal{YB}$ of Yang-Baxter solutions and providing categorical characterisations of the solutions they encode. As an application, we prove that the category of Płonka bi-magmas is isomorphic to the subcategory of $\mathcal{YB}$ consisting of solutions of the Baaj-Long-Skandalis equation. Along the way, we introduce and study a new class of Lyubashenko type solutions and examine the extent to which non-degenerate bijective solutions of the braid equation arise from skew left braces.

papers.title: Type $B$- and $C$- trigonometric weight functions
papers.abstract: We introduce and study trigonometric weight functions of type $B$ and type $C$ arising from integrable lattice models. These functions give $q$-deformations of the factorial $K$-theoretic Schur $P$- and $Q$-functions of Ikeda and Naruse, with the $P$-functions specialized to the type $B$ case. We realize them as specializations of partition functions of a six-vertex model with triangular boundary conditions and derive their algebraic properties using the Yang-Baxter equation and properties of the $R$- and $K$-matrices. We introduce normalized weight functions and establish diagonal evaluation formulas, divisibility properties, and bounds on Newton polytopes analogous to those in type $A$, together with recursive relations and stability. We further derive branching formulas relating these functions to type $A$ weight functions, and prove equal-cardinality orthogonality and all-cardinality biorthogonality relations.

papers.title: Three-point orbits of 2-transitive groups and their combinatorial applications
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite $2$-transitive permutation group. We determine the orbits of $G$ on the unordered triples of its point set, together with the three-point stabilizer and its image inside $S_3$, for every affine and almost simple family in the finite $2$-transitive classification. These data classify the $G$-invariant triple systems and the simple $2$-\mbox{$(v,3,λ)$} designs admitting $G$, and yield in a uniform way the standard objects attached to them: the incidence and block graphs (with arc-transitivity and strong regularity in the Steiner case), the constant-weight and design codes, and the Schurian coherent configurations on triples.

papers.title: Cyclic steepest descent is $R$-superlinearly convergent for almost every initialization on two-spectrum quadratics
papers.abstract: We completely classify cyclic steepest descent (CSD) on strictly convex quadratics whose Hessian has exactly two distinct eigenvalues. At the beginning of each cycle CSD recomputes an exact steepest-descent stepsize and reuses it for $m$ updates. For every $m\ge2$, write $A=aP+bQ$ with $0<a<b$ and spectral projectors $P,Q$. For nonzero spectral blocks, let $r=\|Pg\|_2/\|Qg\|_2$ at a cycle boundary. The exact projective dynamics is $r^+=r^{1-2m}$. Hence the nonzero equal-norm cone $\|Pg_0\|_2=\|Qg_0\|_2>0$ is precisely the nonterminating exceptional set: there the convergence is $R$-linear with factor $(b-a)/(b+a)$, whereas every other nonterminating initialization is $R$-superlinear and one-eigenspace initializations terminate in one step. The exceptional cone has Lebesgue measure zero, so $R$-superlinear convergence holds almost everywhere in this two-spectrum class. The main results of this paper were obtained through a generative-AI workflow using OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol, Anthropic Claude Fable 5, and OpenAI GPT-6 Astra. Further details appear in the disclosure at the end of the paper.

papers.title: A note on the Chern-Yamabe flow on compact Hermitian manifolds with negative Gauduchon degree
papers.abstract: In this note, we prove that on a compact Hermitian manifold with negative Gauduchon degree, the Chern-Yamabe flow introduced in our recent work [13] converges to the solution of prescribed Chern scalar curvature problem, provided that the candidate curvature function is nonpositive and not identically zero.

papers.title: Quadratic polynomials preserving free infinite divisibility
papers.abstract: We characterize non-commutative polynomials of degree 2 which preserve free infinite divisibility as self-adjoint Lie polynomials of degree 2. This extends previous results which characterized homogeneous quadratic forms only. The proof is based on an involution of colored noncrossing partitions cancelling many terms; positive definiteness of the remaining terms is established by an explicit operator model on Fock space. Examples show that higher order Lie polynomials do not preserve free infinite divisibility.

papers.title: Receiver-Constrained Recovery Placement for Encoded-Qutrit Teleportation under Monitored Decay
papers.abstract: Using established probabilistic measurement-reversal theory, we study recovery placement in encoded-qutrit teleportation under monitored decay. We characterize the success advantage of reversing a no-jump map only on the encoded support and compare two receiver capabilities. The restricted-map construction applies to general finite-dimensional supports; explicit timing results are obtained for a coherent V-type sender, a $Λ$-type receiver, and $S=\{0,2\}$, within a prescribed family of maximal exact sender reversals. With one outcome-independent full-space receiver filter, we maximize success probability at fixed total time subject to a minimum success-weighted conditional fidelity. A single preassigned recovery time yields up to three duration-dependent regimes: no sender reversal, the earliest feasible intermediate reversal, and final-time reversal. If recovery times may be randomized independently of the input and only the pooled successful ensemble must meet the fidelity requirement, the optimum over all such timing distributions mixes the two endpoints for $ΓT \ge (\ln 3)/2$. With Bell-outcome-dependent nonunitary receiver recovery, each accepted full-column-rank transfer branch can instead be reversed exactly. For the same model and sender-operation family, omitting sender reversal uniquely maximizes the exact-teleportation success probability for every finite $T>0$ at positive decay rate. Partial pathway coherence further distinguishes relative support gain from absolute recovery success: the long-time dark-state plateau survives only for fully coherent decay. These results show how receiver control capabilities and the meaning of the fidelity constraint determine whether intermediate sender recovery is useful.

papers.title: Non-vanishing of primitive cubic, quartic and sextic L-functions
papers.abstract: We establish lower bounds for the non-vanishing proportions of primitive cubic, quartic and sextic Dirichlet $L$-functions over $\F_q[T]$ in the non-Kummer setting. Adapting the truncated-exponential method of Gao and Zhao, we improve the cubic lower bound of David, Florea and Lalín and obtain positive lower bounds for quartic and sextic families in which every ramified local character has full order. For each family, the lower limit of the non-vanishing proportion exceeds $e^{-e^{66}}$ as the conductor degree tends to infinity with $q$ fixed. We also establish uniform twisted first moments in the quartic and sextic cases, yielding an asymptotic formula for the sextic first moment. All results are unconditional.

papers.title: Counting Rational Points on a Certain Bihomogeneous Threefold
papers.abstract: Let $V\subset\mathbb P^2\times\mathbb P^2$ be the threefold $x_0y_0^2+x_1y_1^2+x_2y_2^2=0$, and let $U$ be the complement of its coordinate hyperplane sections. For the anticanonical height $H([\mathbf x],[\mathbf y])=|\mathbf x|^2|\mathbf y|$, evaluated on primitive integral representatives, we prove \[ N_U(B)=\frac{12π-14}{ζ(2)ζ(3)}B\log B+o(B\log B). \] The two projections combine lattice counting with uniform conic estimates. The main arithmetic step is an average of the fiber singular series, whose two main terms are related by Hilbert reciprocity. A moment estimate controls the full bad-prime part, and shape estimates permit the errors to be summed over the height region. We also check the leading constant with Peyre's constant.

papers.title: Global solutions to the fully nonlinear obstacle problem
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate global solutions to the fully nonlinear obstacle problem. We prove that, after factoring out invariant directions, the coincidence set of any global solution belongs to one of the following four types: a single point, a compact convex set with nonempty interior, a ray for $n=1$, or a slender body for $n\geq 2$, where $n$ denotes the spatial dimension. Furthermore, we establish a bijection between the collection of all global solutions with compact coincidence sets and a family of functions describing the asymptotic behavior of such solutions at infinity.

papers.title: Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for closed axisymmetric hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We establish sharp Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for closed, embedded, axisymmetric hypersurfaces Sigma in n+1 dimensional Euclidean space R^{n+1}, the dimension n > or = 2, with admissible C^{1,1} profiles. Let H_j be the j-th normalized mean curvature. If Sigma is axiconvex, i.e., every hyperplane orthogonal to the symmetry axis meets the enclosed domain in an n-dimensional ball or empty, then \[\left(\frac{\int_ΣH_\ell\,dA}{|\mathbb S^n|}\right)^{1/(n-\ell)} \le \left(\frac{\int_ΣH_k\,dA}{|\mathbb S^n|}\right)^{1/(n-k)}, \qquad 0\le\ell<k\le n-1. \] Without axiconvexity, the inequalities hold for sign-corrected integrals \[\int_Σ\varepsilon_θ^{\,j}H_j\,dA,\] where varepsilon_{theta}= {sgn}(sin {theta}) denotes the sign of the azimuthal principal curvatures. As applications, the Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities remain valid whenever both l and k are even. Equality in each of the above inequalities holds if and only if Sigma is a round sphere. The proof adapts the rearrangement and tangent angle folding approach of Dalphin-Henrot-Masnou-Takahashi from surfaces of revolution in R^3 to n-dimensional axisymmetric hypersurfaces in R^{n+1}. The higher-dimensional construction uses weighted monotone rearrangement to produce convex comparison bodies with C^{1,1} boundaries.

papers.title: Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receivers for OFDM Systems: An Atomic-Comb Design
papers.abstract: Rydberg atomic quantum receivers (RAQR) exhibit exceptional sensitivity to radio-frequency (RF) signals, positioning them as promising candidates for next-generation wireless systems. Extending their capabilities to orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM), however, requires atomic responses that go beyond broadband reception and are tailored to the structured interference of multicarrier signals. To bridge this gap, we develop an atomic-comb Rydberg receiver based on six-wave mixing (SWM) transduction. In particular, injecting a multi-tone local oscillator (LO) into the RAQR generates frequency-shifted replicas of the intrinsic SWM response. By subtly tuning the amplitude and phase of each LO tone, constructive and destructive interference can be selectively induced to preserve desired response components while attenuating harmful frequency offsets. Furthermore, we harness the response-reshaping capability of the proposed atomic comb to proactively mitigate OFDM interference. More explicitly, by exploiting the discrete difference-frequency structure of both carrier-frequency-offset (CFO)-induced and phase-noise (PN)-induced inter-carrier interference (ICI), we optimize the atomic-comb response to suppress dominant ICI components directly. We further reveal an intrinsic coupling between spectral shaping and the time-domain effective channel memory, motivating a joint optimization of both ICI and inter-symbol interference (ISI), which simultaneously suppresses inter-carrier leakage and post-cyclic-prefix (CP) tail energy. Extensive simulation results validate our atomic-comb design, unveiling that the proposed atomic comb can effectively reshape the receiver response over the OFDM, while mitigating ICI, shortening the effective channel memory, and substantially lowering CP overhead.

papers.title: Quaternionic Elasticity Theory with Local Fractional Derivatives
papers.abstract: We develop a quaternionic formulation of linear elasticity in which the classical derivative is replaced by Yang's local fractional derivative and the classical Cauchy--Riemann operator by a fractal Cauchy--Riemann operator. We formulate fractal kinematics, a constitutive law with a material length scale and the equilibrium equation, and show that, for displacement fields with polynomial components, the resulting homogeneous fractal Lamé system is equivalent to the monogenicity of an explicit quaternionic field. On the polynomial sector, that is, for finite combinations of normalized fractal monomials, we prove a fractal Kolosov--Muskhelishvili representation of the displacement field in terms of two monogenic quaternionic potentials, together with its completeness, by a direct construction that uses neither the Galerkin nor the Papkovich--Neuber potentials. The position term of the classical formula has to be replaced by a corrected position operator, which satisfies the exact Weyl relation with the partial local fractional derivatives. Finally a fractal Papkovich-Neuber representation is derived.

papers.title: A note on the logarithmic exponent of Ramsey number $r(4,t)$
papers.abstract: In this short note, we point out that the recent lower bounds for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers $r(s,t)$ with fixed $s\ge 5$, together with the recent proof of the Ajtai--Erdős--Komlós--Szemerédi independence conjecture, imply \[ r(4,t)=\frac{t^3}{(\log t)^{2+o(1)}}. \] This note is solely for informal circulation and will not be submitted for publication.

papers.title: Refining the 7/8 zero-free half-plane for Hecke and Dirichlet L-functions
papers.abstract: Recently, OpenAI announced a uniform $7/8$ zero-free half-plane for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})$, together with its transfer to Dirichlet $L$-functions. Assuming the analytic inputs of that work, we improve the boundary from $7/8=0.875$ to $8748867/10000000=0.8748867$ for the same families. The improvement combines a relaxed direct estimate with an amplified first moment of the reflected numerator, obtained from the existing fourth-moment estimate. A two-stage parameter argument yields the stated boundary without strengthening the inverse-moment estimate.

papers.title: The Norm Spectrum of Barnes-Wall Lattices Below Twice the Minimum
papers.abstract: Let $Λ_m$ be the Barnes-Wall lattice of dimension $2^m$, normalized to have minimum squared norm $d_m:=2^{m-1}$. We determine its complete norm spectrum strictly between $d_m$ and $2d_m$, proving that, for every integer $m\ge1$, $\{\|x\|^2:x\inΛ_m,\ d_m<\|x\|^2<2d_m\}=\{2d_m-2^j:j\in\mathbb Z,\ \lceil m/2\rceil\le j\le m-2\}$. In particular, the norm spectrum in this interval is nonempty for $m\ge4$. The proof uses a Gaussian-integer model in which lattice automorphisms arising from Clifford unitaries transform a vector into a pair of coordinate subvectors in a lower-dimensional lattice. Divisibility of the differences of their squared norms and a matrix Parseval identity provide the arithmetic and averaging constraints needed for induction on $m$. Every listed norm is realized explicitly by a sum of two minimal vectors of the lattice.

papers.title: On the Structure of the Cut Locus in Certain Classes of Warped Product Manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we determine the structure of the cut locus for a class of complete warped product manifolds $M=(R^1\times S^1,dt^2+m(t)^2dθ^2)$, where the warping function $m(t)$ is positive and even, under the assumption that there exists a positive number $t_1$ such that the Gaussian curvature is nonpositive on the domain $t^{-1}\left((t_1,\infty) \right)$ and is decreasing along the subarc $t^{-1}([0,t_1])\capθ^{-1}(0)$ of the upper half meridian.

papers.title: Unipotent quotients in compactified Coxeter varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we extend Lusztig's description of quotients of Coxeter varieties by unipotent radicals of parabolic subgroups, to quotients of certain open neighbourhoods in the smooth compactification of Coxeter varieties. These quotients are products of an affine space with a Coxeter variety for an associated Levi quotient, and this result holds uniformly for any connected reductive group over a finite field. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Wang computing the invariants, under the action of unipotent subgroups, of the cohomology of the Deligne-Lusztig coverings of Coxeter varieties. We also prove that derived Alvis-Curtis duality sends the compactly supported cohomology of these coverings to their ordinary cohomology.

papers.title: A note on stability conditions on product-quotient surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a product-quotient surface, which is by definition a minimal resolution of $(C_1\times C_2)/G$, where $C_i$ are smooth curves of genus $\geq 2$ and $G$ is a finite group. When $G$ acts freely, we show that every product Bridgeland stability condition on $C_1\times C_2$ induces a tilt stability condition on $X$, and that, if $p_g(X)=q(X)=0$, every tilt stability condition on $X$ arises this way. When $(C_1\times C_2)/G$ has only $A_1$-singularities, we use induction \cite{MMS} and derived McKay correspondence \cite{BKR} to produce non-geometric stability conditions $σ_X$ on $X$, which satisfy the full support property and lie in the closure of the geometric chamber. Whether $σ_X$ also lies in the closure of the $\widetilde{\mathrm{GL}}^+(2,\mathbb{R})$-orbit of the tilt stability conditions depends on a single inequality, $ω_X^2 \ge n/8$, where $n$ is the number of $A_1$-singularities. When it fails, the geometric chamber is strictly larger than this orbit.

papers.title: Nonexistence of Stable Solutions to Lane--Emden Equations on Graphs with Polynomial Volume Growth
papers.abstract: We study stable solutions of the Lane--Emden equation $$-Δu=|u|^{p-1}u$$ on graphs with polynomial volume growth. Due to the lack of a chain rule in the discrete setting, we establish suitable algebraic inequalities which serve as substitutes for the usual differential identities. Combining these inequalities with the stability condition and cutoff arguments, we obtain nonexistence results for stable solutions in a range of exponents analogous to the Joseph--Lundgren range. As an application, we derive a lower bound for the Sobolev best constant in the discrete setting.

papers.title: Weighted moments and sharp convergence rates for supercritical multitype branching processes
papers.abstract: Let $Z_n^i=(Z_n^i(1),\cdots,Z_n^i(d)), n\geqslant0$, be a supercritical $d$-type branching process starting from a single particle of type $i\in\{1,\cdots,d\}$, where $d$ is a positive integer. The Kesten-Stigum theorem states that if the mean matrix $M$ of the offspring distribution has spectral radius $ρ>1$ with the associated positive left and right eigenvectors $u$ and $v$, then for all $1\leqslant i \leqslant d$, the sequence $W_n^i=\langle Z_n^i,u\rangle/ρ^n u(i)$ forms a non-negative martingale, and hence converges almost surely to a random variable $W^i$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic properties of the martingale $\{W_n^i\}$, focusing on weighted moments and sharp rates of convergence. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the finiteness of $φ$-moments of $W^i$, where $φ(x)=x^α\ell(x)$ with $α\geqslant1$ and $\ell$ is a positive function slowly varying at infinity. We also determine the sharp exponential rate of convergence of $W_n^i$ to $W^i$ in the $φ$-moment sense, identify a phase transition at the critical rate $ρ^{1/2},$ and characterize the behavior at the critical value. Our proofs rely on the double martingale structure of the fundamental martingale and on convex inequalities for martingales.

papers.title: Optimal detection of geometry in random graphs and kernel matrices at critical thresholds
papers.abstract: Detection of geometry in random graphs and matrices has been extensively studied in recent years. For testing a dense random geometric graph on $n$ vertices with latent points in dimension $d$ against an Erdős--Rényi graph, the detection threshold $d\asymp n^3$ is well known since Bubeck, Ding, Eldan, and Rácz (2016). We sharpen this result by establishing the optimal asymptotic testing error in the critical regime $d/n^3\toλ\in(0,\infty)$. The log-likelihood ratio is shown to be asymptotically normal and dominated by the signed triangle count. Moreover, we consider testing the rank statistics of inner products between latent points against uniformly random ranks. We show that ranks preserve all asymptotic testing information available in the full matrix models, and a cubic statistic based on rank statistics attains the optimal asymptotic error. This then yields an asymptotically optimal test for random kernel matrices with a possibly unknown, strictly monotone kernel. The proofs combine the classical framework of Davies (1985) and Le Cam and Yang (1988) for asymptotic normality under information loss with conditional limit theorems for the models in consideration.

papers.title: Holomorphic Bisectional Curvature on Total Spaces of Holomorphic Vector Bundles
papers.abstract: We study complete K$ä$hler metrics with prescribed signs of holomorphic bisectional curvature on total spaces of holomorphic vector bundles over compact complex manifolds. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions in the nonnegative and strictly negative cases, characterized respectively by unitary flatness and Griffiths negativity of the bundle, together with the corresponding curvature conditions on the base. We also obtain a global metric splitting in the nonnegative case, rule out strictly positive curvature over positive-dimensional bases, and construct counterexamples to the converse in the nonpositive case.

papers.title: Tuza's Conjecture for Graphs of Maximum Degree at Most 10
papers.abstract: For a finite simple graph $G$, let $ν(G)$ be the maximum number of pairwise edge disjoint triangles and $τ(G)$ the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle. Tuza conjectured in 1981 that every such $G$ satisfies $τ(G) \le 2 ν(G).$ We prove the conjecture for the class of graphs with $Δ\le10.$

papers.title: Moment-Calibrated Conformal Prediction with Side Information
papers.abstract: For a fixed conformal score function, standard split conformal prediction calibrates a prediction set using the empirical distribution of the conformal scores, without using available side information about the data. We propose a moment-calibrated approach that uses such information to reduce variability across calibration data sets. Side information involving the covariates, the response, or both is expressed as moment restrictions, which are enforced through empirical likelihood weights on the calibration data points. The resulting weighted empirical distribution of the scores determines the weighted empirical quantile without changing the score function. We establish finite-sample bounds on training-conditional and marginal coverage of the moment-calibrated prediction set. We derive asymptotic distributions for training-conditional coverage and average prediction-set size, show that their asymptotic variances are no larger than the corresponding variances under standard split conformal prediction, and characterize when the reductions are strict. In the semi-supervised setting, we identify an optimal moment function of a given covariate representation, develop implementations using prespecified moment functions or a function learned by cross-fitting, and quantify the effect of the unlabeled sample size. We also extend the method to coverage conditions indexed by a class of functions of the covariates through weighted quantile regression. Numerical studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

papers.title: The a-number of the Serre-type maximal curves of Abdón-Bezerra-Quoos
papers.abstract: For every prime power $q$, we determine the $a$-number of the Serre-type maximal curves $X(q,n)$: $y^{q^2}-y=x^{(q^n+1)/(q+1)}$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^{2n}}$, $n\ge 3$ odd, introduced by Abdón, Bezerra and Quoos as a generalization of Serre's curve $y^4+y=x^3$ over $\mathbb{F}_{64}$. The Weierstrass semigroup at the unique point at infinity gives an explicit basis of holomorphic differentials, on which the Cartier operator acts by monomials; this reduces the $a$-number to a lattice-point count, which we evaluate in closed form.

papers.title: Asymptotics of Random-Lattice Enumeration: Beyond HKZ via Dense Sublattices
papers.abstract: To bridge the gap between worst-case and heuristic analyses of lattice enumeration, we study the sizes of (unpruned) enumeration trees on $n$-dimensional Haar-random lattices. Writing $n^{cn+o(n)}$ for the tree size at the shortest vector radius, we investigate the asymptotic scaling of $c$, and which bases minimize it. For quasi-HKZ bases, we rigorously analyze the random-lattice HKZ geometry and establish $c=1/(2e)\approx 0.1839$. This matches the worst-case enumeration exponent of Hanrot-Stehlé and confirms earlier predictions for the geometry of HKZ bases on random lattices. Searching beyond quasi-HKZ bases, we prove that with high probability, the minimum achievable tree size exponent $c$ over all bases of a random lattice satisfies: \begin{align} 0.1464 \approx \frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{4}\leq c<0.1474. \end{align} For the lower bound, we use Kim's mean-value formula for nested chains of primitive sublattices to rule out bases with small prefix determinants. This strengthens the earlier Rankin-based heuristic lower bound exponent $c \geq 1/8$, discussed by Nguyen and Hanrot-Stehlé, and rules out the existence of random-lattice bases with trees as small as predicted by the geometric series assumption. For the upper bound, we show that with high probability a dense primitive half-rank sublattice exists with determinant at most $n^{n/8 + o(n)}$. Combining dual HKZ on this sublattice with HKZ on its quotient gives a basis with $c \leq 1/(4\sqrt{e}) \approx 0.1516$. Recursively splitting each half lowers the upper bound below $0.1474$, and under a natural heuristic assumption we prove that the lower bound is tight. Combined with the collision search of Feng-Gao-Liu, our two-block construction gives a polynomial-space algorithm solving the closest vector problem with preprocessing (CVPP) on random lattices in query time $n^{0.0892 n + o(n)}$ for arbitrary targets.

papers.title: Bernoulli numbers and the integer group determinants of $C_p \times C_p$
papers.abstract: For a prime $p\ge7$, let $S(C_p\times C_p)$ be the set of integer group determinants and $e(p)$ the least exponent for which $p^{e(p)}\mathbf Z\subseteq S(C_p\times C_p)$. Let $r_p$ be the least integer $r\ge1$ satisfying $(2r+1)i>r(p-1)$ for every irregular pair $(p,2i)$ with $r\mid i$. We prove the unconditional inclusion $p^{p+3+2r_p}\mathbf Z\subseteq S(C_p\times C_p)$. Equality $e(p)=p+3+2r_p$ holds when Vandiver's conjecture holds for $p$ and $r_p\le(p-5)/2$, hence for every prime $7\le p<2^{31}$. The first exception to $e(p)=p+5$ is $p=103$, where $e(103)=116$. A polynomial obstruction from Bernoulli numbers supplies the lower bound, and circular units give the construction. For regular primes, we characterize the entire determinant set through explicit affine systems over $\mathbf F_p$ and principality conditions in $\mathbf Z[ζ_p]$. For regular $p\ge11$, prime cofactors cannot occur at valuation $p+3$; at valuation $p+4$ they have natural density $(p+1)/(hp^{(p-3)/2})$, where $h$ is the class number of $\mathbf Q(ζ_p)$. We also show that $p^{p+5}$ is the least absolute value of a nonzero $p$-divisible determinant for these regular primes.

papers.title: Some Remarks on Regular Sequences and Complete Intersections
papers.abstract: We give an ideal in a polynomial ring in three variables, generated by three elements and having height equal to three, but for which no permutation of its generators is a regular sequence. We prove that in a polynomial ring over an infinite field, an ideal of height n generated by n polynomials, always admits a set of n generators, for which any permutation is a regular sequence.

papers.title: Weighted norm inequalities for operators with new Muckenhoupt type weights in the Bessel setting and applications
papers.abstract: Let $λ>-1/2,\neq0$. Consider the Bessel operators \begin{align*} Δ_λ:=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}-\frac{2λ}{x}\frac{d}{dx} \end{align*} on $\mathbb{R}_+$. In this paper, we first establish several characterizations for $\widetilde{A}_{\infty,λ}$ weights introduced by Li et al. (Math. Z. 309(1) (2025), Paper No. 13, 29pp), which are different from the previous $A_p$ class with respect to the measure $x^{2λ}dx$. Among these characterizations, we obtain the sharp reverse Hölder inequality (RHI) for $\widetilde{A}_{\infty,λ}$ weights. As applications of RHI, we derive a precise open property of $\widetilde{A}_{p,λ}$ weights, and obtain a sharp weighted bounds for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $\mathcal{M}_λ$ associated to $Δ_λ$, which was missing in the previous papers. Next, we also establish several extrapolation theorems related to $\widetilde{A}_{p,λ}$ weights. Furthermore, we characterize the restricted weighted weak type estimates for $\mathcal{M}_λ$ via a new class of weights $\widetilde{A}_{p,λ}^{\mathcal{R}}$, which is strictly larger than $\widetilde{A}_{p,λ}$. Meanwhile, we obtain quantitative restricted weighted weak type $(p,p)$ bounds for sparse operators. As applications, we derive various kinds of weighted inequalities for Riesz transforms, maximal operators, square functions, variation operators and their commutators associated to $Δ_λ$.

papers.title: Post-critically finite polynomials over cyclotomic closures of number fields
papers.abstract: We prove that, for any number field K and and d at least 2, there are at most finitely many monic, centred, post-critically finite polynomials of degree d with coefficients in the extension of K by all roots of unity.

papers.title: Stabilizers and maximal subgroups of topological full groups
papers.abstract: We study closed-set stabilizers in topological full groups of minimal effective ample groupoids with Cantor unit space. For almost finite or purely infinite groupoids, we extend the maximal stabilizer theorem of Grigorchuk and Vorobets to every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup. For a nonempty closed nowhere dense set, maximality of its stabilizer is equivalent to minimality of its stabilizer action, minimality of the regular reduction, and primeness of a canonical wide open subgroupoid. Without assuming almost finiteness or pure infiniteness, we prove spatial rigidity for stabilizers acting minimally on infinite closed nowhere dense sets. Their isomorphism types determine the ambient Kakutani equivalence class and, when Hausdorff, the effective reduction. We also realize every AF groupoid with compact unit space as the full restriction, with its relative topology, of any minimal effective ample groupoid with Cantor unit space to a closed nowhere dense subset. Combining rigidity and realization yields continuum many pairwise nonisomorphic stabilizers in every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup; these stabilizers are maximal when the ambient groupoid is almost finite or purely infinite. The realization also gives explicit AF subquotients of the ambient reduced groupoid $C^*$-algebra, including the CAR algebra, with compatibility on the canonical diagonal subalgebras.

papers.title: Integral Representations and Sharp Numerical Radius Inequalities for Hilbert Space Operators
papers.abstract: We study the numerical radius \(ω(T)\) of a bounded linear operator \(T\) on a complex Hilbert space. Write \(T=A+iB\), where \(A\) and \(B\) are the real and imaginary parts of \(T\). A central result is the exact formula \[ ω(T)=\fracπ{2}\sup_{\|x\|=1}\int_0^1 \left|\left\langle (A\cos πt+B\sin πt)x,x\right\rangle\right|\,dt . \] For every \(n\in\mathbb N\), we also prove the power form \[ ω^{2n}(T)=\frac{4^n}{\binom{2n}{n}} \sup_{\|x\|=1}\int_0^1 \left\langle (A\cos πt+B\sin πt)x,x\right\rangle^{2n}\,dt . \] This yields sharp upper bounds; for \(n=1\), together with the matching integral lower bound, it recovers Kittaneh's classical two-sided inequality \[ \frac14\|T^*T+TT^*\|\le ω^2(T)\le \frac12\|T^*T+TT^*\|. \] Furthermore, we obtain exact numerical radius formulas for some block operator matrices, including a \(3\times3\) nilpotent matrix and longer alternating paths. The factor \(π/2\) is best possible.

papers.title: Explicit Bounds on Hoffman Constants for Sparse Polyhedral Regularizers
papers.abstract: Hoffman constants quantify the distance to the solution set of a polyhedral system in terms of its residual; they control error bounds, geometric conditioning, the convergence rate of first-order iterative algorithms, and the stability of regression estimators to target perturbations. Despite their importance, explicit values of Hoffman constants are rarely available due to their computational complexity. In this paper, we derive explicit bounds on the Hoffman constant for a class of structured polyhedral systems arising in sparse regularization. We show that the constants admit a decomposition into spectral, geometric, and interaction components, which together determine their scaling behavior. This framework explains the gap between worst-case dimension-dependent bounds and the favorable conditioning observed empirically in structured problems. As a primary application, we analyze $\ell_1$-regularized least squares, demonstrating that the effective constants depend on low-dimensional active subspaces rather than the ambient dimension. We then extend to the elastic net and adaptive $\ell_1$-regularized formulations, demonstrating how the underlying optimization geometry is altered by the $\ell_2$ penalty and reweighting scheme. Furthermore, we relate our results to classical statistical assumptions and show that the restricted eigenvalue condition bounds only the primal curvature of the active set, leaving the dual interaction geometry unconstrained and is thus insufficient alone for fast theoretical convergence rates. We further show standard $\ell_\infty$ coherence conditions do not yield dimension-independent Euclidean bounds to close this gap. Our theoretical results show that Hoffman constants admit explicit, interpretable forms in structured regression settings and, in practice, provide actionable tools for post-hoc feature pruning and a priori optimal hyperparameter selection.

papers.title: Quantum Pick's Theorem in two dimensions
papers.abstract: Consider an $n$-dimensional sum of the form $S_k=\sum{q^{f({\bf z})}}$ over lattice points ${\bf z}$ which lie in $K{\mathcal P}$, the $K$ scaling of an $n$-dimensional rational polytope $\mathcal P$. We formulate a conjecture on the structure of $S_K$ considered for $K$ prime, as a power series in $h=q-1$ modulo the $K^{th}$ cyclotomic polynomial, and in particular the existence of a decomposition in powers of the Gauss sum $\mathbb G$, up to the $n^{th}$, whose coefficients are almost independent of $K$, where the leading coefficient is related to the volume of $\mathcal P$ and the coefficient of ${\mathbb G}^r$ has contributions from the codimension $r$ skeleton of $\mathcal P$. The conjecture is proved for $n=1,2$.

papers.title: Monogamy of quantum steering in exciton--cavity optomechanical system
papers.abstract: In this work, we study a theoretical scheme to investigate the monogamy of quantum steering in a hybrid exciton--cavity optomechanical (EOM) system. Within the Gaussian-state formalism, we quantify the steerability among the exciton, photon, and mechanical modes in both the steady-state and dynamical regimes. We establish and verify CKW-type monogamy inequalities for Gaussian steering and demonstrate that the distribution of bipartite steering among the three modes can be controlled through the system parameters. We further examine the influence of thermal noise and temporal evolution on the steering properties and the corresponding monogamy relations. Our results show that increasing the temperature generally suppresses the strength of Gaussian steering and modifies the degree of steering sharing imposed by the CKW-type monogamy relations. In contrast, in the dynamical regime, the steerability can increase with evolution time over suitable temporal windows, indicating that the transient dynamics can be exploited to enhance quantum correlations. These results highlight the potential of hybrid exciton--optomechanical platforms for controllable quantum correlations and provide a promising route toward the generation and manipulation of multipartite quantum resources.

papers.title: Uniqueness of Bound States for Double-Power Scalar Field Equations
papers.abstract: We study the uniqueness of bound states for the following scalar field equation $$ -Δu+u=-\varepsilon |u|^{q-1}u+|u|^{p-1}u \,\ \ \mbox{in}\,\ \mathbb R^N, \,\ \varepsilon>0,\tag*{$(*)$} $$ where $ N\ge3,\ 1<p<(N+2)/(N-2)$ and $q>1$ satisfies $q \neq p$. For each integer $k \geq 1$, we prove that the equation $(*)$ has, up to translation and reflection, a unique bound state with precisely $k$ nodes in a natural coupling regime, where $\varepsilon>0$ is sufficiently small. Our results address a conjecture of [H. Berestycki and P. L. Lions, ARMA, 1983][M. X. Tang, Invent. Math., 2026] on the uniqueness of fixed-node bound states for the equation $(*)$.

papers.title: Explicit descriptions of all 1-Meixner random vectors
papers.abstract: The 1-Meixner random vectors consist of $d$ real-valued random variables, having finite moments of all orders, for which the commutators between their joint semi-quantum operators and the multiplication operators that they generate are linear combinations of these multiplication operators and the identity operator. This property of random variables imposes a system of first-order partial differential equations on their joint Laplace transform on a neighborhood of $0$ in a Euclidean $d$-space. We provide explicit descriptions of all solutions of the system just mentioned in every dimension $d$.

papers.title: Non-Euclidean Gradient Descent Has Many Edges of Stability
papers.abstract: Recent observations that deep learning models train at the edge of stability have renewed interest in understanding stability properties of classical optimization algorithms. For quadratic objectives, standard gradient descent has a sharp stability threshold: it converges from every initialization when $η<2/L$, diverges from almost every initialization when $η>2/L$, and diverges from every nonzero initialization when $η>2/μ$. For non-Euclidean gradient descent, the corresponding known guarantees are weaker: convergence holds for every initialization when $η<2/S$, where $S$ is the generalized sharpness, while every nonzero initialization diverges when $η>2/μ$. The behavior in the intermediate regime $2/S<η<2/μ$ is not fully characterized. We show that Hilbertian norms are the only ones for which $2/S$ is an almost-everywhere sharp threshold for every positive-definite quadratic objective. Using linear conjugacy between non-Euclidean and Euclidean gradient descent, we show that for general norms the intermediate regime can contain arbitrarily many edges of stability associated with distinct attracting directions. We identify a forward-invariant region of exponentially divergent directions beyond the generalized stability threshold. When the directions of minimum curvature are finite and nondegenerate, we prove that, sufficiently close to $2/μ$ from below, only their invariant directions remain convergent. We give smooth two-dimensional constructions with arbitrarily many distinct thresholds, arbitrarily large relative threshold separation and show these properties to be stable.

papers.title: An adaptive Galerkin neural-network method for minimum-norm control of wave equations
papers.abstract: We develop an adaptive Galerkin neural-network method for computing minimum-$L^2$-norm interior controls for wave equations with spatially varying coefficients. Within the Hilbert Uniqueness Method, adjoint waves are approximated directly in space-time by least-squares Galerkin projections onto trial spaces enriched by neural-network basis functions selected through residual-based training. Linear Galerkin solves determine the adjoint approximations, and a separate linear system reconstructs the control. The least-squares objective provides an indicator for adaptive enrichment and stopping; the experiments use a Ritz-based terminal-data version whose continuous-error interpretation additionally requires an eigenpair consistency estimate. The main difficulty is that adjoint errors perturb this reconstruction system. Assuming observability of the continuous equation, we derive sufficient stability conditions involving a worst-case factor $\sqrt{n}$ multiplying the maximal adjoint error, where $n$ is the number of retained terminal modes. A fully discrete error estimate separates terminal-space truncation, adjoint approximation, and assembly errors, yielding convergence to the minimum-norm control when the truncation error, the $\sqrt{n}$-weighted adjoint error, and the assembly errors tend to zero as $n$ grows. For spectral terminal bases, additional regularity and uniform contraction assumptions yield quantitative convergence rates and show that $O(\log n)$ accepted enrichment steps per mode suffice to balance the neural and truncation errors. Numerical experiments on a nonconvex Cassini oval, a square containing a low-speed lens, and a three-dimensional ball with a graded coefficient illustrate the method.

papers.title: A counterexample to Vaught's Conjecture for $L_{ω_1,ω}$
papers.abstract: We construct a sentence of $L_{ω_1,ω}$ having exactly $\aleph_1$ many countable models up to isomorphism, but no perfect set of non-isomorphic models. This disproves Vaught's conjecture for infinitary logic. The construction follows a framework devised by Robin Knight, and the proof has been formally verified in Lean.

papers.title: Polynomial mixing for infinite-energy solutions of the white-forced Navier--Stokes equation in an infinite pipe
papers.abstract: We study the long-time behavior of the infinite-energy solutions to the white-forced Navier--Stokes equation in an infinite pipe $\mathbb{R}\times (-1,1)$ with no-slip boundary conditions. The equation is globally well-posed in uniformly local spaces satisfying the divergence-free condition. Under suitable degeneracy and spatial decay assumptions on the noise, we prove the uniqueness of the invariant measure and establish polynomial mixing in the dual-Lipschitz metric. This provides an affirmative answer to Open Problem 1 posed by Kuksin and Shirikyan \cite{KS17} in the case of zero cross-sectional flux.

papers.title: A computer-assisted proof of Krzyż's conjecture for the sixth coefficient
papers.abstract: We prove Krzyż's conjecture for the sixth coefficient. Every holomorphic function $f(z)=\sum a_kz^k$ from the unit disk to the punctured disk satisfies $|a_6| \le 2/e$. Equality holds precisely for rotations of $\exp(-(1-z^6)/(1+z^6))$. Every extremal has a Herglotz representation with at most six atoms. By the reduction of Agler and McCarthy and the entropy theorem of Lei and Zhang, it suffices to exclude extremals with fewer than six atoms. We do this by a rigorous computer-assisted branch-and-bound, leaving the equality case entirely to the analytic argument. The main ingredients are explicit first-order conditions for extremals with fewer than the maximal number of atoms, which reduce to Chebyshev relations when one atom is missing, and a bound for the total mass obtained by convexity of the Poisson integral. The same method independently establishes the full-degree property for the known cases $n=3,4,5$.

papers.title: Adaptive two-points zero-order accelerated methods for stochastic convex optimization problems
papers.abstract: We study stochastic convex optimization, where each sampled function can be evaluated at two arbitrary points. Our accelerated method chooses step sizes, batch sizes and smoothing radii from function values. A forward difference between smoothing scales controls the radius; we account for changes in the smoothed objective. Under the stated regularity and second-moment assumptions, exact function evaluations give \begin{multline*} \mathbb{E}\bigl[f(x_N)-f(x^\star)\bigr] \le \widetilde{O}\biggl( \frac{\sqrt{d}\,M_2 D}{\sqrt{T}} +\min\biggl( \frac{L D^2}{N^2},\; \frac{d^{1/4} M D}{N}+\frac{\sqrt{d}\,M D^2}{γ_{\max} N^2} \biggr)\biggr). \end{multline*} Here $N,T,d,D$ denote the numbers of optimization steps and paired evaluations, the dimension and a feasible-set diameter bound, respectively. Evaluations are available within Euclidean distance $γ_{\max}$ of the feasible set. For the population objective $f(x)=\mathbb{E}_ξ F(x,ξ)$, $M$ satisfies $|f(x)-f(y)|\le M\|x-y\|_2$, and $M_2$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}_ξ\|\nabla F(x,ξ)\|_2^2\le M_2^2$ for sample weak gradients in the interior of the evaluation domain. The method requires no $L,M,M_2$, where $L$ is a Lipschitz constant of $\nabla f$; set $L=+\infty$ without smoothness. The method uses exactly $2T$ values in $3N$ sequential sampling rounds with predetermined batches, or $5N$ with batches chosen from observations. An extension selects a search radius without a supplied distance bound. Fixed radius parameters can leave nonvanishing error; suitable choices depending on the budgets yield convergence.

papers.title: Selection of Marginally Stable Patterns by Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract: We study the effect of boundary conditions on the selection of wavenumbers in pattern-forming systems. Prior work established that, for a large class of boundary conditions, equilibria only within a narrow band of wavenumbers are compatible with the boundary. We demonstrate here that for a large class of initial conditions, solutions evolve towards an extremal member of this narrow band of equilibria. In fact, this extremal member is neutrally stable, nonlinearly unstable, and the convergence is realized through a series of snapping events at the boundary. We observe this behavior in simulations of the Swift-Hohenberg equation when the pattern forming region is confined to a large spatial interval through a parameter quench. We prove the convergence in a phase-diffusion approximation using comparison principles and astutely chosen subsolutions that mimic the snapping behavior.

papers.title: Extremals for singular Onofri type inequality in weighted Sobolev spaces
papers.abstract: The $N$-dimensional Euclidean Onofri inequality was proved by Del Pino and Dolbeault for smooth compactly supported functions in $\mathbb{R}^N$ with $N \ge 2$. In this paper, we consider the singular version introduced by Lam and Lu, and extend it to a natural weighted Sobolev space. Next, we establish a sharp singular Carleson-Chang type inequality and prove its equivalence with the singular $N$-dimensional Euclidean Onofri inequality. Furthermore, we prove the existence of nontrivial, non-constant optimizers for the functional associated with the singular Euclidean Onofri inequality, answering open questions left by Del Pino and Dolbeault in the non-singular case, and by Lam and Lu in the case with singularities. To this end, we exploit the classification result obtained for a singular Liouville-type equation involving the $N$-Laplacian. We also prove the conformal invariance of the functional, establish the sharpness of the singular $N$-dimensional Euclidean Onofri inequality in terms of optimal constants, and state several consequences, including a sharp Poincaré inequality.

papers.title: Applications of Royen's Gaussian Correlation Inequality in high-dimensional testing
papers.abstract: Royen's Gaussian Correlation Inequality (GCI) is a fundamental result in statistics and probability, but unfortunately, at least by now, the result is not very well known in the statistical community. In this paper, we demonstrate the potential of GCI in high-dimensional testing problems that involve multivariate Gaussian variables. Leveraging the GCI, we establish sharp Type I error bounds under arbitrary Gaussian covariance structures. We also formulate a conjecture and relate it to the well-known Spherical Cap Covering Conjecture in discrete geometry and Weak Simplex Conjecture in information theory.

papers.title: A Symbolic Differentiation_Summation Framework for Power Sums of Arithmetic Sequences
papers.abstract: We give a self-contained derivation of the closed form of the power sums $S_m(n)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}(a_0+(i-1)d)^m$ in which the Bernoulli numbers enter as constants of integration rather than as prescribed coefficients. The derivation rests on an elementary fact: a sum whose terms are polynomial in the index is the restriction to the integers of a unique polynomial, which satisfies the defining difference equation identically and may therefore be differentiated and integrated exactly. Differentiating lowers the power by one; integrating back introduces a single constant, equal to the slope $S_m'(0)$ of the polynomial at the origin and fixed by the value $S_m(1)=a_0^m$. This yields a closed form for $S_m(n)$ in terms of the constants and a recurrence that determines them, obtained without induction on the exponent and without generating functions. With the Bernoulli numbers defined by their classical recurrence, we identify the constants as $d^mB_m(a_0/d)$; the progression starting at $0$ reproduces that recurrence exactly. In the normalized case they are $B_m(1)$, so $C_1=B_1(1)=+\tfrac12$, a value that reflects the summation range; a reflection identity shows, without generating functions, that the odd constants beyond the first vanish. The coefficients of the recurrence are scaled binomial coefficients from a single row of Pascal's triangle, and the same approach gives closed forms for sequences with polynomial differences. The integral recursion behind the method is known in the normalized case; each result is related to its classical counterpart, and a verified implementation is provided.

papers.title: Fuglede--Kadison Determinants of Shifted Matrix Semicircles
papers.abstract: We prove a variational formula for the Fuglede-Kadison determinant of a self-adjoint matrix semicircle $S_a = a \otimes 1 + \sum_j A_j \otimes s_j$ with deterministic mean $a$. For every real $z$, $\log Δ(S_a - z) = -1/2 + \inf_b F_z(b)$, where the infimum is over positive definite matrices $b$ such that the map $X \mapsto bXb - \sum_j A_j X A_j$ is positive semidefinite, and $F_z$ is an explicit geodesically convex function. Both sides equal $-\infty$ exactly when $z$ is an atom of the spectral measure. The formula was proposed, without proof, in a recent post of Speicher. In the centered case $a=0$ it gives a new proof of the Mai-Speicher capacity formula, and by hermitization it yields a finite-dimensional variational formula for the logarithmic potential of the Brown measure of an arbitrary matrix-valued semicircular element. The proof identifies the determinant with the value of the Dyson action at its critical point and rewrites this critical-point problem as a saddle problem in three matrix variables. For a spectral parameter $z + i\varepsilon$ in the upper half-plane, eliminating two of the variables gives a geodesically convex minimization whose global minimizer is the positive factor $b_\varepsilon$ in a symmetric unitary factorization of the matrix Cauchy transform. The formula on the real axis follows by letting $\varepsilon \to 0$ in the optimal values, with no compactness assumption on the minimizers. At points where the boundary value of the Cauchy transform is nondegenerate, the scales $b_\varepsilon$ converge and the infimum is attained at their limit; this minimizer lies on the boundary of the feasible set when $z$ is in the support of the spectral measure and in its interior when $z$ is in the resolvent set.

papers.title: Deformation and Symmetry in Two Hypergeometric Supercongruences
papers.abstract: We prove two supercongruence conjectures of Li--Long--Tu concerning truncated very-well-poised ${}_7F_6(1)$ series and Fourier coefficients of modular forms. The proofs are based on a common deformation method. By deforming the original truncated hypergeometric series to suitable terminating series, we are able to apply classical hypergeometric transformations together with Mishev's $W(D_5)$ symmetry. This reduces both problems to congruences for lower-rank hypergeometric sums that can be treated using the $p$-adic methods of Long--Tu--Yui--Zudilin. Although the two cases require different local arithmetic calculations, their global proof structure is the same. The resulting argument gives a unified explanation of these two supercongruences and suggests that the same deformation-and-symmetry method may apply more broadly.

papers.title: Closed forms all the way up: the sample variance of four observations
papers.abstract: The distribution function $F(y)=\Pr(S^2\le y)$ of the sample variance $S^2$ of four independent observations is elementary on its entire support for every polynomial parent density on $[0,1]$ (without loss of generality), and we give it in finite closed form for the uniform, Beta$(2,1)$ and Beta$(2,2)$ parents. The support splits at $y = 1/6$, $2/9$ and $1/4$, with the ceiling at $1/3$, all fixed by geometry: in coordinates aligned with the cube diagonal the event $S^2\le y$ is a ball of radius $\sqrt{3y}$, the cube projects to a rhombic dodecahedron, and these are the levels at which the ball reaches its faces, edges and two kinds of vertices. The divergence theorem reduces every moment of the clipped ball to integrals along circular arcs, so each regime closes in algebraic functions of $\sqrt{y}$ and inverse trigonometric functions. For the uniform parent the only non-obvious constant is $K_g = 12\sqrt2\arctan\sqrt2$, proportional to the mean width of the cuboctahedron; the Beta constants are rational expressions in $π$, $\sqrt2$, $\sqrt3$ and $\arctan\sqrt2$, as in the uniform case. At $n = 4$ the normal-theory $χ^2$ recipe used in acceptance testing misplaces the $99$th percentile of $S^2$ by $50\%$ for the uniform parent. For three observations, polynomial parents also give elementary closed forms (arXiv:2609.25333), but two elementary cases in a row do not guarantee a third, and we make no claim beyond $n = 4$.

papers.title: Interpolation in path-connected metric spaces using splines on embedded graphs
papers.abstract: We study a local graph-based interpolation framework for data defined on graph vertices embedded in a metric space. The resulting interpolants are constructed from variational graph splines defined on small neighborhoods, yielding continuous-domain extensions of the graph data. We analyze their behavior through energy estimates, Lipschitz continuity, and stability properties, and compare them with $k$-Nearest Neighbor ($k$NN) interpolation as a natural baseline due to its simplicity and widespread use. Numerical experiments on the manifold of symmetric positive definite matrices illustrate the relative performance of the proposed local interpolation schemes and $k$NN interpolation across varying levels of smoothness and noise.

papers.title: Sparsity and uniformity in dynamical Manin--Mumford problems
papers.abstract: For endomorphisms of the complex projective plane of a given degree, we prove that the existence of a special curve of bounded degree, in the sense of the dynamical Manin--Mumford conjecture, is confined to a proper algebraic subvariety of the parameter space. This confirms a conjecture of DeMarco and Mavraki in dimension two. For general regular polynomial endomorphisms of $\mathbb A^k$, we obtain a uniform dynamical Manin--Mumford bound outside an exceptional hypersurface. These results arise from a common strategy, valid in every dimension and codimension, which reduces such questions to the geometry of exceptional loci in the space of pairs formed by subvarieties and maps. We control these loci by combining arithmetic equidistribution, blender constructions, dynamical directions, monodromy arguments, and degenerations at the boundary of parameter space.

papers.title: On the set of orthogonal positive sums in a $C^*$-algebra
papers.abstract: For a $C^*$-algebra $A$ let $\mathcal I(A)$ be the set of all elements $a+b$ with $a,b\in A_+$, $ab=0$ and $\|a\|=\|b\|=1$. We study the algebraic, metric and topological properties of $\mathcal I(A)$. We describe $\mathcal I(A\oplus B)$ and show that $\mathcal I(A/J)\subseteqπ(\mathcal I(A))$ for the quotient map $π:A\to A/J$. For finite-dimensional $A$ we prove $\mathcal I(A)=\operatorname{Sph}^+_A(E(A))$, where $E(A)$ is the set of minimal projections of $A$ and $\operatorname{Sph}^+_A(E)$ is the set of positive norm-one elements at distance one from every element of $E$; we also show that the analogous statement with the minimal projections of the bidual fails in general. When $\mathcal I(A)\neq\varnothing$ the distance from $1$ to $\mathcal I(A)$ is $0$ or $1$, according to whether $A$ has a nontrivial projection. Moreover, $\mathcal I(A)$ is norm compact if and only if $A$ is finite-dimensional, closedness of $\mathcal I(A)$ passes to hereditary subalgebras, $\mathcal I(A)$ is norm closed for every von Neumann algebra, and the extreme points of $\mathcal I(A)$ are exactly its projections. For a compact, locally path connected space $X$ the set $\mathcal I(C(X))$ is closed, whereas $\mathcal I(\ell_c(A))$ fails to be closed when $A$ is unital without nontrivial projections.

papers.title: On Chow and Picard groups of Richardson varieties
papers.abstract: We show that if $Π\subseteq G/P$ is a projected Richardson variety, then the degree map $\mathrm{Pic}(Π) \to A_1(Π)^\vee$ is injective. Moreover, it is an isomorphism in characteristic zero and in all but finitely many positive characteristics. We conjecture that it is an isomorphism in every characteristic. Our proofs are geometric, using a linear paving, topological properties of klt singularities, and reduction to characteristic zero.

papers.title: Zero-divisor graphs and zero-divisor real rank of $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We study two invariants of $C^*$-algebras built from positive zero divisors. First, we associate with a $C^*$-algebra $A$ the graph $Γ_+(A)$ whose vertices are the nonzero positive zero divisors of $A$, two vertices being adjacent when they are orthogonal. We show that $Γ_+$ of the Calkin algebra is connected of diameter $3$, that $Γ_+(B(H))$ is connected of diameter $4$ (for $\dim H\ge3$), that $Γ_+(A)$ is connected of diameter at most $4$ for every von Neumann factor $A\neq\mathbb C,M_2(\mathbb C)$, and of diameter at most $3$ if $A$ is not of type~I, whereas $Γ_+(M_2(\mathbb C))$ is disconnected. Second, we study the zero-divisor real rank $ZDRR(A)$, obtained by replacing invertibility in the definition of real rank with the weaker condition of being a non-zero-divisor, so that $ZDRR(A)\le RR(A)$. For commutative algebras $C(X)$ we prove $ZDRR(C(X))=RR(C(X))=\dim X$ when $X$ is a compact almost-$P$-space, while $ZDRR(C(X))=0$ for separable $X$. Using Levy's connected, totally ordered almost-$P$-space we construct unital commutative $C^*$-algebras $A_n$ with $ZDRR(A_n)=n$ for every $n\in\mathbb N_0$. On the other hand $ZDRR(C(X\times[0,1]))=0$ for every compact Hausdorff space $X$, so $ZDRR$ and $RR$ can differ arbitrarily.

papers.title: Extremal graphs with cycle lengths in a fixed residue class
papers.abstract: For integers $k\ge3$ and $0\le \ell<k$, we call a graph $(\ell\bmod k)$-cycle-restricted if every cycle has length congruent to $\ell$ modulo $k$. Akbari, Jamaali, Mahmoody, and Seyed Fakhari [On the size of graphs whose cycles have length divisible by a fixed integer, Australas. J. Combin. 45 (2009), 67--72] determined the maximum number of edges in a $2$-connected $(0\bmod k)$-cycle-restricted graph and characterized the graphs attaining equality. In this paper, we determine the maximum number of edges in a $2$-connected $(\ell\bmod k)$-cycle-restricted graph for every $\ell \neq 0$, and completely characterize all graphs attaining equality. Combined with the result of Akbari et al., our result gives a complete solution for all residue classes modulo $k$.

papers.title: A quotient of the Bruhat-Tits building classifying maximal matrix orders over curves
papers.abstract: In a previous work, we defined a quotient graph of the Bruhat-Tits tree associated to the degree two special linear group over a local field whose vertex set is in correspondence with the maximal orders in a certain number of spinor genera. This graph has been applied to the study of the structure of some arithmetic groups, their presentations and their (co)homology groups. The genera of Eichler orders, which, for instance, are related to the problem of finding a basis that simultaneously splits two vector bundles with the same generic fiber, can often be described in terms of simpler genera via quotients. Furthermore, some embedding problems of orders can be studied via quotient graphs. These results provide a geometric framework for the study of maximal orders over function fields. In this article, we extend that construction to a higher dimensional setting through the use of singular chain complexes. Then we describe the set of vertices in this quotient that correspond to split maximal orders and the topology of the corresponding region of the quotient complex. More precisely, we show that these ``split vertices'' fall into a finite number of quotients of apartments by suitable subgroups of the corresponding Weyl group, the symmetric group. We relate these ``quotient apartments'' with the cuspidal sectors defined by previous authors who studied the quotient by the group of integral points of the special linear group. Both quotients are indeed related by a ramified cover that is unramified on cusps, as proved here.

papers.title: Nim heaps in the Game of Cycles: the parity conjecture fails on trees
papers.abstract: The Game of Cycles, invented by Francis Su, is a two-player game in which the players take turns drawing arrows on the edges of a plane graph, never creating a sink or a source. On a tree only the sink-source rule matters, and the player who makes the last move wins. Several authors conjectured that on a tree the second player wins exactly when the number of markable edges is even. We show that this parity conjecture is false, and we explain why. The explanation is a hidden game of Nim: a path segment that is blocked by an arrow at one end and free at the other behaves exactly like a nim heap whose size is its length. Combined with a calculus for cutting and gluing trees at vertices next to leaves, this shows that the conjecture fails as soon as a single tree has Grundy value at least 2. The smallest counterexamples have 15 vertices. Trees with Grundy values 2 and 4 first appear at 17 vertices, and every value up to 63 occurs, which answers a question of Fokkink and Zandee. We also refute a related conjecture of Zandee. We then look closely at spiders. The spiders S(2,3,z) violate the conjecture for every z >= 14. The Grundy values of S(1,2j,z) are given by an exact formula governed by binary carries. For 99 pairs (x,y), the value of S(x,y,z) is eventually the parity of z. On the positive side, the conjecture holds for all trees in which every thread has at most two edges, and this bound is sharp. Along the way we prove a twin-branch reduction, give an algorithm that is polynomial for spiders with a fixed number of legs, and collect the questions that we could not answer. The boldest asks whether every non-negative integer is the Grundy value of some tree.

papers.title: When Is Local Time Stepping Worthwhile? A Cost Analysis for Nested Adaptive Mesh Refinement
papers.abstract: In deep hierarchies of adaptive mesh refinement, the update work that subcycling avoids is set mainly by the dimension of what is refined, not of the space. Subcycling (local time stepping) does less work than global stepping, advancing each level with the finest step, provided its extra coordination cost stays below an overhead budget $β=1-1/\Sid$ as a fraction of the global-stepping work. Here $\Sid$ is the ideal speedup that the cell counts give for equal update costs. When each level follows a feature of box-counting dimension $δ$ and the counts grow geometrically, the budget of a code that advances every cell tends to $(r-1)/(r^{δ+1}-1)$ for refinement ratio r. A point leaves a budget near one, while a surface in three dimensions leaves 1/7 at r=2 and 1/21 at r=4, values implied by the planar estimates of Dursi and Zingale. Published comparisons in discontinuous Galerkin and octree codes with local time stepping imply overheads of 0.1 to 5 percent of the work, below 1/7 and comparable with 1/21. In paired runs of one AMReX code on one core, a cost model fixed in advance and fitted on points and filled regions predicted the speedups of curves and surfaces with a median error of 7 percent (22 percent on the saving); post hoc, the update counts alone did as well except for points. The overhead, as defined here, was negative in all 17 configurations, but when computed from speedups like the published values, it ranged from -0.11 to 0.19, and no configuration came near break-even. When an update costs the same under both schedules, one profiled run can show that subcycling pays.

papers.title: On Waring-Goldbach problem for two squares, three biquadratics, one quintic and one septic
papers.abstract: In this paper, it is proved that every sufficiently large odd integer $n$ can be represented as \begin{equation*} n=p_1^2+p_2^2+p_3^4+p_4^4+p_5^4+p_6^5+p_7^7, \end{equation*} where $p_1,\dots,p_7$ are prime variables. This result constitutes an enhancement upon a previous result of Andrade [1].

papers.title: On a variant of the Piatetski-Shapiro prime number theorem
papers.abstract: Denote by $Π_γ(x)$ the number of primes $p \leqslant x$ such that $[p^{1/γ}]$ is also a prime. In this paper, it is proved that the expected asymptotic formula \begin{equation*} Π_γ(x)=\frac{γx}{(\log x)^2} (1+o(1)) \end{equation*} holds for $γ> 15/13$, which constitutes an improvement upon the previous result of Balog [2] who showed that the above asymptotic formula holds for $γ> 6/5$.

papers.title: Weak universality of global dynamics for the fractional hyperbolic $Φ^4_3$-model
papers.abstract: We continue the study of weak universality for the fractional hyperbolic $Φ^4_3$-model initiated by Tzvetkov, Wang, and the author (2023). In this work, we establish weak universality in a regime where the associated Gibbs measure is mutually singular with respect to the underlying Gaussian measure. We first investigate the weak convergence of the Gibbs measures associated with macroscopic models to the fractional $Φ^4_3$-measure constructed by Tzvetkov, Wang, and the author (2023). We then obtain a structured representation for these Gibbs measures via the stochastic quantization method. Finally, we prove dynamical weak universality for the fractional hyperbolic $Φ^4_3$-model by using an extended second order expansion and exploiting the invariance of the Gibbs measures.

papers.title: Double-arc rearrangement and the symmetric isoperimetric problem in Gauss space
papers.abstract: We provide a new rearrangement in Gauss space transforming symmetric sets while decreasing their Gaussian perimeter. We use this rearrangement to analyze the minimizers of the Gaussian perimeter among symmetric sets.

papers.title: Cones of Theta Graphs are Enumeratively Chromatic-Choosable
papers.abstract: Chromatic choosability is a fundamental notion in list coloring. A graph $G$ is chromatic-choosable if its chromatic number $χ(G)$ equals its list chromatic number $χ_{\ell}(G)$. In 1990, Kostochka and Sidorenko introduced the list color function of a graph $G$, denoted by $P_{\ell}(G,m)$, which is the list-coloring analogue of its chromatic polynomial $P(G,m)$. A graph $G$ is enumeratively chromatic-choosable if $P_{\ell}(G,m)=P(G,m)$ for every $m \in \mathbb{N}$. In 2002, Ohba proved that for every graph $G$, there exists an $N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $K_p \vee G$ is chromatic-choosable whenever $p \geq N$. Allred and Mudrock recently conjectured that an analogous statement holds for enumerative chromatic choosability. In this paper, we prove that $K_1 \vee G$ is enumeratively chromatic-choosable whenever $G$ is a theta graph. Our proof combines classical inequalities, the polynomial method, and ideas from DP (or correspondence) coloring.

papers.title: Polynomial Identities for Generalized Fibonacci Sequences
papers.abstract: The Fibonacci, Lucas, and Pell sequences satisfy certain families of ``polynomial'' identities. While a few members of these families are well-known, we are not able to find a general statement of these identities in the mathematical literature. We show that such polynomial identities exist for many generalized Fibonacci sequences, and we classify sequences that have these identities obtained by two distinct approaches. One approach uses the Girard-Waring formula, while the other relies on Binet's formula and linear algebra.

papers.title: The exact worst-case asymptotic rate of Nesterov acceleration for strongly convex optimization
papers.abstract: We study Nesterov's accelerated gradient method with its standard constant parameters for smooth strongly convex optimization. We characterize the exact worst-case asymptotic factor for the squared distance to the minimizer. To this end, we construct candidate worst-case trajectories by combining planar spirals with a common contraction factor that satisfy a self-similarity condition.
