These findings establish a critical benchmark for quantum utility, proving that scalable, neuromorphic quantum machine learning can now address complex, non-linear real-world problems.

papers.title: Bicycle Race: small two-block codes on the Pareto frontier
papers.abstract: Two-block group-algebra codes are among the simplest quantum LDPC codes, and many of them are translation invariant on a twisted torus, which suits neutral-atom arrays and other platforms with movable qubits. We ask how far they go at small sizes when searched systematically across all groups. We use algebraic constraints and screens to design a search pipeline capable of enumerating broad and complete swathes of two-block codes on a laptop. With it we census about $10^8$ two-block codes with up to $320$ qubits at check weights five to nine. Several of these censuses are exhaustive, and support complete statements; for instance, the Gross code is, up to equivalence, the only abelian weight-six two-block code with $n \le 200$ to reach $kd^2/n=12$, no weight-six two-block code with $n \le 300$ beats $[[288,16,16]]$, and the known $[[64,18,8]]$ is the best two-block code by $kd^2/n$ across weights five to nine with $n \le 94$. The censuses are also large enough to give insights into where good codes live - they concentrate in a handful of groups; abelian groups give the best codes at small $n$ and non-abelian groups at large $n$, with the crossover appearing to move out as the check weight grows; and high quality codes become $100$ to $1000$ times rarer per draw from weight six to weights eight and nine. Using the group algebra and the census data to steer a statistical search finds four to fifteen times as many good codes as uniform draws in equal time. Among the codes found are $[[102,20,10]]$ and $[[120,24,10]]$ at check weight nine, which we simulate in noisy syndrome-extraction circuits, and $[[186,20,18]]$, a weight-nine code with every check in a $5\times5$ window. At check weights seven to nine, our best codes exceed the best published $kd^2/n$ with exact distance at the same check weight in most length bands up to $320$ qubits. All codes are available in a public database.

papers.title: GPU-Based Parallel BP Decoding for Quantum LDPC Memory
papers.abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) decoding requires reliable corrections and low latency over long syndrome histories. We extend BP-SF, an oscillation-guided belief-propagation (BP) decoder with independent syndrome-flip trials, by introducing windowed and streaming operations. Our CUDA implementation combines disordered-memory retries, sliding windows, correlation-aware graphs, and layered scheduling. Circuit-level simulations test fixed-basis memory and complete logical Pauli-frame recovery. On the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle code at physical error rate p = 0.002, parallel BP-SF reduces 99.9th-percentile call latency by a factor of 13.15 relative to an eight-chain Relay-BP GPU baseline on 100,000 matched samples for which every tested method's initial BP stage fails within 80 iterations. Windowed BP-SF maintains a flat logical error rate and nearly constant per-round compute time through 512 rounds, reaching a 17.1-fold speedup over monolithic decoding. In 512-round full-frame streaming decoding with 2.97-ms syndrome arrivals, layered BP-SF on a transformed joint graph with 20 retries reduces 99.9th-percentile correction-release age from 166.29 to 36.25 ms relative to the joint graph with flooding updates and 100 retries. These results connect parallel BP post-processing to lower decoding costs and earlier correction release in streaming quantum memory.

papers.title: Best proximity point results of operator type condensing mappings via measure of noncompactness and application to an infinite system of differential equations in $c_0$ and $\ell_1$
papers.abstract: We propose a new class of cyclic (noncyclic) operator type condensing mappings and establish conditions that guarantee the existence of best proximity points (pairs) using measure of noncompactness. The results obtained are further applied to investigate the optimum solution of an infinite system of differential equations in $c_0$ and $\ell_1$.

papers.title: On the saturability of $p$-adic Lie groups
papers.abstract: Lazard theory is becoming increasingly important in $p$-adic representation theory, especially when studying mod $p$ representations. For $G$ a connected reductive group defined over a finite extension $K/\mathbb Q_p$, a question going back to Lazard is when a pro-$p$ Iwahori subgroup of $G(K)$ admits a saturated $p$-valuation. In this article, we establish a deep connection to Moy-Prasad theory, and show that the Moy-Prasad filtration defines a saturated $p$-valuation on $G_{x,\frac{1}{p-1}+}$ for any point $x$ in the semisimple Bruhat-Tits building of $G$, given a mild assumption on the maximal torus of $G$ and that $p>2$. We also compute Lazard Lie algebras defined over $\mathbb Z_p$ and the polynomial ring $\mathbb F_p[\varepsilon]$ associated to the saturated group $G_{x,\frac{1}{p-1}+}$, which allows us to reinterpret the Moy-Prasad isomorphism as an isomorphism of Lie algebras over $\mathbb F_p[\varepsilon]$.

papers.title: Sharp Robertson-type coefficient estimates for radial starlike and quasi-convex of type B mappings of order α in complex Banach spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study biholomorphic mappings $F: \mathbb{B} \to X$ of the form $F(z) = f(z)z$ for $z \in \mathbb{B}$, where $f: \mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{C}$ is a holomorphic function satisfying $f(0) = 1$. Our main contributions are as follows: We establish sharp estimates for the coefficients of starlike functions of order $α$ as well as quasi-convex functions of type $B$ and order $α$ by employing the notion of majorization. The results established here directly extend the results due to Robertson \cite{Robertson-1936} to the broader setting of complex Banach spaces.

papers.title: Characterizing higher-dimensional Hölder domains via spherical geometric functions
papers.abstract: In this paper we characterize the regularity of a domain in terms of the behavior of a certain spherical function. More precisely, given two domains we show that a certain spherical spectral function (first defined in \cite{FTV23}, see also \cite{AKN21}) has Hölder decay if and only if the domains are complementary and separated by a $C^{1,β}$-manifold. This extends the analysis in \cite{Ca24} to dimensions $\geq 3$ and in \cite{FTV23, CTV25} to regularity above the continuous threshold. Along the way, we introduce a spherical analogue of the Jones $β$-numbers and show that the decay of these numbers implies geometric regularity of the domain on which they are defined. We believe this result is of independent interest and partially addresses a question of Fleschler-Tolsa-Villa \cite[Question 1]{FTV23}.

papers.title: On Divisor Function Polynomials and Dirichlet Series
papers.abstract: We find the Dirichlet series and convergence bounds for the counting function of sum systems (collections of sets of non-negative integers whose Minkowski sum is an arithmetic progression). This motivates the definition and study of divisor function polynomials, which are generating functions for the non-trivial divisor function and for the balanced divisor function that counts, up to a sign, non-trivial ordered factorisations into squarefree factors. These divisor function polynomials turn out to be intimately connected between each other and with Bernoulli numbers and ordered Bell polynomials.

papers.title: Degree similar and net-degree similar signed graphs
papers.abstract: Two graphs are degree similar if their adjacency matrices and their degree matrices are simultaneously similar, a notion recently introduced by Godsil and Sun. We extend it to signed graphs in two ways, degree similarity and net-degree similarity, according to whether the degree or the net-degree matrix is used. We prove that signed trees are determined by their degree similarity class, but not by their net-degree similarity class. We then develop constructions of (net-)degree similar signed graphs, based on a signed version of Godsil--McKay switching, on partial transposition and on block extensions. As a byproduct, we obtain infinite families both of pairs of net-degree similar unicyclic signed graphs with non-isomorphic underlying graphs, and of unicyclic signed graphs, not necessarily regular, which are not determined by their degree similarity class. This settles the net-degree version of a problem of Godsil and Sun on unicyclic graphs.

papers.title: Clique and chromatic numbers of graph powers: spectral bounds and anticodes
papers.abstract: Using spectral and polynomial methods, we show several sharp spectral bounds for the clique and chromatic numbers of graph powers that only use spectral information from the original graph. In particular, we strengthen earlier spectral-radius estimates to obtain an asymptotically sharp colouring bound for general graph powers, and prove a sharp bound for powers of line graphs with a complete characterisation of equality. We also develop polynomial methods yielding upper and lower bounds for clique numbers of graph powers. Regarding the connection between the clique and coloring parameters of graph powers, we propose a spectral analogue of Wegner's conjecture, determine the extremal values for graph squares, and establish the conjecture for all powers when the spectral-radius bound is sufficiently small. Finally, we connect our spectral polynomial method with coding theory: we prove that for distance-regular graphs, optimisation over the adjacency algebra recovers Delsarte's linear programming bound for anticodes.

papers.title: Weighted, GIT and Néron--Tate heights on genus-two moduli and Jacobians
papers.abstract: We compare three heights attached to a curve of genus two: the weighted height of its Igusa--Clebsch invariants, the GIT height of a binary sextic defining it, and the Néron--Tate height on its Jacobian. For a morphism from an abelian variety to a weighted projective space we define a weighted Néron--Tate height and show that the weighted height differs from it by a linear form and a bounded function; the linear form vanishes when inversion is induced by an automorphism of the weighted projective space. For binary sextics we prove the explicit inequality $h_{\inv}\le h_{\text{GIT}} + \frac{1}{2} \log 302$, with nonnegative local differences at the finite places that vanish at places of good reduction. We then construct a family of semistable binary sextics over $E\times E$, where $E:y^2=x^3-2$, whose relative Jacobian carries a section of infinite order, and we show that the Jacobian over the base point is absolutely simple. Along every curve in the parameter space through the base point, the Néron--Tate height of the section is a positive multiple of the weighted moduli height up to an error of square-root size, and up to a bounded error when the curve is rational. As applications, we obtain explicit families of genus-two Jacobians of positive rank over $\mathbf{Q}$, an infinite congruence lattice of fibres of positive height, and canonical-limit formulas along elliptic curves in $E\times E$.

papers.title: A counterexample to Nirenberg's conjecture on closed asymptotic curves
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth embedded annulus in $R^3$ with negative Gauss curvature in its interior whose boundary consists of two strictly convex curves in planes tangent to the annulus, and which contains two closed asymptotic curves. This gives a counterexample to a 1962 conjecture of Nirenberg. The construction is based on Lelieuvre's formula, which yields a closed curve that is then realized as an asymptotic curve on a ruled annulus. The second asymptotic curve is obtained from the periodic solution of a Riccati equation.

papers.title: A Network Simplex Framework For Discrete Unbalanced Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: The network simplex method is a classical algorithm for minimum cost flow problems formulated as linear programs, that has attracted recent interest from the optimal transport community. Indeed, discrete optimal transport is a subclass of minimum cost flow for which network simplex techniques compute exact solutions while leveraging the inherent problem sparsity. However, extending these approaches to other, nonlinear optimal transport formulations has yet to be thoroughly investigated. In this paper, we adapt the network simplex algorithm to unbalanced optimal transport. Our proposed framework is applicable to various unbalanced formulations, and can be implemented explicitly in the most common cases, including semi-unbalanced optimal transport. The resulting algorithms are memory-efficient, and perform competitively with existing approaches, as shown by our experiments on a range of transport and barycenter calculations.

papers.title: On diagonal sections of Markov products of copulas
papers.abstract: Given a bivariate copula $C$, the bivariate copula $Ψ(C)$ is defined as the Markov product of $C^T$ and $C$. In this paper we consider the diagonal section of $Ψ(C)$ under the additional assumption that its value at a single point is known. We determine the exact upper and lower bounds for the diagonal section of $Ψ(C)$, given that $Ψ(C)(a,a)=d \in [a^2,a]$, where $a \in [0,1]$ is a fixed point. Furthermore, we describe some additional properties of the transformation $Ψ$, such as its behavior under ordinal sums and the survival operation. We also study checkerboard copulas in the range of $Ψ$ and matrices associated to them.

papers.title: A Hardware-Native Trapped-Ion Hybrid Qudit-Oscillator Instruction Set
papers.abstract: Scaling trapped-ion processors by adding ions remains challenging. A complementary route exploits the multilevel internal structure of each ion to increase the computational Hilbert space per ion. We introduce a hardware-native hybrid qudit-oscillator instruction set for a general d-level internal register coupled to bosonic modes and prove that three of its native operation families suffice for universality of one qudit coupled to several modes. Adding an entangling operation between ions extends universality to a connected register of several qudits. The architecture natively supports both phase-space and sideband instruction sets and is implemented in the open-source framework HybridLane. As a representative application, we reproduce the dissipative vibronic dynamics of a three-chromophore complex previously simulated on a hybrid qubit-oscillator superconducting platform. Moving from a one-qubit-per-state register to a single qudit stores the entire electronic manifold in one ion, so every electronic coupling becomes a local intra-ion transition and the lab-frame Hamiltonian compiles directly into the ISA. Under the stated sequential timing model from a 40Ca+ qudit processor, one Trotter step is projected to run about ten times faster on the qudit, with an average RMSE of approximately 1.1 percent against the published reference.

papers.title: Dimension-free Markov--Bernstein-type inequality for $\mathbb R^2$-valued polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove a dimension-free Markov--Bernstein-type inequality for polynomial mappings $(f_1,f_2)\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^2$ of degree at most $d$. For product probability measures whose one-dimensional marginals have densities bounded by $1$, we obtain a lower bound for the integral of the Gram determinant of $\nabla f_1$ and $\nabla f_2$ in terms of the Gram determinant of the $d$-th derivative tensors $D^df_1$ and $D^df_2$, with a constant depending only on $d$. For pairs in a fixed Wiener chaos, the resulting Gaussian inequality answers a question of Nourdin, Nualart, and Poly concerning a lower bound for the expectation of the Malliavin determinant in terms of the determinant of the covariance matrix.

papers.title: Geometry of semi-infinite geodesics in the Airy line ensemble
papers.abstract: We study the geometry of semi-infinite geodesics in the Airy line ensemble. We establish sharp estimates for disjointness probabilities involving geodesics with nearby directions and endpoints in the top line of the Airy line ensemble. Moreover, we obtain a power law upper bound on the coalescence depth of two semi-infinite geodesics with same asymptotic direction and establish exponential concentration estimates for geodesic jump times more generally. We also establish pathwise Hölder $1/2^-$-continuity of Busemann profiles associated to semi-infinite geodesics with common asymptotic directions (in terms of the asymptotic direction). We characterize exceptional behaviour of semi-infinite geodesics through their Busemann profiles and establish geometric properties of the associated sets of non-coalescence and non-uniqueness. Finally, we determine the Hausdorff dimensions of collections of semi-infinite geodesics: collections with a fixed top-line endpoint and arbitrary positive asymptotic direction almost surely have Hausdorff dimension $1$, while collections with a fixed positive direction and arbitrary endpoint almost surely have Hausdorff dimension $3/2$.

papers.title: Bourgain-Rosenthal-Schechtman spaces in rearrangement-invariant and Hardy spaces
papers.abstract: In 1981, Bourgain, Rosenthal, and Schechtman constructed uncountably many pairwise non-isomorphic complemented subspaces of $L_p$ for $1 < p < \infty$, $p \neq 2$. We extend their construction to rearrangement-invariant spaces and Hardy spaces. For any separable rearrangement-invariant space $X$ with non-trivial Boyd indices, we show that these subspaces are complemented, previously obtained by Ghawadrah via a different argument, and establish the following dichotomy: Either one can extract an uncountable family of pairwise non-isomorphic subspaces, or they are all isomorphic to $X$. To this end, we introduce an ordinal index that detects whether $X$ embeds complementably into an arbitrary separable Banach space. On the other hand, we give sufficient conditions which imply that in certain spaces close to $L_1$ and $H^1$, these subspaces fail to be complemented.

papers.title: Biholomorphic rigidity and symmetry breaking for domains with Bergman metric of constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature
papers.abstract: Based on earlier work by Wiegerinck and Huang-Li, Hayashida-Kamimoto constructed unbounded non-smooth Reinhardt domains in \({\mathbb C}^n\), \(n\geq 3\), whose Bergman spaces are finite-dimensional and whose Bergman metrics have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). In this note, we prove a Sandwich Principle for the Hayashida-Kamimoto domains that allows us to construct, inside every prescribed sandwich, uncountably many pairwise biholomorphically inequivalent smooth non-Reinhardt domains whose Bergman metrics also have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). We also classify biholomorphisms between domains sandwiched by the domains of Hayashida-Kamimoto with the help of an affine rigidity theorem in the spirit of Cartan rigidity, which should be of independent interest. For explicit angular perturbation families, we determine the full automorphism group and obtain, in particular, an abundance of examples with trivial automorphism group.

papers.title: Monodromy of Tate-Linear varieties
papers.abstract: We answer a question of Chai about the rigidity of Tate-linear subvarieties of $\mathcal{A}_g$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$: we show that that a smooth subvariety of a central leaf of $\mathcal{A}_g$ which is Tate-linear at one point is Tate-linear at every point. This is achieved by a careful analysis of the $p$-adic monodromy groups of Tate-linear varieties, building on recent work of D'Addezio and van Hoften.

papers.title: Counting cographs in locally dense graphs
papers.abstract: An $n$-vertex graph $G$ is $(ρ, d)$-dense if for all $U \subseteq V(G)$ of size at least $ρn$, the induced subgraph $G[U]$ contains at least $\frac{d}{2}|U|^2$ edges. In 2010, partly motivated by the theory of quasirandomness, Kohayakawa, Nagle, Rödl, and Schacht conjectured that, for any fixed graph $F$, the number of homomorphic copies of $F$ in a given $n$-vertex $(o(1),d)$-dense graph is at least $(1-o(1))d^{e(F)}n^{v(F)}$. Despite considerable effort, only a few graphs are known to satisfy the conjecture. We find a new broad class of graphs that satisfy the conjecture, including cographs.

papers.title: Two-orbit right-angled Polytopes and Hypertopes
papers.abstract: Abstract polytopes and hypertopes are thin and residually-connected incidence geometries or, equivalently, chamber systems. Their degree of regularity is understood by looking at the action of their automorphism group on the set of their chambers. When this action has only one orbit, they are called regular. In this article, we are interested in polytopes and hypertopes with exactly two orbits on their chambers. Let $I = \{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. For any $J\subsetneq I$ with $|I| \geq 3$, we show that there exists a class $2_J$ two-orbit hypertope whose diagram is any graph on $|I|$ vertices, with edges all labeled by $\infty$. In order to do so, we first establish a general framework for constructing hypertopes as quotient of chamber systems, and then exploit the machinery of acylindrically hyperbolic groups for showing that this framework can be used to create two-orbit polytopes and hypertopes of class $2_J$. Note that all polytopes and hypertopes constructed in this paper are infinite.

papers.title: Existence and uniqueness of bound states with prescribed number of nodes for nonlinear dispersive equations on spherically symmetric manifolds
papers.abstract: Standing waves $e^{iωt}u(x)$ of nonlinear dispersive equations, such as the nonlinear Schrödinger and Klein--Gordon equations, have a profile $u$ that solves a nonlinear elliptic ODE of the form $Δu+f(u)=0$. We prove the existence of radial bound states with a prescribed number of nodal surfaces for this equation, on a large class of spherically symmetric manifolds and nonlinearities $f$. Under mild assumptions, we prove uniqueness of such bound states for the model nonlinearity $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u-u$. Both existence and uniqueness results apply to some manifolds with a singularity at the origin.

papers.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong results in classical code generation and are increasingly used to write the unit tests that safeguard that code. Whether they can do the same for quantum software is less clear, because quantum programs are probabilistic, depend on numerical tolerances, and are judged by domain-specific checkers, so a well-formed test can still disagree with the benchmark's verdict. Existing quantum benchmarks measure whether a model produces a correct solution, but not whether its tests can distinguish correct implementations from faulty ones. We introduce QTestBench, a framework that evaluates LLM-generated quantum test suites against independent benchmark checkers, never treating the tests themselves as ground truth. For each task, QTestBench prompts models to produce syntactic, semantic, and behavioral tests, injects candidate solutions at runtime, and compares each test verdict with the checker's label under three validation cohorts, each answering a distinct diagnostic question. We benchmark five LLMs on eight PennyLane QHack challenges and ten Qiskit HumanEval tasks. Generated suites almost always execute, but discrimination lags behind: the best generator reaches a test quality of 0.71 on QHack and 0.34 on Qiskit HumanEval, so executability alone overstates test quality. Oracle-verified synthetic mutants stabilize bug-detection estimates when natural faulty solutions are scarce, as on three of ten Qiskit tasks that yield none. QTestBench offers a reproducible, cross-framework benchmark for the trustworthiness of LLM-generated quantum tests.

papers.title: Diversity-Aware Ensemble of Quantum-Classical Models via Combinatorial Fusion
papers.abstract: Variational quantum circuits (VQCs) are highly sensitive to circuit architecture, yet most quantum machine learning pipelines select a single best design and discard the remaining candidates. This paper addresses whether the structural diversity across quantum circuit search spaces can be used to produce stronger predictions through model fusion. We apply Combinatorial Fusion Analysis (CFA), a model fusion framework that selects and combines multiple scoring systems using rank-score function (RSF) and cognitive diversity (CD), to a pool of 29 architecturally diverse classical models and quantum circuits. Using a diversity-aware model selection method, we identify subsets of maximally diverse models and combine them with both score and rank combination. Experiments on four binary classification benchmarks covering different domains demonstrate that CFA-based hybrid classical-quantum fusion consistently outperform the best individual model on every dataset considered with improvements up to 6.03% in accuracy. When comparing with relevant literatures, the CFA framework further achieves superior performance across all four datasets.

papers.title: Warm-IP: A Path-Following ADMM Warm Start for Interior-Point Quadratic Programming
papers.abstract: Interior-point (IP) methods are powerful second-order optimization algorithms but can make slow progress during early iterations. We propose Warm-IP, a hybrid framework that combines a path-following variant of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with a primal--dual IP method. The ADMM phase generates a warm start that remains close to the central path, enabling the subsequent IP phase to rapidly refine the solution to high accuracy. We evaluate Warm-IP on a diverse collection of real-world and synthetic quadratic programming (QP) instances and compare it with leading commercial solvers (MOSEK and Gurobi) and open-source solvers (Clarabel, PIQP, and OSQP). We also curate and release a new benchmark of large-scale QPs from cancer radiotherapy treatment planning, built from real patient data and provided in canonical QP form, with instances containing hundreds of thousands of constraints. Warm-IP substantially outperforms existing solvers on large-scale problems. On the large-scale radiotherapy benchmark comprising 60 lung cancer cases, for example, Warm-IP solves an instance in 47 seconds on average with no failures, while the strongest competitors, MOSEK and Gurobi, average 55 seconds with failures on 23\% of the cases and roughly 240 seconds with no failures, respectively. To support reproducibility and future benchmarking, we publicly release the implementation and benchmark data through a \href{https://github.com/Radiotherapy-Optimization/Warm-IP}{GitHub repository}. These results demonstrate that appropriately warm-started IP methods can combine the rapid initial progress of first-order methods with the high-accuracy convergence of second-order methods.

papers.title: Constrained Probabilistic Numerics: Gaussian Process Solvers for Linear PDEs under Linear Inequality Constraints
papers.abstract: Gaussian process solvers for linear partial differential equations (PDEs) return posteriors rather than point estimates, but they condition only on equality information: the PDE residual, boundary data, and measurements. Many solutions of interest also obey inequality constraints, including nonnegativity, monotonicity, and absence of arbitrage, which equality conditioning cannot enforce. We prove that conditioning a Gaussian process prior jointly on linear equality observations and a finite-dimensional inequality event is equivalent to conditioning sequentially in terms of Borel measures on the solution space. The physics-informed posterior is therefore a valid prior for the inequality update at virtual points. The combined law is non-Gaussian yet computable through truncated-Gaussian moments, and neither the PDE conditioning nor the inequality update requires modification. We evaluated the construction on a Poisson benchmark, option-price surfaces, and air-quality fields. Under incomplete boundary data, a monotonicity constraint lowered the error of a two-dimensional Poisson reconstruction by $63\%$. On a real S&P 500 option chain thinned to $20$ retained quotes, no-arbitrage constraints reduced held-out extrapolation error by $22\%$ and cut the calendar-arbitrage rate from $10\%$ to $1\%$. On four real air-quality snapshots, nonnegativity reduced a Gaussian moment-based sub-zero-tail proxy by $74\%$ at the sparsest monitor count. Changes in mean accuracy and constraint diagnostics differed across data regimes. The probability of the noisy virtual constraint event under the equality posterior measures agreement with the specified bounds before the update. The construction turns admissibility from a post-processing step into conditioning information for probabilistic PDE solvers.

papers.title: The (right) homotopy between two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms
papers.abstract: Let $f$, $g\colon A\to B$ be two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms between two A$_{\infty}$-algebras (linear over a commutative ring $\mathbb{K}$). In this paper, we compare different notions of (right) homotopy between $f$ and $g$. We note that the A$_{\infty}$-algebra $B\otimes R$, where $R:=\mathbb{K}[t,dt]$, is a model for the interval $[0,1]\times B$ in the sense of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono, and we give a short alternative proof, in the unfiltered case, of the existence of comparison morphisms between such models. We use it to prove that two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms are homotopic à la Seidel if and only if, considered as morphisms of 2-colored DG operads, they are elementary homotopic à la Markl-Shnider-Stasheff through a homotopy which is constant on the two monochromatic parts. We also provide an example of two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms which are elementary homotopic but not weakly equivalent (and so homotopic à la Seidel). Moreover, over a field, we observe that the models for the interval are good path objects in the category of A$_{\infty}$-algebras with (non strict) A$_{\infty}$-morphisms, and we explain why weakly equivalent A$_{\infty}$-morphisms need not be homotopic.

papers.title: Replica Transition at Measurement-Altered Ising Criticality
papers.abstract: Performing measurements on gapless quantum ground states can give rise to new universal phenomena, whose origins remain poorly understood even for the paradigmatic Ising critical point. Replica methods offer a natural framework to study such post-measurement ensembles, with the replica limit $Q\to 1$ describing physical Born-averaged observables. Here we show that, for the monitored critical Ising chain, the replicated post-measurement ensemble of states itself undergoes a phase transition precisely at the physically relevant replica limit $Q \to 1$, preventing standard replica treatments. We use boundary conformal field theory (BCFT) methods to explain the underlying mechanism of this transition. Our methods yield a perturbative analytic calculation of the universal $O(1)$ constant in the Shannon entropy of the measurement record, previously known only numerically. We also apply our tools to study measurement-averaged spin correlators, providing a unified description of the universal properties of measurement outcomes and post-measurement states in the critical Ising chain.

papers.title: Linearity of Graph Manifold Groups
papers.abstract: We complete the proof that every compact 3-manifold group is linear. Specifically, we construct a faithful representation in GL5(Q[u]) for a finite-index subgroup of every closed non-geometric graph-manifold group.

papers.title: Initialization-Dependent Solution Selection by the Euler-Maruyama Scheme for a Degenerate SDE
papers.abstract: We study the Euler-Maruyama approximation of the degenerate stochastic differential equation $dX_t = |X_t|^α\,dW_t$, $0 < α< 1/2$, $X_0 = 0$, for which uniqueness in law fails. The Euler scheme started exactly from zero is trapped by the absorbing solution, whereas a nonzero initialization $x_h \to 0$ can select a different weak solution. We identify the initialization-dependent limiting regimes. The critical spatial scale is $r_h = h^{1/[2(1-α)]}$, and the relevant depth parameter is $Θ_h = h\log(1+\log^+(r_h/|x_h|))$. If $Θ_h \to 0$, the scheme converges to the non-sticky weak solution. If $Θ_h \to θ\in (0,\infty)$, it converges to the solution that stays at zero for the deterministic time $θ/|\logα|$ and then evolves as the non-sticky solution. If $Θ_h \to \infty$, the scheme converges to the absorbing solution. The proof is based on an exact scale-invariant Euler chain, a logarithmic exit-time law of large numbers, a discrete Tanaka occupation estimate, and a compact-uniform restart argument. Every finite deterministic delay can be obtained by a suitable vanishing initialization, while oscillating depth parameters yield process-level nonconvergence. Thus a vanishing initialization can survive in the limit as a macroscopic deterministic delay and thereby act as a solution selector for the Euler-Maruyama approximation.

papers.title: Adaptive Variance Reduction without Knowing Oracle Smoothness
papers.abstract: Variance reduction improves the convergence rate of stochastic non-convex optimization under the average smoothness condition. Existing adaptive variance reduction methods are especially designed for average smoothness and do not adapt to standard smoothness. In this paper, we study how one algorithm can adapt to these two settings and the noiseless setting without knowing the smoothness constants or the variance bound. Given the gradient budget $T$, we develop a two-phase method. The first phase compares two independent gradients and switches to normalized momentum when their difference exceeds a threshold. This phase provides both a candidate with standard smooth and noiseless guarantees and also ensures a bounded expected function gap for the second variance reduction phase. The resulting rates are $O(T^{-1/3})$ under average smoothness, $O(T^{-1/4})$ under standard smoothness, and $O(T^{-1/2})$ without noise. When $T$ is unknown, we propose a method with two paths that attain the corresponding rates with logarithmic factors in the stochastic settings. Here, we use a variance reduction path to deal with average smoothness and employ the AdaGrad-Norm for standard smoothness and noiseless setting. Neither method restarts from the initial point or requires a growing number of oracle calls in each round.

papers.title: On the failure of additivity of inversion numbers for dijoins
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be an oriented graph. For $X \subseteq V(D)$, the inversion of $X$ in $D$ is the oriented graph that is obtained via changing the direction of all edges which have both endpoints in $X$. The inversion number of $D$, $\operatorname{inv}(D)$, is the minimum number of inversions necessary in order to remove all cycles from $D$. A dijoin $D_1 \to D_2$ is the oriented graph obtained by taking disjoint copies of $D_1,D_2$ and adding edges from all $v \in V(D_1)$ to each $u \in V(D_2)$. It was conjectured by Bang-Jensen, da Silva and Havet that $\operatorname{inv}(D_1 \to D_2) = \operatorname{inv}(D_1) + \operatorname{inv}(D_2)$ for all $D_1, D_2$. This was disproved by simultaneous constructions of various $D_1$, $D_2$ with $\operatorname{inv}(D_1 \to D_2) = \operatorname{inv}(D_1)+\operatorname{inv}(D_2)-1$. However, no known constructions achieved more than this gain of 1. Moreover, all of the constructions exploit a gap of 1 between $\operatorname{inv}(D)$ and the minimum rank of a family of related matrices, a gap that can never be more than 1, suggesting that perhaps something close to the original conjecture might be true. We prove that in fact additivity fails badly. In particular, for all $\varepsilon>0$ we show that there exist tournaments $D_1$, $D_2$ with arbitrarily large inversion numbers such that $\operatorname{inv}(D_1 \to D_2) \leq \left(\frac{1}{2} +\varepsilon\right)(\operatorname{inv}(D_1)+\operatorname{inv}(D_2))$.

papers.title: Analysis of an inexact Schwarz domain decomposition method in 3D
papers.abstract: We consider an inexact version of the Schwarz domain decomposition method in $3$D to solve a Laplace problem in a domain that is the union of two overlapping spheres. We solve each subproblem approximately by projecting its boundary data $L^2$-orthogonally onto the space of spherical harmonics of degree at most $N$. The model problem arises from the ddCOSMO solver used for implicit solvation in computational chemistry. We analyze the Schwarz-spherical domain decomposition method by establishing a new variant of the maximum principle.

papers.title: The generator problem for C*-algebras with comparison
papers.abstract: We show that certain classes of unital, simple, separable C*-algebras with comparison are singly generated, including tracially AF algebras and monotracial crossed products of actions on the Cantor space. In particular, we show that simple, separable, tracially AF algebras have generator rank one.

papers.title: Randomized Momentum Transport with Cheap Predictors
papers.abstract: Momentum methods such as STORM and second-order momentum track the gradient by adding a transport correction to momentum, at the cost of an extra oracle call per iteration. We introduce randomized momentum transport, which evaluates the correction with probability $q$ and otherwise uses a cheap prediction, with importance weighting that preserves the conditional mean and adds $(q^{-1}-1)$ times the prediction loss to the variance. Under transport-bias, second-moment, and residual-control assumptions, linear minimization oracle (LMO) updates, including normalized, sign, and exact spectral (Muon) directions, retain an $O(T^{-1/3})$ stationarity bound for each fixed $q>0$ with a single-gradient initialization. For unnormalized STORM, some $q<1$ lowers the leading coefficient of our sufficient gradient budget if and only if the gradient-difference noise modulus exceeds the smoothness constant, by at most about $10\%$. An online diagonal predictor admits a regret-to-convergence guarantee. At approximately equal oracle cost, querying a quarter of the corrections lowers the final training loss by $18$ to $43\%$ on MNIST1D and raises the test accuracy of Hessian-vector transport on CIFAR-10 by $1.5$ points.

papers.title: Optimal Algorithms for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Stochastic Optimization with Constraints
papers.abstract: We present new algorithms for stochastic optimization problems in which the objective is neither smooth nor convex, subject to a convex constraint set. Our algorithms return a $(δ,\varepsilon)$-Goldstein stationary point, as recently defined for constrained problems by Liu et al. (2024), with improved complexities, and are the first to achieve optimal convergence rates for this task in several settings. In particular, we design projection-based and projection-free algorithms that achieve a $\widetilde O(δ^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3})$ rate using stochastic gradients, which we show to be optimal, and a $\widetilde O(dδ^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3})$ rate using zeroth-order queries, which is also optimal in its dependence on the dimension $d$ and improves over prior work. Notably, our lower bound is given in terms of the Frank-Wolfe gap and holds even for smooth problems, which is of independent interest. These results show that in nonconvex stochastic optimization, the convergence rate is degraded neither by the presence of constraints nor by nonsmoothness. Our analysis is based on a reduction to online linear optimization, extending a related technique from unconstrained optimization.

papers.title: Geometry-Aware Multi-Objective Optimization: Norm-Constrained Oracles with Entropic Weight Updates
papers.abstract: Multiple-gradient descent is typically formulated in Euclidean geometry, whereas matrix-aware optimizers use directions induced by other norms. We analyze a single-loop multi-objective method combining a norm-constrained linear minimization oracle with entropic updates of task weights. For any finite-dimensional norm pair, we establish an $O(T^{-1/2})$ ergodic stationarity rate in the deterministic setting, deriving the required trajectory gradient bound from smoothness and lower-boundedness in the unregularized case. With stochastic gradients and a bounded-gradient assumption, one persistent blended-gradient momentum buffer yields an $O(T^{-1/4})$ rate whose leading term has no explicit dependence on the number of tasks. We also establish static regret for the inner weighting objective on arbitrary bounded gradient sequences and, with entropy regularization and a weight floor, iteration-wise inner-gap control after burn-in while retaining ergodic stationarity, conditional on a trajectory gradient bound. The optimal blended gradient can be nonunique in spectral and sign geometries, motivating a selection-independent inner gap. Our analysis extends the spectral construction studied by concurrent MOON to general norms. Experiments compare the method with existing multi-task optimizers and examine its oracle, weighting, and momentum choices.

papers.title: Pseudofinite abelian groups and asymptotic classes of finite abelian groups
papers.abstract: This paper studies pseudofinite abelian groups and counting properties of definable sets in finite abelian groups and their ultraproducts. First, we characterize pseudofinite abelian groups in terms of Szmielew invariants and, building on results of Macintyre, extend this analysis to obtain a characterization of pseudofinite $ω$-stable abelian groups. We then give an alternative proof that the class of finite abelian groups forms a multidimensional exact class, explicitly describing the possible cardinalities of definable sets in classes of finite abelian groups. We also investigate $N$-dimensional asymptotic classes of finite abelian groups and provide a series of examples showing that, despite the exactness result, several natural classes of finite abelian groups fail to be $N$-dimensional asymptotic classes for every $N\geq 1$. Finally, in an appendix, we characterize the SU-rank of pseudofinite abelian groups, building on work of Rogers. In particular, we show that for every pseudofinite abelian group $A$, either $\operatorname{Th}(A,+)$ is superstable of finite SU-rank or it is strictly stable.

papers.title: Scattering for the KP-II equation
papers.abstract: We prove scattering in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ for real-valued solutions of the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili II (KP-II) equation with localized initial data. No smallness assumption is made, no zero mean condition is imposed, and the admissible data include all Schwartz functions. The proof uses the inverse scattering transform attached to the heat operator. It rests on three ingredients: an a priori bound for the scalar $\bar\partial$ problem which depends on the size of the scattering coefficient but not on its oscillating phase, a nonlinear Plancherel identity proved by analytic continuation from small data, and an estimate showing that the nonlinear part of the reconstruction is negligible on the propagation cones of free waves. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result establishing scattering for the KP-II equation for every real-valued Schwartz initial datum.

papers.title: Asymmetric minimal mass blow-up for the quintic NLS on a star graph
papers.abstract: This work is concerned with the focusing quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a star graph with two edges, with a delta interaction of arbitrary strength at the vertex. We construct a non-radial, minimal mass, finite time blow-up solution, whose singularity forms at an arbitrarily prescribed interior point of one edge. Our approach is based on a suitable cut-off of the standard pseudoconformal blow-up solution of the focusing quintic NLS on the line, inspired by Ogawa-Tsutsumi and Burq-Gérard-Tzvetkov. A noteworthy feature of our construction is the persistence of the domain of the Hamiltonian under the flow, obtained by the persistence of regularity method of Kato. We also identify a two-parameter family of distinct blow-up profiles, which should play a central role in the classification of non-radial minimal mass blow-up solutions on the star graph. Our construction is generic and can be extended to a star graph with an arbitrary number of edges. It can certainly also be adapted to other types of metric graphs.

papers.title: Estimation, Sensitivity Analysis, and Optimization of Distortion Risk Measures via Simulation
papers.abstract: We present a simulation-based method for the estimation, sensitivity analysis, and optimization of distortion risk measures (DRMs), a class of performance measures that capture a wide range of risk attitudes through an underlying distortion function. Existing simulation approaches often approximate DRMs using numerical partitions or empirical distributions. We show that, when the distortion function is piecewise polynomial, the nonlinear structure of a DRM can be handled exactly, without introducing distortion discretization error, using only simulated system outputs. This representation enables the development of a computational method that integrates finite-difference techniques for sensitivity analysis and for solving a broad class of differentiable risk-based optimization problems. Under suitable conditions, we establish strong consistency and convergence rates for DRM estimation, sensitivity analysis, and optimization. We further extend the approach to non-polynomial distortion functions through polynomial approximation. Numerical experiments on synthetic and calibrated financial examples demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach across a range of applications.

papers.title: Travel time tomography for elliptically anisotropic elastic planar media
papers.abstract: We study the gauge of the travel time tomography problem for elliptically anisotropic planar media. Under this assumption the respective slowness surfaces consist of an inner ellipse and an outer circle. Hence, the singularities of seismic waves propagate on geodesics given by two Riemannian metrics of which the one related to shear waves is conformally Euclidean. We show that if both of these metrics are lens rigid then, up to boundary fixing diffeomorphisms, each elliptically anisotropic stiffness tensor is uniquely determined by the lens data whenever it has at least one isotropic point. If none of those points exists, then there are exactly two elliptically anisotropic stiffness tensors with the same lens data. Clearly, not all boundary fixing diffeomorphisms preserve the imposed structure of the slowness surface. We show that the set of well-behaved diffeomorphisms is never a subgroup of all boundary fixing diffeomorphisms. Our proofs are based on an interplay of algebra and geometry, and the key of the proofs is a characterization of the elliptic anisotropy via several polynomial conditions.

papers.title: Topping's conjecture for solutions of harmonic map flow with isolated bubbles
papers.abstract: By establishing a weighted Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality for maps which are close to a fixed harmonic map modulo scaling, we prove Topping's conjecture on continuity of the body map in the case of finite time singularities at which only isolated bubbles form.

papers.title: The $E_6$ normal forms: semisimple deformations, geometry, DT invariants, and the $E_{6,\infty}$ order
papers.abstract: We study the completed Jacobi algebras of $x^3+xy^3+p(y)$ for $\operatorname{ord}_yp=n\ge4$. The explicit normal-form morsification, the filtered length and centre proofs, and the cyclic terminal identities give finite free semisimple deformations. For every parameter of finite order we construct a polynomial curve neighbourhood and a local projective small contraction; the resulting geometric GV and Donaldson--Thomas calculations identify the block multiplicities. The one-dimensional limit $E_{6,\infty}$ is studied separately as an order: we determine its normalization, conductor, radical-idealizer chain, and maximal overorders. The canonical chain yields a nine-dimensional finite quotient whose Ringel dual is isomorphic to its opposite. An expanded construction gives a choice-independent $22$-dimensional quotient and a $40$-dimensional Ringel dual; a corner quotient relates the two finite constructions. The length and centre formulas are proved by a filtered comparison with a homogeneous matrix order and by terminal identities at the exceptional endpoint.

papers.title: Stabilized SQP Method for Convex Piecewise Linear-Quadratic Composite Optimization Problems
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the local convergence analysis of the stabilized sequential quadratic programming method for a class of composite optimization problems with convex piecewise linear- quadratic (CPLQ) modeling functions. We demonstrate that an appropriate second-order sufficient condition (SOSC) -formulated for composite problems- alone is sufficient to guarantee local superlin- ear convergence of the primal-dual sequence generated by this method. Furthermore, we examine the relaxation of the SOSC and show that it can be replaced with a weaker noncriticality of the associated Lagrange multiplier, provided, the modeling function is polyhedral and a relative interior condition is satisfied. We also present counterexamples showing that the relative interior condition is indispensable and that this relaxation fails for general CPLQ modeling functions.

papers.title: Sharp upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products
papers.abstract: We obtain sharp isoperimetric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products whose bases are compact Riemannian manifolds with boundary and whose fibres are closed Riemannian manifolds. These bounds involve the volume of the warped product and of its boundary, as well as the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator on the fibre and the Steklov eigenvalues of the base. After separation of variables, these bounds are obtained by comparison with auxiliary Helmholtz-Steklov problems on the base involving weighted Laplace operators naturally induced by the warping function. We also study the effect of various natural geometric constraints, such as the warping function being identically equal to one on the boundary. The proofs make use of various spectral approximation methods, including homogenisation on manifolds when the fibres are one-dimensional.

papers.title: Adjoint-Based Stochastic Analysis for Fatigue of Aeroelastic and Frictional Systems
papers.abstract: As engineering systems are optimized to reduce weight and improve performance, vibration behavior, including nonlinear effects, is becoming increasingly important to analyze. While methods such as harmonic balance are popular for analyzing periodic nonlinear vibration behavior, these analyses often only consider deterministic loading. However, real applications experience additional noise in the excitation, and alternative approaches are frequently limited to smaller models. This work expands on a recent approach to calculate a time-varying covariance using a linearized system around a periodic nonlinear response. Specifically, numerical conditioning is addressed and improved for cases increasing from a few degrees of freedom to hundreds of degrees of freedom. The algorithm is then extended to capture correlations across both space and time via a period-spanning covariance matrix. Model reduction is proposed for this calculation to maintain computational efficiency. The period-spanning covariance matrix is used to sample full stochastic cycles and estimate fatigue-relevant statistics up to 1393 times faster than stochastic time integration. Importantly, the present methodology uses the same gradient information as stability analyses and continuation solutions, so it can easily be applied for many nonlinear analyses. The methodology is demonstrated for two beam systems: one with unsteady aerodynamic forces and another with a Bouc-Wen frictional tip force. For the aeroelastic model, statistics are accurately estimated via the present approach. For the frictional system, some errors are introduced compared to stochastic time integration and are attributed to the linear time-periodic nature of the system used in the present stochastic calculations. However, estimated stochastic statistics remain useful given the significant reduction in computation time.

papers.title: The tensor product of the Fremlin tensor product of Banach lattice algebras
papers.abstract: We study the Arens regularity of the Fremlin projective tensor product of Banach lattice algebras. We firrst introduce and investigate L-weakly almost periodic functionals, a class of functionals defind in terms of L-weak compactness of their orbits. We obtain a characterization of these functionals in terms of bounded disjoint sequences and use it to analyze the Fremlin projective tensor product. In particular, we prove that, for nontrivial Banach attice algebras A and B, Arens regularity of A j jB implies Arens regularity of both A and B. The converse, however, fails: we construct two Arens regular Banach lattice algebras whose Fremlin projective tensor product is not Arens regular. We also establish several sufficient conditions for the Arens regularity of A j jB, including conditions involving the positive Schur property and order continuity of the norm on the space of regular operators. Finally, we show that when both factors are Banach f-algebras, their Fremlin projective tensor product is Arens regular.

papers.title: List chromatic number of $G(n,r,s)$ graphs
papers.abstract: We study the list chromatic number of generalized Johnson graphs. Recall that the vertices of such graphs are all possible $r$-element subsets of $[n] = \{1, \dotsc, n\}$ and an edge is drawn between two vertices if and only if corresponding sets have exactly $s$ common elements. We prove that for any fixed $s \geq 1$ and $r \geq 2s + 2$ we have $χ_L(G(n,r,s)) = Θ(n^{s+1}\ln n)$. In case where $s = 0$ we prove that for all $4\ln n \leq r \leq n/20$ we have $χ_L(G(n,r,0)) \geq \frac{n}{120}\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)$. Together with previous results of Bulankina, Inozemtsev and Kupavskii this proves that $χ_L(G(n,r,0)) = Θ\left(n\ln\left(\frac{en}{r}\right)\right)$ uniformly for $2 \leq r \leq (1/2-\varepsilon)n$.

papers.title: Holomorphic approximation for Hamiltonian diffeomorphism groups via the Symplectic Density Property
papers.abstract: We show that the cotangent bundle of a holomorphically flexible Stein manifold has the symplectic density property. As application we deduce holomorphic approximation for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of real cotangent bundles by complex symplectic automorphisms of the complexified cotangent bundles, which preserve the real bundle, in the Carleman sense, i.e. in the Whitney topology.

papers.title: Non-Bloch band theory for finite banded non-Hermitian Toeplitz matrices
papers.abstract: Non-Bloch band theory recovers the open-boundary spectrum of a non-Hermitian chain from its Bloch Hamiltonian evaluated along the generalised Brillouin zone rather than the unit circle. We develop its finite-size counterpart for banded Toeplitz matrices with real open-boundary spectrum. Reality of the spectrum forces the generalised Brillouin zone to be parametrised by an analytic polar curve, so the known sufficient condition for a real spectrum is also necessary under some mild non-degeneracy conditions. At finite size $n$, the eigenvalues of the original and the symmetrised Bloch Hamiltonians are given by samples at $n$ quantised momenta from the same limiting band, although separated by a phase mismatch of order $1/n$ which we obtain in closed form. Iterating this correction $K$ times yields a quantisation rule on the generalised Brillouin zone reproducing the finite spectrum with an error $\mathcal{O}(n^{-K-1})$ for any fixed $K$. At finite size, the generalised Brillouin zone itself is unchanged and only its parametrisation depends on $n$.

papers.title: Relaxed Centralized Circumcentered-Reflection Methods for Convex Feasibility: Convergence and Finite Termination
papers.abstract: Projection methods are among the most widely used techniques for solving convex feasibility problems due to their simplicity and robustness. However, classical projection-based algorithms and existing circumcentered-reflection methods generally provide only asymptotic convergence. In this paper, we introduce a relaxed version of the centralized circumcentered-reflection method (cCRM) obtained through an extrapolation of the circumcenter step. We first analyze the two-set case and then extend the proposed approach to the successive framework for multiple convex sets, including under- and over-relaxation and a backtracking strategy. The convergence analysis establishes Fejér monotonicity and global convergence under suitable conditions, while local error-bound assumptions yield linear convergence and standard regularity assumptions imply superlinear convergence. Motivated by finitely convergent projection methods based on perturbed feasible sets, we further investigate a perturbed relaxed formulation designed to achieve finite termination. Numerical experiments show good practical performance, comparable to and competitive with the finitely convergent PACA method. The results also provide clear numerical evidence of finite termination in the tested instances.

papers.title: Dynamical Lie Algebras for Fixed-Gate Quantum Ansätze
papers.abstract: Parameterized Quantum Circuits have emerged as a central framework for variational quantum algorithms in the NISQ regime, with major applications in quantum simulation, combinatorial optimization, and, more recently, quantum machine learning (QML). By developing a new approach for computing dynamical Lie algebras associated with quantum circuits combining parametrized gates and non-parametrized entangling gates, we aim to extend the applicability of recent algebraic results to architectures that are actually used in quantum machine learning.

papers.title: A 9-dimensional nilpotent Lie algebra isomorphic to its complex conjugate admitting no real form
papers.abstract: We give an explicit example of a 9-dimensional 5-step nilpotent complex Lie algebra, generated by two elements, that is isomorphic to its complex conjugate but has no real form. In contrast to the earlier 10-dimensional examples, our proof is completely elementary and very short.

papers.title: Critical Ising model as the $M(4,3)$ minimal model of conformal field theory
papers.abstract: We construct a linear map from the space of spin polynomials in the critical Ising model on a lattice to the state space of the $M(4,3)$ minimal model of conformal field theory. The kernel of the map consists precisely of null fields, i.e., spin polynomials that vanish in all correlations. For a polynomial $\Op$ which is not a null field, we define its scaling dimension $Δ_{\Op}\in\Z_{\geq0}\cup(\Z_{\geq0}+\frac{1}{8}),$ to be the lowest $\Loper{0}+\Loperbar{0}$ eigenvalue in the decomposition of its image into homogeneous components. We show that as the mesh size $δ$ goes to zero, the rescaled field $δ^{-Δ_{\Op}}\Op$ has a non-trivial scaling limit, when inserted in correlations with other such fields. Moreover, all these limits can be expressed in terms of correlations of primary fields of $M(4,3)$ and the Virasoro action in the continuum. The highest weight vectors of $M(4,3)$, the joint eigenvectors of $\Loper{0}$ and $\Loperbar{0}$ with the same eigenvalues $0,1/16,1/2$ for both, are the images of the constant $1$, the spin at a single lattice vertex, and the energy at a single lattice edge, respectively. For the proof, we construct a map from a larger lattice field space, accommodating also fermion and disorder insertions, to a direct sum of two fermionic Fock spaces. This direct sum contains contains the state spaces of both the $M(4,3)$ and the free fermion CFT. The main technical ingredient of the proof is a new version of the exact fermionic current action on the space of lattice local fields due to C. Hongler, K.K. and F. Viklund, combined with some new advances in discrete complex analysis. Our results are valid on arbitrary isoradial graphs.

papers.title: The second type of power mean bounds for the hypergeometric mean
papers.abstract: In this paper, by using signs rule for a class of special power series and for the Laplace integrals, we find the best power mean bounds for the hypergeometric function (sharp at the right endpoint). Our results contain many known conclusions.

papers.title: QTN-RQNN: Quantum Tensor Network-Based Recurrent Quantum Neural Network
papers.abstract: Resource constraints and imperfect quantum operations remain major challenges for quantum machine learning (QML) on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices, particularly for fault-diagnosis tasks involving imbalanced and heterogeneous data. This work proposes QTN-RQNN, a Quantum Tensor Network-Based Recurrent Quantum Neural Network that integrates tensor-network-inspired nearest-neighbor interactions with recurrent quantum processing. The model sequentially encodes input features while propagating quantum memory across recurrent steps and incorporates QSMOTE for class balancing. QTN-RQNN is evaluated on four heterogeneous fault-diagnosis datasets SPID, CWRUBD, EFDD, and SFDD and compared with QNN, QTN-QNN, and RQNN baselines through classification, ablation, multi-seed, convergence, and quantum-resource analyses. Results show dataset-dependent predictive behavior, indicating that increased quantum architectural complexity does not universally improve classification. On SPID, QTN-RQNN improves the RQNN F1-score from 0.3077 to 0.4516 and ROC-AUC from 0.4485 to 0.6970, while the remaining datasets exhibit different performance-resource trade-offs and sensitivity to recurrent timesteps and circuit depth. Across all datasets, QTN-RQNN reduces the two-qubit-gate count from 32 to 24 per sample relative to RQNN, corresponding to a 25% reduction without increasing the four-qubit requirement; the same relative reduction is obtained for QTN-QNN over QNN. These findings establish QTN-RQNN as a resource-conscious recurrent quantum architecture and highlight the need to jointly consider predictive performance and circuit-resource requirements for near-term quantum fault diagnosis.

papers.title: On a conjecture on Romanoff type representations
papers.abstract: Let $r_1,\ldots,r_t$ be positive integers, and let $\mathcal A$ be the set of integers of the form $2^{k_1^{r_1}}+\cdots+2^{k_t^{r_t}}$, where $k_1,\ldots,k_t$ are positive integers. For any positive integer $n$, let $r(n)$ be the number of representations $n=p+a$ with $p$ an odd prime and $a\in \mathcal A$. We prove that if $r_1^{-1}+\cdots+r_t^{-1}=1$, then, for every fixed positive integer $m$, the set of integers $n$ with $r(n)\ge m$ has positive lower asymptotic density. In particular, this confirms a conjecture of Chen.

papers.title: Spread-out Furstenberg sets II: general configurations and fractal restricted projections
papers.abstract: We prove optimal dual Furstenberg estimates for Frostman and Katz--Tao configurations for which the shadings are not locally concentrated near pencils. The starting point is the sticky estimate of Orponen and Shmerkin in a companion paper. We deduce restricted projection theorems in the plane and in higher dimensions. In particular, Ahlfors-regular measures on the circle satisfy a Marstrand-type projection theorem. Applications include restricted projections to surfaces in the $\mathbb{G}(4,2)$ Grassmannian, pinned distances, discretized sum-product, and a new proof of the dimension formula for planar self-affine sets.

papers.title: Diffraction of waves by finite thin coatings: asymptotic expansion and effective models
papers.abstract: We consider the Helmholtz equation in a Dirichlet angular sector (which may be locally perturbed) covered on one side by a thin homogeneous layer. First, we propose an asymptotic expansion of the solution at any order and for any angle when the thickness of the layer tends to 0, using a matched asymptotic expansion. This consists in introducing different asymptotic expansions in three subdomains -- the vicinity of the corner, the layer and the rest of the domain -- that are linked through matching conditions. The presence of the corner makes these matching conditions delicate to derive because the fields have complex singular behaviors. We overcome this difficulty using a novel system of algebraic tools, including formal series and operators on these series. Moreover, we justify the asymptotic expansion with error estimates and provide details on the form of the expansion depending on the angle. We numerically validate this expansion up to order 5. This requires computing the behavior at infinity of some corner profiles. To do this, we introduce a Galerkin-type method enriched by complements at infinity. These complements are known functions that appear in the behavior at infinity of the corner profiles with coefficients that become unknowns of the system. Finally, we propose effective models of order 3, resp. 5 where, far from the corner, the layer is replaced with an effective Robin, resp. Ventcel, boundary condition and, near the corner, an artificial boundary is introduced and a Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) type condition is imposed. The DtN map relies on a modal decomposition of the truncated asymptotic expansion at order 3, resp. 5. The modes take into account the singular behavior of the expansion terms, the corner profiles and some algebraic matching coefficients. We prove the well-posedness of our effective models, as well as error estimates, and provide numerical results.

papers.title: Spread-out Furstenberg sets I: the sticky case
papers.abstract: We introduce spread-out measures, a notion of local non-concentration near pencils for measures on Grassmannians. We establish an optimal $δ$-discretized dual Furstenberg estimate for ``sticky spread-out'' shadings. A simple-to-state corollary is the following. Assume that $ν$ is an Ahlfors $s$-regular measure on $\mathbb{G}(2,1)$ with $s > 0$. Let $E \subset \mathbb{R}^{2}$ be a Borel set with equal Hausdorff and packing dimension. Then, $\dim_{\mathrm{H}} Π_{V}(E) = \min\{\dim_{\mathrm{H}} E,1\} \quad \text{for $ν$-a.e. } V \in S^1$. The general $δ$-discretized estimate for ``sticky spread out'' configurations here is the starting point for a more general theorem in the companion paper of Cohen, Shmerkin, Wang and Zakharov, where the ``stickiness'' hypothesis is removed. For instance, the assumption of equal Hausdorff and packing dimension in the result stated above will be dispensed with in the companion paper.

papers.title: Statistical inference for rough Burgers-type stochastic partial differential equations
papers.abstract: We consider the Burgers-type stochastic PDE \[ du = θ\,\partial_x^2 u\,dt + f(u)\,dt + g(u)\,\partial_x u\,dt + σ\,dW(t), \] driven by space--time white noise on the one-dimensional torus, where \(θ>0\) is the diffusivity parameter and \(σ>0\) the noise intensity. The transport term \(g(u)\,\partial_x u\) admits no classical interpretation, and we work with the mild solutions defined via rough paths following~\cite{Hairer2011}, for which the solution decomposes as \(u=ψ+R\) with \(ψ\) a stationary centred Gaussian process solving a damped stochastic heat equation and \(R\) a remainder. We first show that, away from the initial time, \(R\) is Lipschitz in space and Hölder in time of order strictly greater than \(1/2\), hence strictly smoother than \(ψ\) in both variables. We then compute exactly the spatial quadratic variation and the temporal quartic variation of \(ψ\), almost surely and not merely in \(L^{2}(Ω)\), and prove that the corresponding variations of \(u\) are unaffected by the remainder. Combined with an exact time-scaling identity, this separation of regularity scales yields strongly consistent pathwise estimators of \(θ\). To our knowledge this is the first inference procedure for an SPDE whose solution is defined only pathwise, as a measurable function of a rough path, rather than as an Itô process.
authors: Simon Chony Acosta Christian Olivera Ciprian Tudor

papers.title: TAP variational formula for 2-spin models with general interaction matrix and marginality
papers.abstract: We establish a Thouless--Anderson--Palmer (TAP) variational formula for the free energy of spherical $2$-spin models whose interaction matrices have a compactly supported limiting spectral distribution. The formula holds at every inverse temperature and, in particular, extends the TAP representation previously obtained for the spherical Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model. Our main contribution is a new microcanonical proof designed to handle marginality. We partition the sphere according to the smallest collection of top eigendirections carrying a prescribed fraction of the norm. On every element of this partition, the remaining degrees of freedom are effectively at high temperature and their contribution can be computed through spherical-integral asymptotics. The resulting auxiliary variational problem separates the macroscopic low-temperature contribution from the high-temperature fluctuation term; its maximization recovers the usual TAP functional and Plefka condition. This decomposition also shows why neighborhoods of the TAP maximizers alone do not capture the Gibbs mass: all eigendirections associated with large eigenvalues contribute on the same exponential scale, a manifestation of the marginality of spherical $2$-spin states.

papers.title: A discrete analogue of $\mathscr{N}=2$ super Weil-Petersson volumes
papers.abstract: We introduce a discrete spectral curve from $\mathscr{N}=2$ double-scaled SYK whose topological recursion defines quasi-polynomial volumes in integer boundary lengths. The curve has two edge theories: a local $\mathscr{N}=2$ theory at the lower edge and a bosonic theory at the upper edge. Focusing on the local $\mathscr{N}=2$ theory, we compute its finite-$q$ volumes and independently check the first few using the string equation. In the $q\rightarrow 1$ continuum limit, these recover the super Weil-Petersson volumes of Turiaci and Witten. Finally, we give an all-genus intersection-theoretic interpretation of these local volumes on the moduli space of stable marked curves, in terms of a deformed spin class with a gap-dependent $κ$-class dressing.

papers.title: Judd-Ofelt analysis and coherent spectroscopy of europium-based molecular complexes for quantum information applications
papers.abstract: Rare-earth-ion based molecular crystals are emerging as a promising platform for quantum information applications, combining long optical coherence times with the chemical tunability of coordination chemistry. Here we present a comprehensive optical characterisation of twelve Eu$^{3+}$-based molecular complexes, with a focus on the coherent $^{5}\text{D}_{0} \longrightarrow \ ^{7}\text{F}_{0}$ transition at $\sim$580 nm. Judd-Ofelt analyses are performed across all complexes, providing insights into ligand-field environments, local point-group symmetries, and the resulting branching ratios of the coherent transition. We find that lower point-group symmetry (C$_1$, C$_2$) yields higher branching ratios of the $^{5}\text{D}_{0} \longrightarrow \ ^{7}\text{F}_{0}$ transition, exceeding 1\% in several complexes. Optical inhomogeneous linewidths measured at 4.2 K reveal narrow linewidths for some complexes of below ten GHz, indicative of a highly ordered crystalline environment. Optical coherence measurements of one of the complexes, 5-Eu, yields an optical coherence time of $T_{\text{2}}^{\text{opt}} = 2.3~μ\mathrm{s}$ at 4.2 K, comparable to the best-performing molecular systems reported to date. Systematic characterisation and quantitative comparison will be key to find structure-property relations guiding rational design of optimised complexes for quantum information applications.

papers.title: The Renormalized Area--Willmore Relation
papers.abstract: In [1, Proposition 8.1], Alexakis and Mazzeo showed that the renormalized area of minimal surfaces in the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^3$ approaching the ideal boundary $\partial_\infty\mathbb{H}^3$ is the negative of the Willmore energy of their Euclidean conformal compactifications. In this paper, we investigate whether there are other geometric surface equations for which these two quantities satisfy a universal proportionality relation. We answer this question in the affirmative by extending the Alexakis--Mazzeo result to a broader class of geometric equations containing, as two distinguished cases, the equations defining generalized singular minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and linear Weingarten surfaces in $\mathbb{H}^3$. Moreover, for rotational linear Weingarten surfaces, we express both energies in terms of generalized hyperelliptic integrals and show that their doubles form a family of rotational tori in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose Willmore energies realize all values in $(2π^2,\infty)$, with a particular subfamily converging to the Clifford torus in $\mathcal{W}^{2,p}$ for every $1\leq p<\infty$, as the optimal value $2π^2$ is approached.

papers.title: Conditioning diffusions on a terminal bearing
papers.abstract: We study sampling of a diffusion on $[0,T]$ conditioned on its terminal position lying on a prescribed ray, i.e. on an exactly observed bearing. For a linear drift we derive closed-form expressions for the Doob $h$-function and its gradient. For a broad class of tracking models admitting a Kronecker block structure, the guiding term is obtained from a single row of a matrix exponential, and the conditioned process decomposes into independent radial and angular components. For a nonlinear drift, we construct a guided process using the $h$-function of the linear model and prove absolute continuity of the law of the true conditioned process with respect to the law of the guided process, with an explicit likelihood ratio. This result is used to devise an auxiliary particle filter for bearings observed sequentially in time without noise. Numerical experiments show that the proposed filter approximates the filtering distribution and estimates the log-likelihood considerably more accurately than the shifted Rayleigh filter, at the cost of a higher computing time.

papers.title: Regularization of a Divergent Arithmetic Product via the Asymptotic Monoid: The Case of $(-1)^{ω(n)}$
papers.abstract: We apply the generalized monoid of words and logarithmic-prefix functionals of \cite{C1} to the regularization of the divergent product \[ P_ω=\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} n^{(-1)^{ω(n)}}, \] where \(ω(n)\) is the number of distinct prime divisors of \(n\). The associated Dirichlet series \(D_ω(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}(-1)^{ω(n)}n^{-s}\) has a natural boundary at \(\Re(s)=0\), as established by Meretov (1987) and recovered here as a special case of the Estermann--Dahlquist theory of Euler products, which makes zeta regularization impossible: the derivative \(D_ω'(0)\) does not exist. This product therefore lies completely beyond the reach of classical regularization methods. We construct the canonical net encoding the sign sequence, define the logarithmic-prefix functional with exponent \(α=2\), and extract a finite value through the weighted evaluation functional of the monoid framework. The evaluation functional is shown to converge absolutely, and this convergence is unconditional: it follows from the classical zero-free region of \(ζ(s)\) (de la Vallée Poussin), which yields the effective bound \(T_ω(x)=O(x\,e^{-c\sqrt{\log x}})\) for some \(c>0\). Numerical computation up to \(N=10^7\) gives the regularized value \[ P_{ω,\mathrm{ren}}\approx 0.7731, \] a new constant of arithmetic origin that cannot be obtained by any classical summation method. We also compute the second derivative of the Dirichlet series at \(s=1\), \[ D_ω''(1)=8\,C_2\ln 2, \] where \(C_2\) is the Hardy--Littlewood twin prime constant, which provides an unconditional analytical link to the arithmetic structure of the sequence \((-1)^{ω(n)}\). A self-contained proof of the natural boundary, based on the Estermann--Dahlquist theorem, is given in Appendix~A.

papers.title: Compact lcK manifolds with Gauduchon parallel vector fields
papers.abstract:
We prove that on a compact locally conformally Kähler manifold, the existence of a non-trivial parallel vector field with respect to a Gauduchon connection $
abla^t$, for $t
e  rac{1}{3}$, forces the metric to be either Vaisman (for $t=-1$), globally conformally Kähler (for $t=1$), or Kähler for all other values of $t$. As a consequence, we characterize compact Vaisman manifolds in terms of their Bismut holonomy group. Moreover, we show that in complex dimension two, the existence of a non-trivial $
abla^ rac{1}{3}$-parallel vector field forces the metric to be globally conformally Kähler.

papers.title: Metastable confinement of particle systems near linearly stable McKean-Vlasov equilibria
papers.abstract: We establish a general metastability principle showing that the local stability of a McKean-Vlasov equilibrium implies exponentially long confinement of the associated particle system. Consider interacting diffusions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a general smooth and bounded interaction kernel and a globally Lipschitz drift that is dissipative at large distances. Assume the McKean-Vlasov equation has at least one equilibrium which is locally exponentially stable. We prove that the probability that the empirical measure leaves a sufficiently small fixed Wasserstein-1 neighborhood of the selected equilibrium before time $T$ is bounded by $C(1+T)e^{-cN}$, where $N$ is the number of particles and $C,c>0$ are independent of $N$ and $T$. Consequently, confinement holds up to times $e^{γN}$, for every $0<γ<c$, with exponentially small exit probability. The proof combines an explicit Volterra construction of the linearized Fokker-Planck semigroup, a mild representation of empirical fluctuations, and exponential maximal estimates for stochastic convolutions. Our approach does not require a gradient flow structure or reversibility of the equations.

papers.title: Finite-Size Limits of Adaptive Pauli Prediction
papers.abstract: Can quantum data reliably answer questions chosen from earlier results? We prove that $M$ adaptive Pauli predictions on $n$ qubits require $Ω(\sqrt{\min\{n,M\}})$ copies at fixed accuracy. Published upper bounds make this tight for $M\le n$. Thus $n$ adaptive predictions cost $Θ(\sqrt n)$ copies, whereas a fixed list costs only $O(\log n)$. The lower bound uses diagonal states and commuting observables, identifying a statistical cost of adaptation. We also quantify how this cost increases with precision.

papers.title: Actions of Fell bundles, II: tensor products and Fourier-Stieltjes algebras
papers.abstract: In the context of Fell bundles over discrete groups, we introduce and analyze suitable notions of direct sum and tensor product of actions of Fell bundles on Hilbert bundles. For $C^*$-dynamical systems, where actions arise from equivariant representations, we discuss how the tensor product of two such actions is related to the action associated with the tensor product of the underlying equivariant representations.
